P0215.title: Engine Shutoff Solenoid
P0215.summary: The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails.

causes.text: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger)
Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty
Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector
Pump control module faulty
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls while driving
Engine keeps running after ignition off (solenoid stuck open)

P0216.title: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
P0216.summary: P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings.

causes.text: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail
Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally
Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty
Low supply pressure on distributor pumps (lift pump, filter)
Pump installed incorrectly, drive gear misaligned

symptoms: Hard starting or stalling (distributor pump), smoke

P0217.title: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
P0217.summary: P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fuel to individual cylinders.

causes.text: Low coolant (leak, head gasket)
Thermostat stuck closed
Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged
Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading)
Extreme load (towing, gradient, heat) with an intact cooling system

symptoms: Temperature gauge in the red, overheat warning
Loss of power, limp mode, cylinders possibly shut off
Steam or coolant smell, coolant loss

P0218.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition
P0218.summary: P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent.

causes.text: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat)
Transmission fluid low or aged
Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system
Torque converter clutch slipping or internal damage
Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

P0219.title: Engine Overspeed Condition
P0219.summary: P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm for 1 s; Saab 2.2 diesel above 6,200 rpm, although fuel is cut from 5,000 rpm.

causes.text: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox)
Descending in too low a gear
Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring)
Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection

symptoms: Usually no lasting symptoms, only a stored code
Briefly very high revs, limiter intervening
After real overspeed: rattling, loss of power

P021A.title: Cylinder 7 Injection Timing
P021A.summary: P021A reports a fault in the injection timing of cylinder 7 on a diesel engine. Unlike P01D7/P01D8 ('over retarded/advanced', the result of the injector learning routine in overrun), this code has no direction, and what it checks is up to the manufacturer.

causes.text: Injector of cylinder 7 faulty (coil, armature, wear, deposits)
Injector wiring or connector: contact resistance, corrosion, chafing
Engine software sets the code falsely (update available for some models)
Injector driver stage or boost voltage in the engine module
Wrong injector code, contaminated fuel or loose injector clamp

symptoms: Rough running or misfire, rough idle
Loss of power, smoke or knocking possible

P0220.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P0220.summary: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor.

causes.text: Throttle body or sensor B faulty (worn track)
Wiring or connector at the throttle body (corrosion, break)
5 V reference disturbed (short in another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module input or monitoring processor faulty

symptoms: Check engine light and throttle warning light

P0221.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance

P0222.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low

Throttle body or sensor B faulty internally
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
Connector corrosion or water ingress
Engine module faulty

P0223.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High

P0224.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent

P0225.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0225.summary: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel.

causes.text: Sensor C or second throttle body faulty
Wiring or connector (supply, signal line)
5 V reference disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light and powertrain fault lamp

P0226.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
P0226.summary: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel.

causes.text: Wear or dirt on sensor C or the second throttle body
Contact resistance at connector or wiring
Throttle dirty or sticking
Engine module or software

P0227.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low
P0227.summary: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it.

causes.text: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground or open (chafing, connector)
5 V reference to the sensor open or loaded
Sensor C or second throttle body faulty
Corrosion or water in the throttle body connector
Engine module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (Ford also the wrench light)

P0228.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit High
P0228.summary: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it.

Signal wire shorted to 5 V or system voltage
Sensor C or throttle body faulty
Connector corroded or water ingress

P0229.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Intermittent
P0229.summary: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position signal; its role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors, GM does not use it.

causes.text: Loose contact at the second throttle body connector (spread pins, corrosion)

symptoms: Check engine light and wrench light (Ford)
Brief jerking or loss of power

P022A.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open
P022A.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Wire or connector at the bypass actuator open
Actuator or solenoid of the bypass flap faulty (coil, motor)
Fuse or relay of the actuator supply
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P022B.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit Low
P022B.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground (chafing)
Actuator winding shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0230.title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit
P0230.summary: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side.

causes.text: Fuel pump relay faulty (coil open or shorted)
Control wire from module to relay open or shorted to ground or voltage
Relay supply, ground or fuse missing
With a pump control module: its supply, ground or the module itself
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
No pump prime noise at ignition on; with a short to voltage the pump runs on and drains the battery

P0231.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low
P0231.summary: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system.

causes.text: Power wire from relay or module to pump shorted to ground (chafing at tank or underbody)
Relay contact not closing, fuse or battery feed to the relay missing
Pump motor jammed or shorted (high current)
Connector at the tank flange corroded or burnt
Pump control module faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start

P0232.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit High
P0232.summary: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0232 means there is voltage in the pump power circuit although the pump should be off – a welded relay contact or a power wire shorted to another supply.

causes.text: Relay contact welded or sticking
Pump power wire shorted to another supply
Pump control module output stage shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector causing leakage current

symptoms: Fuel pump keeps running after switch-off
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)

P0233.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent
P0233.summary: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0233 reports brief, recurring dropouts in the pump power circuit that count neither as steadily low nor high.

causes.text: Loose contact at pump connector, tank flange or relay socket
Relay contacts burnt (intermittently high resistance)
Harness chafing at underbody or tank with intermittent contact
Pump motor with commutator or brush dropouts

P0234.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Overboost Condition
P0234.summary: P0234 is a function code, not a sensor fault: the engine module compares target and actual boost, and actual boost stays above target although the control is already lowering it (wastegate opened, variable vanes opened). GM petrol engines set it at 20–35 kPa over target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels with variable vanes at 7–10 kPa, after two trips; Ford EcoBoost at about 28 kPa (4 psi) over 5 s while the wastegate is already commanded fully open.

causes.text: Wastegate stuck closed, actuator or linkage sticking, control hose off or blocked
Variable turbine vanes sooted or stuck closed (diesel)
Boost control valve or electric actuator faulty
Boost or manifold sensor reading too high (drift)
Software or calibration, tuning

symptoms: Limp mode with clear loss of power
Boost overshoots on acceleration, then power drops
Knocking under full load (petrol) or smoke (diesel)

P0235.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit
P0235.summary: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure.

causes.text: Connector at the boost sensor corroded or loose, broken wire
Boost sensor faulty, often oily from crankcase ventilation
Charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes causing an implausible value
5 V reference shorted by another sensor

symptoms: Clear loss of power, only base boost
Boost reading implausible in a scan tool

P0236.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0236.summary: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. P0239.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit
P0239.summary: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes.

causes.text: Connector or wire to sensor B open or corroded
Sensor B faulty or oily
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Uneven boost build-up on twin turbos

P023A.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P023A.summary: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023A means GM's driver diagnosis has found an open circuit (more than 200 kΩ between output and ground with the low-side driver off).

causes.text: Wire or connector at the pump open (front area, corrosion)
Pump faulty (motor or electronics)
Fuse, pump relay or supply missing
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)

P023B.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P023B.summary: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023B means GM's driver diagnosis has found a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less between output and ground with the driver off).

causes.text: Control wire to the pump shorted to ground
Pump shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P023C.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High

P023D.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P023D.summary: P023D compares the manifold pressure sensor (after the throttle) with boost sensor A (before the throttle): with the engine stopped both must read the same ambient pressure. Saab's 2.8 V6 checks this once per trip with the ignition on before starting and sets the code at a difference of more than 12 kPa, with the warning light and limp mode limited to 170 Nm.

P023F.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit/Open
P023F.summary: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0241.summary: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes.

causes.text: Signal or 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
Connector unplugged or corroded
Sensor faulty internally
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor

symptoms: Boost B reads very low in a scan tool

P0242.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit High
P0242.summary: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes.

causes.text: Sensor ground open, or signal wire open on a pulled-up input
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Boost B shows its maximum value

P0243.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A
P0243.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0243 is the general circuit fault of actuator A.

causes.text: Connector at the wastegate valve or actuator loose, corroded or with spread contacts
Valve coil or electric actuator winding open
Supply voltage to the valve missing (ignition, relay, fuse)
Broken control wire between module and valve
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0244.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Range/Performance
P0244.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0244 means the actuator does not respond as commanded although its circuit is electrically sound, and manufacturers implement it differently.

causes.text: Wastegate rod unhooked, retaining clip missing or linkage worn
Wastegate flap coked or sticking
Control hose to the wastegate can leaking, off or swapped; diaphragm torn
Wastegate solenoid mechanically stuck
Position sensor of the electric actuator not learned correctly

symptoms: Lack of power or surging, too high boost
Rattle or whistle at the turbo possible

P0245.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Low
P0245.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0245 means the control circuit of actuator A reads low – typically the ground-switched control wire shorted to ground, so the valve would be permanently energised.

causes.text: Control wire to the wastegate valve chafed through to ground
Solenoid shorted internally
Shared supply shorted (e.g. by the bypass valve)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0246.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A High
P0246.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0246 means the control circuit of actuator A reads high – the control wire is shorted to voltage, so the driver cannot switch the valve to ground.

causes.text: Control wire touching voltage (damaged harness, neighbouring wire)
Solenoid shorted internally (very low resistance, driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0247.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B
P0247.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two.

causes.text: Connector at wastegate valve or actuator B loose or corroded
Coil or motor winding of actuator B open
Broken control or supply wire
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0248.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B Range/Performance
P0248.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two.

causes.text: Retaining clip of the wastegate rod missing or fitted wrongly, rod unhooked
Wastegate flap B coked or sticking
Position sensor learned value outside limits (e.g. not relearned after turbo replacement)
Pneumatic wastegate: control hose or can B leaking

symptoms: Missing turbo boost, lack of power

P0249.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B Low
P0249.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two.

causes.text: Control wire of wastegate B chafed through to ground
Valve or actuator winding B shorted
Connector damage or moisture
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P024A.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance
P024A.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Bypass flap sticking, coked or oily (oil from crankcase ventilation or turbo)
Actuator weak or vacuum line leaking
Engine software (FCA 2.0 turbo)
Position sensor inaccurate or connector corroded

symptoms: Longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature
Possibly less power from boost limitation

P024B.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck
P024B.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Flap seized or coked
Actuator faulty (gear, motor)
Vacuum supply missing (pneumatic type)
Position sensor reading constant

symptoms: Stuck open: higher charge air temperature, loss of power

P024C.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit
P024C.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Connector or wiring to the actuator's sensor part
Built-in position sensor faulty
5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
Engine module

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024D.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P024D.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Flap or linkage misadjusted or sticking
Sensor drifting or track worn
Contact resistance at the connector
End stops not learned after replacement

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024E.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P024E.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground or open
5 V reference missing
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024F.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit High
P024F.summary: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can.

causes.text: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or system voltage
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P0250.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B High
P0250.summary: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two.

causes.text: Control wire of wastegate B shorted to voltage
Winding shorted internally (overcurrent)
Connector corroded or damp
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0251.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0251.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve.

causes.text: Metering actuator coil open
Connector at the actuator corroded or loose, broken wire
Supply voltage to the actuator missing
Distributor pump: internal electronics or quantity valve faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0252.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0252.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve.

causes.text: Metering actuator with shorted turns, too low resistance (driver overheats)
Actuator mechanically sticking or dirty (fuel quality, wear debris)
Wiring with contact resistance
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0253.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0253.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0253 means the actuator A circuit reads low.

causes.text: Control wire to the metering actuator chafed to ground
Connector or wire open (where makers include it under low)
Metering actuator faulty internally
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Limp mode with limited power and speed

P0254.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0254.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0254 means the actuator A circuit reads high or draws too much current – typically the control wire shorted to voltage.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to voltage
Metering valve with shorted turns (overcurrent)
Connector corrosion with leakage current
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Engine stalls or will not start (Saab 3.0 diesel)

P0255.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0255.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0255 reports brief open or short circuits in the actuator A circuit that come and go – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering actuator connector
Harness chafing intermittently (vibration)
Actuator coil with a temperature-dependent fault
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (often goes out again)

P0256.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0256.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. Actuator B is a second metering actuator, for example on pumps with two metering valves such as on Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel.

causes.text: Metering valve B open
Connector or wire to valve B open
Engine module

P0257.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0257.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0257 is the functional fault of actuator B: the metering does not achieve its target.

causes.text: Rail pressure or metering target not reached (leak, relief valve open)
Poor low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air)
Metering actuator or pumping element worn
Software or diagnostic level

symptoms: Hard starting, low rail pressure when cranking

P0258.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0258.summary: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0258 means the actuator B circuit reads low.

causes.text: Supply wire, fuse or relay of the metering valves open or shorted to ground
Connector at the pump corroded or loose
Metering valve shorted to ground internally
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after the second trip)
Raised idle speed in limp mode

P0259.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0259.summary: Fuel metering actuator B is a second electrically controlled metering valve on a diesel injection pump; A has the codes P0251–P0255. P0259 means its circuit reads high or draws too much current – a short to voltage or a shorted turn.

causes.text: Metering valve B shorted internally
Control wire to the valve shorted to voltage, chafing
Connector at the valve corroded or wet
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Limp mode with limited power and speed

P025A.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
P025A.summary: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025A means the control line from the engine module to pump module A is open or faulty.

causes.text: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame
Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
Pump control module faulty (input)
Module ground or supply poor
Engine module output faulty

symptoms: Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025B.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P025B.summary: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025B means pump module A receives a signal, but an invalid command – the duty cycle is outside the valid window or implausible.

causes.text: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control line or connector distorting the duty cycle
Pump control module faulty
Interference or poor ground between engine module and pump module
Engine module software or output

symptoms: Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025C.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low
P025C.summary: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025C means the control circuit to pump module A reads low, typically a short to ground.

causes.text: Control line chafed to ground at the frame
Water or corrosion at the pump module connector
Ground point loose or corroded
Pump control module faulty internally
Pump relay faulty (Ford 6.7)

symptoms: Loss of power from low supply pressure

P025D.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit High
P025D.summary: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025D means the control circuit to pump module A reads high, typically a short to voltage.

causes.text: Control line shorted to battery voltage or another wire
Moisture in the connector (leakage to voltage)
Pump control module faulty
Relay stuck or faulty (Ford 6.7)

symptoms: Pump runs all the time or not at all

P025E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P025E.summary: Boost sensor A measures the pressure between charge air cooler and throttle (Ford TIP, GM TIAP). P025E counts brief excursions outside its valid voltage range that are each too short for the low or high code P0237/P0238 – Ford's limits are below 0.19 V and above 4.88 V.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Wire or 5 V reference breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor faulty internally (erratic signal)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor

symptoms: Occasional loss of power, boost limited

P025F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic
P025F.summary: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on twin-turbo engines or a second stage. P025F counts brief excursions of its signal outside the valid range that are too short for the low or high code – the counterpart of P025E, which Ford sets after 10 such events in one drive cycle.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor B faulty

P0260.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0260.summary: P0260 reports brief dropouts or jumps in the circuit of fuel metering actuator B on a diesel injection pump that do not last long enough for the low or high code (P0258/P0259) – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using P0260 was found; the description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and Saab's diagnosis of the same two-valve pump, which recommends a wiggle test with the valves activated.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering valve B connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness to the pump (vibration, heat)
Metering valve B with internal dropouts
Unstable supply or ground

symptoms: Occasional jerking or brief loss of power

P0261.title: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit Low
P0261.summary: P0261 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector chafed to ground in the harness
Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0262.title: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit High
P0262.summary: P0262 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0263.title: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance
P0263.summary: P0263 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 1 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips.

causes.text: Injector of cylinder 1 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel

P0264.title: Cylinder 2 Injector A Circuit Low
P0264.summary: P0264 means the control wire of the cylinder 2 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 2 injector chafed to ground in the harness
Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0302
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0265.title: Cylinder 2 Injector A Circuit High
P0265.summary: P0265 means the control wire of the cylinder 2 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 2 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0302
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0266.title: Cylinder 2 Contribution/Balance
P0266.summary: P0266 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 2 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips.

causes.text: Injector of cylinder 2 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 2 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel

P0267.title: Cylinder 3 Injector A Circuit Low
P0267.summary: P0267 means the control wire of the cylinder 3 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 3 injector chafed to ground in the harness
Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0303
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0268.title: Cylinder 3 Injector A Circuit High
P0268.summary: P0268 means the control wire of the cylinder 3 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply.

causes.text: Control wire of the cylinder 3 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0303
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0269.title: Cylinder 3 Contribution/Balance
P0269.summary: P0269 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 3 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips.

causes.text: Injector of cylinder 3 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 3 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel

P026A.title: Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold
P026A.summary: P026A means the charge air cooler is not cooling enough. The module compares the temperature drop across the cooler with the maximum possible (inlet minus ambient) or with a model: GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel sets it below 25 % efficiency, later GM diesels below 50 %, both after two trips; Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels when the measured temperature is 18–35 °C (3.0: 35–65 °C) off the model over about 10 s.

causes.text: Charge air cooler clogged on the outside (insects, leaves, dirt) or fins damaged
Coolant-cooled cooler: pump faulty, air in the low-temperature circuit, low coolant
Charge air or ambient temperature sensor inaccurate
Charge air cooler bypass stuck open
Software or calibration

symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat
High intake air temperature in live data

P026B.title: Injection Timing Performance
P026B.summary: P026B is the engine-wide injection timing monitor: CARB requires diesels from 2010 to detect injection that is too early or too late overall, or a timing control at its limit. Unlike P020A ff (per cylinder) it concerns the engine as a whole.

causes.text: Engine module software (false setting)
Injectors coked or worn (changed start of injection)
Rail pressure or fuel supply problems (pump, filter, fuel quality)
Crankshaft or camshaft signal inaccurate

symptoms: Possibly knocking, rough running or more smoke

P026C.title: Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P026C.summary: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets.

causes.text: Injectors coked or clogged (too little flow)
Airflow or boost measurement wrong, NOx sensor lambda inaccurate
Weak low- or high-pressure supply (filter, pump, rail pressure)
Fuel quality or contamination
Software

P026D.title: Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected
P026D.summary: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets.

causes.text: Injector dripping or worn, or wrong injector type fitted
EGR valve not closing or EGR differential pressure sensor wrong
Boost sensor or turbo vanes faulty, intake leak
NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong
Software

symptoms: Black smoke, higher soot load, more frequent filter regeneration

P026E.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance
P026E.summary: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit with an electric pump. P026E means that pump is electrically sound but does not deliver as commanded – judged from feedback by the pump electronics or from the missing temperature drop.

causes.text: Air in the low-temperature circuit or low coolant (pump runs dry)
Pump faulty internally (bearing, impeller, electronics)
Software or calibration
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector

symptoms: Loss of power in heat or under load
Level in the auxiliary coolant tank drops

P026F.title: Coolant Thermostat Performance
P026F.summary: P026F is a general functional code for the coolant thermostat. CARB requires that the coolant reaches the temperature needed for other diagnostics in the approved time and comes within 11 °C of the thermostat's regulating temperature; from model years 2019–2021 petrol engines must also detect it dropping back below that temperature, and electric pumps or valves controlling coolant flow are monitored like a thermostat.

causes.text: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early
Thermostat stuck closed or opening too late
Map-controlled thermostat: heating element or control faulty
Coolant temperature sensor inaccurate
Low coolant or air in the system

P0270.title: Cylinder 4 Injector A Circuit Low
P0270.summary: P0270 means the control wire of the cylinder 4 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground.

Driver stage in the engine module faulty

Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

P0272.title: Cylinder 4 Contribution/Balance

Low compression on cylinder 4 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel

P027A.title: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit/Open
P027A.summary: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles.

causes.text: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame
Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
Pump control module faulty (input)
Module ground or supply poor

symptoms: Fuel shortage when running from the second tank

P027E.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P027E.summary: P027E is the cold-start counterpart of P026C: during cold start the engine gets less fuel than commanded, for example because a catalyst-heating injection does not arrive. The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity.

causes.text: Injectors coked or clogged
Rail pressure builds too slowly at cold start (filter, wax, pump)
Airflow or lambda measurement inaccurate
Software

symptoms: Poor cold start, rough running when cold

P027F.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected
P027F.summary: P027F is the cold-start counterpart of P026D: during cold start the engine gets more fuel than commanded, for example from a leaking injector or an EGR valve or throttle in the wrong position that reduces fresh air. The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity.

causes.text: Injector leaking or worn
EGR valve or intake/exhaust throttle in the wrong position (less fresh air)
Lambda/NOx sensor or airflow sensor reading wrong
Software

symptoms: White or black smoke after a cold start

P028A.title: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit/Open
P028A.summary: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler; a Deere patent describes such a fan that the module switches and reverses to blow out dirt. P028A means the fan's control circuit is open or has a general fault, detected by the driver stage.

causes.text: Wire or connector to the fan open or corroded
Fan relay or fan control module faulty
Fan motor open internally
Fuse blown
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power in heat or traffic

P028B.title: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Performance/Stuck Off
P028B.summary: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028B means the module commands the fan on but sees no effect – no speed or current feedback from a fan control module, or the charge air does not cool – although the circuit is electrically sound (circuit faults are P028A, P028D and P028E).

causes.text: Fan motor seized or worn
Fan blocked (debris, dirt, ice)
Fan relay or fan control module without output
Fan fuse or supply

symptoms: Loss of power in heat or at low speed
High charge air temperature, possibly P026A

P028C means the fan runs although the module has switched it off – speed or current feedback, or the voltage at the output, does not match the off command.

causes.text: Relay contact welded
Driver stage or fan control module shorted
Control wire shorted (to ground on low-side, to voltage on high-side control)

symptoms: Fan runs all the time, even after switch-off

P0297.title: Vehicle Overspeed Condition
P0297.summary: P0297 is a condition code: the engine module detects that road speed – from the vehicle speed sensor or wheel and output shaft speed – exceeded the calibrated maximum. Electronic speed limiters cut fuel or throttle at that limit, and the event is stored.

causes.text: Limiter speed genuinely exceeded (downhill, trailer)
Wrong tyre size or axle ratio programmed, larger wheels fitted
Wheelspin on the driven axle
Speed signal disturbed (loose contact, interference, tone wheel)

symptoms: Usually no warning light, code only stored
Vehicle limits speed at its maximum
With a disturbed signal: jumping speedometer, odd shifting

P0298.title: Engine Oil Over Temperature
P0298.summary: P0298 is a protection code: engine oil temperature – from its own sensor, often combined with the oil level sensor, or modelled – has exceeded the protection limit. Saab's 3.0 diesel limits injection quantity when the oil stays at 135 °C or more for over 10 s, until it cools down; a heavy-duty bus engine warns in two stages and then derates.

causes.text: High load in heat (trailer, mountain pass, stop-and-go)
Cooling or fan problem (clogged radiator, fan, thermostat, low coolant)
Oil cooler clogged or oil thermostat stuck
Oil temperature or level sensor reading too high
Low oil level or wrong oil

P0299.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Underboost Condition
P0299.summary: P0299 means actual boost stays below target for a period although the control already demands more. Thresholds: GM petrol 30–55 kPa below target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels 10–50 kPa, two trips; Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi (about 28 kPa) for 5 s with the wastegate already commanded fully closed; Ford diesels 30–40 kPa for 10–15 s, with a further underboost code P2263.

causes.text: Leak in the charge air path (hose off or torn, cooler leaking, clamps)
Wastegate faulty (rod off, preload lost, vacuum or solenoid, diaphragm)
Turbo vanes sticking or turbo worn (diesel)
Bypass valve leaking (torn diaphragm) or its control
Ice in the charge air cooler, boost sensor or connector, or software

symptoms: Whistling or hissing from the charge air path under load

P029A.title: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
P029A.summary: These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. P02CA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition
P02CA.summary: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes.

causes.text: Wastegate B stuck closed, linkage seized
Boost control valve or actuator B faulty, vacuum line swapped or leaking
Boost sensor reading wrong
Turbo B vanes sooted (diesel)
Software or calibration, tuning

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced power, limp mode

P02E0.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.summary: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back.

causes.text: Connector at the throttle corroded or loose
Broken motor wire
Motor winding of the valve open
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Filter regeneration does not run, soot load rises

P02EC.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P02EC.summary: Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels control the air mass through the EGR valve and the intake throttle. P02EC means the measured air mass stays above target with the control at its limit – too little EGR, or the throttle cannot restrict enough – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0).

causes.text: EGR valve stuck closed or EGR cooler clogged
Intake throttle stuck open (P02E4)
Mass airflow sensor reading too high
Boost too high

causes.text: EGR valve stuck open
Air filter or intake clogged
Intake throttle stuck closed or coked
Mass airflow sensor reading too low (dirty)

symptoms: Smoke, high soot load in the filter

P02EE.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
P02EE.summary: P02EE reports an electrically implausible response of the cylinder 1 injector – not an open or short circuit (those are P0201, P0261, P0262), but a current or voltage pattern outside the expected range. GM's 8-cylinder diesel checks the time the current takes to fall from hold to zero (outside 20–50 µs in 10 of 20 samples, two trips); GM's petrol direct injection evaluates the voltage feedback of the opening and closing; Ford's diesels flag the injector's voltage or charge regulator at its limit (90 s), Ford's petrol direct injection its controlled-valve-operation adaptation at its limit.

causes.text: Injector electrically aged (piezo capacitance, coil resistance)
Contact resistance in the injector 1 connector or wiring
Injector mechanically sticking (valve lift)
Injector driver stage in the engine module

P02F4.title: Cylinder 7 Injector Circuit Range/Performance

P02FB.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
P02FB.summary: Cold start fuel injection is an extra injection system for cold starts – for example on flex-fuel engines running on high ethanol blends, where a Hyundai patent describes a small auxiliary tank, a cold-start injector and a heater. Broken wire in the harness

Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Hard or no start in cold weather (especially with high ethanol)

P02FF.title: Propulsion System Inactive Timer Performance

P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.summary: The engine module detects misfire from crankshaft speed: a cylinder that does not fire gives no acceleration impulse. At a catalyst-damaging rate (CARB: at least 5 % per 200 revolutions) the warning light flashes; at an emissions-relevant rate (at least 1 % per 1,000 revolutions – GM about 2–5 %, Ford 0.9–1.5 %) it comes on after two trips.

Worn or wrong spark plugs on several cylinders, faulty ignition coils
Fuel pressure too low or high, contaminated fuel
Valve timing (stretched chain), valves, compression on several cylinders
False detection: tone wheel or pulley, rough road, vibration, software

symptoms: Check engine light on, flashing at a catalyst-damaging rate
Smell of unburnt fuel, higher consumption

P0313.title: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel
P0313.summary: When the tank is nearly empty the fuel pump can draw air in corners or on gradients, which causes misfires. CARB allows misfire detection to be switched off at 15 % fuel or less; some manufacturers instead report misfires detected in this state under P0313 rather than P030x.

causes.text: Tank nearly empty – the fuel pump draws air (corners, gradients, braking)
Actual misfire cause (ignition, injector, false air) that happened at low fuel
Weak fuel pump, clogged strainer or filter, faulty swirl pot
Fuel level sender reading too low

symptoms: Check engine light on (flashing at a catalyst-damaging rate)
Jerking or power loss with an almost empty tank, especially in corners or uphill

P0314.title: Single Cylinder Misfire (Cylinder Not Specified)
P0314.summary: P0314 means the misfire is attributable to a single cylinder, but the module does not say which one. CARB generally requires cylinder-specific codes and allows a general code only with approval where the cylinder cannot be identified reliably; for diesels identification is required only where possible without extra hardware.

causes.text: Injector of one cylinder clogged or leaking (diesel), or coil/plug (petrol)
Leaking high-pressure line, fuel bridge or injector washer
Air, water or petrol in the diesel, clogged filter, low supply pressure
Compression loss (valve, piston)

symptoms: Loss of power, limp mode with quantity limit (Saab diesel)

P0315.title: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned

causes.text: Relearn not performed after replacing sensor, crankshaft, damper, engine or engine module
Learned values lost through voltage loss (battery disconnected)
Tone wheel damaged or shifted, crankshaft runout, dirt on the sensor
Interference in the crankshaft sensor circuit
Engine module memory faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM; Ford depending on application)
Misfire readiness not set – emissions test fails

P0316.title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)

causes.text: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp
Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start)
Worn or sooted spark plugs that only fire cleanly when warm
Wrong temperature sensor value or engine software

symptoms: Rough running right after a cold start, then normal
Delayed start, fuel smell at start

causes.text: Module configuration does not match the equipment (after engine or ABS module replacement)
ABS/ESP module not responding (supply, CAN line)
Separate rough-road sensor missing or unplugged, where fitted
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Possibly false misfire codes on rough roads

The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff).

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Input of the ignition module or coil shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P031F.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit High
P031F.summary: Ignition D is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff).

causes.text: Control line shorted to a supply wire
Ignition module or coil faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P0320.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit
P0320.summary: P0320 originally covered the engine speed signal from the distributor or ignition module to the engine module (early OBD II); today Ford's engine module evaluates the crankshaft sensor directly and uses this code for it. Ford checks continuously from 200–500 rpm and sets it within 5 s when the number of teeth after the gap is wrong, the tooth time is implausible (below 30 or above 9,000 rpm) or the gap appears in the wrong place; fuel and spark are then cut briefly to resynchronise, and on electronic throttle P2106 limits power.

causes.text: Crankshaft or distributor speed sensor faulty or wrong air gap
Wiring, connector or shielding disturbed (loose contact, interference from ignition or radios)
Tone wheel damaged or dirty (missing tooth, metal chips)
Ignition module faulty on older vehicles
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Reduced power on electronic throttle (Ford P2106)

P0321.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
P0321.summary: P0321 belongs to the same signal as P0320 and P0322: the speed and reference input of the ignition, formerly the distributor's Hall pickup, today practically always the crankshaft position sensor. Range/Performance means a signal is present but implausible – wrong number of teeth between the reference gaps, erratic tooth times, or a speed that does not fit the camshaft signal.

causes.text: Crankshaft position sensor faulty or aged (weak, noisy signal)
Sensor loose or air gap wrong
Tone wheel damaged or clogged with metal chips
Interference, poor ground or damaged wiring
Engine module or software

P0322.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
P0322.summary: P0322 means the speed and reference input of the ignition – today the crankshaft position sensor – delivers no signal although the engine is turning. Ford proves the rotation with the camshaft sensor: if it shows more than one engine revolution without a crank signal (from 500 rpm, detected within 5 s), Ford sets P0322 or, depending on the engine, P0335; with electronic throttle the throttle software adds P2106 and goes into limp mode.

causes.text: Crankshaft position sensor failed (often heat-related)
Open or short in signal, ground or 5 V supply, corroded connector
Sensor loose, air gap too large or tone wheel damaged
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same supply
Engine module

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
Check engine light on, with electronic throttle limp mode (P2106)

P0323.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
P0323.summary: P0323 stands for a speed and reference signal at the ignition input – today the crankshaft position sensor – that drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. None of the manufacturer documents available to us (GM 2014–2019, Ford 2012 and 2020–2023, Saab workshop information) uses P0323; the sporadic crank sensor check runs under P0339 at Ford and under P0336 at GM.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Chafed wiring, break under vibration
Sensor dropping out when hot
Interference from neighbouring wires

symptoms: Brief stumbling or stalling, then normal again

P0324.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Control System Error
P0324.summary: P0324 concerns the knock control as a whole rather than a single sensor circuit. GM and Saab's GM-based engines set it when excessive knock persists on one cylinder – knock despite ignition retard, or mechanical noise taken for knock – for more than 8–10 s; GM's 2018 engines in the first trip, older ones after two.

causes.text: Genuine knock: low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, high intake or coolant temperature, lean mixture
Mechanical noise taken for knock (loose parts, brackets, valve train, bearings)
Knock sensor damaged, wrongly torqued or mounted with sealant
Engine software or calibration

symptoms: Loss of power from ignition retard
Audible pinging or knocking under load

P0325.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit
P0325.summary: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor A is the first sensor (bank 1 or a single sensor).

causes.text: Wiring or connector chafed, broken or corroded (sensor often under the intake manifold)
Knock sensor faulty (cracked piezo, moisture, heat damage)
Sensor loose or wrongly torqued
Engine software or diagnostic calibration
Engine module input stage

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P0326.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0326.summary: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor A is the first sensor (bank 1 or a single sensor).

causes.text: Sensor loose, wrongly torqued or mounted with sealant or on a dirty surface
Engine software or calibration (bulletins for some models)
Genuine knock on a whole bank or mechanical noise
Sensor aged or damaged (low sensitivity)

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P0327.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Low
P0327.summary: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor A is the first sensor (bank 1 or a single sensor).

Moisture or corrosion in connector or sensor
Sensor faulty internally (series issue on some models)

P032F.title: Combustion Engine Producing Insufficient Torque
P032F.summary: P032F is a plausibility code: the engine module compares the torque the combustion engine actually delivers with the expected or requested torque. On hybrids the actual torque can be measured precisely through the generator; if it stays too low for a calibrated time, the code sets.

causes.text: Internal mechanical engine damage (connecting rod bearings, crank drive)
Engine software (false setting)
Poor combustion (misfire, fuel or air shortage, low compression)
Increased internal friction (wrong oil, seizing parts)

symptoms: Check engine light and warning (Ford: wrench, stop safely)
Reduced power, combustion engine shut off
Knocking or metallic noise from the engine

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
P0335.summary: The crankshaft position sensor reads a tone wheel with a reference gap (GM 58X, i.e. 60-2; Ford 36-1, 40-1 or 60-2) and gives the engine module speed and crank angle for injection and ignition.

causes.text: Crankshaft position sensor faulty (heat, age – typical hot-start failure)
Connector or wiring corroded, chafed, oil-soaked or open
5 V reference shorted by another sensor on the same supply
Tone wheel damaged, loose or clogged with chips; air gap wrong after engine work
Engine module

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
Engine stalls while driving or at idle
Hot-start problem: starts again after cooling down
Tachometer drops out, check engine light on

P0336.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0336.summary: P0336 means the crankshaft position sensor delivers pulses, but their pattern is implausible: the reference gap is missing or in the wrong place, the number of teeth between the gaps is wrong (58 on a 60-2 wheel) or the module keeps losing synchronisation. GM sets it after at least 4 resynchronisations in under 5 s, a gap not found within 0.4 s running or 1.5 s cranking, or a wrong tooth count in 8 of 10 revolutions, after two trips.

causes.text: Tone wheel damaged, bent, loose or teeth clogged with chips
Sensor signal weak or noisy (air gap, ageing)
Interference, poor ground or shielding
Wrong tone wheel or flywheel fitted after a repair
Loose contact in the connector

symptoms: Check engine light on, misfire codes may be added

P0337.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0337.summary: By its J2012 name P0337 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a low level without changing state – signal wire shorted to ground, missing supply on a Hall sensor or a sensor stuck low. Few manufacturers use the code.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground or open
Crankshaft position sensor faulty (output stuck low)
Sensor supply missing or shorted
Connector corroded or pin pushed back
Engine module input

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
Engine stalls while driving or at idle
Tachometer drops to zero or flickers

P0338.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0338.summary: By its J2012 name P0338 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a high level – signal wire shorted to supply, or an open signal output that the module's pull-up holds high on a Hall sensor. GM 2014–2019 and Ford do not use the code.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to supply or open (pull-up holds the level high)
Interference pulses from poor ground or shielding
Crankshaft position sensor faulty
Tone wheel damaged or dirty (gap not recognised)

P0339.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0339.summary: P0339 means the crankshaft position signal drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. Ford's 2020–2023 petrol engines use it, depending on the engine, instead of P0320 for tooth errors: wrong tooth count after the gap, tooth time outside 30 to 9,000 rpm, gap at an unexpected position, from 500 rpm, detected within 5 s.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or an in-line connector
Sensor dropping out when hot
Sensor mounting or air gap mechanically wrong (machining error, bracket)
Electrical interference
Tone wheel slightly damaged

symptoms: Check engine light on (not on all Ford engines)

P033A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit
P033A.summary: The knock sensor is a piezoelectric structure-borne sound sensor bolted to the engine block; the module evaluates its signal per cylinder and retards ignition when it detects knock. Sensor D is a fourth sensor on engines with four knock sensors (McLaren 12C V8, Ford's 2020–23 systems).

causes.text: Wiring or connector chafed, broken or corroded (sensor often under the intake manifold)
Knock sensor faulty (cracked piezo, moisture, heat damage)
Sensor loose or wrongly torqued
Engine software or diagnostic calibration
Engine module input stage

symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

Sensor loose or wrongly torqued
