symptoms: Loss of power, sluggish response from ignition retard

P033F.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Loss Of Synchronization
P033F.summary: To know which stroke each cylinder is in, the engine module matches the crank angle with the camshaft phase. P033F means this synchronisation is lost while running or cannot be established.

causes.text: Noisy or disturbed crankshaft signal (sensor, air gap, interference)
Disturbed camshaft signal
Timing chain or belt jumped or heavily stretched
Wiring or connector
Tone wheel damaged or loose

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0340.summary: The camshaft position sensor, almost always a Hall sensor, tells the engine module which stroke cylinder 1 is in – one crank revolution alone is ambiguous – and measures the actual cam phase with variable timing. Sensor A is the intake camshaft, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1.

causes.text: Camshaft position sensor faulty (heat, moisture)
Connector or wiring corroded or open, 5 V reference disturbed
Tone wheel on the camshaft or phaser damaged, loose or at the wrong distance
Timing drive jumped or wrongly assembled
Moisture in the engine oil from short trips (Ford hybrids)

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0341.summary: P0341 means the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM counts the pulses while the crank is in sync: 4 to 6 in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the 4X wheel of the cam phaser; outside that in 8 of 10 checks the code is set after two trips.

causes.text: Sensor with interference pulses or weak signal, air gap
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted
Connector or wiring fault (corrosion, interference)
Crankshaft signal disturbed (wrong reference)

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0342.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0342.summary: P0342 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the Hall sensor faulty. Ford's 2023 diesel sets it when the signal stays at 0 V over 10 or more crank revolutions (3 s), while cranking or running.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V or 12 V supply of the sensor missing
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Connector corroded or wiring chafed

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0343.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0343.summary: P0343 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at supply level without edges. Causes are a signal wire shorted to positive, an open signal wire that the module's pull-up holds at 5 V, a broken sensor ground or a faulty sensor.

causes.text: Signal wire open or shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0344.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Bank 1 or Single Sensor
P0344.summary: P0344 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) is disturbed for moments: edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0344 and switches cam timing off (loss of power and torque), from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s.

causes.text: Moisture or oil inside the sensor, dropping out when hot
Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or loose
Interference or chafed wiring
Crankshaft signal disturbed (wrong reference)

symptoms: Sporadic loss of power (cam timing off)

P0345.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Bank 2
P0345.summary: P0345 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0340: the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 – only on V and boxer engines with one cam sensor per bank – delivers no or too few pulses while the crankshaft turns in sync. GM uses the same criteria as for P0340, e.g.

causes.text: Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector or wiring of bank 2 corroded or open
Tone wheel or phaser of bank 2 damaged
Timing drive of bank 2 jumped

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0346.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P0346.summary: P0346 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0341: the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM applies the same counting criteria as for P0341, e.g.

causes.text: Bank 2 sensor with disturbed signal, air gap
Tone wheel on the bank 2 phaser damaged or wrongly fitted
Connector, wiring or interference
Crankshaft reference signal disturbed

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0347.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low Bank 2
P0347.summary: P0347 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0342: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the sensor faulty. A code-specific manufacturer description exists only from GM: on the Saab 9-4X V6 (GM LAU) the signal must stay low without pulses for more than 1 s, or 10 s cumulatively, and the code follows after two trips.

causes.text: Bank 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing
Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector or wiring damaged

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0348.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High Bank 2
P0348.summary: P0348 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0343: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 stays at supply level without edges. Causes are a signal wire shorted to positive, an open signal wire held high by the module's pull-up, a broken sensor ground or a faulty sensor.

causes.text: Bank 2 signal wire open or shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Camshaft position sensor bank 2 faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

P0349.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P0349.summary: P0349 is the bank 2 counterpart of P0344: the signal of the intake camshaft sensor on the side without cylinder 1 is disturbed for moments – edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0349 and switches cam timing on bank 2 off, from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the bank 2 connector
Sensor dropping out when hot or due to oil moisture
Tone wheel of bank 2 damaged
Interference or chafed wiring

symptoms: Sporadic loss of power (cam timing off)

P034A.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Start Position Incorrect
P034A.summary: Engines with start-stop or hybrid autostart store the crankshaft rest position when the engine stops, so that they can inject and fire correctly at once on restart. This needs a direction-sensing crank sensor, because a cylinder under compression can push the crankshaft backwards after shut-off.

causes.text: Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty or aged
Interference pulses in the sensor circuit during shut-off
Air gap or tone wheel – teeth not detected at low speed
Engine module software

P034B.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Direction Incorrect
P034B.summary: Direction-sensing (bidirectional) crank sensors count the rest position for start-stop even when the crankshaft rocks back after shut-off. In normal running the sensor must never report reverse rotation – if it does, the signal is disturbed.

causes.text: Interference in the sensor circuit (wiring routed next to switching lines)
Direction-sensing crankshaft position sensor faulty
Ground or connector fault
Tone wheel or air gap

symptoms: Low idle or stalling after an autostart
Follow-on effects such as transmission slip or cruise control dropping out (GM LFY)

P034C.title: Ion Sense System Performance
P034C.summary: With ion current sensing the spark plug serves as a sensor after the spark: a measuring voltage across the gap drives a current through the ions in the flame, from which the module detects combustion, misfire and knock – a Delphi patent describes coils with built-in ion sensing, and Saab's Trionic engines detected misfire this way. P034C means this measuring system works implausibly, so misfire and knock detection are no longer reliable.

causes.text: Engine software or calibration
Spark plugs sooted, oily or wrong type or gap
Ignition coil or cassette with ion circuit faulty
Wiring or connector of the ion current return line

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

P0350.title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit/Open
P0350.summary: P0350 is the general ignition coil circuit code without assignment to a coil: the engine module detects a fault in the primary or secondary circuit of a coil but does not report which one. This typically concerns older systems with a shared output stage or ignition module, or a shared feedback line for all coils.

causes.text: Ignition coil, coil pack or ignition module faulty
Shared supply (fuse, relay, ignition feed) or ground open

P0351.title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit/Open
P0351.summary: Modern engines have one coil-on-plug ignition coil per cylinder, with the output stage either in the engine module or in the coil itself. P0351 monitors the primary control circuit of coil A – the line from the engine module to the coil or its built-in output stage – for an open circuit or high resistance.

causes.text: Ignition coil A faulty (output stage in the coil or primary winding open)
Connector at the coil corroded, loose or with a spread pin
Control, supply or ground wire open or chafed
Fuse or relay of the coil supply (then usually several codes)
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running on cylinder 1, often also P0301
Loss of power, jerking under load
Cylinder shut off (injection off), risk to the catalyst if driven on

P0363.title: Misfire Detected - Fueling Disabled
P0363.summary: P0363 is a reaction code: the engine module has detected misfire severe enough to damage the catalyst – through its crankshaft-based misfire monitor – and has therefore shut off injection to the affected cylinder or cylinders. CARB allows exactly this: a vehicle that cuts fuel immediately on catalyst-damaging misfire may turn the check engine light on steadily instead of flashing it, and may switch fuel back on to re-check at most every 30 s.

causes.text: Ignition coil or spark plug of the affected cylinder faulty
Injector sticking or leaking, or fuel pressure too low
Engine module software (misfire detection, cold-start mixture)
Mechanical cause: loss of compression, valve or carbon deposits, vacuum leak

symptoms: Check engine light on steadily instead of flashing
Clearly rough running, one cylinder without power
Jerking or stalling, especially when cold

The code is a late assignment in the P03xx block: older code lists show the slot as reserved, and the other DC/AC converter codes sit in the P2DAx range (P2DA8–P2DAB).

Software of the modules involved

symptoms: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer
Converter function restricted (for example power socket or hybrid drive)

P0370.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A
P0370.summary: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal, to time and meter injection precisely – the high resolution signal. GM's 6.5-litre diesel (1997) had an optical sensor in the injection pump that delivers a high resolution track and one cam reference pulse per cylinder; P0370 is set if more than 8 consecutive cam pulses pass without progress on the high resolution counter, in the first trip.

causes.text: Optical sensor in the injection pump faulty (6.5-litre)
Wiring or connector between pump or sensor and module
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel (LB7: 57X signal)
Injector driver module, engine module or CAN communication

P0371.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A Too Many Pulses
P0371.summary: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal – the high resolution signal – for precise injection timing and metering. P0371 means signal A delivers more pulses than expected within the reference window – for example more high resolution pulses per reference pulse than the nominal ratio, which on GM's 6.5-litre diesel is 64 ± 4 per cam pulse; the usual cause is interference pulses.

causes.text: Sensor faulty or dirty
Loose contact or interference in the signal wire
Sensor disc or tone wheel damaged
Engine module

P0372.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A Too Few Pulses
P0372.summary: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal – the high resolution signal – for precise injection timing and metering. P0372 means signal A delivers fewer pulses than expected within the reference window – marks are missing, for example from a weak signal, a dirty sensor disc or too large an air gap; on GM's 6.5-litre diesel the nominal ratio is 64 ± 4 pulses per cam pulse.

causes.text: Sensor faulty or dirty
Loose contact or interference in the signal wire
Sensor disc or tone wheel damaged
Engine module

P0373.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A Intermittent/Erratic Pulses

P0373 means signal A delivers pulses with erratic spacing or with occasional dropouts – typical of a loose contact or electrical interference.

causes.text: Sensor faulty or dirty
Loose contact or interference in the signal wire
Sensor disc or tone wheel damaged
Engine module

P0374.title: Timing Reference High Resolution Signal A No Pulses
P0374.summary: Some diesel systems give the injection control a finely divided angle signal in addition to the normal reference signal – the high resolution signal. By its J2012 name P0374 means signal A delivers no pulses at all although the engine turns.

causes.text: Sensor (pump or crankshaft) faulty or dirty
Loose contact or interference in the signal wire

P037A.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit Low
P037A.summary: Diesel engines show the driver a wait-to-start lamp while the glow plugs preheat; the engine module switches it with a high-side driver. P037A means the lamp control circuit is too low – in practice a short to ground on the line to the instrument cluster.

causes.text: Lamp control wire chafed through to ground between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED driver in the instrument cluster shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the module or cluster connector
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on or stays dim
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early, possibly poor cold start

P037B.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit High
P037B.summary: P037B is the counterpart of P037A: the control circuit of the wait-to-start lamp is too high, i.e. the line carries voltage although the engine module's driver is off, or the driver sees a short to battery voltage.

causes.text: Lamp control wire chafed against battery or ignition positive
Fault in the instrument cluster feeding voltage back
Water damage in a connector bridging to a neighbouring pin
Driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Glow plug light stays on or flickers
Check engine light on (after two trips)

P037C.title: Cold Start Camshaft Profile System Performance
P037C.summary: To heat the catalyst quickly after a cold start, some engines select a particular camshaft profile; CARB counts altered valve timing among these cold-start measures and requires components of the cold-start strategy to have their own diagnostics. P037C checks whether the requested profile is actually engaged during this phase.

causes.text: Engine module software (GM L3B, reprogramming)
Profile actuator (sliding cam pin) sticking or not switching
Actuator circuit (connector, wiring)
Wrong oil viscosity or low oil level, mechanism stiff when cold

symptoms: Rough running or stalling when cold (for example on remote start)

P037D.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit
P037D.summary: To check the glow plugs, the engine module reads back the voltage or current of the glow plug supply through a sense circuit – CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop, and from model year 2010 the failure of a single plug to be detected. In the J2012 scheme P037D is the general code for this sense circuit, P037E and P037F its low and high counterparts.

causes.text: Sense wire open or high resistance, connector corroded
Glow relay or glow plug control module giving an implausible feedback
Fuse or fusible link of the glow plug supply blown
Engine module internal

symptoms: Check engine light or glow plug light on
Possibly poor cold start if the cause also affects the glow plug supply

P037E.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit Low
P037E.summary: P037E means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too low. GM's 2016/2018 diesels, whose glow plug output stages sit in the engine module, compare the feedback with the battery voltage while glowing: if it is lower by more than a calibrated, current-dependent threshold – excessive voltage drop or a short to ground of the sense line – a sample counts as faulty, and 60 of 120 samples in a 50 ms grid set the code, roughly 3 of 6 s.

causes.text: High contact resistance in the glow plug supply (connector, ground, fusible link)
Measuring circuit or output stage in the engine module
Sense or supply wire shorted to ground
Weak battery or vehicle voltage at the edge of the enable range

symptoms: Possibly hard starting or knocking when cold

P037F.title: Glow Plug Sense Circuit High
P037F.summary: P037F means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too high. GM's 2016/2018 diesels set it when the feedback lies above a threshold derived from the run/crank relay voltage, with a feedback above 5.0 V – for example voltage is reported although the plugs are not energised, or the sense line is shorted to positive.

causes.text: Sense wire chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow relay sticking or output stage shorted (supply stays on)
Measuring circuit in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plugs possibly energised permanently (flat battery, plug damage)

P0380.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A
P0380.summary: P0380 concerns glow plug circuit A – depending on the manufacturer the first group of plugs, glow relay 1 or feedback line A of the glow plug control module. Saab's 3.0 TiD (9-5, 2002) has two feedback lines from the control module; if line A at the engine module stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a plug or circuit fault, checked once per drive cycle with the warning lamp on.

causes.text: Glow plug(s) in circuit A burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay faulty
Wiring or connector fault (feedback line, plug connector, supply)
Missing battery or ignition supply of the control module (fuse)

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

P0381.title: Glow Plug/Heater Indicator Control Circuit/Open
P0381.summary: P0381 monitors the circuit of the wait-to-start lamp for an open circuit or, more generally, for faults that keep the lamp dark when commanded – CARB names a burnt-out bulb as the example, with exemptions for LCD clusters and for engines that only release the starter after preheating. GM's 2015–2018 diesels detect an open circuit in the driver by a high load impedance (about 200 kΩ in 2015), in 0.2 s or 10 of 15 samples, with the check engine light after two trips; on the 2014 Duramax LML P0381 still covered all lamp circuit faults including a short to ground.

causes.text: Control wire open or connector fault between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED in the instrument cluster burnt out
Instrument cluster faulty or communication problem (Ford)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Glow plug light does not come on at key-on
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early in the cold

P0382.title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit B
P0382.summary: P0382 is the counterpart of P0380 for glow plug circuit B – depending on the manufacturer the second group of plugs, glow relay 2 or feedback line B of the glow plug control module. A code-specific manufacturer description exists from Saab: the 3.0 TiD V6 diesel in the 9-5 (2002) reads two feedback lines from its glow plug control module, and if line B stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a fault in the second group of plugs; the check runs once per drive cycle, the warning lamp comes on and there is no further system reaction.

causes.text: Glow plug(s) in circuit B burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay 2 faulty
Feedback line B, plug connector or busbar faulty

symptoms: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing

P0383.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit Low
P0383.summary: Many diesels have a separate glow plug control module that the engine module commands over a control line. P0383 means this line is too low.

causes.text: Control line between engine module and glow plug module shorted to ground or open
Corroded connector at the glow plug module in the engine bay
Glow plug control module faulty (input pulls the line down)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0384.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Control Circuit High
P0384.summary: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive.

causes.text: Control line chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow plug control module faulty internally (feeding back)
Ford: supply of the module outside 6.5–16.5 V or open (battery, alternator, fuse)
Engine module

symptoms: No or irregular preheating, hard starting when cold
Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer

P0385.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit
P0385.summary: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel, which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. P0385 means its signal is missing or does not match.

causes.text: Crankshaft position sensor B faulty
Connector or wiring open or corroded
Tone wheel or second track damaged
Engine module

P0386.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0386.summary: P0386 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor or second tone wheel track is present but implausible. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 sets it after 5 resynchronisations within 10 s, after two trips.

causes.text: Interference pulses (wiring near the ignition, shielding)
Sensor dirty or air gap wrong
Tone wheel damaged
Sensor faulty

P0387.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P0387.summary: By its J2012 name P0387 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor stays at a low level – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a missing or shorted sensor supply, or with an inductive sensor an amplitude that is too small. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0387: the engines with a sensor B that we found (GM Northstar 4.6 and 3.8-litre V6, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline) report its electrical faults under P0385 and implausible signals under P0386.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Sensor supply too low or shorted
Engine module

symptoms: Rough running, no start if sensor A also fails

P0388.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit High
P0388.summary: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0388 means the signal of sensor B stays above its upper limit – with a Hall sensor typically an open signal wire held high by the module's pull-up, or a short to positive.

causes.text: Signal wire of sensor B open or connector corroded or loose
Signal wire shorted to positive or reference voltage
Sensor ground open
Sensor B faulty internally
Engine module input

symptoms: Often no noticeable symptoms while sensor A takes over

P0389.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P0389.summary: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel – GM's 3.4/3.5/3.8-litre V6 use the low resolution track of a dual Hall sensor, the Honda 3.5-litre in the Saturn Vue Redline a second sensor – which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. By its J2012 name P0389 means the signal of sensor B drops out for moments or becomes erratic – missing or extra edges – without staying permanently low or high.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire break or chafing that appears with engine movement
Electrical interference (add-on devices, routing near ignition or relays)
Tone wheel damaged or dirty, air gap too large
Sensor faulty, temperature-dependent

symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly only after several trips

P038A.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit/Open
P038A.summary: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff).

causes.text: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)
Ignition module or coil with integrated driver of this group faulty
Supply or ground of the ignition module faulty
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P038B.title: Ignition I Control Signal Circuit Low
P038B.summary: Ignition I is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff).

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Input of the ignition module or coil shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power, possibly cylinders shut off

P0390.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Bank 2
P0390.summary: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0390 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive from bank 2 while the crankshaft turns.

causes.text: Connector or wiring of the bank 2 exhaust sensor open or corroded (signal, 5 V, ground)
Camshaft position sensor faulty
Oil contamination or leak at the sensor, sensor loose
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted after timing chain work
Engine module, or 5 V reference shorted by another sensor

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0391.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P0391.summary: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0391 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal is present, but the number or position of its pulses does not fit the crankshaft.

causes.text: Tone wheel on the bank 2 exhaust phaser damaged, loose or wrongly fitted
Interference or loose contact producing extra edges
Sensor loose, wrong O-ring or gap, chips on the magnet
Timing chain stretched or jumped
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0392.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Low Bank 2
P0392.summary: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0392 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays low without edges – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a sensor output stuck low or a missing 5 V reference.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally (output stuck low)
5 V reference missing (shorted by another sensor on the same circuit)
Engine module

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0393.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit High Bank 2
P0393.summary: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0393 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays high without edges.

causes.text: Signal wire open or connector off
Sensor ground open
Signal wire shorted to positive
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)

P0394.title: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P0394.summary: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0394 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal now and then appears at a position where it is not expected relative to the crank reference – sporadic extra or missing edges.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or harness
Interference (ignition wiring, add-on devices, ground problems)
Tone wheel or phaser damaged, or sensor loose
Sensor faulty, temperature-dependent

P0395.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0395.summary: Some diesels have a combustion pressure sensor in the glow plug; the engine module uses it to control injection for each cylinder. This code concerns cylinder 1.

causes.text: Connector at the pressure-sensing glow plug loose or corroded
Reference, signal or ground wire open or shorted
Sensor electronics in the glow plug faulty
Engine module (reference voltage or input)

symptoms: Check engine light on (often after two trips)
Usually barely noticeable – combustion control for the cylinder is switched off
Possibly rougher running, more noise or slightly higher consumption

P0396.title: Cylinder 1 Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance

Contact resistance in connector or ground
Actual compression pressure differs (valve, rings)

symptoms: Combustion control for the cylinder off – slightly rough running, more noise

P03E5.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Bank 1
P03E5.summary: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E5 is the general circuit code for this sensor: the module sees an open circuit or a signal outside its valid window on the supply, signal or ground line.

causes.text: Connector or harness to position sensor C open or corroded
Position sensor C faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed (also by another sensor on the same circuit)
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E6.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Range/Performance Bank 1
P03E6.summary: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E6 means the sensor signal is electrically valid but implausible – for example the number or position of its edges per engine cycle does not match the crankshaft sensor, it jumps, or it lies outside the phaser's adjustment range.

causes.text: Sensor dirty (metal debris on the magnet) or air gap wrong
Phaser or sensor target damaged or wrongly fitted (timing)
Loose contact or interference
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E7.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit Low Bank 1
P03E7.summary: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E7 means the sensor signal stays below its lower limit – signal or reference wire shorted to ground, supply open, or the sensor shorted internally; if the 5 V reference is the cause, other sensors on the same circuit often set codes too.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed harness)
5 V supply open or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E8.title: A Camshaft Position Actuator Position Sensor C Circuit High Bank 1
P03E8.summary: On some engines the intake cam phaser (camshaft position actuator A) has its own position sensors, which tell the engine module where the phaser actually is; sensor C is the third of them, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1. P03E8 means the sensor signal stays above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground, a signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, or a faulty sensor.

causes.text: Sensor ground open or connector corroded
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or vehicle voltage
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing held in its base position, loss of power
Possibly rough idle or higher consumption

P03E9.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator Position Sensor A Exceeded Learning Limit
P03E9.summary: Engines with cam profile switching move the intake camshaft between lift profiles with actuators – for example pins that shift a sliding cam – and position sensors report which profile is engaged. The engine module learns reference values of position sensor A, such as its end-position levels or the expected pulse position relative to the crankshaft and camshaft sensors; a Ford patent describes correcting this position for the cam phase.

causes.text: Position sensor A or actuator with integrated sensor worn or faulty (signal drift)
Actuator pin or sliding piece stiff, guide worn, dirty oil
Actuator not relearned or wrongly fitted after replacement
Connector or wiring with contact resistance
Engine module software (learning algorithm)

symptoms: Profile switching disabled: less power at high revs or higher consumption
Possibly further profile actuator or sensor codes

P03EC.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P03EC.summary: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position.

causes.text: Actuator connector loose, corroded or pin pushed back (often after valve cover work)
Actuator solenoid open
Wire broken in the engine harness
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Lift switching and cylinder deactivation blocked, higher consumption
Possibly rough running if a cam piece stays in the wrong position

P03ED.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator C Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P03ED.summary: With a sliding camshaft, the intake camshaft (camshaft A) carries movable cam pieces with several lift profiles; solenoid actuators shoot a pin into a groove in the piece and shift it axially. Actuator C is the third of these actuators – not a profile position.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Shorted turns in the actuator solenoid
Oil or moisture in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Lift switching and cylinder deactivation blocked, higher consumption

P03FA.title: Ignition K Control Signal Circuit/Open
P03FA.summary: Ignition K is one of up to twelve control signal lines (A to L) from the engine module to an ignition coil with integrated output stage or to an ignition module – plausibly the 11th channel, but the code standard leaves the assignment to the manufacturer. Misfire on the cylinder of this channel, rough running
Loss of power, cylinder possibly shut off

P0400.title: EGR A Flow
P0400.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0400 is the general flow fault of EGR system A, used where the module does not classify the error as too little (P0401) or too much (P0402).

causes.text: EGR passages or valve carboned up
EGR valve stiff or faulty
Leak in the intake or EGR pipe
MAP or MAF sensor inaccurate

symptoms: Pinging under load or rough idle, depending on direction

P0401.title: EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated.

causes.text: EGR passages, valve or cooler carboned up
EGR valve faulty or stuck closed
Ford: DPFE sensor or its hoses blocked, cracked or swapped
Diesel: air mass meter drifting or air leak after the turbo
Vacuum control of the valve faulty

P0402.title: EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P0402.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0402 means too much exhaust is recirculated, or exhaust flows although the valve should be closed – CARB explicitly requires a leaking valve to be detected.

causes.text: EGR valve stuck open, dirt under the seat
Ford: DPFE sensor drifting or hose wrong
Diesel: air leak between air mass meter and turbo, MAF drift
Valve control opens unintentionally

symptoms: Diesel: black smoke, loss of power

P0403.title: EGR A Control Circuit/Open
P0403.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0403 concerns the electrical drive of the EGR valve – solenoid, stepper motor, DC motor or vacuum regulator.

causes.text: Connector at the EGR valve corroded or loose
Broken control or supply wire
Coil or motor in the EGR valve burnt out
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EGR switched off: pinging (petrol) or higher NOx

P0404.title: EGR A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0404 is the function check of the valve drive: on valves with a position sensor the module compares commanded and actual position, and a persistent deviation means the valve sticks, is coked or its drive is too weak (GM diesel 2018 above 10 %, GM petrol 2004 above 15 %, both MIL after two trips).

causes.text: Valve coked or stiff
Valve drive (motor, gear) worn
Position sensor in the valve inaccurate
Supply voltage too low or ground fault

symptoms: Rough idle or jerking if the valve hangs open

P0405.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Low
P0405.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor with a 5 V supply; on Ford until about 2011 it was the DPFE differential pressure sensor.

causes.text: Wire or connector to the EGR valve open or shorted to ground
Position sensor in the EGR valve faulty (usually one unit with the valve)
Older Ford: DPFE sensor faulty
Shared 5 V reference shorted

P0406.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit High
P0406.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor; on Ford until about 2011 the DPFE differential pressure sensor.

causes.text: Sensor ground or return wire open
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or positive
Sensor in the EGR valve faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0407.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low

causes.text: Sensor wire shorted to ground
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded (near coolant or exhaust)
Engine module input

symptoms: EGR or EGR cooler protection possibly restricted

P0408.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit High
P0408.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor B is depends on the manufacturer – on systems with a second valve or pressure sensor it is that second sensor.

causes.text: Signal or ground wire open, connector off
Sensor faulty

P0409.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit
P0409.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor (on older Fords the DPFE pressure sensor).

Engine module

P040A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P040A.summary: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it.

causes.text: Connector or wire at the sensor (heat, corrosion)
Sensor faulty
Engine module input

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P040B.summary: EGR temperature sensor A measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. P040C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low

Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it.

Sensor shorted internally
Water in the connector
Actual extreme gas temperature (EGR cooler faulty)

symptoms: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended

P040D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit High

causes.text: Connector off, broken wire or open circuit

Engine module input

Whether it sits before or after the cooler depends on the maker: GM diesels have sensor A after and B before the cooler, Ford diesels sensor B after it.

causes.text: Loose contact in the connector or chafed wire

P040F.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
P040F.summary: The two EGR temperature sensors measure the gas temperature in the EGR path, before and after the cooler – which is A and which is B depends on the maker. P040F compares sensors A and B: after a long stop (GM: at least 8 hours) both must read about ambient temperature.

Contact resistance at one sensor's connector
Connectors swapped after a repair
Unrecognised heat source (auxiliary heater)

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P0410.title: AIR System A
P0410.summary: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0410 is the general function code for secondary air system A.

causes.text: Secondary air pump failed (water ingress, seized)
Combination or shut-off valve carboned up or stuck
Vacuum hose or electric changeover valve leaking or faulty
Pump relay or fuse faulty
Air ducts in the head carboned up or hose off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud

P0411.title: AIR System A Incorrect Flow Detected
P0411.summary: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0411 means the measured air flow does not match the expected value.

causes.text: Pump weak or failed (water, filter debris)
Combination valve partly stuck or check valve faulty
Hoses blocked, leaking or off; ducts in the head carboned up
Pressure sensor port blocked or sensor drifting (pressure-sensor systems)
Pump relay or supply with contact resistance

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud

P0412.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit
P0412.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0412 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve A, detected by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state.

causes.text: Switching valve A faulty (coil open or shorted, water ingress)
Connector corroded or wire open or chafed
Valve supply missing (fuse, main relay)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0413.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Open
P0413.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0413 means the control circuit of valve A is open: with the driver switched off the module does not see the expected supply or pull-up level.

causes.text: Wire to the valve open or connector loose or corroded
Valve coil burnt out
Fuse of the valve supply blown
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0414.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Shorted
P0414.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0414 means the control circuit of valve A is shorted.

causes.text: Valve coil with shorted turns (water ingress)
Wire chafed against ground or supply
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0415.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit
P0415.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0415 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve B, the second valve on two-valve or two-bank systems such as V engines or Subaru's turbo boxer.

causes.text: Switching valve B faulty
Wire or connector to valve B faulty
Valve supply or fuse
Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air inactive on the second bank
Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0416.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit Open
P0416.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0416 means the control circuit of valve B is open – the module does not see the expected level with its driver switched off.

causes.text: Wire or connector to valve B open

Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P0417.title: AIR System Switching Valve B Circuit Shorted
P0417.summary: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0417 means the control circuit of valve B is shorted.

causes.text: Coil of valve B with shorted turns (water ingress)

P0418.title: AIR System Control A Circuit
P0418.summary: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. Control A is the drive circuit of pump A – in practice the coil of the pump relay, which the module switches to ground; the old wording was Relay A.

P0419.title: AIR System Control B Circuit
P0419.summary: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. causes.text: Pump relay B faulty

Engine module

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

P041C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low

P041D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P041D.summary: EGR temperature sensor B measures the gas temperature in the EGR path – for cooler monitoring, component protection and the EGR model. P041E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P041E.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR temperature sensor B is the second temperature sensor in the EGR path; on GM diesels it sits before the cooler, on Ford diesels after it.

P041F.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit Low
P041F.summary: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything.

causes.text: Control wire chafed against ground
Water or corrosion in the valve connector
Valve coil shorted to its housing
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0420.summary: The engine module checks whether the catalyst of bank 1 still converts enough. On petrol engines it estimates the oxygen storage capacity by comparing the sensors before and after the catalyst – a good catalyst smooths the rear signal.

causes.text: Catalyst aged or poisoned (oil consumption, silicone, coolant)
Catalyst overheated by misfire or rich running
Rear oxygen sensor sluggish, dirty or unsuitable
Exhaust leak ahead of or at the rear sensor
Diesel: oxidation catalyst sooted or poisoned, post-injection faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on, otherwise often no change in driving
Emission test failed (higher HC, CO, NOx)
Rattling or loss of power if the catalyst has broken up

P0421.title: Catalyst 1 Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0421.summary: Catalyst 1 is the first catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the close-coupled or warm-up catalyst that lights off first after a cold start; the older wording was Warm Up Catalyst. P0421 means it no longer converts enough.

causes.text: Close-coupled catalyst aged, overheated or coating detached
Misfire or rich running as prior damage
Sensor after the close-coupled catalyst sluggish or faulty
Engine module software (Mitsubishi: update for 2006 Eclipse V6)

symptoms: Check engine light on, otherwise often no change in driving
Emission test failed (higher HC, CO, NOx)
Rattling or loss of power if the catalyst has broken up

P0422.title: Catalyst 2 Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0422.summary: Catalyst 2 is the second catalyst in the flow direction of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) – the main or underfloor catalyst behind the close-coupled one; the older wording was Main Catalyst. P0422 means it no longer converts enough.

causes.text: Main or underfloor catalyst aged or poisoned
Diesel: exhaust fuel injector coked, doses too little
Temperature or oxygen sensor after the catalyst wrong
Misfire or mixture fault as prior damage

symptoms: Diesel: possibly more frequent filter regenerations

P0423.title: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P0423.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of a support catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start (Emitec EMICAT, 12–48 V); it was tried on Californian petrol cars in the 1990s and is used today mainly on diesels, for example Audi's 3.0 TDI from 2014 and 48-volt diesel vans. P0423 means the heated catalyst of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1) no longer converts enough; CARB requires it to be assessed like any other catalyst.

causes.text: Heated catalyst aged or poisoned
Heater not working, catalyst active too late
Sensor used for the assessment faulty
Calibration (Ram: software update per bulletin)

symptoms: Higher emissions after a cold start

P0424.title: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold Bank 1
P0424.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of a support catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start (Emitec EMICAT, 12–48 V); it was tried on Californian petrol cars in the 1990s and is used today mainly on diesels, for example Audi's 3.0 TDI from 2014 and 48-volt diesel vans. P0424 implements CARB's heated-catalyst rule for bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): the catalyst must reach its intended temperature within a time set by the manufacturer after the start, measured by a temperature sensor or modelled from heating power.

Supply too weak (battery, 48 V system, relay, contact resistance)
Catalyst temperature sensor reads wrong
Engine module or calibration

symptoms: Higher emissions after a cold start

Engine module input

symptoms: Usually no noticeable change (substitute value from the model)
Diesel: filter regeneration distorted or blocked, possibly further codes such as P2459 or P0420

P042E.title: EGR A Control Stuck Open
P042E.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P042E means the position-controlled EGR valve A is more open than commanded and cannot be closed.

causes.text: Valve or disc coked, does not close
Actuator motor, gear or return spring faulty
Position sensor in the valve reads wrong
Weak supply to the drive or connector fault

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)
Loss of power, possibly limp mode

P042F.title: EGR A Control Stuck Closed

Actuator motor or gear weak or faulty
Position sensor or connector gives a wrong value

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM after one trip)

P043E.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
P043E.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires.

causes.text: Reference orifice or pump module dirty or blocked by liquid (overfilled tank, splash water)
Leak detection pump faulty (weak or blocking pump, changeover valve stuck)
Engine module software (false detection)
Pump connector or supply (voltage dip)

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

P043F.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
P043F.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Systems with a leak detection pump (Bosch DM-TL at VW, Audi, BMW and Maserati, Denso's canister pump module at Toyota/Lexus) first measure a reference value with the pump working only through a built-in 0.5 mm (0.020 in) orifice; it is the yardstick for the small-leak test that CARB requires.

causes.text: Leak detection pump faulty (weak pump, leaking changeover valve, liquid damage)
Purge valve does not seal
Pump supply or connector (contact resistance, corrosion)
Leaking hose between pump module and canister

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

P0440.title: EVAP System
P0440.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0440 is the general code for a fault in this system without further narrowing down – leak, purge flow or component.

causes.text: Fuel cap leaking, loose or wrong
Purge valve leaking or sticking
Leaking or cracked EVAP hoses, canister or vent valve
Engine module software

symptoms: Readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0441.title: EVAP System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0441 means the actual purge flow does not match the target – too little, or flow although the purge valve is closed.

causes.text: Purge valve stuck open or not sealing
Purge valve stuck closed, purge line blocked, kinked or off
Leak detection pump with tolerance fault (VW)
Canister saturated or damaged, turbo purge check valve faulty

symptoms: Rough idle or hard start after refuelling (valve stuck open)

P0442.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (small leak)
P0442.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0442 reports a small leak; what size that means depends on the maker.

causes.text: Fuel cap seal worn, wrong or not clicked in
Cracked or porous EVAP hoses or leaking connections
Purge or vent valve does not seal
Leak detection pump itself leaking (VW/Audi)
Filler neck corroded, tank or sender seal leaking

symptoms: Readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0443.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit
P0443.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0443 is the electrical check of purge valve A, which the module switches to ground in pulses; it compares the driver's feedback voltage with the commanded state.

causes.text: Purge valve connector corroded, loose or off
Purge valve coil open or shorted
Control wire broken or chafed, or supply missing (fuse, main relay)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run

P0444.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Open
P0444.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0444 belongs to the older scheme of circuit, open and shorted codes for purge valve A; Saab's Trionic T7 and VW use it, while GM reports an open circuit as P0443 and Ford covers everything in P0443.

causes.text: Purge valve connector off or corroded
Valve coil open
Supply wire, fuse, main relay or control wire open
Control wire shorted to ground (Saab definition)

P0445.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Shorted
P0445.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0445 is the short-circuit code of the older scheme for purge valve A, used by Saab's Trionic T7 and VW; GM reports shorts as P0458/P0459, Ford covers them in P0443.

causes.text: Purge valve coil shorted (shorted turns)
Control wire shorted to positive (chafed)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

P0446.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit
P0446.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and closes for the leak test.

causes.text: Vent valve or filter blocked by dirt, dust or water (GM reading)
Vent valve electrically faulty, coil open or shorted (Ford reading)
Connector or wire to the vent valve corroded or open
Canister clogged with charcoal or liquid (overfilling)
Vent hose kinked or blocked by an insect nest

symptoms: Refuelling problems, nozzle clicks off early (blocked vent)
Hissing when opening the fuel cap (vacuum)
EVAP leak test does not run

P0447.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Open
P0447.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0447 belongs to the older scheme for the vent valve circuit (P0446 circuit, P0447 open, P0448 shorted), used by Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X), VW and Nissan; GM reports an open vent circuit as P0449, Ford as P0446.

causes.text: Vent valve connector corroded or off (underbody, splash water)
Vent valve coil open (resistance outside 10–100 Ω)
Wire to the module or supply from the main relay open
Engine module or its connector

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not run, readiness not set

Vent valve coil shorted (below 1 Ω)
Control wire shorted to positive

P0449.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit/Open

P044A.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit
P044A.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor C is depends on the maker: on Ford petrol engines from 2020 it is the DPFE sensor, which measures the pressure drop across an orifice in the EGR pipe (sensor A there is the valve position sensor); GM diesels assign it to the position sensor of a low-pressure EGR valve, but only within fault groups.

causes.text: Connector or wire to sensor C open or corroded
Sensor faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed (with other sensor codes)
Engine module

symptoms: EGR readiness not set, EGR possibly switched off

P044F.title: AIR System Switching Valve A Circuit High
P044F.summary: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air into the exhaust; switching valve A is the electrically driven valve that opens this path. GM checks the valve circuit in three codes – P0412 open, P041F shorted to ground, P044F shorted to positive – while other makers use P0413/P0414 or P0412 for everything.

causes.text: Valve coil shorted internally (low resistance)
Control wire chafed against a supply wire
Water in the connector bridging to the supply
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Secondary air readiness not set, possibly P0411

P0450.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0450.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests.

causes.text: Connector at the tank pressure sensor corroded or loose (underbody, splash water)
Tank pressure sensor faulty
Damaged 5 V, ground or signal wire
Engine module software

symptoms: EVAP readiness not set, emission inspection not passed

P0451.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0451.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The tank pressure sensor measures small pressures around ambient for the leak tests.

Vent line or canister blocked (pressure does not release)
Sensor hose or port leaking, kinked or blocked
Tank overfilled, fuel in the lines

P0455.title: EVAP System Leak Detected - Large Leak
P0455.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0455 means a large leak or that no vacuum builds up.

causes.text: Fuel cap missing, not clicked in or seal faulty (or capless flap)
Hose off or cracked (canister, filler neck, purge line)
Vent valve stuck open or purge valve stuck closed
Canister or filler neck cracked or corroded

symptoms: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0456.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (very small leak)
P0456.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0456 reports a very small leak of 0.020 in (0.5 mm), as CARB requires.

causes.text: Fuel cap seal worn or cap not clicked in
Purge or vent valve not sealing
Porous hoses or O-rings, hairline crack in canister or filler neck
Leak detection pump itself leaking (VW/Audi)

symptoms: Check engine light on (possibly a check fuel cap message)
EVAP readiness or emission inspection not passed

P0457.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (fuel cap loose/off)
P0457.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0457 is a large leak attributed to the fuel cap: Ford detects refuelling and treats a vacuum that is not reached afterwards (about −2 kPa in 30 s) as an open cap.

causes.text: Fuel cap not closed, not clicked in or forgotten
Fuel cap seal faulty or non-original cap
Filler neck sealing surface damaged or capless flap sticking
Vent valve stuck open

symptoms: Check fuel cap lamp or check engine light on

P0458.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P0458.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Purge valve A is switched to ground by the module and fed from the main relay.

causes.text: Purge valve control wire chafed against ground
Purge valve coil shorted internally
Connector scorched or wet
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Rough idle or rich mixture possible (valve permanently open)

P0459.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage or supply
Purge valve coil low-resistance (shorted turns)
Connector or harness damaged
Engine module

P045A.title: EGR B Control Circuit

EGR B is a second EGR valve next to valve A – on diesels with two EGR circuits the low-pressure valve, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor.

Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Low-pressure EGR switched off, possibly higher NOx

P0460.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
P0460.summary: The fuel level sensor is a float on a resistor track in the tank unit. It is no emission part, but other monitors depend on it – the EVAP leak tests, for example, need at least 15 % fuel – so CARB requires it to be monitored and the usual exemption from the warning lamp does not apply.

causes.text: Resistor track worn or float arm sticking
Wire or connector at the tank unit open or shorted (corrosion)
Instrument cluster or gateway sends a wrong value (if the level comes via the bus)
Frequent topping up or overfilling (plausibility test fails without a defect)

symptoms: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or jumping
Range display and low-fuel warning wrong
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0465.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit
P0465.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. Sensor (heater or thermistor) faulty
Engine module

P046A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation Bank 1
P046A.summary: Some engines measure the catalyst temperature with sensors instead of only modelling it. P046A compares catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 of bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1): both are electrically valid, but their readings do not match – for example they differ after a long stop, or the difference does not fit the operating state.

causes.text: One of the two sensors drifting (soot on the tip, ageing)
Sensors fitted or connected the wrong way round
Contact resistance at one sensor's connector
Exhaust leak between the sensors

P046B.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation Bank 2

P046B compares catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 of bank 2 (the side without cylinder 1): both are electrically valid, but their readings do not match – for example they differ after a long stop, or the difference does not fit the operating state.

causes.text: One of the two sensors drifting (soot on the tip, ageing)

P046C.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P046C.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensors A and B are depends on the maker: sensor A is usually the position sensor of EGR valve A; GM's Duramax diesels of 2017/18 use sensor B for the coolant temperature sensor at the inlet of the high-pressure EGR cooler, FCA for the position sensor of the low-pressure valve.

P0470.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0470.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or heat-damaged near the manifold
Broken or chafed signal or 5 V wire
Engine module or software

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P0475.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A

Wire or connector at the exhaust damaged or corroded

Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Flap without function: sound unchanged, rattling
Diesel: longer warm-up, exhaust brake weak or EGR faults
