P047A.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P047A.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or heat-damaged near the manifold
Broken or chafed signal or 5 V wire
Engine module or software

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047B.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P047B.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Sensor drifting or faulty
Sensing tube or hose blocked or coked
Real high back pressure from a clogged particulate filter or catalyst
Leaking sensing tube or exhaust leak ahead of the sensor

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047C.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P047C.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted (often shared with other sensors)
Sensor faulty internally
Connector damaged by heat or corrosion

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047D.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P047D.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Signal wire open or sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Connector loose or corroded

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047E.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P047E.summary: The exhaust pressure sensor measures the pressure ahead of the turbine or in the manifold (Ford: turbine upstream pressure, Cummins: exhaust manifold pressure, older Ford diesels: EBP). The module uses it to calculate EGR flow, to control the variable turbine and engine braking, and to protect against overpressure.

causes.text: Loose contact at connector or wire near the hot manifold
Sensing tube partly blocked (sluggish, jumping values)
Engine module software (Ford 6.7, 2018)
Sensor faulty

symptoms: EGR and turbo control on a substitute value, possibly reduced power
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without function

P047F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Open
P047F.summary: The exhaust pressure control valve is a flap in the exhaust: on older Navistar/Ford diesels a warm-up flap that raises back pressure when cold, on Ram and others an exhaust brake, on VW's 2.0 TDI a flap that drives the low-pressure EGR, and on Audi and Bentley a sound flap. P047F means valve A stays open although it is commanded to close, detected by the flap's position sensor or by missing back pressure.

causes.text: Flap shaft corroded or seized
Soot or carbon on the flap
Actuator or linkage faulty or unhooked
Position sensor reports wrongly

symptoms: EGR flow too low (P0401), higher NOx
Exhaust brake or warm-up flap without effect, possibly louder exhaust

P0480.title: Fan 1 Control Circuit
P0480.summary: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously.

causes.text: Fan relay (coil open) or fan control module faulty
Connector at fan or relay corroded, water ingress or pin pushed out
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Fan motor or fan assembly faulty
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Radiator fan does not run, or runs constantly
Overheating at standstill or in traffic

P0481.title: Fan 2 Control Circuit
P0481.summary: The engine module switches the radiator fan either through a relay, whose coil it pulls to ground, or with a PWM signal to a fan control module. The circuit is an output that CARB requires to be checked continuously.

causes.text: Fan relay 2 (or 2/3) faulty
Corrosion or water in relay or fan connector
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: One fan stage or fan not working, or running constantly

P0482.title: Fan 3 Control Circuit
P0482.summary: The engine module switches cooling fan stages through relays, pulling each relay coil to ground. P0482 concerns the control circuit of the third stage or relay: with the driver off the line should sit at battery voltage through the coil, and the internal pull-up level means an open circuit (Saab ME9: more than 1 s, 10–18 V, engine running).

causes.text: Fan relay 3 faulty (coil open) or not seated properly
Control wire open or high-resistance, corroded or backed-out pins
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, supply wire)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: One fan stage fails – temperature rises in traffic or when towing

P0483.title: Fan Rationality Check
P0483.summary: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0483 checks the fan's function, not its circuit.

causes.text: Viscous clutch worn or leaking, or its solenoid faulty – fan does not reach or leave target speed
Electric fan motor stiff or worn, or fan blocked
Fan speed sensor or wiring giving a wrong value
Radiator or condenser clogged, coolant low (Subaru logic)
Drive belt slipping (belt-driven viscous fan)

symptoms: Check engine light on (after two trips)
Constant fan roar, or temperature rise at standstill
Air conditioning weak at low speed

P0484.title: Fan Circuit Current High
P0484.summary: P0484 monitors the current drawn in the fan's load circuit: if it exceeds a threshold – blocked or stiff motor, shorted turns, a short in the load circuit – the code sets. This is only possible where the fan runs on a current-measuring semiconductor driver or fan module; plain relay circuits do not measure load current.

causes.text: Fan motor stiff (bearing damage) or blocked (foreign object, ice, bent blade)
Shorted turns or worn brushes in the fan motor
Short in the load circuit (pinched or chafed wire)
Fan control module faulty (wrong current measurement)

symptoms: Fan does not run, runs only briefly or at reduced power
Humming or grinding at the fan, possibly blown fan fuse

P0485.title: Fan Power/Ground Circuit
P0485.summary: P0485 monitors the supply or ground path of the fan or its control module – not the control line. It is typical of fans with their own module (PWM or LIN), which can report undervoltage or a missing ground.

causes.text: Fan or fan module ground loose, corroded or broken
Fan fuse blown or fuse holder overheated or corroded
Relay power contact burnt – voltage drop under load
Connector at the fan scorched, water ingress
Fan control module faulty

symptoms: Fan does not run or only intermittently
Overheating at standstill, weak air conditioning
Possibly burnt smell or discoloured connector

P0486.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit
P0486.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Which part EGR sensor B is depends on the maker: FCA uses it for the position sensor of the low-pressure EGR valve, GM's Duramax diesels for the coolant temperature sensor at the EGR cooler inlet.

causes.text: Connector or harness to sensor B corroded or open (heat at the exhaust)
Sensor B faulty
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module or software

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P0487.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A/Open
P0487.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop.

causes.text: Connector at the flap corroded or loose, wire open
Flap actuator motor faulty (winding open)
Pneumatic version: vacuum converter faulty
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off

P0488.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0488.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The EGR throttle is a regulating flap ahead of the intake manifold on diesels: by closing partly it lowers manifold pressure below exhaust back pressure so that enough exhaust is recirculated, and it also helps filter regeneration and shuts off air at engine stop.

causes.text: Flap coked by soot and oil mist (EGR plus crankcase ventilation)
Actuator gear or motor worn or broken
Position sensor in the flap faulty or implausible
Corrosion on flap or housing

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode possible
Shaking when the engine is switched off

P0489.title: EGR A Control Circuit Low
P0489.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0489 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A – solenoid, stepper or DC motor – is shorted to ground.

causes.text: Harness chafed at the exhaust with short to ground
EGR valve winding shorted to its housing
Water or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Rough idle or stalling if the valve stays open

P048A.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P048A.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

causes.text: Flap or flap shaft corroded or coked (stiff)
Flap actuator (motor or gear) faulty or too weak
Linkage between actuator and flap broken or misadjusted
Position sensor reports wrongly

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048B.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
P048B.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

causes.text: Actuator with integrated position sensor faulty
Connector or wire at the underbody corroded, chafed or open
Engine module (sensor supply or input)

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P048C.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P048C.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed

P048D.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P048D.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

Connector corroded

P048F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P048F.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve A is the first such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the actuator connector
Wire broken by vibration or heat

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed
VW/Audi TDI: EGR fault P0401 possible

P0490.title: EGR A Control Circuit High
P0490.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0490 means the drive circuit of EGR valve A is shorted to battery voltage, or its output stage sees overcurrent.

causes.text: Harness shorted to a supply wire (chafing)
EGR valve with shorted turns (low resistance, overcurrent)
Moisture in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P0491.title: AIR System Insufficient Flow Bank 1
P0491.summary: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0491 means too little air reaches bank 1 (the side with cylinder 1).

causes.text: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Combination valve stuck or stiff
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0492.title: AIR System Insufficient Flow Bank 2
P0492.summary: After a cold start the secondary air pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; CARB requires the air flow to be monitored per bank. P0492 means too little air reaches bank 2 (the side without cylinder 1).

causes.text: Secondary air passages in the cylinder head coked
Combination valve stuck or stiff
Vacuum supply or changeover valve leaking, valve closes too early
Secondary air pump weak or water in the pump
Hose between pump and valve leaking or off

symptoms: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Possibly no pump noise after a cold start

P0493.title: Fan Overspeed
P0493.summary: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0493 is documented only on GM petrol engines of 2004–06 with a viscous fan: the measured fan speed exceeds a limit that is hardly physically possible (about 6400 rpm), so it is effectively a plausibility check of the speed signal or a seized clutch at high engine speed.

causes.text: Viscous clutch seized – fan runs rigidly with the belt drive
Interference or faulty signal from the fan speed sensor
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck at fully engaged
Engine module or software

symptoms: Loud fan roar at higher revs

P0494.title: Fan 1 Underspeed
P0494.summary: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0494 means fan 1 turns slower than commanded, judged from the speed reported by a LIN fan module or the clutch's speed sensor.

causes.text: Fan motor or fan module faulty or worn (brushes, bearings, electronics)
Fan slowed or blocked (water, snow, ice, foreign object, distorted shroud)
Viscous clutch slipping or low on fluid, clutch valve faulty
High-resistance supply or ground, connector problems
Faulty speed signal (sensor or LIN feedback)

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Temperature rises at standstill or when towing

P0495.title: Fan 1 Overspeed
P0495.summary: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0495 mainly concerns viscous fans: with the fan commanded off it turns faster than the permitted drag speed, so the clutch does not release.

causes.text: Viscous clutch does not release (gummed, overfilled, seized)
Clutch solenoid or its control stuck open (short to positive, valve sticking)
Wrong speed signal (sensor, wiring, interference)
Electric fan: module runs uncontrolled at full speed or relay sticking

symptoms: Loud fan roar even with a cold engine or at idle

P0496.title: EVAP System High Purge Flow
P0496.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0496 means vapour flows into the intake although the module is not purging – usually a purge valve that leaks or sticks open.

causes.text: Purge valve leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust in the seat)
Vent valve stuck closed or vent filter or line blocked
Vapour line kinked or blocked
Tank pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Hard or long starting right after refuelling
Hissing vacuum when opening the fuel cap

P0497.title: EVAP System Low Purge Flow
P0497.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. P0497 is the counterpart of P0496: the module purges but sees too little or no purge flow, judged indirectly from fuel trim, idle control or tank vacuum – CARB requires missing purge flow to be detected.

causes.text: Purge valve stuck closed, does not open
Purge line off, kinked or blocked (check valve sticking)
Canister or vent filter blocked (e.g. after overfilling)
Vent valve stuck closed

P0498.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
P0498.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module; P0449 (open), P0498 and P0499 form the newer code scheme for its circuit, used mainly by GM and Saab models with GM engines, while Ford uses P0446.

causes.text: Vent valve control wire chafed against ground (underbody, tank area)
Vent valve coil shorted internally
Corrosion or water in the connector
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Vacuum noise when opening the fuel cap

P0499.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
P0499.summary: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system stores fuel vapour from the tank in a charcoal canister; a purge valve lets the engine draw it off, and a vent valve opens the canister to fresh air. The vent valve is normally open and switched to ground by the module (GM scheme P0449/P0498/P0499; Ford uses P0446).

causes.text: Control wire touching battery positive or the valve supply (chafed harness)
Vent valve coil with shorted turns, driver switches off
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver in the engine module

P049A.title: EGR B Flow
P049A.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels).

causes.text: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or sticking
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked or leaking
Flap creating the pressure difference faulty
Sensors (air mass, pressure difference, position sensor B) implausible

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P049B.title: EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
P049B.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels).

causes.text: Software or calibration (false trigger)
Low-pressure EGR valve sooted or stuck closed
Low-pressure EGR cooler or line blocked
Implausible sensors (air mass, pressure difference)

P049C.title: EGR B Flow Excessive Detected
P049C.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels).

causes.text: Low-pressure EGR valve stuck open or not sealing (soot)
Position sensor B implausible (valve seemingly closed)
Leak between exhaust side and intake
Air mass meter reading too low

symptoms: Rough idle or misfire, in extreme cases stalling

P049D.title: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049D.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P049D checks the learned zero point – the fully closed position – of EGR valve A.

causes.text: Soot or deposits at the valve seat, valve does not close fully
Position sensor A faulty or characteristic shifted
New or cleaned valve not taught in, or wrong part
Position sensor circuit fault as the primary cause

symptoms: EGR possibly switched off, rough idle if the valve stays open

P049E.title: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049E.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Circuit B is the second EGR path; on diesels with two circuits it is the low-pressure EGR, which takes exhaust after the particulate filter and feeds it in before the turbo compressor (GM diesels 2016–18, FCA's 2.2 and 3.0 diesels).

causes.text: Low-pressure EGR valve sooted, does not close fully
Position sensor of the low-pressure valve faulty or shifted
Valve replaced without teaching in
Harness or connector of the low-pressure valve

symptoms: EGR switched off, usually no noticeable change

P049F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B
P049F.summary: An exhaust pressure control valve is an electrically driven flap in the exhaust with a position sensor or end-position switch, usually inside the actuator. Valve B is the second such flap; Bentley's V8 assigns A to bank 1 and B to bank 2.

causes.text: Flap actuator faulty (commutator short)
Wire or connector at the actuator damaged
Control wire open
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Flap without function, exhaust sound changed

EGR valve sticking or not opening fully
EGR rate mismeasured (temperature sensor contacts, air mass meter, pressure sensor)
Software or driving profile with long low-load operation

symptoms: Higher NOx, petrol engines may knock

P04DA.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit - Flow Too High
P04DA.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DA is the counterpart of P04D9: the control cannot lower the flow far enough even at the end of its range.

causes.text: EGR valve not closing (soot at the seat, stuck open)
Air mass meter reading too little fresh air (EGR rate calculated too high)
Position or EGR temperature sensor giving a wrong value
Intake or exhaust throttle wrong (pressure difference too large)

symptoms: Smoke or soot (diesel), possibly stalling at idle (petrol)

P04DB.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
P04DB.summary: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons.

causes.text: Ventilation hose off or quick connector not latched (often after intake work)
Hose cracked or porous, or nipple broken
PCV valve stuck closed or oil separator blocked or frozen (simulates a disconnection)
Pressure sensor in the hose giving a wrong signal

symptoms: Hissing, false air, rough idle or lean running
Oil mist or smell in the engine bay

P04DC.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P04DC.summary: Plug-in and some full hybrids keep the fuel tank sealed while driving, separated from the charcoal canister by a valve. When the driver presses the fuel button, the system opens the valve, lets the pressure escape into the canister and only then unlocks the filler door.

causes.text: Switch mechanically jammed or misadjusted (reports one state permanently)
Door or actuator damaged or missing
Signal or connector fault with a valid but wrong level
Fuel level sensor faulty (refuelling misdetected)

symptoms: Fuel door open message although the door is closed, or missing when it is open
Door may not open or only after a delay

P04DD.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P04DD.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DD monitors EGR A while a cold-start emission reduction strategy is active and commands EGR: if the flow does not react as intended, too little exhaust is recirculated in the warm-up phase.

causes.text: EGR valve position sensor faulty (follow-on code)
EGR valve sticking or not opening when cold (soot, icing, condensate)
EGR path or cooler narrowed
Pressure, temperature or air mass sensor misreading

symptoms: Higher NOx after a cold start

P04DE.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P04DE.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04DE is the counterpart of P04DD: during an active cold-start strategy the flow of EGR A is too high – the strategy calls for little or limited EGR, but the valve lets more through.

causes.text: EGR valve not closing fully (soot, condensate, stuck open)
Position sensor reports a wrong position
Air mass or pressure difference misreading

symptoms: Rough idle after a cold start
Smoke or soot after a cold start (diesel), stalling possible

P04DF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance/Stuck Open
P04DF.summary: Purge valve A is the main EVAP purge valve between charcoal canister and intake manifold (on turbo engines the low-load path); its electrical circuit faults are P0443, P0458 and P0459. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows GM's comparable check P0496, Subaru's valve B counterpart P04AE and CARB's purge flow requirement.

causes.text: Purge valve A leaking or stuck open (charcoal dust or dirt on the seat)
Canister broken down, charcoal dust in the valve
Tank pressure sensor giving a wrong signal
Hoses swapped or wrongly routed

symptoms: Hard starting or stumbling idle right after refuelling

P04E0.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P04E0.summary: Purge valve A is the main EVAP purge valve between charcoal canister and intake manifold (on turbo engines the low-load path); its electrical circuit faults are P0443, P0458 and P0459. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows GM's comparable check P0496, Subaru's valve B counterpart P04AE and CARB's purge flow requirement.

causes.text: Purge valve A stuck closed (gummed, charcoal dust, spring or armature)
Purge line kinked or blocked
Canister or vent blocked
Tank pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Nozzle clicks off early when refuelling

P04E1.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit
P04E1.summary: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons.

causes.text: Sensor connector not latched or corroded
Signal, 5 V reference or ground wire open
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E2.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low
P04E2.summary: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons.

causes.text: Signal line open or shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted (often shared with other sensors)
Connector not latched or corroded
Sensor faulty

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E3.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High
P04E3.summary: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor ground open
Sensor faulty
Corroded or wet connector

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E4.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P04E4.summary: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system routes blow-by gas from the crankcase into the intake; CARB requires a disconnection between crankcase and intake to be detected. GM's 2.0-litre LSY has a pressure sensor in the PCV hose: with the hose connected it must see a pressure drop that grows with air flow, plus pressure pulses from the pistons.

causes.text: Loose contact at the sensor connector
Chafed wire with intermittent short
Sensor faulty or measuring port blocked (oil sludge, ice)
Engine module

symptoms: Disconnection check P04DB does not run

P04E5.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P04E5.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. The code standard allows up to four EGR temperature sensors, A to D – for example before and after the cooler, or in the high- and low-pressure circuits; which is which depends on the maker.

causes.text: Wire or connector fault
Sensor faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Usually no change in driving (EGR on a substitute value or off)
Possibly EGR flow or cooler codes (P0401, P2457)

P04E6.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P04E6.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot.

causes.text: Sensor drifting (soot or oil crust, ageing)
Contact resistance in connector or harness (heat, corrosion)
Real temperature deviation: EGR cooler or bypass faulty, valve sticking
Comparison sensor faulty

P04E7.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P04E7.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot.

causes.text: Signal line chafed against ground or the engine
Sensor shorted internally
Water or corrosion in the connector
Module input faulty

P04E8.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P04E8.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot.

causes.text: Connector off or loose, or pin corroded
Sensor open internally (heat damage)
Sensor ground line open
Signal line shorted to positive

P04E9.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P04E9.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Sensor D is the fourth of up to four EGR temperature sensors, conceivable on engines with high- and low-pressure EGR and a sensor before and after each cooler; it is usually an NTC whose low voltage means hot.

causes.text: Loose contact in connector or harness (vibration, heat)
Sensor with an internal hairline crack
Chafed harness
Module or ground connection

symptoms: Check engine light on, may come and go

P04EA.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EA.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Fuel cap or seal leaking or not closed properly (tether trapped)
Filler neck or tank vent line leaking
Sender or pump flange seal leaking
Tank valve or tank pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EB.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04EB.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Crack or leaking connection at the canister or vent lines
Vent valve or leak check module not sealing
Purge valve leaking
Rodent bite or chafing on lines under the car

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EC.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EC.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Fuel cap not closed properly or tether trapped
Cap or filler neck sealing surface poor
Recirculation or vent line loose at the quick connector
Tank pressure sensor or valve faulty

symptoms: Check fuel cap message, often right after refuelling

P04ED.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04ED.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Line at the canister or leak check module off or broken
Vent valve or leak check module not closing
Canister housing cracked
Purge valve stuck open

symptoms: Possibly check fuel cap message or slight fuel smell

P04EE.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected - Fuel Tank Side
P04EE.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Fuel cap seal deformed or dirty, tether trapped
Purge valve not sealing (Ford hybrids) – plus software
Leaking quick connector or vent line at the tank
Hairline crack in tank lines or flange seal

P04EF.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected - Fresh Air Side
P04EF.summary: Hybrids with a sealed fuel tank have a valve separating the tank from the charcoal canister and its vent side. CARB allows such sections to be leak-checked separately with their own codes; a Ford patent checks the tank side via tank pressure with the valve closed and the canister side with a leak check module.

causes.text: Purge valve not sealing
Vent valve or leak check module leaking
Hairline crack or leaking connections at the canister
Module software (misjudgement)

P04F0.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
P04F0.summary: Turbocharged engines also purge the charcoal canister under boost, through a high-load line to the compressor inlet via a venturi; check valves keep boost out of the EVAP system, and CARB requires this path to be monitored. P04F0 checks it: Ford (2020–23, replacing P144C) runs the test once per trip under boost with the vent closed and purge open, and sets the code if tank pressure rises faster than 0.5 or 1 inH2O/s or the vacuum rate is out of range, within 5–10 s.

causes.text: Check valve in the purge line leaking, stuck open, fitted wrongly or missing
High-load purge line to the turbo or venturi off, cracked or blocked
Purge line pressure sensor wrongly connected or faulty (VW group)
Purge valve or venturi faulty

symptoms: Possibly fuel smell, EVAP readiness not set

P04F1.title: EVAP System Purge Line Performance
P04F1.summary: P04F1 is the function check of a purge line that is not the high-load path A – by the wording of another code list the low-pressure path to the intake manifold, counterpart of P04F0. The purge valve opens and the tank pressure or mixture reaction is missing or wrong: the line is blocked or off, or a check valve sticks.

causes.text: Purge line to the intake manifold off, kinked or blocked
Check valve in the low-load path sticking
Purge valve not opening fully
Tank pressure sensor misreading

P04F2.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1
P04F2.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: 48 V or high-voltage supply weak (battery, charge, cold, DC-DC converter)
Fuse, relay or power switch faulty
Contact resistance or corrosion at high-current connector or ground
Module or voltage measurement faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P04F3.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 2
P04F3.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: 48 V or high-voltage supply weak (battery, charge, cold, DC-DC converter)

P04F4.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: Feed shorted to ground (chafed at the exhaust, heat)

P04F5.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 2
P04F5.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

P04F6.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: Wire shorted to the supply

P04F7.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 2
P04F7.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

P04F8.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 1
P04F8.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: Loose contact at the heater or module connector
Wire broken near the exhaust
Corrosion at ground or connector
Internal contact point of the heating disc

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P04F9.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 2
P04F9.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

Internal contact point of the heating disc

P04FA.title: EGR A Control Temperature Too High
P04FA.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P04FA is a protective check of the electrically driven EGR valve A (DC motor on an H-bridge with position sensor): the module detects overtemperature or thermal overload of the actuator, modelled from current, actuating work and position behaviour, and limits or switches off EGR.

causes.text: EGR valve stiff from coking (motor working against resistance)
High thermal load (full load, poor valve cooling, low coolant)
Valve motor or H-bridge driver faulty (overcurrent)
Module software

symptoms: Rough idle or jerking if the valve hangs
Loss of power, possibly limp mode

P04FB.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range/Performance
P04FB.summary: The crankcase ventilation hose connection sensor is a pressure sensor in the PCV line that measures pressure relative to atmosphere; it is the basis for detecting a disconnected hose (P04DB). P04FB is its plausibility check: GM's 2.0-litre LSY checks the zero point with the engine stopped (at least 10 s, coolant 70 °C or more) – a reading outside ±0.63 kPa or a frozen value sets the code in 128 of 160 samples, MIL after two trips.

causes.text: Pressure sensor drifting (zero point error)
Sensor port or line blocked by oil or ice (value frozen)
Contact resistance in supply, ground or signal
Residual crankcase pressure after switch-off (blocked ventilation)

P04FC.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance
P04FC.summary: The crankcase ventilation routes blow-by gas into the intake, and CARB requires it to be monitored. P04FC is a general function check: pressure or flow in the system deviates from the model.

causes.text: Module software (FCA false trigger)
PCV valve or oil separator blocked or sticking
Ventilation or fresh-air hose leaking or loose, oil filler cap leaking
Increased blow-by (piston rings)

symptoms: Possibly oil consumption or oil in the intake

P04FD.title: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance
P04FD.summary: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. Some EGR actuators have their own electronics (smart actuators), with position control inside the actuator and communication with the engine module by bus or PWM.

causes.text: Engine or actuator software (false trigger)
Electronics in the EGR actuator faulty (heat, moisture)
Actuator supply or ground unstable
Valve stiff, causing a control fault in the actuator

P04FE.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1
P04FE.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: Heating disc aged (resistance increased, cracks, electrode damage)
Supply drops under load (cold or weak 48 V battery, contact resistance)
Catalyst or exhaust temperature sensor implausible
Software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P04FF.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 2
P04FF.summary: An electrically heated catalyst has a heating disc ahead of the catalyst so that it works soon after a cold start; Emitec's EMICAT runs on 12, 24 or 48 V and draws up to about 300 A. It is in series production on 48-volt mild-hybrid diesel vans since 2022.

causes.text: Heating disc aged (resistance increased, cracks, electrode damage)

Catalyst or exhaust temperature sensor implausible
