symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on the maker)
Higher emissions after a cold start

P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0500.summary: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0500 is the general code for this signal.

causes.text: ABS/ESP module or wheel speed sensor faulty (signal source)
Output speed sensor or vehicle speed sensor faulty or dirty (metal debris on the magnet)
Wire or connector open or shorted, corrosion
CAN communication fault (message missing)
Wrong tyre or axle data programmed

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0501.summary: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0501 means the signal is present but does not fit the driving state or lies outside the physically possible range.

causes.text: Wheel speed sensor or tone ring damaged or dirty (ABS source)
Wrong tyre size, axle ratio or coding
Sensor with weak signal or damaged tone wheel
Interference from damaged shielding or ground

P0502.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P0502.summary: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. Despite its wording, all makers found check plausibility: the car is clearly moving (load, torque, overrun), yet the signal stays at zero.

causes.text: Speed or output speed sensor faulty
Wire open or shorted to ground, connector corroded
ABS module sends no speed signal
Tone wheel damaged or sensor dirty

P0503.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P0503.summary: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0503 combines three fault patterns: sporadic signal loss, jumping values and a value that is too high.

causes.text: Loose contact, chafed wire, corroded connector
Interference from damaged shielding or the ignition
Sensor with weakened magnet or damaged tone wheel
ABS/ESP fault (signal source)

symptoms: Cruise control drops out, jerky shifting

P0504.title: Brake Switch A/B Correlation
P0504.summary: The brake pedal switch has two contacts – A usually for the brake lights, B for cruise control and brake information – working in opposite sense, so the module expects opposite states on every brake application. P0504 means they disagree.

causes.text: Brake light switch faulty (burnt or corroded contact)
Switch misadjusted or retaining clip or stop pad worn
Wire, connector or brake light fuse faulty
Moisture in fuse or junction boxes

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on
Brake lights stay on or do not come on
Selector lever cannot be moved out of P

P0505.title: Idle Control System
P0505.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: Throttle body or idle valve dirty or gummed
False air (hoses, intake gasket, crankcase ventilation)
Idle valve faulty mechanically or electrically
Learned values not reset after cleaning

symptoms: Idle speed fluctuates, too high or too low
Engine stalls at idle or when coasting

P0506.title: Idle Control System RPM - Lower Than Expected
P0506.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: Deposits at the throttle or bypass channel, or gummed idle valve
Extra load: stiff accessory drive, gearbox or converter
Intake or exhaust restricted (air filter, catalyst)
Idle valve or throttle actuator faulty, wrong learned value
Mechanical engine damage (low compression)

symptoms: Engine stalls when stopping or with A/C on
Check engine light after two trips

P0507.title: Idle Control System RPM - Higher Than Expected
P0507.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: False air (vacuum hose, intake gasket, brake booster)
Crankcase ventilation leaking or wrongly routed
Throttle not closing fully (deposits, ice, stop misadjusted)
Idle valve stuck open
Wrong throttle learned value after cleaning or replacement

P0508.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
P0508.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: Idle valve coil faulty
Control wire shorted to ground or open
Supply missing (main relay, fuse)
Connector contact at valve or module
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on at once

P0509.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
P0509.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to positive
Idle valve with shorted turns
Connector corroded or wet, interference
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on at once

P050A.title: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
P050A.summary: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults.

causes.text: Throttle or idle valve dirty or coked, not enough air when cold
False air or vacuum leak
Fault in the throttle or idle valve circuit
Extra load at cold start (alternator, A/C), stiff engine

symptoms: Idle after a cold start too low, too high or hunting
Occasional stalling shortly after a cold start

P050B.title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
P050B.summary: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults.

causes.text: Engine module software or calibration
Idle control takes back the retard because speed would drop (false air, dirty throttle)
Knock control or knock sensor intervenes
Extra load or alternator at cold start

symptoms: Catalyst warms up more slowly after a cold start

P050C.title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
P050C.summary: P050C is documented only on Bosch ME9 in the Saab 9-3 V6 2.8 turbo: a cold-start plausibility check of the coolant temperature sensor. After a long stop coolant and intake air must read about the same; the code sets if coolant is more than 10 °C below or 15 °C above intake air, once per trip with the warning lamp.

causes.text: Coolant temperature sensor drifting, wrong characteristic
Contact resistance or corrosion at the coolant or intake air sensor connector
Intake air temperature sensor reading wrong
Auxiliary heater or block heater not recognised, very short stop

symptoms: Rough running after a cold start
Radiator fan runs with a cold engine

P050D.title: Cold Start Rough Idle
P050D.summary: GM's direct-injection petrol engines (from about 2016) split the injection into two pulses and retard the ignition after a cold start to heat the catalyst. P050D counts engine cycles with incomplete combustion via the crankshaft misfire detection during this strategy; if the rate reaches the catalyst-damaging misfire threshold, the code sets – once per trip, while the strategy is active (under 45 s running, coolant up to 66 °C).

causes.text: Injector with poor spray pattern or deposits, or injector circuit fault
Spark plug or ignition coil weak
Engine module software or calibration
Poor fuel or low fuel pressure

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on calibration)
Rough idle or jerking in the first seconds after a cold start

P050E.title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
P050E.summary: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults.

causes.text: Idle or air control does not reach the cold-start target (dirty throttle, false air)
Ignition not retarded enough (knock or torque intervention)
Engine module software
Air mass meter reading wrong

P050F.title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
P050F.summary: GM (from about model year 2017/18) monitors the brake booster with a vacuum sensor: with the pedal at rest and high intake vacuum the booster must hold its vacuum; a loss over time is filtered as a drift ratio, and above a threshold P050F sets, MIL after two trips. It runs with the engine on, during start-stop auto-stops and after switch-off.

causes.text: Leaking vacuum hose or check valve
Leaking diaphragm in the brake booster
Vacuum sensor or its seal faulty
Electric or mechanical vacuum pump weak (where fitted)

symptoms: Hard brake pedal, especially after auto-stop
Hissing at the pedal, start-stop stops less often

P0510.title: Closed Throttle Position Switch
P0510.summary: Older engines with a mechanical throttle have a separate idle contact on the throttle or the combined throttle position sensor (Bosch Motronic throttle switch, Nissan and Toyota sensors with idle switch). The module uses it to recognise idle – for idle control, fuel cut-off on overrun and idle ignition timing – and as a substitute if the position sensor fails.

causes.text: Idle switch or throttle sensor misadjusted
Switch contacts worn, dirty or corroded
Wire or connector open or shorted
Throttle not closing (deposits, sticking cable, stop misadjusted)
Value not relearned after replacement

symptoms: No fuel cut-off on overrun (higher consumption)

P0511.title: Idle Air Control Circuit
P0511.summary: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists.

causes.text: Idle valve faulty (coil open or shorted)
Wire open or shorted
Connector corroded, pins pushed back
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Idle too high, too low or fluctuating

P0512.title: Starter Request Circuit
P0512.summary: The engine module reads a start request – from the ignition switch, a start button via the body module, or start-stop – and drives the starter relay with it. P0512 flags a fault in this signal.

causes.text: Ignition or start switch, or start button, faulty or sticking
Harness chafed, short to ground or positive
Selector or clutch switch in the start path
Starter relay sticking

symptoms: Engine does not start, starter does not crank
Starter keeps running after the start (noise)
Check engine light (Subaru after two trips)

P0513.title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
P0513.summary: The engine module receives a secret code from the immobiliser or body module (Chrysler SKIM/SKREEM/RF hub, Saab CIM); if it does not match the stored code, P0513 sets and starting is prevented – Saab cuts fuel and blocks the starter. The most common trigger is a replaced or reflashed engine module that was not taught to the immobiliser (FCA, Saab), less often handshake timing on FCA hybrids or a key not programmed.

causes.text: Engine module replaced or reflashed and not taught to the immobiliser
Key or transponder not programmed or faulty
Immobiliser, body or RF hub module replaced or faulty
Software fault in the handshake

symptoms: Engine does not start or stops after 1–2 s

P0514.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0514.summary: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0514 is the plausibility check of the temperature signal.

causes.text: Engine module software (false trigger)
Battery sensor or NTC drifting
Corrosion at sensor or connector near the battery acid
Sensor fitted wrongly after a battery change

symptoms: Charging voltage too high or too low

P0515.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0515.summary: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0515 is its general circuit fault – open or short – without separating low and high; the charging voltage is then fixed or conservative.

causes.text: Sensor or connector corroded (battery acid)
Wire open or chafed
Sensor not plugged in after a battery change
Module

P0516.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0516.summary: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0516 means the signal voltage stays below its limit for a minimum time; with an NTC in a voltage divider a low voltage means very hot, or more often a signal line shorted to ground or an internal short.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to ground (chafed at the battery tray)
Sensor shorted internally
Moisture or acid in the connector
Module

symptoms: Battery weak, starting problems in the cold

P0517.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0517.summary: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0517 means the signal voltage is above its limit, close to the reference; with an NTC that means very cold, or more often an open circuit – sensor unplugged, wire broken – or a short to positive.

causes.text: Sensor unplugged or forgotten after a battery change
Wire or connector open or corroded
Sensor open internally
Signal line shorted to positive

P0518.title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
P0518.summary: Older engines without electronic throttle have a separate idle air control valve bypassing the closed throttle; CARB requires its output to be checked but not the fault types to be coded separately. P0518 means its circuit fails sporadically – the signal or current briefly leaves its valid range and returns.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the idle valve connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness
Valve coil with shorted turns (temperature-dependent)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Engine stalls when coasting or stopping
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0519.title: Idle Air Control System Performance
P0519.summary: P0519 means the idle control fails functionally with an electrically sound circuit – the actual idle speed deviates strongly despite fully used control. It is documented only on Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X, electronic throttle, around 2005): idle at least 1000 rpm above target with the control already at zero for 2 or 5 s sets the code with the warning lamp at once, and a fail-safe cuts fuel to cylinders to stop the engine racing.

causes.text: False air behind the throttle (intake, gasket, vacuum hose)
Throttle or idle valve stuck open (foreign body, coking)
Throttle actuator motor faulty (follow-on P2101)
Follow-on fault of other codes (sensors, pedal)

symptoms: Idle far above target, engine races
Jerking from cylinder cut-off in limp mode

P051A.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P051A.summary: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051A is the sensor's general circuit fault.

causes.text: Connector or supply, ground or SENT signal wire open or corroded
Sensor electronics faulty
Oil or moisture in the connector
Engine module

P051B.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P051B.summary: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051B is its plausibility check.

causes.text: Sensor zero point drifting
PCV or blow-by valve sticking, ventilation blocked or frozen (real overpressure)
Engine module software (known false trigger)
Increased blow-by from engine wear

symptoms: Possibly oil leaks or oil mist (real overpressure)

P051C.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P051C.summary: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051C means the signal of the analogue ratiometric sensor is too low – Ford sets it below 0.44 V for 5 s.

causes.text: 5 V reference or signal line open or shorted to ground
Connector corroded or oily
Sensor faulty
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor

P051D.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P051D.summary: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051D means the signal is too high – Ford sets it above 4.56 V for 5 s.

causes.text: Sensor ground open
Signal line shorted to positive
Sensor faulty
Engine module

P051E.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P051E.summary: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051E means the signal jumps or briefly drops below or above its limits – physically impossible changes, usually from a loose contact.

causes.text: Loose contact at the sensor connector
Chafed harness
Oil or water in the connector
Sensor faulty internally

P051F.title: PCV Filter Restriction
P051F.summary: The crankcase ventilation has an oil mist separator or filter element that can clog; the crankcase pressure sensor then sees rising pressure at a given flow. P051F reports this restriction.

causes.text: Separator or filter clogged with oil, soot or sludge
Icing in the separator or hose on short winter trips
Oil change intervals exceeded (sludge)
Pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Oil leaks at seals or dipstick
Oil mist in the intake, higher oil consumption

P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0520.summary: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0520 is the general circuit fault, used differently: Ford petrol and diesel engines set it for the digital SENT sensor when it reports an internal fault, does not initialise or sends values out of range (lost communication is U0600), after 5 s.

causes.text: Sensor or switch faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily (oil creeping through a leaking sensor)
Signal line open or shorted to ground
5 V reference or supply faulty (usually with other sensor codes)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Oil pressure gauge or warning wrong
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly disabled

P0521.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Range/Performance
P0521.summary: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0521 is the plausibility check.

causes.text: Sensor drifting or stuck (offset)
Oil pump control valve or two-stage pump stuck in the wrong stage
Wrong viscosity, low oil level or foaming oil
Worn oil pump or bearings

symptoms: Oil pressure reading implausible or fluctuating
Cylinder deactivation or cam phasing possibly disabled

P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Low
P0522.summary: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0522 means the signal voltage is below its limit: GM 2018 below 5 % of the 5 V reference, Ford petrol below 0.25 V, Ford diesel below 0.018 V, about 5 s.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to ground or open
5 V reference failed or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Oil pressure gauge at zero or warning despite normal pressure
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly disabled

P0523.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A High
P0523.summary: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0523 means the signal voltage is above its limit: GM 2018 above 95 % of the 5 V reference, GM 2006 above 4.89 V, Ford petrol above 4.75 V, Ford diesel above 4.992 V, about 5 s.

causes.text: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Oil or moisture in the connector

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly restricted

P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
P0524.summary: P0524 is not a sensor fault but a condition: the measured oil pressure is below a minimum depending on speed, load and temperature (Ford diesel 30–90 kPa) for about 5 s, with the sensor itself plausible. Its purpose is engine protection; Ford petrol engines with mid-lock cam phasers drive them into the locked position.

causes.text: Oil level too low, oil loss or consumption
Too thin oil, fuel dilution or clogged pick-up screen
Oil pump or pressure control valve faulty or stuck
Worn crankshaft or camshaft bearings
False setting by software in the cold (Ram EcoDiesel)

symptoms: Oil pressure warning and/or check engine light

P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0525.summary: P0525 concerns vehicles with a separate cruise control servo – a vacuum or electric actuator on the throttle cable driven by the engine module: the control circuit is electrically sound, but the response does not match the command. With electronic throttle the engine module controls the throttle itself, so the code hardly applies there.

causes.text: Servo worn or sticking, cable misadjusted
Vacuum leak at hose or diaphragm (vacuum servo)
Wiring, connector or fuse to the servo
Brake or clutch switch interrupting the servo release

symptoms: Cruise control inoperative or switches off

P0526.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
P0526.summary: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0526 means no usable signal although the clutch is driven: GM Duramax below 500 rpm with fan duty at least 36 % for 2 s; the 6.6 L LML distinguishes a level stuck low or high; GM petrol V8s set it when no pulses arrive with the engine running.

causes.text: Hall sensor at the fan clutch faulty
Wiring or connector (chafing at the shroud, corrosion)
Clutch not turning despite command
Engine module or supply

symptoms: Fan permanently on or off, loud fan noise
Weak air conditioning at low speed, overheating under load

P0527.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0527.summary: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0527 means a signal is present but implausible – spikes, jumps or a speed that does not fit the clutch command and engine speed.

causes.text: Sensor or trigger element damaged, wrong air gap
Interference or ground fault on the sensor line
Viscous clutch slipping or sticking (real speed off)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0528.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0528.summary: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0528 means no pulses arrive from the sensor although the fan should be turning.

causes.text: Sensor faulty
Wire open or connector off
Fan or clutch really not turning

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Fan permanently on or not at all

P0529.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0529.summary: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0529 means the speed signal drops out or jumps at times.

causes.text: Loose contact at connector or wiring at the fan (vibration, chafing)
Sensor in the fan clutch intermittently faulty
Clutch itself faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Fan running permanently or not at all

P052A.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P052A.summary: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index.

causes.text: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052B.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P052B.summary: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index.

causes.text: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (stuck in base position)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052C.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P052C.summary: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index.

causes.text: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052D.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P052D.summary: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index.

causes.text: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052E.title: PCV Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.summary: P052E is a function fault of the crankcase ventilation pressure regulating valve. Audi's 3.0 TFSI has a diaphragm valve whose torn diaphragm or elbow causes false air and whistling; Mercedes' M270/M274 have a switched part-load ventilation valve that blocks with oil carbon and lets oil into the intake – blue smoke, rough running, lack of power; Mercedes extended the emission warranty on the intake module.

causes.text: Diaphragm of the regulating valve torn or fatigued
Part-load ventilation valve blocked (oil carbon, sludge)
Elbow or hose at the valve cracked, clamp leaking
Engine module software

symptoms: Whistling or hissing in the engine bay
Rough idle, blue smoke or oil consumption, lack of power

P052F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
P052F.summary: Diesel glow plugs are switched by a separate glow plug control module fed from the battery, with its own ground, a command from the engine module and a diagnostic line back. P052F means its supply voltage is out of range.

causes.text: Main feed to the module open or high-resistance (fuse, connector, corroded ring terminal)
Poor ground of the glow plug module
System voltage too low or too high (weak battery, regulator fault)
Glow plug module faulty internally

symptoms: Hard cold start, long cranking, white smoke
Several glow plug codes at once

P0530.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0530.summary: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008).

causes.text: Connector or contacts corroded or loose
Pressure sensor faulty
Wire open or chafed
5 V reference shorted by another sensor

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0531.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0531.summary: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008).

causes.text: Pressure sensor drifting or stuck
Refrigerant charge wrong (too little or too much)
Compressor or control valve delivering poorly
Condenser dirty or fan weak

P0532.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P0532.summary: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008).

causes.text: Signal line open or shorted to ground
Pressure sensor faulty
Connector corroded or loose
5 V reference shorted or failed

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0533.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0533.summary: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008).

causes.text: Signal line shorted to positive (e.g. 5 V reference)
Sensor ground open
Pressure sensor faulty internally
Extreme overpressure (overcharge, blocked condenser, fan off)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0534.title: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss
P0534.summary: P0534 reports too little refrigerant (a leak), not a sensor circuit: the module compares pressure or temperature in the circuit with a model, and the compressor is locked out for protection. FCA's 2020 Ram EcoDiesel sets it with the warning lamp; a software update fixed false setting.

causes.text: Refrigerant leak (condenser, joints, compressor shaft seal, service ports)
Pressure or temperature sensor offset (misjudgement)
Software or calibration
Traction battery chiller faulty (electric and hybrid only)

symptoms: Air conditioning weak or not cooling
Check engine light or high-voltage service message (electric)

P0535.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0535.summary: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor.

causes.text: Sensor faulty
Connector corroded by condensate
Wire open or shorted
Engine module

symptoms: Air conditioning not or weakly cooling

P0536.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0536.summary: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor.

causes.text: Sensor drifting
Sensor not seated correctly in the evaporator
Refrigerant shortage or compressor fault
Contact resistance in the connector

P0537.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0537.summary: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Condensate in the connector (leakage to ground)
Engine module

symptoms: Compressor permanently on or locked out

P0538.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0538.summary: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor.

causes.text: Connector off or corroded, wire open
Sensor open internally
Ground line open
Short to positive

symptoms: Air conditioning not cooling (compressor locked out)

P0539.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0539.summary: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Broken wire from movement or chafing
Sensor with internal intermittent contact

P053A.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit/Open
P053A.summary: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground.

causes.text: Heating element burnt out
Connector or wire open, corrosion
Fuse of the ignition supply blown
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053B.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.summary: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground.

causes.text: Control line chafed against ground
Heating element shorted to its housing
Engine module driver shorted

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P053C.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
P053C.summary: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground.

causes.text: Control line shorted to 12 V

Engine module

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1

P054A.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1

P0550.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
P0550.summary: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB.

causes.text: Connector or wire open or corroded (splash zone at the pump)
Sensor or switch faulty, often also leaking
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Idle drops when steering at standstill, engine may stall

P0555.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0555.summary: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump.

causes.text: Connector or wire to the sensor open or corroded
Sensor faulty
5 V reference disturbed (short at another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or brake booster warning

P0564.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit

P05CC.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1

These 'performance' codes are GM's current form (since about 2015/16; older GM engines and Ford use the direction codes P052A ff and P054A ff): fault when commanded and actual position differ by more than 4° or 6° once the target is stable.

Phaser worn or lock pin not releasing; on electric phasers a damaged phaser motor
Timing chain stretched or skipped
Engine module software

symptoms: Check engine light on (GM mostly after two trips)
Often no noticeable symptoms, possibly rough cold idle
Rattle from the timing drive (GM electric phaser)

P05DB.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P05DB.summary: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored.

P05E0.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P05E0.summary: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems measure brake pedal travel with a two-channel sensor; the channels often run in opposite directions (Toyota RAV4 hybrid 2024–25: one rises from about 1 V, the other falls from about 4 V). P05E0 means both channels are electrically fine but no longer match each other.

causes.text: Pedal travel sensor faulty internally (channels drift apart)
Contact resistance or corrosion in the connector or harness of one channel
Sensor not calibrated after replacement or pedal work

Brake or hybrid control module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light or service warning
Brake, ABS or stability warning lamp
Hard brake pedal, reduced brake assist

P05E1.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E1.summary: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector (front end, splash water)
Chafed or broken wire (5 V, signal, ground)
Sensor faulty internally (signal jumps)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor

symptoms: A/C intermittently not cooling (compressor switched off)
Radiator fan runs unnecessarily or irregularly
Idle speed fluctuates when A/C engages
Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E2.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector

Sensor B faulty

symptoms: A/C or heat pump intermittently switched off
Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E3.title: Park Brake Sensor/Switch Circuit
P05E3.summary: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored.

causes.text: Broken wire or corroded connector at the park brake switch or sensor
Switch or pressure sensor faulty
Faulty diode in the switch circuit (Volvo)
Vehicle or brake module delivers a wrong status

symptoms: Check engine light or OBD warning (heavy-duty)
Park brake warning in the cluster
Stop-start or idle shutdown not working

P05E8.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05E8.summary: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass.

causes.text: Connector at the valve loose, corroded or spread
Valve solenoid coil open
Broken wire in the harness
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position

P05EB.title: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.summary: After a cold start a diesel heats its exhaust actively – retarded and post injection, intake or exhaust throttling, higher idle, EGR cooler bypass – so the SCR catalyst quickly reaches the temperature at which urea dosing can start (around 180–200 °C). P05EB sets when the measured temperature at the SCR inlet stays below the expected or modelled value within a set time after the start: the heating strategy is not working.

causes.text: Engine module software or calibration (false trigger)
Exhaust temperature sensor before the SCR reads low or slow
Heating measure not effective: throttle, EGR cooler bypass or turbo vanes sticking
Post or retarded injection not effective (injectors)
Exhaust leak before the sensor or extremely cold conditions

symptoms: Higher NOx emissions after cold start (not noticeable)

P05EC.title: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
P05EC.summary: To heat the exhaust after a cold start, a diesel shifts its start of injection, usually later, plus post injections. CARB requires faults of such elements during the cold start strategy to be reported under codes separate from normal operation – hence P05EC.

causes.text: Engine module software or internal fault (request and execution differ)
Cold start mode blocked by other faults (coolant or fuel temperature, rail pressure)
Injector driver or injector circuit
Weak battery during cold start

symptoms: Possibly more white smoke or rougher running after cold start

P05ED.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.summary: Some diesels use a separate control module or power stage for the DEF heaters in tank, pump and lines; without heating, frozen fluid cannot thaw in winter and dosing stays blocked. P05ED reports that this module's supply voltage is outside its allowed window – a blown main fuse, an open feed or ground, or system voltage too low or too high.

causes.text: Main fuse or feed wire to the heater module faulty, connector corroded (splash zone)
Poor module ground
Weak battery or charging fault (system voltage too low or too high)
Heater control module faulty internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
In cold weather: DEF frozen, dosing blocked, further heater codes

P05EE.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P05EE.summary: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function.

causes.text: Connector at the pump or tank module corroded or loose
Open wire in the harness to the tank
Fuse or relay of the pump supply faulty
Pump or tank module open internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

Pump shorted internally or stiff (high current)
Weak battery or charging system

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart

P05F2.summary: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. P05F3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P05F3.summary: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function.

causes.text: Relay missing, coil open or not seated properly
Corroded connector or relay socket
Harness damaged
Output driver in the engine module faulty

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for heaters, pump or NOx sensor supply

P05F4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P05F4.summary: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. CARB requires such outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function.

Corroded connector or relay socket
