P06AF.title: Torque Management System Forced Engine Shutdown
P06AF.summary: GM uses P06AF for a cross-check between two control modules: the monitored module (engine or transmission module, each with main and secondary processor) sends a fixed answer sequence over CAN only if both its processors work together correctly; the monitoring module (engine, transmission or hybrid control module) sets P06AF if the pattern is wrong or missing. In all GM tables from 2016 to 2025 it is type A – lamp in the first trip – and the torque management may shut the engine down for safety.

causes.text: Software fault in engine, transmission or hybrid module
Processor fault in one of the modules
CAN communication disturbance between the modules
Supply interruption or poor ground of a module

symptoms: Engine shuts off or does not start

Internal supply circuit of the motor control module faulty
Connector or wiring fault

P06B6.title: Internal Control Module Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Processor 1 Performance
P06B6.summary: To detect an open knock sensor circuit, GM's engine modules feed a 20 kHz test signal into the sensor circuit and check whether it returns. P06B6 checks the internal test circuit or knock signal processor for sensor 1: it sets when the returned 20 kHz component lies between the open-circuit thresholds, so the module cannot decide 'connected' or 'open'.

causes.text: Engine module software (GM bulletin)
Internal knock processor or test circuit faulty
Knock sensor wiring with high resistance or intermittent contact
Knock sensor faulty

symptoms: Retarded ignition, less power and higher consumption

P06B8.title: Internal Control Module Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) Error

Ford sets P06B8 when the checksum of this permanent-code memory is wrong; a common companion is P068A (main relay dropped out too early, memory write incomplete).

Engine module software
Weak battery or poor ground
Memory defect in the module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the vehicle)

P06B9.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance

causes.text: Glow plug cylinder 1 aged or high-resistance
Contact resistance at plug connector or terminal nut
Wrong plug type or a plug with a manufacturing fault
Engine or glow module software (Ram 6.7 L from 2025)

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Rough running and white smoke after a cold start

causes.text: Wrong glow plug type fitted in cylinder 1 (steel/ceramic, voltage rating)

Glow module software or check during cranking (false report)
Contact resistance at the plug connector

symptoms: Check engine and glow plug lamp
Harder cold start or white smoke
Possibly plug burnt out (low-voltage plug on 11 V control)

P06D1.title: Internal Control Module Ignition Coil Control Performance
P06D1.summary: On ignition systems where the coils are driven through a separate driver chip inside the engine module, P06D1 reports that this internal coil control does not work correctly. Ford checks the communication with the coil driver chip continuously and sets the code within 1 s at 200–3200 rpm, positive torque and 11–16 V.

causes.text: Coil driver chip or internal communication in the engine module faulty
Engine module software
Supply or ground problem at the module
Shorted coil overloading the driver

P06D2.title: Sensor Reference Voltage E Circuit/Open
P06D2.summary: The engine module feeds sensors from several regulated 5 V reference circuits; a short at one sensor pulls the whole circuit down and all its sensors report at once – unplug them one by one to find the culprit. P06D2 is the general code for circuit E.

causes.text: Short in the wire or sensor of a connected sensor
Chafing or water in harness or connector
A connected sensor faulty internally
Module internal voltage regulator or components

Low oil pressure at high engine speed, possibly oil pressure warning

P06DC.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit High
P06DC.summary: A switchable or variable oil pump saves fuel by lowering its output at part load; a solenoid valve sets the stage. GM and Ford design it so the pump runs at full output, i.e.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to positive
Valve coil shorted (looks like a short to positive at the driver)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Usually no noticeable symptom, oil pressure permanently high

P06DD.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P06DD.summary: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; unpowered it delivers high pressure. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start.

causes.text: Control valve stuck or broken, screen clogged
Oil level too low, wrong viscosity or sludge
Mechanical pump or drive damage (tensioner, drive gear, pump face)
Valve not seated correctly (retaining clip)
Oil pressure sensor inaccurate

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Oil pressure stays high – or, with pump damage, low or fluctuating

P06DE.title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck On
P06DE.summary: A switchable oil pump changes its output via a solenoid valve; powered it runs at the low stage. To test it, the module switches the pump between stages (GM up to 15 times, with oil at 50–110 °C and 1350–2500 rpm, expecting more than 100 kPa difference) and watches the oil pressure sensor; Ford checks each switch-over of a two-stage pump within 1 s, or a variable pump over 10 s, from 30 s after start.

causes.text: Control valve stuck in the powered position
Low oil level, diluted or sludged oil, aeration
Pump wear or internal leakage
Engine module software (FCA 3.6 L)
Oil pressure sensor

symptoms: Oil pressure warning at higher engine speed possible
Possibly reduced power or raised idle
Valvetrain or chain tensioner noise from lack of oil

P06DF.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Memory Checksum Error
P06DF.summary: A diesel glow plug control module has its own microcontroller. On power-up it forms a checksum over its memory and compares it with the stored value; P06DF means they differ, so the module's program or data cannot be trusted.

causes.text: Glow plug control module faulty internally (memory, controller)
Failed or interrupted programming of the module
Voltage dip or spike at power-up (weak battery, poor ground)
Moisture or corrosion in module or connector

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
White smoke and knocking after cold start

P06E0.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P06E0.summary: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E0 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent.

causes.text: Cylinder 11 glow plug shorted internally
Plug wire chafed through to ground
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture
Driver stage in the glow module defective

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start

P06E1.title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P06E1.summary: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E1 means the circuit to the cylinder 11 glow plug is shorted to positive: voltage is present although the driver is off, or no current flows when it is on.

causes.text: Plug wire shorted to supply in the harness
Driver stage in the glow module shorted (permanently on)
Moisture or corrosion bridging to a supply pin
Glow module software

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start
Plug may glow permanently and fail early

P06E2.title: Cylinder 12 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P06E2.summary: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E2 means the circuit to the cylinder 12 glow plug is shorted to ground or draws overcurrent.

causes.text: Cylinder 12 glow plug shorted internally
Plug wire chafed through to ground
Burnt connector or terminal nut, tracking through oil or moisture
Driver stage in the glow module defective

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start

P06E3.title: Cylinder 12 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P06E3.summary: Diesel glow systems switch each plug through its own power semiconductor and switch off a faulty channel; CARB requires single-plug detection from model year 2010. P06E3 means the circuit to the cylinder 12 glow plug is shorted to positive: voltage is present although the driver is off, or no current flows when it is on.

causes.text: Plug wire shorted to supply in the harness
Driver stage in the glow module shorted (permanently on)
Moisture or corrosion bridging to a supply pin
Glow module software

symptoms: Check engine light (GM: also glow plug lamp)
Rough cold idle, white smoke after cold start
Plug may glow permanently and fail early

P06E4.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Performance
P06E4.summary: Control modules are woken by a dedicated wake-up line or a network wake-up – at ignition on, when a charging cable is plugged in, or on a timer for engine-off diagnostics and battery management. P06E4 means this wake-up signal is implausible: the module wakes too late or not at all, stays awake, or the line state does not match the network status.

causes.text: Module software (false setting, permanent code does not clear)
Wake-up line or connector open or shorted
Weak 12 V battery, voltage dips at wake-up
Engine or hybrid control module faulty

P06E5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Performance
P06E5.summary: P06E5 means glow plug control module 1 does not respond correctly to the glow command: its outputs do not switch or its internal drivers report faults or overheating. Ford's 2023 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke list P06E5 among the glow module checks, run continuously, with a fault after about 1 s when internal drivers for glow plugs, DEF heaters or relays fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s – Ford does not assign each threshold to a single code.

causes.text: Glow plug control module faulty internally (drivers do not switch)
Poor supply or ground of the module (main feed, fuse, ground)
Module overheating (mounting location, short at a plug)
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
White smoke and rough running after cold start
Often stored together with plug codes or P064C/P263C

P06E6.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit/Open
P06E6.summary: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit.

causes.text: Open circuit or connector problem in the supply circuit
Short in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Vehicle under- or overvoltage

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E7.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit Low
P06E7.summary: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit.

causes.text: Short to ground in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Connector problem in the supply circuit
Vehicle undervoltage

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E8.title: Sensor Power Supply C Circuit High
P06E8.summary: 'Sensor power supply' is a separate J2012 family next to the 5 V sensor reference (P0697 ff): an additional supply from the module for sensors or drivers – in GM hybrids a 15 V supply for resolvers and inverter gate drivers, there as supplies A and B. Supply C is a third such circuit.

causes.text: Short to positive in the supply wire or a supplied sensor
Supply regulator inside the module faulty
Vehicle overvoltage (alternator)

symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time
Limp mode or reduced power possible
Possibly starting problems or rough running

P06E9.title: Engine Starter Performance
P06E9.summary: On cars with stop-start or keyless start the engine module operates the starter relay itself and watches the start: if cranking is commanded but the engine does not turn, turns too slowly or the start is aborted, it sets P06E9. CARB counts an engine start from 150 rpm below warm idle.

causes.text: Starter worn or solenoid contacts intermittently open
Weak battery, voltage drop on main cables or ground
Starter relay or its control
Engine module software

symptoms: Check engine light depending on manufacturer (FCA: yes)

P06EA.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P06EA.summary: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EA means this control unit of sensor 1 (before the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault.

causes.text: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location)
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software

symptoms: Check engine light or emissions warning
Message to check AdBlue/emission system, possibly countdown to start lock
Follow-up codes for SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility

P06EB.title: NOx Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P06EB.summary: A modern NOx sensor is a smart sensor: a ceramic sensing element with pump cells and heater plus its own control unit with a microcontroller, which regulates the pump currents, calculates NOx and oxygen and sends them to the engine module over CAN. P06EB means this control unit of sensor 2 (after the SCR catalyst) reports an internal fault – its self-tests of RAM and ROM or EEPROM checksums fail – so the electronics, not the sensing element, are at fault.

causes.text: Faulty electronics in the NOx sensor control unit
Moisture or corrosion in control unit or connector (underbody location)
Under- or overvoltage or dips in the sensor supply
Unsuitable replacement sensor or software

symptoms: Check engine light or emissions warning
Message to check AdBlue/emission system, possibly countdown to start lock
Follow-up codes for SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility

P06EC.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P06EC.summary: P06EC is a notice code like P0700: a separate fuel injector control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module over CAN to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault is stored in that module and must be read there; simple OBD readers show only P06EC.

causes.text: Emission-related fault in the injector control module or its injectors/sensors (code stored there)
Supply, ground or relay problem of the module
Internal module fault (memory, processor)
Software level of engine or injector module

symptoms: Generic scanner shows only P06EC – details in the injector module
Depending on the fault, power loss, misfire or limp mode

P06ED.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Low
P06ED.summary: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06ED means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high.

causes.text: Speed output wire chafing against ground
Receiver (instrument, add-on device) shorted internally
Aftermarket tachometer or accessory wired wrongly
Engine module driver stage

P06EE.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit High
P06EE.summary: The engine module turns the crankshaft signal into a cleaned-up square wave for the tachometer, transmission or body-builder modules – Saab's 1999 9-3, for example, sends two pulses per revolution, about 30 Hz at idle. P06EE means this output is too high, typically shorted to supply voltage, so it can no longer switch to ground; the driver may shut down for protection.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to 12 V
Wrongly connected accessory (speed pick-up)
Receiving device faulty
Engine module

symptoms: Tachometer shows nothing or full scale

P06EF.title: Engine Restart Performance
P06EF.summary: P06EF concerns the automatic restart after the system itself has stopped the engine – stop-start or hybrid. The restart, by starter, reinforced stop-start starter or belt starter-generator, takes too long or fails.

causes.text: Starter or starter-generator worn, contacts intermittently open
Engine module software
Weak stop-start battery (AGM/EFB) or battery sensor
Fuel pressure or ignition at restart

symptoms: Engine does not restart or restarts late after stop-start

P06F0.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P06F0.summary: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat.

causes.text: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F1.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P06F1.summary: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat.

causes.text: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F2.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P06F2.summary: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat.

causes.text: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F3.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P06F3.summary: Some SCR diesels have a separate reductant control module that drives the DEF pump, heaters and dosing valve – Ford calls it the pump motor controller (fault above 130 °C under P20FF), GM's L5P an SCR power module. It measures its own board temperature with an internal sensor to protect itself from heat.

causes.text: Reductant control module or pump unit faulty (sensor is on the board)
Water ingress or corrosion in the module (DEF crystals, underbody location)
Supply or ground problems at the module
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Check engine light or SCR warning
Message to check AdBlue system, possibly countdown to start lock
DEF heating or pump inactive (no thawing in frost)

P06F4.title: Stop-Start Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06F4.summary: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes.

causes.text: Wire or connector to the indicator open or shorted
Indicator or instrument cluster faulty
Engine module driver stage

symptoms: Stop-start indicator not working or permanently lit

P06F5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2
P06F5.summary: SAE J2012 provides a complete code family for a second glow plug control module, mirroring module 1 code for code. P06F5 is the general or internal fault of module 2, the counterpart of P064C.

causes.text: Glow plug control module 2 faulty internally
Poor supply or ground of module 2
Module software or configuration

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06F6.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit/Open
P06F6.summary: P06F6 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is open or has a general circuit fault – the counterpart of P0670 for module 1. The engine module's output driver detects an open load while the driver is off.

causes.text: Line from engine module to glow module 2 open, connector loose or corroded
Input of glow module 2 faulty or module not connected
Engine module output driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06F7.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Low
P06F7.summary: P06F7 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is too low, typically shorted to ground – the counterpart of P0383 for module 1. The engine module's output driver detects the short by its current when switched on or by the line voltage when switched off.

causes.text: Command line to glow module 2 chafed through to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the connector bridging to ground
Input of glow module 2 or engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06F8.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit High
P06F8.summary: P06F8 means the command line from the engine module to glow plug control module 2 is too high, typically shorted to positive – the counterpart of P0384 for module 1. Note that Ford's 2023 diesels use P0384 differently, for the supply voltage of the glow module (below 6.5 V or above 16.5 V); in J2012 that is P052F, and for module 2 P06F9.

causes.text: Command line shorted to positive or supply
Corrosion in the connector bridging to a B+ pin
Engine module driver shorted

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06F9.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 System Voltage
P06F9.summary: P06F9 means the supply voltage of glow plug control module 2 is out of range – the counterpart of P052F for module 1. For module 1, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke flags below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or an open supply after about 1 s; GM's L5P checks the same under P163C (below 6.0 V with ignition above 9 V, or implausible against ignition voltage, 4 s).

causes.text: Main feed to glow module 2 open or high-resistance (fuse, fusible link, B+ wire)
Weak battery or discharged auxiliary battery
Module ground corroded
Charging voltage too high

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06FA.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance
P06FA.summary: P06FA means glow plug control module 2 does not respond correctly to the glow command – the counterpart of P06E5 for module 1. For module 1, Ford's 2023 Power Stroke flags internal drivers that fail to switch or overheat for more than 1 s; GM's L5P files the same check under P064C (under 3.2 A with 0 V at the plug for 3.5 s, two trips).

causes.text: Glow module 2 faulty internally (drivers do not switch)
Poor supply or ground of module 2
Module overheating
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06FB.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error
P06FB.summary: P06FB means glow plug control module 2 has found a memory checksum error – the counterpart of P06DF for module 1. The module forms a checksum over its memory at power-up and compares it with the stored value.

causes.text: Glow module 2 faulty internally (memory)
Interrupted programming or faulty software
Voltage dip at power-up

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06FC.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit
P06FC.summary: P06FC means the feedback or communication from glow plug control module 2 to the engine module is missing, or the line is open or shorted – the counterpart of P0683 for module 1. Depending on design the module reports over a single feedback wire (Bosch-type systems expect it inverse to the command line) or over the bus; GM and Ford report a lost bus link as U0106 rather than P0683.

causes.text: Feedback or bus line open or shorted, connector corroded
Glow module 2 without supply (does not transmit)
Glow module 2 or engine module interface faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06FD.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit Range/Performance
P06FD.summary: P06FD means signals or messages from glow plug control module 2 arrive at the engine module but are implausible – wrong duty cycle or pattern, feedback not matching the command, or single messages timing out. It is the counterpart of P0684 for module 1; Saab's Bosch-based diesels, for example, expect the feedback signal to be inverse to the command line.

causes.text: Loose contact or contact resistance in the feedback or bus line
Ground offset between module and engine module from glow currents
Software mismatch between modules or module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly glow plug/wait-to-start lamp
Hard cold start, long cranking in frost
Rough cold idle and white smoke, often one cylinder bank only

P06FE.title: Cold Start Diesel Intake Air Flow Control Performance
P06FE.summary: 'Diesel intake air flow control' is the diesel's electric intake throttle with position sensor (P02E0 ff). During cold start many diesels close it partly: the extra load raises exhaust temperature so the catalysts light off sooner.

causes.text: Intake throttle coked with soot and oil (EGR, crankcase ventilation)
Throttle motor or gear stiff, position sensor faulty
Ice or condensate in the intake in frost
Contact resistance in connector or wiring, low voltage

symptoms: Check engine light, usually after two trips
Possibly more smoke or smell while warming up

P06FF.title: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06FF.summary: When the engine module switches a lamp through its own wire, it checks the output driver electrically like other lamp outputs: with the lamp off the line must carry supply voltage, with it on nearly 0 V – GM's MIL driver, for example, flags an open circuit at 200 kΩ or more. It cannot see whether the bulb lights, and on cars that send the lamp command over CAN such faults appear as U codes.

causes.text: Wire or connector to the lamp open or shorted
Lamp or instrument cluster faulty
Engine module

symptoms: ECO indicator not working or permanently lit

P0700.title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
P0700.summary: P0700 is a notice code: the separate transmission control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault – a sensor, solenoid, ratio or speed sensor code – is stored in the transmission module and must be read with a tool that can address it; simple OBD readers often show only P0700.

causes.text: Actual fault stored in the transmission module (sensor, solenoid, ratio, speed sensor)
Wrong transmission fluid level or condition causing slip or ratio codes
Harness or connector at the transmission corroded or damaged
Low system voltage or weak battery
Transmission module or software faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly transmission warning
Depending on the transmission fault: limp mode, harsh or delayed shifts
Often no symptoms if the fault was intermittent
Simple OBD reader shows only P0700

P0701.title: Transmission Control System Range/Performance
P0701.summary: P0701 means the transmission control system works outside its expected range or its function is implausible – without a circuit fault. What exactly is checked is up to the manufacturer; no GM, Ford, Saab or bulletin document available to us describes the strategy.

causes.text: Transmission control faulty internally or software
Implausible input signals (speed or range sensor) without own circuit fault
Wrong fluid level or quality – hydraulics do not respond
Harness or connector with contact resistance

symptoms: Transmission warning (at Ford no check engine light)
Limp mode with fixed gear or missing gears

P0702.title: Transmission Control System Electrical
P0702.summary: P0702 reports an electrical fault in the transmission control system as a whole – typically the supply of the transmission actuators (solenoid supply, transmission relay, supply switch in the module) or a circuit fault not assigned to a single component. No manufacturer document available to us describes it in detail; Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks stores it without the check engine light.

causes.text: Transmission actuator supply interrupted (fuse, relay, ground)
Harness or connector at transmission or module damaged, corroded or oil-soaked
Transmission module output stage or supply switch faulty
Low or fluctuating system voltage

symptoms: Transmission limp mode with fixed gear
Transmission warning; check engine light depending on the maker
No or harsh shifts, further solenoid codes

P0703.title: Brake Switch B Circuit
P0703.summary: Brake switch A is usually the brake light switch, B a second, redundant contact or signal used to cancel cruise control, release the converter clutch, check 'brake before throttle' and for stop-start. Since about 2014 GM receives it as a CAN message from the body module and checks its integrity (rolling counter, protection value: 3 of 10 faulty in 2014, 9 of 17 in 2025) without the check engine light; cruise control is disabled.

causes.text: Brake light or double switch worn, corroded or misadjusted
Wiring or connector at the pedal damaged, fuse blown
CAN message from the body module disturbed (GM: software, bus fault)
Aftermarket LED lamps or trailer module distorting the circuit

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or drops out
Brake light stays on or does not work
Selector cannot be moved out of P (shift lock)
Check engine light depending on the maker

P0704.title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit
P0704.summary: Only on cars with a clutch pedal: the clutch switch tells the engine module that the clutch is depressed, used to cancel cruise control, smooth load changes when shifting and for stop-start. The check is a plausibility test over driving events rather than a voltage check: Saab's Trionic T8 expects a change of state every time the car pulls away from 3 to 50 km/h (four misses in a row), the EDC16 diesel at gear changes (25 in a row, above 35 km/h and 1500 rpm), and Ford compares its two clutch switches continuously.

causes.text: Clutch switch faulty or misadjusted (does not switch or too late)
Connector or wiring at the pedal box damaged or corroded
Floor mat or pedal stop shifted, switch bracket broken
Driving style (pulling away or shifting without fully depressing the clutch)

symptoms: Cruise control not working or not cancelling when declutching
Jerks or rev hang when shifting

P0705.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit (PRNDL Input)
P0705.summary: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805).

causes.text: Range sensor worn, dirty or with oil or water ingress
Sensor misadjusted or selector cable out of adjustment
Harness or connector at the transmission damaged, short to ground
Transmission or engine module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0706.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.summary: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805).

causes.text: Range sensor or transmission module with integrated sensor faulty
Selector cable or sensor misadjusted (position between two ranges)
Contact resistance in sensor supply or ground
Moisture or oil in harness or connector

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0707.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.summary: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805).

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafing at the transmission case)
Sensor faulty internally
Sensor supply missing (5 V reference, fuse)
Connector corroded or oil in the connector

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock

P0708.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit High
P0708.summary: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805).

causes.text: Sensor connector off or signal/ground wire open
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Poor sensor or transmission ground

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0709.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

P070A.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit
P070A.summary: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump (capacitive or voltage-based) report the oil level to the transmission module; measurements are only valid under defined conditions – an Allison patent names fluid temperature, vehicle at rest, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions.

causes.text: Fluid level sensor faulty
Wire or connector to the sensor (often through the sump or transmission connector) open or oil-soaked
Transmission module input faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning or 'check fluid level' message

P070B.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance

Fluid level actually wrong (over- or underfilled) or wrong fluid

symptoms: Warning or message about transmission fluid level
Fluid level display implausible or unavailable

P070C.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Low
P070C.summary: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump report the oil level to the transmission module as a voltage; an Allison patent converts it to millimetres and only accepts readings with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions.

Level sensor faulty internally
Transmission connector soaked in oil or corroded
Module input faulty

symptoms: Fluid level display missing or warning to check transmission fluid
Transmission warning lamp depending on manufacturer

P070D.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit High

P070E.summary: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump report the oil level to the transmission module as a voltage; an Allison patent converts it to millimetres and only accepts readings with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid, low input speed and a tilt correction. P070F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too Low
P070F.summary: P070F is not a circuit fault but a condition: a working fluid level sensor reports a level below the target band. In the Allison patent the module compares the measured height in millimetres with a tilt-dependent band and reports at least a quart too little or too much – only with the vehicle at rest, fluid above about 30–40 °C and low input speed.

P0710.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0710.summary: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit.

causes.text: Fluid temperature sensor faulty (often part of the internal harness or valve body)
Transmission connector leaking or corroded, oil in the connector
Wire open or shorted
Transmission or engine module faulty

symptoms: Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool

P0711.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0711.summary: P0711 means the fluid temperature signal is electrically valid but implausible. Manufacturers check three things: the fluid does not warm up as expected (GM 2025 still below 15 °C after the calibrated warm-up time, Saab's AF40 below 20 °C after 10 minutes of driving), the value is stuck (Ford: within ±2 °F for about 2.5 minutes below 70 or above 225 °F), or it jumps unrealistically.

causes.text: Fluid temperature sensor drifting or stuck
High contact resistance in connector or harness (oil, corrosion)
Very cold weather or short trips (fluid does not reach warm-up threshold)
Outdated module software
Fluid cooler thermostat faulty

symptoms: Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool

P0715.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0715.summary: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing.

causes.text: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear, harsh shifts
Torque converter clutch does not apply
Input speed shows 0 or implausible in the scan tool

P0716.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

P0719.title: Brake Switch B Circuit Low
P0719.summary: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking.

Wire to the module open (GM) or shorted to ground (Saab T8)
Connector at the pedal box corroded
Brake light circuit fuse blown

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be activated or switches off
Unusual shifting, converter clutch behaviour changed
Brake lights stay off or on

P071A.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit
P071A.summary: A transmission mode switch selects an alternative shift schedule such as sport, winter or tow/haul; J2012 does not define which button is A or B. No manufacturer document available to us uses P071A–P071F: GM monitors its analog drive mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, 200 of 250 samples, two trips), which shows how such buttons are read as coded voltages.

causes.text: Mode switch A faulty (selector lever or console)
Wiring or connector in the console damaged (spilled drinks, chafing)
Resistor coding drifted (analog buttons)
Control module faulty

symptoms: Mode A cannot be selected or stays active
Transmission stays on the normal shift schedule

P0720.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit
P0720.summary: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0720 is the general circuit code.

causes.text: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Warning lamp, limp mode or fixed gear
Harsh shifts, cruise control not working

P0721.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0721.summary: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0721 means the output speed is present but implausible: too high (Ford 6R80 above 7450 rpm), not matching wheel or input speed in the engaged gear (ZF 6HP26 more than 200 or 250 rpm apart, Ford's F21 more than 15 % for 10 s), or jumping (Allison 1000: 500 rpm within 0.15 s).

causes.text: Output speed sensor faulty or dirty (metal debris)
Contact problems or interference in the sensor circuit
Wrong tyre size or axle ratio, faulty wheel speed sensor
Reluctor wheel damaged or sensor mounted wrongly

symptoms: ABS/ESP warning possible if wheel speed is affected

P0722.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal

P0722 means the output speed signal is missing while the vehicle is driving.

P0725.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit
P0725.summary: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. Today it almost always arrives over CAN from the engine module with a validity flag; only GM's 2007 Allison 1000 tables show a separate engine speed sensor read by the transmission module.

causes.text: Crankshaft or camshaft sensor fault in the engine module (speed invalid there)
CAN fault between engine and transmission module (wiring, termination, connector)
Engine module software or fault
Transmission module faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp, possibly check engine light
Often an engine code (crankshaft sensor) as well

P0729.title: Gear 6 Incorrect Ratio
P0729.summary: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL.

causes.text: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch for sixth gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in sixth gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P072A.title: Stuck in Neutral
P072A.summary: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged.

causes.text: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts

Clutch or brake for fifth gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in fifth gear, engine speed higher than expected
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit/Open
P0740.summary: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed.

Internal transmission harness or mechatronic unit

P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off

Solenoid mechanically sluggish (electrically fine)

symptoms: Check engine light or 'service hybrid system' message

Slipping, engine speed rises without drive
Jolt when the engine starts or stops

P07A2.title: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off
P07A2.summary: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. P07A2 concerns clutch A.

causes.text: Clutch A plates worn or piston seal leaking
Too little apply pressure (fluid, pump, valve)
Clutch actuator or valve sticking (DCT: electric actuator)
Module software or lost adaption

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Gear missing or slipping, weak acceleration

P07A3.title: Transmission Friction Element A Stuck On
P07A3.summary: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. GM's hybrid transmissions use only the stuck-on codes: when a clutch should release, the module expects slip to build and flags it if slip stays near zero – the Two-Mode SUVs (2008–13) at 80 rpm or less for 4.5 s with more than 320–350 Nm on the clutch, after two trips; the Volt Gen 1 and ELR when clutch 1 shows no slip while released ('applied or welded'), three attempts, after one trip; Volt Gen 2, Malibu Hybrid and CT6 plug-in by comparing actual slip with the target release profile, after one trip.

causes.text: Clutch A stuck, welded or piston hanging
Valve or spool sticking in the applied position
Contaminated fluid (debris)
Module software

symptoms: Check engine light or 'service hybrid system' message
Jolt or tie-up on mode or gear changes
Engine stalls or drags when stopping

On GM's shift-by-wire selectors (2017 LaCrosse, XT4/XT5, Bolt EV, later SUVs and pickups) it is the P button, read by two redundant analog sensors A and B with separate 'released' and 'pressed' voltage zones.

causes.text: Loose contact in the selector connector or harness
Sensor with intermittent fault
Off-centre pressing or a hand resting on the button

symptoms: Check engine light, 'service transmission' or 'unable to shift' message
Park cannot be selected by button, or the car will not shift out of P

P07BF.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07BF.summary: These low/high codes are a purely electrical check of the sensor's signal voltage at the module and run even with the vehicle at rest – unlike the circuit, range, no-signal and intermittent codes, which evaluate speed while driving. Low means a short to ground, high a short to supply or, depending on the circuit, an open.

causes.text: Signal or supply wire shorted to ground (chafing at the case)
Sensor shorted internally
Oil or moisture in the connector
Module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (GM after one trip)
Limp mode, harsh shifts, no converter lock-up

P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance
P07CB.summary: Many automatics have a thermostat in the fluid cooler circuit or a coolant-to-oil heat exchanger: a BMW patent describes a wax thermostat that bypasses the cooler until about 76 °C, a Ford patent a heat exchanger that warms transmission fluid from the coolant after a cold start. P07CB means this thermostat does not work as expected: fluid warms up too slowly (stuck open) or overheats (stuck closed).

causes.text: Transmission fluid thermostat stuck open or closed
Fluid temperature sensor drifting
Cooler lines or heat exchanger blocked or leaking
Very cold weather or short trips

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Converter clutch applies late, higher consumption

P07CC.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low
P07CC.summary: Transmission mode switches select alternative shift programs such as sport, winter or tow/haul; the J2012 family runs from A (P071A–P071C) and B (P071D–P071F) to C (base code P078F), D and E. No manufacturer document available to us uses switches C to E; GM reads its analog mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, two trips) and newer drive mode selectors under P05D0–P05D3.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Button stuck pressed (switching to ground)
Moisture or dirt in the button
Control module

symptoms: Mode C cannot be selected or stays active
Transmission stays on the normal program

P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8
P07D7.summary: P07D7 means gear 8 cannot be disengaged: the module commands a shift out of 8th, but the transmission stays in it. It is the counterpart to P07D8, where gear 8 cannot be engaged.

causes.text: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 8 and will not downshift

P07D8.title: Unable to Engage Gear 8
P07D8.summary: 'Unable to Engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – here 8th. Documented users are eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes with hydraulically moved, position-monitored shift forks.

causes.text: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged

symptoms: Gear 8 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07D9.title: Gear 8 Incorrect Ratio
P07D9.summary: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7.

causes.text: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 8
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 8 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07DA.title: 6-7 Shift
P07DA.summary: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. They continue the series P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift'.

causes.text: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Engine speed flares during the shift

P07DB.title: 7-8 Shift
P07DB.summary: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. They continue the series P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift'.

causes.text: Shift or clutch valve sticking

P07DC.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 1
P07DC.summary: The series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA and P07FD for 9 and 10) covers a shift that leaves the starting gear but lands in a gear other than the commanded target – a skipped or overshot gear. A module can see this after the shift because the measured ratio matches the wrong gear.

causes.text: Shift or pressure control valve sticking in the valve body
Clutch or brake pack worn or leaking
Fluid low or contaminated
Wrong adaptives or software
Turbine or output speed signal wrong

symptoms: Wrong or skipped gear when shifting out of gear 1
Harsh shift or engine speed jump
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode in a fixed gear

P07E4.title: Unable to Engage Park
P07E4.summary: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E4 means park is not reached or not held within the allowed time.

causes.text: Manual park release cable misrouted or actuated
Range actuator misaligned or its coupling offset
Control module software
Park lock actuator or its ground faulty
Range or park position signal wrong

symptoms: Park cannot be selected, 'Park not available' message
Vehicle may roll away if not secured

P07E5.title: Unable to Engage Drive

P07E5 means drive is requested but not reached in time.

causes.text: Range control actuator misaligned or faulty
Software or after-effect of an over-the-air update

Forward clutch or line pressure missing

symptoms: Range falls back to N or P

P07E6.title: Stuck in Park
P07E6.summary: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E6 means park cannot be left: the pawl stays engaged or its position feedback keeps reporting P.

causes.text: Park lock actuator failed internally
High resistance at the park motor ground
Control module software
Low system voltage

symptoms: Vehicle stays in P and cannot be driven away
P flashes on the selector, P in the cluster dark

P07E7.title: Stuck in Drive
P07E7.summary: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E7 means drive cannot be left: after a request for P, N or R the transmission stays in D.

causes.text: Range actuator or selector shaft sticking
Range sensor wrongly reporting D
Selector sensor or software

symptoms: Range stays in D despite the selector request
P or N cannot be reached, warning message

P07E8.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit/Open
P07E8.summary: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M.

causes.text: Wire or connector between selector and shift module open
Position sensor in the selector faulty
Shift module input faulty

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED
