P07EA.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.summary: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M.

causes.text: Selector sensor wire shorted to ground (chafed harness, connector)
Sensor supply in the selector open
Selector or module faulty

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EB.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High
P07EB.summary: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to 5 V or 12 V supply
Selector faulty internally
Shift module

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EC.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit
P07EC.summary: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8).

causes.text: One position sensor in the selector faulty
One sensor wire open or shorted
Dirt or sticking mechanism in the selector

symptoms: Selected range taken over with a delay of a second or more

P07ED.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.summary: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8).

causes.text: Selector sensor board faulty
Selector connector corroded or loose (several pins)
Liquid spilled into the center console

symptoms: No range can be selected, vehicle in neutral
MIL and red or yellow shift warning

P07EE.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.summary: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8).

causes.text: Electric shift module faulty (hardware or software)
Outdated module software
Selector or harness

symptoms: Vehicle goes to neutral, shifting blocked

P07EF.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.summary: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8).

causes.text: Selector plug disconnected or its supply or ground open
Selector sensor board faulty
Electric shift module

symptoms: Vehicle in neutral, no range selectable
Fault appears right after switching the ignition on

P07F0.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.summary: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8).

causes.text: Selector signal wires shorted to the supply
Selector faulty
Shift module

symptoms: Shift warning or MIL (depends on manufacturer)

P07F1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.summary: P07F1 is the general circuit code of a third input or turbine shaft speed sensor, after sensor A (P0715) and B (P2765); low and high for sensor C are P07C3 and P07C4. No production use could be found in GM tables from 2015 to 2025, Ford's summaries of 2012 and 2020–23, Mitsubishi's code index or manufacturer bulletins; such a sensor would make sense on transmissions with three input shafts or a hybrid input.

causes.text: Sensor wire or connector open
Speed sensor faulty
Control module or software

symptoms: Harsh shifts, converter clutch stays open

P07F2.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.summary: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F2 reports a fault in its communication.

causes.text: Shift-by-wire module faulty or its software
Communication wire or connector
Weak battery during start-up

symptoms: Usually no restriction; neutral if the transmission is affected too
U codes in other modules possible

P07F3.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.summary: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F3 is the electrical low check of its communication line: the line is shorted to ground and stays at a low level.

causes.text: Communication wire shorted to ground
Module output stage faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F4.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.summary: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F4 is the electrical high check of its communication line: the line is shorted to the supply and stays at a high level.

causes.text: Communication wire shorted to the supply
Module faulty
Connector fault

symptoms: Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F5.title: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.summary: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F5 means its supply voltage is too low.

causes.text: Weak battery or charging system
Fuse, supply or ground wire of the module with high resistance
High actuator motor current on a weak supply

symptoms: Range or park lock reacts late or not at all
Often together with battery voltage codes

P07F6.title: Gear 9 Incorrect Ratio
P07F6.summary: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7.

causes.text: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 9
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 9 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F7.title: Gear 10 Incorrect Ratio
P07F7.summary: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7.

causes.text: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 10
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 10 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F8.title: Stuck in Gear 9
P07F8.summary: P07F8 means gear 9 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 9th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 9 and will not downshift

P07F9.title: Unable to Engage Gear 9
P07F9.summary: P07F9 means the transmission does not reach the commanded 9th gear – the counterpart to P07F8, where 9th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged

symptoms: Gear 9 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FA.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 9
P07FA.summary: P07FA belongs to the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9, P07FD for 10): when leaving 9th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 9th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 9th

P07FB.title: Stuck in Gear 10
P07FB.summary: P07FB means gear 10 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 10th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 10 and will not downshift

P07FC.title: Unable to Engage Gear 10
P07FC.summary: P07FC means the transmission does not reach the commanded 10th gear – the counterpart to P07FB, where 10th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged

symptoms: Gear 10 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FD.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 10
P07FD.summary: P07FD closes the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9): when leaving 10th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 10th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it.

causes.text: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 10th

P07FE.title: Stuck in Gear Not Specified
P07FE.summary: P07FE is the catch-all of the 'Stuck in Gear' family: the transmission stays in a gear it was commanded to leave, but the module cannot or does not name the gear. The gear-specific codes are P072B–P073C for reverse and gears 1–7, P07D7 for 8th, P07F8 for 9th and P07FB for 10th.

causes.text: Shift actuator or shift valve sticking
System pressure low or unstable
Mechanical damage in the gear train
Position or speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Transmission no longer shifts and stays in one gear

P07FF.title: Cold Start Transmission Performance
P07FF.summary: P07FF means the transmission does not work as expected during the cold-start phase, shortly after starting with cold, thick fluid – for example a gear preselection or a clutch or valve response outside the expected window. The only documented user is Mercedes-Benz: its 2024 bulletin for the eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox 8G-DCT in the compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLA, GLB) names P07FF together with P0921, with reverse not available, a possible limp-home mode and the MIL; after switching off and on everything works again, and the fix was new control unit software.

causes.text: Transmission control module software misjudging the cold phase
Shift valve or hydraulics too slow with cold fluid
Wrong or aged fluid, low level
Fluid temperature sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Reverse not available (message in the cluster)
Limp-home mode shortly after a cold start
Normal again after switching off and on

P0800.title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
P0800.summary: P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it.

causes.text: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch)
Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion)
Transfer case module software
Transfer case module faulty

symptoms: All-wheel drive or low range cannot be selected

P0801.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit/Open
P0801.summary: On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open.

causes.text: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Reverse hard or impossible to engage
Service note in the driver display, usually no MIL

P0802.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.summary: On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit.

causes.text: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded
Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Module output or input faulty
Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line

symptoms: Transmission faults no longer light the MIL

P0803.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
P0803.summary: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open.

causes.text: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness damaged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout no longer works (1-2 always possible)

P0804.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit
P0804.summary: With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command.

causes.text: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty
Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted
Instrument cluster board faulty
Engine module output faulty

symptoms: 1-4 lamp never lights or stays on

P0805.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit
P0805.summary: The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault.

causes.text: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator)
Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted
Transmission module software (Nissan)
Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver)

symptoms: Idle stop disabled ('Idle Stop System Fault')
Jerky driving or harsh clutch engagement (dual clutch)

P0806.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.summary: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.

causes.text: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty
Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work
Harness or connector with contact resistance
Clutch actuator motor faulty (DPS6)
Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return

symptoms: Cruise control and start-stop not working
Engine starts only with the pedal fully pressed, or not at all
Dual clutch: jerky take-off, limp mode

P0807.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.summary: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.

causes.text: Signal wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference of the sensor missing
Pedal sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or pins loose

symptoms: Start-stop disabled, possibly no engine start

P0808.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.summary: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.

causes.text: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Pedal sensor faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0809.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.summary: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.

causes.text: Clutch A actuator motor or its Hall sensors faulty
Loose contact at the actuator connector
Transmission module Hall evaluation faulty
Supply voltage dips

P080A.title: Clutch Position Not Learned
P080A.summary: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.

causes.text: Relearn not done after sensor, clutch or module replacement
Clutch badly worn or misadjusted
Pedal sensor misadjusted or wrongly fitted
Engine module reprogrammed or replaced

symptoms: Start-stop, cruise control or hill start assist disabled
Engine may start only with the pedal at the stop

P080B.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.summary: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit.

causes.text: Solenoid coil with shorted turns or resistance out of range
Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value
Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance)
Control module or software

symptoms: 1-4 lockout works not at all or only sometimes

P080C.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.summary: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through to ground at gearbox or frame
Solenoid coil shorted to its housing
Connector corroded or water ingress
Older GM modules: circuit open or solenoid unplugged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: 1-4 lockout permanently active or not working
1-4 lamp possibly unrelated to the lockout

P080D.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.summary: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (damaged harness)
Solenoid coil with shorted turns (resistance near zero)
Substitute resistor ('eliminator') with too low a value
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips

P0810.title: Clutch Position Control Error
P0810.summary: P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor.

causes.text: Control unit software with too tight parameters
Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty
Clutch position sensor inaccurate
Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch

symptoms: Loss of drive until the next key cycle

P0811.title: Excessive Clutch A Slippage
P0811.summary: P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published.

causes.text: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture)
Clutch worn or overheated
Fluid burnt or wrong (wet clutch)
Clutch pressure or actuator too low
Input speed sensor faulty

P0812.title: Reverse Input Circuit
P0812.summary: P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors.

causes.text: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted
Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work)
Back-up lamp circuit fuse blown
Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position

symptoms: Back-up lamps never or always on
Reversing camera or parking aid does not switch on

P0813.title: Reverse Output Circuit
P0813.summary: P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short.

causes.text: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted
Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty
Connector corroded
Module output stage faulty

symptoms: Reversing camera or parking beeper does not activate

P0814.title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
P0814.summary: P0814 concerns the drive or data circuit of the range display – the PRNDL or PRNDM display or lighting on the selector, sometimes in the instrument cluster. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: the electronic shift module stores P0814 with the MIL on, the selector lighting flickers or goes dark, and in a 2020 bulletin the lever could be moved out of park during cranking so that the engine stalled.

causes.text: Shift module software (Jeep Compass)
Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster
Display LED or selector module faulty
Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range

symptoms: Range display on the selector flickers or stays dark
Lever can leave P during cranking, engine stalls (Jeep)

P0815.title: Upshift Switch Circuit
P0815.summary: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch.

causes.text: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty
Clockspring or steering wheel wiring (paddles)

symptoms: Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode

P0816.title: Downshift Switch Circuit
P0816.summary: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch.

causes.text: Downshift switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly faulty
Body or transmission module

symptoms: Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode

P0817.title: Starter Disable Circuit/Open
P0817.summary: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V).

causes.text: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted
Connector corroded or pins pushed back
Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty
Body module faulty

symptoms: Engine does not crank in P or N
Start possible in only one of the two ranges

P0818.title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
P0818.summary: P0818 concerns a switch input that reports whether the driveline is disconnected – on four-wheel-drive vehicles typically the neutral position of the transfer case or an axle disconnect, on hybrids a disconnect clutch between engine and transmission, as a Ford patent uses the term. It matters for OBD because in transfer case neutral the engine runs without load and wheel speed does not match the ratio, so misfire, ratio and vehicle speed monitors must know about it; CARB requires monitoring only then.

causes.text: Neutral or disconnect switch at the transfer case or axle faulty
Underbody wiring or connector corroded or damaged
Transfer case actuator does not reach its end position
Control module or software

symptoms: All-wheel drive or neutral cannot be selected
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0819.title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.summary: P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken.

causes.text: Tap switch sticking or faulty
Range sensor or selector sensor misadjusted or faulty
Selector cable misadjusted
Selector wiring or connectors

symptoms: Tap or manual mode not working

P081A.title: Starter Disable Circuit Low
P081A.summary: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V).

causes.text: P/N line to the engine module shorted to ground
Line or connector open
Connector oxidized or pins pushed back
Transmission module output stage faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or only sometimes
Starter does not crank in P or N

P081B.title: Starter Disable Circuit High
P081B.summary: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V).

causes.text: P/N line shorted to positive (chafed against a supply wire)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Transmission module output stage faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or starts unreliably
Start release in the wrong range possible (safety risk)

P081C.title: Park Input Circuit
P081C.summary: P081C concerns the input 'park position' – the P contact of the selector or shift module, or the park pawl feedback – which controls switching off the ignition, key release, starter release and the 'not in park' warning. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: a 2022 bulletin lists P081C with the MIL on, with 'Vehicle not in Park' shown although P is engaged; the car cannot be switched off, modules stay awake and the battery drains.

causes.text: Shift module software (Jeep Compass)
P contact or selector switch faulty or misadjusted
Selector cable misadjusted
Wire or connector

symptoms: 'Not in park' message although P is engaged
Ignition cannot be switched off, battery drains

P081D.title: Neutral Input Circuit
P081D.summary: P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics.

Selector or shift cable misadjusted
Wire or connector
Control module or software

symptoms: Engine does not start in N (only in P)

P081E.title: Excessive Clutch B Slippage
P081E.summary: P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit.

Clutch 2 worn or overheated
Fluid or pressure
Input speed sensor B faulty

symptoms: Reverse or even gears not available

P081F.title: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
P081F.summary: The brake transmission shift interlock (BTSI) is a solenoid or actuator that locks the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed, as US rule FMVSS 114 requires. 'Signal correlation' is the plausibility check between the interlock command or feedback and its input signals – brake switch and selector position: for example the lock released without a brake signal, or still active although the brake is pressed.

causes.text: Brake lamp switch misadjusted or faulty
Interlock solenoid or locking mechanism sticking
Wire or connector to the selector
Selector module, control unit or software

symptoms: Selector cannot be moved out of P
Selector moves out of P without the brake

P0820.summary: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0825.title: Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate)
P0825.summary: P0825 concerns a switch on the selector that reports pushing or pulling the lever – sequential + and – shifting – or the start of a shift movement, hence 'shift anticipate'. Its purpose: the control unit of an automated manual gearbox can prepare clutch and engine torque before the actual gear change is detected; a LuK patent describes such shift-intent detection, which reports intent when the lever signal exceeds a filtered, load-dependent reference and cancels on a reversal.

P0826.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.summary: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0826 is the general fault of the shared circuit.

P0829.title: 5-6 Shift

P0830.summary: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. Which switch is A or B is up to each manufacturer – FCA calls the pedal-up switch A.

P0836.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit
P0836.summary: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs.

causes.text: Loose contact or corrosion at the gearbox connector
Chafed spot in the harness
Dirt at sensor or valve causing signal jumps
Sensor faulty internally

P084F.title: Park/Neutral Switch Output Circuit
P084F.summary: P084F concerns an output: a gearbox, hybrid or selector module passes the park/neutral status as a switched signal to other modules, for example for start release. The module watches its own driver for open circuits and shorts.

causes.text: P/N output line or connector open or shorted
Module software misjudging the output
Output driver in the module faulty
Receiving module pulls the line wrongly

symptoms: Engine or ready mode does not start in P/N
Warning about gear or park position

P0850.title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
P0850.summary: The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors.

causes.text: Range or inhibitor switch faulty or misadjusted
Selector cable misadjusted or stretched
Wiring or connector between switch, gearbox module and engine module
Module input or software

symptoms: Engine does not crank in P or N
Engine cranks in a drive range (safety risk)

P0853.title: Drive Switch Input Circuit
P0853.summary: The drive switch input reports to the engine or gearbox module that range D is selected, usually through its own contact in the range switch or selector next to the park/neutral contact. causes.text: Range switch or D contact faulty or misadjusted
Wire or connector open or corroded
Selector cable misadjusted
Module input or software

symptoms: Fault stored, MIL depending on maker

P0856.title: Traction Control Input Signal
P0856.summary: The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead.

Software of engine or brake module, module faulty
CAN fault, connector or ground at the brake or engine module
Low supply voltage

symptoms: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off
No torque reduction when wheels spin
C0242 or similar in the brake module

P0863.title: TCM Communication Circuit
P0863.summary: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL.

causes.text: Wire or connector between engine and gearbox module open or corroded
Gearbox module without power or ground
Gearbox module faulty
Input of the engine module faulty

symptoms: Gearbox warning or limp mode possible
Gearbox faults not passed to the engine module

P0867.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure
P0867.summary: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff).

causes.text: Fluid level extremely low or leak
Fluid pump or its drive faulty
Pressure regulator or relief valve sticking
System pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp or MIL on
Limp mode, car may be stranded

P086A.title: Neutral Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P086A.summary: Neutral position sensor A is a position sensor, usually a three-wire Hall sensor, on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox. It tells the engine module that neutral is selected, which start-stop needs before it may switch the engine off.

P0870.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0870.summary: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. P087A.title: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit
P087A.summary: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). symptoms: Reverse or even gears missing, limp mode

P0880.title: TCM Power Input Signal
P0880.summary: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting.

Harsh engagement into D or R

P0881.summary: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting.

causes.text: Contact resistance in supply or ground, voltage drop under load
Alternator or battery problem
Relay with worn contacts
Internal measurement of the module faulty

P0882.title: TCM Power Input Signal Low
P0882.summary: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting.

causes.text: Weak battery or alternator not charging
Transmission relay, fuse or fuse box module faulty (Chrysler)
Corroded ground or supply wire, connector at the module
Module faulty

symptoms: Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting

P0883.title: TCM Power Input Signal High
P0883.summary: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting.

causes.text: Alternator voltage regulator faulty (overcharging)
Jump start with 24 V or charger in boost mode
Poor battery ground, regulator measures wrongly
Module measurement faulty

symptoms: Charging warning or unusually bright lights

P0884.title: TCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
P0884.summary: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting.

causes.text: Loose or unlatched connector at fuse box or module
Ignition switch or relay with contact dropouts
Battery terminal or ground loose
Internal module reset

symptoms: Gearbox jerks or briefly enters limp mode while driving
Engine may stall with a combined powertrain module

P0885.title: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P0885.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Relay faulty (coil open) or missing
Wire between relay and module open, connector or fuse box contact
Fuse of the relay coil blown
Module software (FCA 948TE reflash)

symptoms: Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0886.title: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P0886.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Control wire chafed to ground
Relay coil shorted
Module driver faulty

symptoms: Relay does not click or stays pulled in

P0887.title: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
P0887.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Gearbox module software (FCA 948TE)
Control wire shorted to voltage
Relay faulty
Gearbox module faulty

P0888.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit
P0888.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Relay contacts burnt or corroded
Fuse in the load circuit
Wire between relay output and module
Module

symptoms: Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0889.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P0889.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Relay contact with high resistance
Moisture or corrosion in relay or socket
Ground or supply problem

P088A.title: Transmission Fluid Filter Deteriorated
P088A.summary: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes.

causes.text: Filter change interval reached
Heavy contamination from clutch wear
Filter changed without resetting the monitor
Faulty main valve body (Allison serial range)

symptoms: Wrench or TRANS SERVICE indicator flashing
Usually no change in driving behaviour

P088B.title: Transmission Fluid Filter Very Deteriorated
P088B.summary: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes.

causes.text: Filter change overdue
Monitor not reset after the change
Increased internal wear debris
Faulty main valve body (Allison)

symptoms: Message to service the transmission filter

P088C.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit Low
P088C.summary: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code.

causes.text: Wire between engine module and gearbox chafed to ground (tunnel, near exhaust)
Solenoid coil shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in the gearbox connector
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked

P088D.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit High
P088D.summary: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Solenoid coil low-resistance or shorted (driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion between supply and control pin
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Reverse cannot be engaged (lockout not released) or is not blocked

P088E.title: Planetary Gear Set Failure
P088E.summary: P088E means the module has found that a planetary gear set no longer keeps the fixed speed relation between its sun, carrier and ring gear, for example through broken planet gears, seized planet pins or stripped teeth. No maker's table or bulletin documents the code.

causes.text: Planet gears or pins seized or broken (lubrication, overheating)
Tooth damage on sun or ring gear
Speed sensor (engine, motor-generator, output) reading wrong
Low or worn fluid

symptoms: Grinding or whining from the gearbox
Power loss, limp mode (hybrids drive electrically only)

P0890.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0890.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Relay contacts frozen or corroded (Subaru ignition relay)
Outdated engine module software (Subaru)
Fuse or wire between relay and gearbox module
Weak battery

symptoms: Starter does not crank after a short trip in frost (Subaru)
MIL on, P0700 in the engine module
False oil level or other warnings

P0891.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P0891.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Relay contact welded or sticking
Sense or output line shorted to voltage
Wrong relay fitted

P0892.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P0892.summary: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command.

causes.text: Loose contact in relay socket or connector
Relay with worn contacts
Wire broken by vibration

symptoms: Brief limp mode or shift shock

P0893.title: Multiple Gears Engaged
P0893.summary: P0893 means more shift elements are applied than the commanded gear allows, so the gearbox binds up. It is detected through speeds, when the ratio matches no valid gear and input speed collapses, or through commanded clutch capacities: a GM patent flags capacities above their limits for longer than roughly 200 to 500 ms and reacts by downshifting or falling back to the hydraulic limp mode.

causes.text: Gearbox module software or calibration
Shift or pressure valve sticking (dirt), control valve body faulty
Clutch plates stuck or welded
Speed sensor false signal

symptoms: Sudden limp mode, harsh jolts or judder
Strong braking or locking feeling during a shift

P0894.title: Transmission Component Slipping
P0894.summary: P0894 reports slip of a gearbox component, found by comparing speeds. GM's 4L60-E applies it to the torque converter clutch: with lock-up commanded, slip between 100 and 550 rpm for 12.75 s on the third attempt in 4th gear sets it, type B with MIL after two trips; the module first freezes adaptation and raises line pressure.

causes.text: Low, wrong or worn fluid
Converter clutch PWM solenoid cracked or regulator bore worn (GM 4L60-E)
Worn clutch plates or converter clutch lining
Pump not priming, cracked suction filter (Allison)
Control module software

symptoms: Engine speed rises without matching acceleration, mostly when warm
Harsh shifts from maximum pressure, limp mode possible

P0895.title: Shift Time Too Short
P0895.summary: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside.

causes.text: Pressure control valve stuck towards high pressure or line pressure too high
Shift adaptation faulty or reset, wrong software
Valve body: sticking spool, faulty damper or accumulator
Wrong fluid or level

P0896.title: Shift Time Too Long
P0896.summary: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside.

causes.text: Low or worn fluid, low pressure (pump, filter)
Worn clutch plates or band
Pressure or shift valve sticking, leaking piston seals
Lost or reset adaptation, software

symptoms: Delayed shifts, engine flares between gears
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0897.title: Transmission Fluid Deteriorated
P0897.summary: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes.

causes.text: Fluid change interval exceeded
Fluid changed without resetting the oil life monitor
Heavy duty (heat, stop-and-go, retarder) shortens calculated life
Prognostics disabled afterwards (Allison special case)

symptoms: TRANS SERVICE or wrench indicator after each start beforehand

P0898.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
P0898.summary: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866.

causes.text: MIL request wire shorted to ground
Engine or gearbox module connector corroded
Gearbox module output faulty

symptoms: Gearbox faults may not be indicated correctly

P0899.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit High
P0899.summary: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866.

causes.text: Wire open (pull-up in the engine module)
Short to voltage
Gearbox module without power or ground
Gearbox module faulty

symptoms: Gearbox faults may not be reported
Limp mode as well if the gearbox module has no power

P089A.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089A.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Sensor 2 in the selector faulty
Spilled liquid in the centre console

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089B.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P089B.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly faulty or drifting
Selector mechanism worn or bent
Loose contact or interference on the PWM line
Liquid in the console

symptoms: Only P available if both sensors fail

P089C.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P089C.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor 2 faulty
Supply of the selector sensor open
Connector corrosion from spilled drinks

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089D.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P089D.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Signal wire open (pull-up) or shorted to voltage
Sensor 2 faulty
Sensor ground open

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089E.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P089E.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Loose contact at the selector connector
Sensor 2 with internal dropouts
Wire chafed in the console

P089F.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089F.summary: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high.

causes.text: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Sensor 2 faulty
Corrosion from liquid in the console

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A0.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P08A0.summary: Sensor 2 is the redundant second Hall sensor that reports the Y-axis travel of an electronic selector lever as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses it in its electronic range selection (ECM and ICCM tables 2019–2025, Cadillac XT4 among them).

causes.text: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly drifting or faulty
Selector mechanism worn, bent or binding, lever leaves its nominal path
Loose contact or interference on the PWM signal line
Spilled liquid in the centre console

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shift lever message or occasional unaccepted range selection
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A1.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P08A1.summary: The selector lever's Y-axis sensor 2 is one of two redundant Hall sensors that send the lever travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM documents P08A1 for its electronic range selection: the code sets when the measured duty cycle of Y sensor 2 drops below 17 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or below 5 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025), checked 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms or 10 of 12 in later years.

causes.text: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply open or connector backed out
Sensor 2 in the selector assembly without output
Connector corrosion from liquid in the console

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Normally no change in driving, sensor 1 takes over

P08A2.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P08A2.summary: Y sensor 2 is the backup Hall sensor of an electronic selector lever and reports the lever's Y-axis travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses P08A2 in its electronic range selection and sets it when the duty cycle of Y sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or above 95 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025); 3 failures in 4 samples at 25 ms, in later calibrations 10 of 12.

causes.text: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Internal fault of sensor 2 in the selector assembly

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Range selection normally still works via sensor 1

P08A3.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08A3.summary: This code covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the second, redundant Y-axis sensor of an electronic selector lever. No manufacturer documents P08A3 publicly.

causes.text: Loose or fretting contact at the selector connector
Harness chafed by console or lever movement
Sensor 2 with intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Stored fault that comes and goes, often without driver complaint
Possibly check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A4.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A4.summary: An electronic selector lever with redundant sensing measures the X axis with two sensors. P08A4 means the two X readings no longer agree although each may be within its own limits.

causes.text: One of the two X sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path

symptoms: Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A5.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A5.summary: P08A5 is the Y-axis twin of P08A4: the two redundant sensors that measure the selector lever's Y travel disagree beyond a calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents P08A5 publicly.

causes.text: One of the two Y sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path

symptoms: Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A6.title: Gear Lever Position Sensor System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
P08A6.summary: Here the module compares the combined gear lever position information with other evidence and finds no consistent picture. Two makers document it.

causes.text: Tyre size changed without relearning the top-gear ratio (FCA manual)
Control module software needing an update
Internal fault or connector problem of the electronic shift module
Modified transfer case gearing, fault only in 4Low

symptoms: Start-stop and gear indicator disabled, clutch overheat or service transmission message
On shift-by-wire, no gear can be selected

P08A7.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P08A7.summary: Sensor A is the analog or PWM sensor that reports how far the clutch pedal of a manual car is pressed; the engine controller needs it for start-stop, cruise control, gear detection and starter release. P08A7 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that sensor.

causes.text: Loose connector or broken wire at the pedal sensor (pedal box wiring flexes with every clutch stroke)
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor A
Missing 5 V reference or sensor ground
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module

symptoms: Engine may not crank if the starter release relies on the sensor

P08A8.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P08A8.summary: P08A8 flags a clutch pedal sensor whose signal is electrically valid but contradicts how the car is actually driving. GM uses it on manual cars since model year 2018 (before: P0806), e.g.

causes.text: Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket, so its reading no longer matches pedal travel
Worn or drifting sensor track giving an offset signal
Driver resting a foot on the clutch pedal, or a floor mat holding it down
Corroded connector adding resistance to signal or ground

symptoms: Start-stop and cruise control switched off
Rev-matching or hill-start functions may be disabled

P08A9.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P08A9.summary: The sensor is designed with dead bands at both ends, so a signal near 0 V can only come from a fault. GM sets P08A9 when the signal stays below 4 % of the 5 V reference (low voltage or open circuit) for 400 of 500 samples taken every 12.5 ms, with the engine not cranking and system voltage above 9 V (10 V in some 2018 tables); Type A, MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground in the pedal area
Open signal wire or missing 5 V reference (connector off, broken wire)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Shared 5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Engine may refuse to crank on vehicles that release the starter via the sensor

P08AA.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P08AA.summary: P08AA is the mirror image of P08A9: the pedal sensor signal climbs into the upper dead band that a healthy sensor never reaches. GM's threshold is above 96 % of the 5 V reference for 400 of 500 samples at 12.5 ms, engine not cranking, system voltage above 9 V; Type A, MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Open sensor ground wire or corroded ground pin
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Clutch status shown incorrectly in scan tool data

P08AB.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08AB.summary: P08AB is meant for a clutch pedal sensor A signal that jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than a foot could move the pedal, without staying out of range long enough for the low or high codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or worn terminals in the pedal sensor connector
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes with the pedal
Worn sensor track causing signal dropouts at certain pedal positions
Moisture or corrosion in the footwell connector

symptoms: Start-stop or cruise control cutting out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Erratic clutch pedal value in scan tool data while the pedal is held still

P08AC.title: Clutch Pedal Position Not Learned
P08AC.summary: The engine controller has to know at which pedal position the clutch is fully released or disengaged. GM teaches the fully applied position at the factory and then adapts it over time to clutch wear.

causes.text: Relearn not performed after replacing the sensor, clutch parts or engine control module
Learned position drifted out of the allowed window (worn clutch, wrong pedal stop, air in hydraulics)
Learn procedure aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Faulty or misaligned clutch pedal sensor preventing a valid learn

symptoms: Start-stop, cruise control or automatic parking brake release not working as expected

P08AD.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08AD.summary: A neutral position sensor tells the engine module whether a manual gearbox is in neutral, which start-stop, remote start and rev matching rely on. Sensor B is a second sensor or channel next to sensor A (P086A ff).

causes.text: Wire to the sensor broken or stretched by shift shaft movement
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Sensor B open internally

symptoms: Start-stop no longer switches the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster

P08AE.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08AE.summary: Sensor B is the second neutral sensor or channel on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox, complementing sensor A (P086A ff). P08AE means its signal is electrically present but implausible: it stays outside the expected window, does not change when gears are engaged, or reports neutral while the gear ratio says otherwise.

causes.text: Sensor B or its magnet misaligned after gearbox work
Sensor B drifting or faulty
Worn shift shaft or detent giving an unclear neutral position

symptoms: Start system or gear indicator message in the cluster

P08AF.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08AF.summary: The signal of neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel of a manual gearbox, has fallen below its lower electrical limit. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor without output.

causes.text: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Sensor supply open
Sensor B without output
Water or corrosion in the connector at the gearbox

symptoms: Start system warning in the cluster

P08B0.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B0.summary: P08B0 reports that the signal of neutral position sensor B on a manual gearbox is above its upper electrical limit. With a three-wire Hall sensor this usually points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage.

causes.text: Signal or ground wire pulled apart, harness too short
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Sensor B open internally

symptoms: Start-stop does not switch the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster
Fault may come and go with gear changes

P08B1.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B1.summary: Neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel on a manual gearbox's shift shaft, delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments. No manufacturer documents P08B1 publicly.

causes.text: Wire strained or partly broken by gearbox movement
Loose or fretting connector contact
Sensor B with intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Start-stop works only now and then
Fault returns after clearing without visible cause

P08B2.title: Neutral Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B2.summary: On a manual gearbox with two neutral sensors or two channels, the engine module compares A and B. P08B2 means they disagree: one reports neutral, the other a gear, or their values differ beyond a calibrated limit, while each may look fine electrically.

causes.text: One of the two neutral sensors drifting or faulty
Magnet on the shift shaft shifted or sensor misaligned after repair
Neutral position not relearned after component replacement

symptoms: Start system warning in the cluster
Gear indicator may be blank or wrong

P08B3.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Not Learned
P08B3.summary: Analog neutral sensors report a position value, and the control module must learn which value means neutral to cover part and fitting tolerances. P08B3 says no valid learned value exists for sensor B, typically after replacing the sensor, gearbox or module, after a software update, or after an aborted learn.

causes.text: Learn procedure not done after sensor, gearbox or module replacement
Learn run aborted, lever unsteady or linkage misadjusted
Learned values erased by software update or module reset
Sensor mounted outside the learnable range or faulty

symptoms: Appears right after a repair or software update

P08B4.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08B4.summary: Some manual cars read the clutch pedal with two independent sensors so a single failure can be detected; Ford's 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary describes such a dual PWM layout. Sensor B is the second channel.

causes.text: Loose connector or broken wire on the sensor B channel
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor B (often a shared housing with sensor A)
Missing supply or ground for sensor B
Faulty sensor B input in the engine control module

symptoms: Correlation code P08B9 may be stored as well

P08B5.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08B5.summary: P08B5 covers a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal lies within its electrical limits but is implausible on its own, for example stuck at one value while the pedal moves or not matching the driving state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Sensor B drifting or worn so its value no longer follows pedal travel
Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket
Corrosion adding resistance in the sensor B circuit

P08B6.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08B6.summary: P08B6 means the signal of the second clutch pedal sensor has dropped below its valid range. Ford lists it in the 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary under dual PWM clutch sensors, together with P08A9/P08AA for sensor A, P08B7 for sensor B high and P08B9 for the A/B comparison; monitoring runs continuously and needs less than one second to flag a fault.

causes.text: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Lost supply voltage to sensor B (open wire, connector off)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

symptoms: P08B9 correlation code may set alongside

P08B7.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B7.summary: P08B7 is set when the second clutch pedal sensor reports a value above its valid range. Ford uses it on vehicles with two PWM clutch pedal sensors, as listed in its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary next to P08B6 (sensor B low), P08A9/P08AA (sensor A) and P08B9 (A/B correlation); the check is continuous and decides within one second.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B, leaving the input at its pull-up level
Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage source
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

symptoms: Sensor B reading pinned at maximum in scan tool data

P08B8.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B8.summary: P08B8 is intended for a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal drops out briefly or jumps without staying out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or worn terminals in the sensor B connector
Wire fatiguing where the harness flexes with pedal movement
Sensor B producing glitches internally

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes

P08B9.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B9.summary: P08B9 is stored when two independent measurements of the clutch pedal disagree. Ford uses it in two ways per its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary: with dual PWM sensors it compares sensor A with sensor B and decides within a second; with a single analog sensor plus two clutch switches it covers an in-range rationality fault or any switch-related mismatch, the switch part being judged over about 40 clutch cycles at different speeds.

causes.text: One of the two sensors drifting or worn so the channels no longer agree
Sticking or misadjusted clutch switch on systems with one sensor plus switches
Corroded connector or wiring adding resistance to one channel
Sensor assembly or pedal stop misaligned after repairs

P08BA.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L
P08BA.summary: Base code for the twelfth pressure control solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve carries the letter L is up to the manufacturer. Toyota is the one documented user: bulletin T-SB-0094-24 for the 2024 Tacoma and Tacoma Hybrid lists it as P08BA71, actuator stuck, next to the stuck faults of solenoids A, C, D, G and H and a torque converter clutch stuck off.

causes.text: Solenoid or its control valve sticking inside the valve body
Internal transmission fault from production, debris spreading through the hydraulics
Contaminated or wrong transmission fluid
Connector or harness fault at the solenoid

symptoms: Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08BB.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Performance/Stuck Off
P08BB.summary: Set when pressure control solenoid L is commanded but the pressure or shift element it serves does not respond, i.e. the valve acts as if it were stuck in its off state.

causes.text: Valve spool held closed by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Leaking seal or circuit downstream of the valve

P08BC.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Stuck On
P08BC.summary: Set when pressure control solenoid L keeps applying pressure although the control module has commanded it off, so the element it feeds stays loaded. No manufacturer publishes this code.

causes.text: Valve spool held open by debris
Worn bore in the valve body letting pressure through
Output stage or wiring keeping the solenoid energised

symptoms: Harsh engagement or binding during shifts
Transmission locked in a fallback gear

P08BD.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Electrical
P08BD.summary: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid L that the module does not break down further into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly; Toyota, the one known user of letter L, has only published the stuck fault P08BA71.

causes.text: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Corroded connector or damaged internal harness
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module

P08BE.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Intermittent
P08BE.summary: Reports a fault of pressure control solenoid L that comes and goes, typically a circuit that drops out briefly or a valve response that is only occasionally implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and in earlier packages the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids also proved unused.

causes.text: Loose or spread terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Chafed wire touching ground intermittently
Debris making the valve hang only now and then

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes

P08BF.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit/Open
P08BF.summary: Points to an open control circuit of pressure control solenoid L: the module sees no load where the coil should be. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only known user of letter L, has published just P08BA71.

causes.text: Connector loose, unplugged or corroded
Broken wire in the internal or external harness
Solenoid coil burnt open

P08C0.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C0.summary: Set when the control circuit of pressure control solenoid L is electrically intact but its behaviour is implausible, for example the current through the coil does not match the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71.

causes.text: Coil resistance out of specification
High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module

P08C1.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08C1.summary: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too low, usually a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid or moisture in the connector

P08C2.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08C2.summary: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too high, typically a short to battery voltage or to a neighbouring output. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between adjacent solenoid wires in the internal harness
Defective output stage in the transmission control module

P08C3.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M
P08C3.summary: Base code for the thirteenth pressure control solenoid; the letter is assigned by the manufacturer. GM uses letter M in the Tremec eight-speed dual clutch of the Corvette (RPO M1L/M1M): its 2023–2025 TCM tables name the part synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft, while valves 2 to 5 report under P27B9 onwards.

causes.text: Valve sticking from debris in the valve body
Fault in the solenoid wiring or connector
Worn or failed solenoid

symptoms: Rough or missing shifts in odd gears

P08C4.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Performance/Stuck Off
P08C4.summary: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft, is hydraulically stuck off. The test runs inside a synchronizer recovery or integrity routine, started after a shift-related fault or when the stored gear does not match the sensed gears at start-up: the shift rods are moved slightly, and if a rod travels 100 µm or less where the valve should move it, a current profile check of the valve has to fail three times before the fault is confirmed.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Low system pressure or fluid level

symptoms: Odd gears not engaged or engaged late

P08C5.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Stuck On
P08C5.summary: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, serving the odd-gear shaft, keeps pressure on although it is commanded off. The check runs whenever the selector pilot valve changes position: a valve stuck on keeps pushing a shift rod, so after the switch the pressure is routed elsewhere.

causes.text: Valve held open by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Worn valve bore in the control valve body

symptoms: Clunks or unwanted gear engagement on the odd shaft

P08C6.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Electrical
P08C6.summary: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid M without a finer split into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Damaged connector or internal harness
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P08C7.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Intermittent
P08C7.summary: Reports an on-and-off fault of pressure control solenoid M, such as brief circuit dropouts or occasional implausible responses.
