No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, lists no intermittent code for it, and earlier packages found the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids unused as well.

causes.text: Loose terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Chafed wire with intermittent contact
Debris causing occasional valve hang-ups

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes

P08C8.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit/Open
P08C8.summary: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for an open circuit at synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft. The open-load test runs with the low-side driver switched off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin to battery voltage, so if the driver chip can hold it between about 1.7 and 3 V (each ±0.5 V) with a very small current, the circuit is considered open.

causes.text: Connector at the control valve body loose or corroded
Broken wire in the internal harness
Solenoid coil open

P08C9.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C9.summary: Meant for a control circuit of pressure control solenoid M that is not open or shorted but behaves implausibly, for instance a coil current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Coil resistance out of specification
High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module

P08CA.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Low
P08CA.summary: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for a short to ground in the circuit of synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft. The test runs while the low-side driver is switched on: the sense pin should then sit at a defined level, and if the driver chip reports it below about 1.7 V (±0.5 V), a ground short is assumed.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid in the transmission connector

P08CB.title: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit High
P08CB.summary: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for synchronizer actuation valve 1 (odd-gear shaft) in two situations. First, a short to battery voltage: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7, 0.9 or 1.1 V (±0.1 V), depending on supply voltage, counts as a shorted load, confirmed after 150 ms.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short to an adjacent solenoid wire in the internal harness
Defective driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Code may appear right after starting

P08CC.title: Shift Solenoid J
P08CC.summary: Base code for the tenth on/off shift solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve gets the letter J is decided by the manufacturer. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Shift solenoid J faulty (coil or valve)
Contaminated or degraded transmission fluid restricting the valve
Connector or harness fault between TCM and solenoid
Transmission control module output fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08CD.title: Shift Solenoid J Performance/Stuck Off
P08CD.summary: Set when shift solenoid J is switched on but the gear or clutch it controls does not respond, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the off position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Worn clutch pack or leaking seal in the circuit served by the valve
Solenoid coil too weak to move the valve

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during or after a shift
A gear is missing or skipped
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08CE.title: Shift Solenoid J Stuck On
P08CE.summary: Set when shift solenoid J is switched off but its clutch or shift valve stays applied, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its on position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the applied position by debris or varnish
Contaminated transmission fluid after internal wear
Control circuit shorted so the solenoid stays energised
TCM output driver does not switch off

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement, possible binding feel

P08CF.title: Shift Solenoid J Electrical
P08CF.summary: General electrical fault of shift solenoid J, used when a manufacturer does not split the circuit fault into open, low, high or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid coil open or shorted internally
Damaged harness, corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Fault in the internal transmission harness or solenoid body
TCM output driver fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear

P08D0.title: Shift Solenoid J Intermittent
P08D0.summary: Reserved for a shift solenoid J fault that comes and goes instead of being present continuously, typically brief circuit dropouts or erratic valve response. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the intermittent codes of the earlier shift solenoids, such as P0754 for solenoid A, are not used in the GM and Ford sources checked either; those makers report dropouts through their open, short or functional codes.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector losing contact under vibration or heat
Chafed harness with intermittent short or break
Valve sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid
Solenoid coil failing only when hot

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart

P08D1.title: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08D1.summary: Set when the control circuit of shift solenoid J is electrically intact but its measured values, usually solenoid current or driver feedback, lie outside the expected window for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector pins or internal harness
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM or solenoid feed
Faulty current sensing in the TCM output stage

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08D2.title: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Low
P08D2.summary: Set when the TCM sees too little voltage on the control line of shift solenoid J, typically because the line or the coil is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J would be a tenth on/off valve, which none of the known transmission sources assigns.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Solenoid coil with internal short
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the TCM

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08D3.title: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit High
P08D3.summary: Logged when the control line of shift solenoid J reads higher than the commanded state allows, pointing to a short to battery voltage or, on some designs, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying conductor
Open solenoid coil (on systems that report opens as high)
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08D4.title: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit/Open
P08D4.summary: Dedicated code for an open control circuit of shift solenoid J: the TCM drives the valve but no current flows through wire, connector or coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Broken control wire or loose terminal
Burnt-out solenoid coil
Transmission connector not fully seated after service

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
One gear missing or transmission stuck in one gear

P08D5.title: Shift Solenoid K
P08D5.summary: Base code for shift solenoid K, the eleventh on/off shift valve in SAE's lettering. Which valve carries the letter is up to the manufacturer, and none documents K publicly: Ford's gasoline OBD summary lists shift solenoids only up to SS E, Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG for the Genesis 8-speed ends at shift control solenoid F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 tables contain no code of the K group.

causes.text: Shift solenoid K faulty (coil or valve)
Harness or connector fault between TCM and solenoid
Degraded or contaminated transmission fluid
TCM output fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08D6.title: Shift Solenoid K Performance/Stuck Off
P08D6.summary: Indicates that shift solenoid K was commanded on but the gear or clutch behind it never engaged, as if the valve stayed in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Valve or shift spool held in rest position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak line pressure
Leaking seal or worn clutch pack in the circuit fed by the valve

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during shifts
A gear is skipped or missing

P08D7.title: Shift Solenoid K Stuck On
P08D7.summary: Stored when shift solenoid K is switched off but the circuit it feeds stays pressurised, so a clutch remains applied. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Valve or shift spool jammed in applied position
Metal debris in the fluid after internal wear
TCM output or shorted wire keeps the solenoid energised

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08D8.title: Shift Solenoid K Electrical
P08D8.summary: Collective electrical fault for shift solenoid K, used by makers that do not split circuit faults into low, high, open or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Damaged harness or corroded connector
TCM output driver fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear

P08D9.title: Shift Solenoid K Intermittent
P08D9.summary: Meant for a shift solenoid K fault that appears and vanishes, such as a connector losing contact over bumps or a coil dropping out when hot. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the sources checked even uses the intermittent code of solenoid A, P0754; GM and Ford catch brief interruptions with their open, short and functional codes instead.

causes.text: Loose or fretted terminal in the transmission connector
Chafed wire that touches only under vibration
Solenoid coil dropping out at high fluid temperature

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart

P08DA.title: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08DA.summary: Points to a control circuit of shift solenoid K that is neither open nor shorted, yet whose measured values, usually coil current, do not fit the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is not used in the GM or Ford sources either.

causes.text: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Corroded or loose pins adding resistance
TCM output stage no longer delivers correct current

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08DB.title: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Low
P08DB.summary: The TCM's output stage reports a voltage on the shift solenoid K control circuit below what the commanded state requires, the classic sign of a control wire rubbing through to ground or a coil with an internal short. No manufacturer documents this K code publicly.

causes.text: Control wire rubbed through to ground
Internally shorted solenoid coil
TCM output stage fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission stays in a limp-home gear
Reduced acceleration due to missing gears

P08DC.title: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit High
P08DC.summary: The monitored control line of shift solenoid K sits closer to supply voltage than it should, for instance because it touches a powered wire or, depending on the driver design, because the coil is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Control wire touching a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM low-side driver no longer pulls the line down

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08DD.title: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit/Open
P08DD.summary: Signals that the control circuit of shift solenoid K is open, so commanding the valve produces no current: a broken wire, a pushed-out terminal, a burnt coil or a failed internal transmission harness. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Broken wire or pushed-out terminal
Failed internal transmission harness
Burnt-out solenoid coil

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08DE.title: Shift Solenoid L
P08DE.summary: Base code for shift solenoid L, which in SAE's lettering would be the twelfth on/off shift valve of an automatic transmission. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Shift solenoid L faulty
Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit
Debris in the valve body affecting the valve

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08DF.title: Shift Solenoid L Performance/Stuck Off
P08DF.summary: Functional fault of shift solenoid L: the TCM switches the valve on, but speed sensor data show that the intended clutch did not take up, so the valve acts as if stuck off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Shift spool jammed by debris
Low line pressure or low fluid level
Leak in the clutch circuit fed by the valve

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08E0.title: Shift Solenoid L Stuck On
P08E0.summary: Functional fault of shift solenoid L in the opposite direction: although switched off, the valve keeps its circuit applied, leaving engaged a clutch that should be released. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Shift spool seized in applied position
Contaminated fluid after clutch or bearing wear
TCM output stage does not switch off

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08E1.title: Shift Solenoid L Electrical
P08E1.summary: General electrical malfunction of shift solenoid L, intended for transmissions whose TCM does not distinguish or separately report low, high and open circuit faults. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid L coil failed electrically
Harness or connector damage on the solenoid circuit
TCM output fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08E2.title: Shift Solenoid L Intermittent
P08E2.summary: Reserved for an unstable fault of shift solenoid L that is detected, disappears and may return, typically from a loose terminal, a chafed wire that only touches under vibration or a heat-sensitive coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose terminal or poor pin tension in the connector
Insulation chafed at a bracket or edge
Coil that fails intermittently when hot

symptoms: Limp mode that disappears after restart

P08E3.title: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08E3.summary: Plausibility fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L: the circuit is not open or shorted, but voltage or current during actuation is implausible for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the matching code for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise absent from the GM and Ford documents checked.

causes.text: Coil resistance drifting with temperature
Corroded pins adding resistance
TCM output stage losing drive strength

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08E4.title: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08E4.summary: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L. Usually it means a short to ground on the control wire, less often a coil with shorted windings that pulls the voltage down.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Coil with shorted windings
Fluid or moisture in the connector creating a path to ground

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission locked in a substitute gear

P08E5.title: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08E5.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L, set when the line shows battery voltage or a floating high level while the TCM expects otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM output stage fault

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P08E6.title: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit/Open
P08E6.summary: Open circuit in the control path of shift solenoid L: harness, connector, internal transmission wiring or the coil itself no longer carry current, so the valve cannot be energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Break in the harness or internal transmission wiring
Open solenoid coil
Connector unlatched or terminal backed out

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear range missing or fixed gear

P08E7.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit
P08E7.summary: Covers the enable line with which a drive motor control module activates the actuator of a clutch that couples or uncouples electric drive motor A from the wheels. The code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that line, typically an open circuit or an implausible state.

causes.text: Enable wire open or connector at the clutch actuator not seated
Internal electronics fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Corroded or water-damaged connector near the drive unit
Faulty enable driver in the drive motor control module

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive or assist from the affected axle

P08E8.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit Low
P08E8.summary: Set when the voltage on the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator stays below the expected range, usually because the wire or the actuator input is shorted to ground. The control module can then no longer switch the actuator on, so the clutch cannot be engaged or released on command.

causes.text: Enable wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short at the actuator enable input
Water ingress in the actuator connector
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Reduced performance, no electric launch or all-wheel drive

P08E9.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit High
P08E9.summary: Set when the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator reads higher than it should, for example because it is shorted to a supply voltage or the line floats due to an open ground. The module then cannot reliably switch the actuator off or confirm its state.

causes.text: Enable wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open ground or reference circuit of the actuator
Internal fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive on the affected axle switched off
Possible clunk when the system tries to couple the motor

P08EA.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit
P08EA.summary: Concerns the sensor or switch that reports where the pawl of the drive motor A disconnect clutch sits, i.e. whether the form-locking clutch is engaged or released.

causes.text: Faulty disconnect clutch position switch or sensor
Open signal or reference wire to the position switch
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Faulty input stage in the drive motor control module

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive or all-wheel drive unavailable

P08EB.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit Low
P08EB.summary: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays below its valid range, which points to a short to ground in the signal wire, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that has failed low. The module then cannot tell whether the pawl has engaged.

causes.text: Position signal wire shorted to ground
Missing supply voltage to the position switch
Position switch or sensor failed low

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Hybrid modes with electric assist not selectable

P08EC.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit High
P08EC.summary: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays above its valid range. Typical reasons are an open signal or ground wire, which lets the input float high, or a short to a supply voltage.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire of the position switch
Signal wire shorted to a supply circuit
Position switch or sensor failed high

symptoms: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive from the affected axle
All-wheel drive or electric launch missing

P08ED.title: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Performance
P08ED.summary: A plausibility fault: the pawl position reported for the drive motor A disconnect clutch does not match what the control module commanded, or the clutch did not reach the expected position, even though the circuit itself is electrically intact. GM documents the code for the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, whose front electric drive unit uses a clutch pawl and a disconnect clutch actuator; bulletin 24-NA-165 says it is stored in the drive motor control module, lights the MIL and is usually caused by the disconnect clutch switch, which is replaced as an external part.

causes.text: Faulty drive motor disconnect clutch switch (GM E-Ray bulletin)
Disconnect clutch actuator not moving the pawl fully
Worn or binding pawl or clutch teeth inside the drive unit

symptoms: Electric front-axle drive unavailable or intermittent

P0900.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit/Open
P0900.summary: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator that opens and closes clutch A in an automated or dual-clutch transmission. The code sets when the module detects an open circuit, so it cannot energise the actuator.

causes.text: Failed clutch A actuator motor (open winding or internal fault)
Loose connector or broken wire between TCM and actuator
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

symptoms: Erratic or missed shifts, vibration on take-off
Transmission in limp mode, possibly no drive

P0901.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0901.summary: Set when the clutch A actuator circuit is electrically present but does not behave as expected, for instance when the measured current or response deviates too far from the target. Usage differs by maker.

causes.text: Weak or worn clutch A actuator motor (dual-clutch units)
High resistance in the transmission harness or sub-harness
TCM fault or outdated TCM software

symptoms: Shudder, harsh engagement or missed shifts
Failsafe mode with a held gear

P0902.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Low
P0902.summary: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a low state, in practice a short to ground on a motor or control line. Ford defines it exactly this way for the DPS6 PowerShift transmission: the TCM tests the three-phase clutch A motor for open circuit (P0900), short to ground (P0902) and short to power (P0903), next to hall sensor and sequence checks.

causes.text: Clutch A actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground

symptoms: No drive or only some gears available

P0903.title: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit High
P0903.summary: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a high state, meaning a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford names P0903 as the short-to-power test of the clutch A motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox of the Fiesta and Focus, part of a set with P0900 for an open circuit and P0902 for a short to ground.

causes.text: Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Internal fault in the clutch A actuator motor
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

symptoms: Limp mode, gears missing or no drive

P0904.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A
P0904.summary: Circuit A of the gate select position sensor tells the control module of an automated manual gearbox where the shift mechanism stands in the select direction, i.e. which gate (for example 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or reverse) is lined up.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the gate select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gate select position sensor (often integrated in the shift and select actuator)
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in one gear
Neutral indicator flashes or vehicle will not pull away

P0905.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0905.summary: Plausibility fault of the gate select position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The signal is electrically within limits, but it does not fit what the control module expects: typical checks compare the measured select travel with the learned gate positions and the commanded target gate.

causes.text: Worn or drifting gate select sensor, main and redundant tracks disagree
High resistance at connector pins distorting the sensor voltage
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or TCM replacement
Loose or displaced magnet or sensor mounting on the select shaft

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral or refuses certain gears
Slow or jerky gear changes in fallback mode

P0906.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Low
P0906.summary: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Common causes are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing sensor supply, or an internal sensor defect; with many sensor designs a broken signal wire also reads low.

causes.text: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard

P0907.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A High
P0907.summary: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Typical causes are a short of the signal line to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, a broken sensor ground, or an internal sensor fault.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0908.title: Gate Select Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0908.summary: Points to a gate select position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox, too briefly or too irregularly for a steady low or high fault. Loose terminals, a damaged harness that moves with the engine, or moisture in the connector at the shift and select actuator are the usual reasons.

causes.text: Loose or spread terminals at the sensor or actuator connector
Harness damage that only opens or shorts under engine movement
Moisture or corrosion in the connector near the gearbox

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional drop to neutral or refused shift
Fault often disappears after restarting the engine

P0909.title: Gate Select Control Error
P0909.summary: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox commands the select actuator to a new gate, but the measured select position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits may be electrically fine; the fault lies in the closed loop as a whole.

causes.text: Stiff or jammed select shaft, shift head or internal selector mechanism
Worn select motor (brushes, gears) with too little force
Select sensor offset or gate positions not relearned
Weak battery or voltage drop on the actuator supply

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Certain gears cannot be engaged or gearbox stays in neutral
Clicking or whirring from the actuator without a gear change

P090A.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit/Open
P090A.summary: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator for clutch B, the second clutch of a dual-clutch transmission, and sets when the module finds an open circuit. Ford uses it on the DPS6 PowerShift of the Fiesta and Focus: the clutch B electric motor is tested for driver faults (P087A), hall sensor faults (P087B), sequence errors (P087E), an open circuit (P090A), a short to ground (P090C) and a short to power (P090D).

causes.text: Failed clutch B actuator motor
Loose connector or broken wire to the clutch B motor
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM

symptoms: Even gears or reverse missing, erratic shifts

P090B.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Performance
P090B.summary: Set when the clutch B actuator circuit is electrically connected but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example too slowly or with an unexpected current draw. Ford uses P090B on the DPS6 PowerShift transmission.

causes.text: Worn or sluggish clutch B actuator motor
TCM fault (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Damaged harness between TCM and clutch B motor

symptoms: Shudder or slipping in even gears and reverse
Delayed or missed shifts, possible limp mode

P090C.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Low
P090C.summary: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a low state, which on the documented application means a short to ground. Ford defines P090C as the short-to-ground check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox, paired with P090A for an open circuit and P090D for a short to power.

causes.text: Clutch B actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground

P090D.title: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit High
P090D.summary: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a high state, i.e. a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage.

causes.text: Failed clutch B actuator motor (Ford program 20B23)
Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Faulty motor driver in the TCM

symptoms: Erratic or missed shifts and vibration

P0910.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit/Open
P0910.summary: Concerns the drive circuit of the gate select actuator, the motor or valve that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox sideways from gate to gate. The code sets when the control module finds this output open or electrically faulty, for example when no current flows although the driver stage is switched on.

causes.text: Open winding or worn brushes in the select motor
Broken actuator wire or terminal pushed out of the connector
Corroded actuator connector near the gearbox
Faulty actuator driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox cannot change between gates, only some gears available
Vehicle may stay in neutral and not drive off

P0911.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0911.summary: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but the current, voltage or response measured on it does not fit the command, for example a current that is too high or too low for the requested movement.

causes.text: Worn select motor drawing abnormal current
Stiff select mechanism overloading the actuator
High resistance in actuator wiring or connector

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow, hesitant or aborted gear changes
Gearbox enters fallback mode with limited gears

P0912.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit Low
P0912.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state, which usually means a short to ground on a motor or control line, or an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the affected output off to protect the driver stage.

causes.text: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the select motor, e.g. from brush debris
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gate change possible, gearbox stays in current gear or neutral

P0913.title: Gate Select Actuator Circuit High
P0913.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Usual causes are a short of a motor or control line to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on the circuit design an open load can also read high.

causes.text: Actuator wire shorted to battery voltage
Open motor winding read as high voltage by the driver stage
Driver stage in the transmission control module stuck on

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops changing gates or holds one gear
Actuator may run noisily or get hot

P0914.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A
P0914.summary: Circuit A of the gear shift position sensor reports how far the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox has moved in the shift direction, i.e. whether a gear is engaged, in neutral or in between.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gear shift position sensor
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stops shifting or stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0915.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0915.summary: Plausibility fault of the gear shift position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, but the reading does not fit: the signal does not change while the shift actuator moves, or the engaged position does not match the learned gear positions.

causes.text: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, redundant tracks disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rod
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or TCM replacement
High resistance at connector pins distorting the signal

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox drops to neutral while driving
Gears refused or engaged only after a delay

P0916.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Low
P0916.summary: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. A short to ground on the signal line, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor defect are the usual causes; depending on the sensor design a broken signal wire reads low as well.

causes.text: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
No gear changes possible or gearbox stays in neutral
Engine may not start because neutral cannot be confirmed

P0917.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A High
P0917.summary: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor itself may be faulty.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Warning message about the transmission on the dashboard

P0918.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0918.summary: Flags a gear shift position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox. The module sees implausible steps or brief losses that are too short or too irregular for a lasting low or high fault.

causes.text: Connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit losing contact under vibration
Chafed or partially broken sensor wire near the gearbox
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Shift position sensor with an internal contact or track fault

symptoms: Gear changes abort now and then or the gearbox drops to neutral
Fault often appears on rough roads or in wet weather

P0919.title: Gear Shift Position Control Error
P0919.summary: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox drives the shift actuator towards a gear, but the measured shift position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits can be electrically intact; the fault concerns the closed loop as a whole.

causes.text: Stiff or jammed shift rail, shift fork or synchroniser
Worn shift motor or leaking shift cylinder that no longer delivers full force
Low pressure in the hydraulic supply on hydraulically actuated units
Shift positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement

symptoms: Gear does not engage or engages only after a delay
Gearbox remains in neutral or locks in one gear

P091A.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B
P091A.summary: Circuit B is a second channel reporting the shift position of an automated manual gearbox, for instance a redundant sensor track or a separate sensor on another shift rail. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that matches none of the more specific B variants.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at the shift position sensor
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit B
Faulty shift position sensor B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral

P091B.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P091B.summary: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit B in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, yet the value does not fit: it disagrees with circuit A, does not change while the shift actuator moves, or does not match the learned gear positions.

causes.text: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, channels A and B disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

symptoms: Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P091C.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Low
P091C.summary: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the signal line is shorted to ground, the sensor supply is missing, or the sensor has failed internally.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to ground
Open or shorted sensor supply line
Faulty shift position sensor B

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed

P091D.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit B High
P091D.summary: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor may be faulty.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground
Faulty shift position sensor B

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Restricted gear changes or a held gear
Engine start may be blocked if neutral cannot be confirmed

P0920.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit/Open
P0920.summary: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the forward shift direction. Depending on design this is one of two solenoid valves on a double-acting shift cylinder or one rotation direction of an electric shift motor.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Some gears cannot be selected, the gearbox skips them or stays in neutral
Vehicle may only move off in a limited set of gears

P0921.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0921.summary: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting movement do not fit the command, for example a current that is too high for the requested stroke or a shift position that hardly changes.

causes.text: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

symptoms: Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P0922.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Low
P0922.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually points to a short to ground on a valve or motor line, or to an internal short in the actuator.

causes.text: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

symptoms: Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear

P0923.title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit High
P0923.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Typical reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on circuit design an open load can also read high.

causes.text: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

symptoms: Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally

P0924.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit/Open
P0924.summary: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the reverse shift direction, i.e. opposite to the forward actuator.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Some gears cannot be selected or the gearbox stays in neutral
Gear changes out of the current gear may fail

P0925.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0925.summary: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the actuator that moves the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting shift movement do not match the command.

causes.text: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units

symptoms: Slow, harsh or aborted gear changes in one direction
Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P0926.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Low
P0926.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the one moving the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction, shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually means a valve or motor line shorted to ground or an internal short in the actuator; the module often switches the output off to protect itself.

causes.text: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector

symptoms: Certain gears can no longer be engaged
Gearbox may stay in neutral or hold one gear

P0927.title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit High
P0927.summary: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Common reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage or a driver stage that no longer switches off; on some circuit designs an open load also reads high.

causes.text: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs

symptoms: Gearbox locks in one gear or refuses to shift
Possible grinding when a gear is pushed unintentionally

P0928.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A/Open
P0928.summary: The module that drives the shift lock (brake transmission shift interlock, BTSI) sees no continuity on control circuit A, so it cannot reliably release the selector from Park. FCA/Chrysler uses the code as P0928-00 BTSI Control: bulletin 08-072-14 (2013-14 Ram 1500, 2014 Durango with 8-speed) and 21-034-15 (2015 Chrysler 300 rotary shifter) name it when the selector will not leave Park or the knob turns without the brake applied; the cure there is a new electronic shifter.

causes.text: Internal fault in the electronic shifter module, often logged together with P0607 (documented by FCA)
Shift lock solenoid coil open
Broken wire, poorly crimped or pushed-out terminal on the shift lock circuit

symptoms: Selector lever will not move out of Park even with the brake pressed
Problem may disappear after the ignition is switched off and the modules go to sleep
Rotary or electronic shifter can be moved without the brake applied
Shift position flashes or a message asks to return the selector to Park

P0929.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0929.summary: Set when the shift lock actuator on circuit A is electrically present but does not respond as commanded, for example it fails to reach the locked or released position. Ford stores it in the gear shift module (GSM): SSM 51057 and 53039 list P0929:77 (commanded position not reachable) on Mach-E, Escape, Bronco Sport, Maverick and Transit, fixed by GSM software or replacement; TSB 25-2045 adds P0929:00, :07 and :9A on 2021-24 F-150 together with a selector that will not leave or enter Park, and checks pin 3 of connector C211.

causes.text: Gear shift module software that misjudges the actuator position (Ford reprogramming bulletins)
Worn or binding lock actuator inside the shifter assembly
Poor pin fit or damaged pin at the shifter connector

symptoms: Wrench or transmission warning lamp on
Selector will not leave Park or will not go back into Park
Clicking from the shifter or a selector that does not stow or unstow

P092A.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B/Open
P092A.summary: Reports an open on control circuit B of the shift lock. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none says which lock is B.

causes.text: Broken wire or loose terminal on circuit B at the shifter
Open coil in the second lock solenoid
Shifter connector not fully seated after console work

symptoms: Selector lever locked in one position although the brake is pressed
Lock no longer engages, lever moves freely without brake
Warning message about the shifter or transmission

P092B.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P092B.summary: Set when the actuator on shift lock circuit B is wired correctly but does not reach or report the commanded lock or release state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Lock pin or actuator binding inside the shifter assembly
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator response
Weak battery or poor supply leaving the solenoid too little force

symptoms: Lever releases late or only after several tries
Lever stays locked in one position
Transmission or wrench warning lamp on

P092C.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Low
P092C.summary: The voltage on shift lock control circuit B is lower than expected, usually because the wire or the solenoid has a path to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or names the lock behind circuit B.

causes.text: Circuit B wire chafed to ground near the shifter
Shorted turns in the second lock solenoid
Liquid spilled into the shifter causing leakage to ground

symptoms: Lever locked in a position despite brake applied
Lock does not engage, lever moves without brake

P092D.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B High
P092D.summary: The module sees a higher voltage on shift lock circuit B than the commanded state allows, such as a short to supply or, with a low-side driver, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Circuit B wire shorted to a supply voltage
Poor crimp or loose terminal at the second lock solenoid
Open coil in the second lock solenoid

symptoms: Lever will not release from its locked position
Warning message about the shifter or transmission

P0930.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Low
P0930.summary: The voltage on control circuit A of the shift lock solenoid stays below the expected level, typically a short to ground or a driver output pulled low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Shift lock control wire chafed through to ground in the console or under the carpet
Shorted turns in the shift lock solenoid coil
Spilled liquid in the shifter area causing leakage to ground

symptoms: Selector lever stuck in Park although the brake is pressed
Selector can be moved out of Park without pressing the brake
Shift lock override slot needed to move the lever

P0931.title: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A High
P0931.summary: The control module reads a voltage on shift lock circuit A that is higher than the commanded state allows. FCA documents the code directly: in recall 16V-249 the Jefferson North plant found 2016 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles with active or stored P0931-00 whose selector would not release from Park.

causes.text: Poorly crimped or loose terminal on the shift lock solenoid harness (FCA recall 16V-249)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open shift lock solenoid coil seen as high voltage by a low-side driver

symptoms: Selector lever will not release from Park
Lever may lock in Park or Neutral unexpectedly after stopping
Fault comes and goes with vibration or temperature

P0932.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0932.summary: General electrical fault in the circuit of the sensor that reports hydraulic pressure in the gearbox, usually line pressure in an automatic or system pressure in an automated manual or dual-clutch unit. The module sees a signal it cannot use at all, without a clear low or high pattern.

causes.text: Fault in the solenoid pack or valve body module that carries the pressure sensor (open solenoid, internal lead frame)
Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector terminals
5 V reference or sensor ground interrupted
Transmission or powertrain control module fault

symptoms: Warning light or transmission warning on
Harsh engagements and firm shifts from maximum line pressure
Possible limp mode with limited gears

P0933.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0933.summary: The pressure reading is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state. Chrysler RFE, RLE and TES transmissions set it when measured line pressure is more than 25 psi (172 kPa) above the commanded value while staying below the highest pressure ever used in that gear; Sonnax notes that a maximum-pressure condition from an open pressure control solenoid circuit can trigger it and mislead toward the sensor.

causes.text: Open circuit or fault in the line pressure control solenoid causing real excess pressure
Pressure sensor drifting or reading offset
Worn or sticking valves in the valve body
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid

symptoms: Harsh or firm engagements and shifts
Shift quality does not adapt and may stay rough

P0934.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0934.summary: The pressure sensor signal sits below its valid window. Chrysler RFE transmissions feed the line pressure sensor with a 5 V reference and expect 0.35 to 4.75 V; P0934 sets when the signal stays at or below 0.35 V for 0.18 s, monitored continuously with the engine running.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted
Pressure sensor or the solenoid pack carrying it failed
Control module fault

symptoms: Harsh shifts due to default maximum pressure

P0935.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0935.summary: The pressure sensor signal sits above its valid window. On Chrysler RFE transmissions the line pressure sensor normally reads between 0.35 and 4.75 V; P0935 sets when the signal stays at or above 4.75 V for 0.18 s with the engine running.

causes.text: Sensor ground open or poor terminal contact
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor or solenoid pack failed internally
Control module fault

P0936.title: Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0936.summary: The hydraulic pressure signal drops out or jumps for short periods, too briefly or irregularly for a lasting low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector
Chafed harness making intermittent contact
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault

P0937.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0937.summary: General electrical fault in the circuit of the temperature sensor for the hydraulic fluid of an automated gearbox, without a clear low or high pattern. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Connector at the temperature sensor loose, corroded or oil-soaked
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox or cooler lines
Temperature sensor failed

symptoms: Rougher shifts or clutch engagement, especially when cold

P0938.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0938.summary: By J2012 wording the hydraulic oil temperature reading is electrically valid but implausible, for example frozen, rising too slowly after a cold start or disagreeing with other temperature values. Ferrari uses P0938 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, but describes it in its bulletin as no signal, an electrical fault rather than a plausibility check; the code is read in the NCR gearbox ECU.

causes.text: Temperature sensor drifting or reacting sluggishly
Signal lost through connector or wiring fault (as in Ferrari's no-signal case)
Real temperature anomaly from a cooler or thermostat fault

symptoms: Shift and clutch quality inconsistent with operating temperature

P0939.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0939.summary: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits below its valid window. With the usual NTC thermistor, a low voltage corresponds to an implausibly hot reading and typically comes from a signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor shorted internally.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Temperature sensor shorted internally
Control module input fault

symptoms: Reduced performance or altered shift behaviour

P093A.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit/Open
P093A.summary: The control circuit of the solenoid that opens or locks a hydraulic accumulator in the gearbox is open. Such accumulators store pressurised fluid, for example to keep clutches applied during engine stop-start, as GM's patents on a stop-start accumulator and an accumulator with solenoid valve describe.

causes.text: Accumulator solenoid coil open
Connector unplugged or wire broken between module and solenoid
Fault in the internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Jolt or slip when driving off after an engine restart

P093B.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit Low
P093B.summary: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads low, usually a control wire shorted to ground or a coil with very low resistance. No manufacturer documents P093B publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid control wire shorted to ground
Solenoid coil shorted internally
Output driver in the control module failed

P093C.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Circuit High
P093C.summary: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads high, typically a control wire shorted to battery voltage so the driver cannot switch the valve as commanded. No manufacturer documents P093C publicly.

causes.text: Solenoid control wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Jolt when pulling away after a restart

P093D.title: Hydraulic Accumulator Solenoid Performance
P093D.summary: The accumulator solenoid circuit is electrically sound, but the accumulator system does not deliver the expected hydraulic result. No manufacturer documents P093D publicly.

causes.text: Accumulator solenoid stuck open (drains) or closed (no fill)
Accumulator piston or bore leaking
Leakage at clutch seals or a worn valve body
Missing or misplaced check ball after a rebuild

symptoms: Lurch or bang when the engine restarts
Firm shifts with adaptive learning frozen

P0940.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0940.summary: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits above its valid window. With an NTC thermistor this matches an extremely cold reading, typically from an open circuit, an unplugged connector, a broken ground or a short to a voltage source.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire, or connector unplugged
Temperature sensor open internally
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

symptoms: Shifts or clutch engagements feel rough once warm

P0941.title: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0941.summary: The hydraulic oil temperature signal jumps or drops out briefly, too short or irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Since fluid temperature changes slowly, a sudden step is a clear sign of an electrical problem rather than a real temperature change.

causes.text: Loose contact at the sensor connector under vibration or heat
Chafed wiring near hot gearbox or cooler parts
Sensor with an intermittent internal fault

P0942.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit
P0942.summary: General fault of the unit that generates and stores hydraulic pressure for an automated gearbox or its auxiliary oil supply: motor-driven pump, accumulator and pressure control. Toyota sets P0942 on the 2001 to 2005 MR2 Spyder sequential gearbox together with the SMT warning light and a buzzing pump, or with gears that can no longer be changed; fluid seeping from the reservoir cap or the seal of the hydraulic power unit is a known cause, fixed with new seal rings.

causes.text: Fluid loss at the reservoir cap or hydraulic power unit seals
Worn pump motor or faulty pump relay
Damaged wiring, connectors or power supply of the pump
Transmission control module fault

symptoms: Transmission or gearbox warning light on
Pump buzzing or running for long periods
Gears cannot be changed or shifts are delayed
Auto stop-start disabled or engine restarts immediately

P0943.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short
P0943.summary: In a hydraulic pressure unit the pump charges an accumulator up to a cut-out pressure and switches off until pressure falls to the cut-in point. By J2012 wording this code means the pump switches on again too soon, so the interval between charging cycles is shorter than expected.

causes.text: Accumulator has lost its gas precharge
Internal leakage at valves, seals or actuator cylinders
Faulty pressure switch or pressure sensor giving wrong cut-in point
Low or aerated hydraulic fluid

symptoms: Pump can be heard switching on unusually often

P0944.title: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
P0944.summary: The pump runs but the expected hydraulic pressure does not build or collapses. Stellantis names it Loss of Hydraulic Pump Prime: a 2023 STAR case lists it with P0868 and a slow engagement after the vehicle has stood, both set as the only transmission codes with the MIL on, and the fix was a new transmission; an FCA defect file from 2015 also shows it beside line pressure low.

causes.text: Pump loses prime (air drawn in through filter, seal or strainer pipe)
Blocked oil strainer or suction tube
Worn or failed pump (mechanical or electric)
Leaking check valve or internal leak in the valve body

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Slow engagement after the vehicle has been parked
Auto stop-start not available or engine restarts at once
Slipping, no drive or limp mode

P0945.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit/Open
P0945.summary: The control module drives the motor of the hydraulic pump through a relay or a direct output. This code reports a general circuit fault or an open in that control path, so the pump cannot be switched reliably.

causes.text: Pump relay coil open or relay not seated
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Failed output stage in the control module

symptoms: Pump does not run, pressure is not built
Gears cannot be changed or auto stop-start disabled

P0946.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0946.summary: The pump control circuit is electrically intact, but its behaviour does not match the command, for example a pump that keeps running after being switched off, or one that switches but is not followed by the expected feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Relay contacts welded or sticking
Pump supply or control wire shorted to battery voltage
Faulty pump state feedback or control module

P0947.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Low
P0947.summary: The voltage on the control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver is lower than the module expects for the commanded state. Usually the line is shorted to ground or the relay coil is shorted, so the output may be overloaded and the pump runs when it should not, or the driver shuts down.

causes.text: Relay control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Shorted relay coil
Damaged output stage in the control module

symptoms: Pump runs continuously or not at all
Gearbox in limp mode or stop-start disabled

P0948.title: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit High
P0948.summary: The control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver shows a higher voltage than expected, typically because it is shorted to battery voltage or the relay coil is open on a low-side driver. The pump then cannot be switched on, or the module sees it as active when it is not.

causes.text: Relay control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open relay coil seen as high level by the driver
Control module fault

symptoms: Gear changes not possible or stop-start disabled

P0949.title: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete
P0949.summary: Status code for an automatically shifted manual gearbox: the control unit has not yet finished learning its adaptation values, above all the clutch touch point and the end positions of the shift actuators. Such learning runs after a new control unit, clutch or actuator, after a software update and sometimes after the battery was disconnected; Hyundai and Kia patents show how the touch point is found and corrected from shaft speed changes.

causes.text: Relearn not run after clutch, actuator or control unit replacement
Adaptation values erased by software update or battery disconnection
Learning aborted by low voltage or worn clutch outside the learn window

symptoms: Gearbox warning or message to perform teach-in
Restricted gear selection until learning completes

P094A.title: Hydraulic Pump Driver Performance
P094A.summary: Concerns the electronic driver that powers the motor of a hydraulic or electric oil pump, often a separate pump controller. The driver reports, or the module infers, that it cannot deliver the commanded speed or current although the circuit is not open or shorted.

causes.text: Internal fault of the pump controller or driver stage
Pump motor drawing excess current (worn bearings, fluid in motor)
High resistance in supply or ground of the driver

P094B.title: Hydraulic Pump Stuck On
P094B.summary: The hydraulic pump keeps running although the module has switched it off, or it never reaches its cut-out point. Causes are a welded relay or shorted driver, or a pump that cannot reach cut-out pressure because of leakage.

causes.text: Pump relay contacts welded closed
Leakage or lost accumulator charge keeps pressure below cut-out
Shorted driver stage or supply wire shorted to battery voltage

symptoms: Pump audible after the vehicle is switched off

P094C.title: Hydraulic Pump Performance/Stuck Off
P094C.summary: The pump is commanded on but does not deliver: it does not turn, turns too slowly or produces too little pressure. The module judges this from pressure or speed feedback.

causes.text: Air in the pump after service or a suction leak
Seized or failed pump motor
Blocked strainer or leaking check valve
Supply or relay fault stopping the pump

symptoms: Engine restarts at once or stop-start not available

P094D.title: Hydraulic Pump Over Temperature
P094D.summary: The hydraulic or electric oil pump, or its integrated controller, has become too hot. The temperature is usually measured on the controller board and the pump is derated or switched off to protect it.

causes.text: Pump running too long because of leakage or a stuck relay
Defective pump controller board
Very hot transmission fluid or blocked cooling

symptoms: Burning smell near the pump in severe cases

P094E.title: Hydraulic Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P094E.summary: Fault in the power feed of the hydraulic or electric oil pump: fuse, supply wire, connector or relay output. The module sees missing or implausible supply at the pump or its controller.

causes.text: Blown pump fuse
Open or corroded supply wire or connector
Weak battery or poor main ground lowering pump supply voltage

symptoms: Stop-start disabled or gearbox in limp mode

P0950.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit
P0950.summary: General electrical fault in the circuit that carries the driver's manual up and down requests to the transmission control, as used by tip-shift gates on automatics and by automated manual gearboxes. A Chrysler patent shows the classic design: a transverse gate beside the drive positions with a proximity switch that signals upshift on one side and downshift on the other.

causes.text: Failed up/down switch or sensor in the selector lever or paddles
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter (e.g. after spilled liquid)
Clockspring or steering column wiring fault on paddle-shift vehicles

symptoms: Manual or tip shifting does not respond

P0951.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0951.summary: Plausibility fault in the circuit that reports the driver's manual upshift and downshift requests, typically the tip gate of an automatic selector lever or steering wheel paddles. The signal is electrically valid but makes no sense, for example both requests active together or a request held far longer than any tap.

causes.text: Sticking or worn up/down tip switch, request signal stays active
Displaced magnet or damaged Hall sensor board in the selector lever
Spilled liquid or dirt in the shifter causing cross-talk between contacts
Faulty input stage in the transmission or shifter control module

symptoms: Tip shifting or paddles do not respond or respond erratically
Unwanted gear changes in manual mode
Warning message, automatic mode keeps working

P0952.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low
P0952.summary: The control unit sees the voltage on the manual up/down request circuit below its expected window, typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch stuck in the grounded state. In many tip gates the moving contact switches to ground, as a Nissan patent shows, so a short to ground can mimic a permanently held request; a Volkswagen patent describes checking the Hall tip sensors for shorts and breaks while the lever is in P or R.

causes.text: Signal wire of the up/down circuit chafed through and shorted to ground
Tip switch stuck in the closed position
Moisture or spilled drink in the shifter creating a leakage path to ground
Low supply voltage to a Hall-type tip sensor

symptoms: Gear indicator shows no manual gear or a warning message
Normal automatic driving in D still possible

P0953.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High
P0953.summary: Voltage on the manual up/down request circuit lies above its expected window. Common reasons are a signal wire shorted to battery voltage or, where the input is pulled up internally, a broken wire or a switch that never closes.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the shifter harness
Broken wire or unplugged connector on a pulled-up input
Missing ground of the tip switch or Hall sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Tip gate or paddles have no effect
Warning or message about manual mode

P0954.title: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Intermittent
P0954.summary: The manual up/down request signal drops out or flickers for short moments, so a single tap may arrive twice, late or not at all. Unlike P0952 and P0953 the voltage is not stuck outside its window; it jumps between states without a matching lever movement.

causes.text: Loose or spread pins in the selector lever connector
Harness broken internally where it moves with the lever or steering column
Worn or oxidised tip switch contacts

symptoms: Manual shifts occasionally ignored or executed twice
Fault comes and goes, often over bumps

P0955.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit
P0955.summary: Fault in the circuit that tells the transmission control whether the driver has moved the selector lever from D into the manual gate. A Nissan patent shows a dedicated manual mode switch with two contacts on separate inputs, so a break or a short to ground can be told apart; a Hyundai patent uses a microswitch on the lever.

causes.text: Failed manual mode switch or microswitch in the selector lever
Corroded or loose connector at the selector lever assembly
Damaged wiring between selector lever and transmission control module

symptoms: Manual mode cannot be selected or is not displayed
Check engine or transmission warning light on

P0956.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance
P0956.summary: The manual mode signal is electrically valid but contradicts other information, for example manual mode reported while the range sensor reads P, R or N, or the mode switch never changing although the up/down requests arrive. A Hyundai patent uses a microswitch with two opposing contacts and treats identical or missing signals on both inputs as a defect; a Nissan patent likewise compares two contacts of the manual mode switch.

causes.text: Mode switch or its actuating foot misaligned on the lever
Worn switch contacts giving contradictory states on both inputs
Transmission range sensor out of adjustment, disagrees with the mode signal
Worn selector lever bushings allowing side play

symptoms: Manual mode drops out or will not engage
Display shows manual mode while lever is in D, or the reverse

P0957.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low
P0957.summary: Voltage in the manual mode circuit, the signal that reports the selector lever in the manual gate, is below the expected range. Mostly the signal line has a short to ground or the switch contact hangs in its grounded position.

causes.text: Mode signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Mode switch stuck in the grounded position
Liquid or dirt in the selector lever housing

symptoms: Manual mode not available or permanently indicated

P0958.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit High
P0958.summary: The manual mode signal from the selector lever reads above its expected range. Possible causes are a short to supply voltage or, with an internally pulled-up input, an open circuit or missing switch ground that keeps the line high.

causes.text: Broken mode signal wire or disconnected shifter plug
Missing ground at the mode switch
Mode signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire

symptoms: Manual gate has no effect, gearbox stays in automatic mode
No manual gear shown on the display

P0959.title: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Intermittent
P0959.summary: The signal reporting the selector lever in the manual gate drops out or toggles briefly while the lever is not moved, so the transmission control switches between manual and automatic mode on its own. The voltage is not stuck out of range as with P0957 or P0958 but jumps.

causes.text: Loose pins in the selector lever connector
Worn or bouncing mode microswitch
Harness damaged where it moves with the lever

symptoms: Manual mode switches on or off by itself
Gear display flickers between D and manual gear
Fault often appears on rough roads

P095A.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C
P095A.summary: Circuit C is a third channel reporting the shift position inside an automated manual gearbox, for example a further sensor track or a sensor on another shift rail or selector shaft. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault of that signal that fits none of the more specific C variants.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at shift position sensor C
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit C
Faulty shift position sensor C
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode
Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral

P095B.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P095B.summary: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit C of an automated manual gearbox. The voltage is electrically acceptable, but the value does not fit: it contradicts the other position channels, stays put while the shift actuator moves, or misses the learned gear positions.

causes.text: Worn or drifting shift position sensor C disagreeing with the other channels
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

symptoms: Fallback mode with fewer available gears

P095C.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Low
P095C.summary: The signal of shift position sensor C in an automated manual gearbox lies below its permitted voltage window. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a sensor with an internal fault pulling its output down.

causes.text: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
Open or shorted 5 V supply of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on
Gearbox may refuse to leave neutral

P095D.title: Gear Shift Position Circuit C High
P095D.summary: Shift position sensor C of an automated manual gearbox delivers a voltage above its permitted window. This usually points to a signal wire shorted to the supply, a broken sensor ground or, with a pulled-up input, an interrupted signal line.

causes.text: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to the 5 V supply or battery voltage
Open ground circuit of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C

symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on

P0960.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
P0960.summary: Open-circuit fault in the driver circuit of pressure control solenoid A: the module measures an impedance far above the coil value, as if a wire, pin or winding were broken. Which solenoid carries the letter A depends on the gearbox.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body or solenoid assembly
Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the transmission connector or pass-through
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission warning or MIL on, fault message in the cluster
Very firm or harsh shifts due to maximum line pressure
Transmission stays in a fixed limp gear

P0961.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0961.summary: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid does not behave as commanded. On GM's six-speeds, where A is the line pressure solenoid, the Saab 9-4X 6T70 sets it when measured and commanded current differ for 5 s, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s; both Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Solenoid with internal electrical or mechanical fault, current no longer follows the command
Debris or varnish in the fluid sticking the solenoid or regulator valve
High resistance at connector or pass-through distorting the current
Low fluid level causing pressure errors (CVT pulley monitor)

symptoms: MIL or transmission warning after the second drive
Slipping or ratio flare on CVT applications

P0962.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0962.summary: Pressure control solenoid A circuit low: the driver sees a short to ground. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid this way; a short there opens a high-side switch that cuts power to the shift solenoids and leaves park, reverse, neutral and one fixed forward gear at maximum line pressure.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through and touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid coil
Transmission fluid or water in the connector bridging pins
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on immediately
Limp mode with only one forward gear and reverse
Harsh engagements, poor acceleration from standstill

P0963.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0963.summary: Pressure control solenoid A circuit high: the driver detects a short to voltage, and on GM's six-speeds also an open circuit, since those units have no separate open code.
