The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (line pressure solenoid) sets it after 5 s as Type B, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s over two trips; the module then commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations.

causes.text: Open coil or high-resistance connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated connector at the transmission
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Firm or harsh shifts at maximum line pressure
Warning light, on some vehicles only after two drives or not at all

P0964.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
P0964.summary: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid B. What B controls differs by gearbox: GM's 8-speed uses it for clutch 2 (CB12345R), the 9-speed for CB29 and the 10-speed for CB128910R, Allison 1000 for pressure control solenoid 2, and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the even-clutch pressure valve.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Certain gears missing or limp mode
Dual-clutch gearbox drives on one sub-gearbox only

P0965.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0965.summary: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid B: wiring is intact, but current or resulting pressure does not match the command. In the Saab 9-4X 6T70, solenoid 2 feeds the 3-5-reverse clutch; a current mismatch for 5 s sets a Type C code without MIL and freezes that clutch's adaptations, and GM's 2016 six-speed table also lists it without MIL.

causes.text: Worn or internally faulty solenoid, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or its regulator valve
Internal leak in the CVT primary pulley circuit
High resistance in connector or pass-through

symptoms: Rough or delayed 3rd, 5th or reverse engagement
CVT ratio fluctuates, engine speed flares
Often no warning light on six-speed applications

P0966.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0966.summary: Pressure control solenoid B circuit low, meaning a short to ground in the driver circuit. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch; a short lasting 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) or 1 s (Saab) sets a Type A code with a fixed limp mode: reverse and 5th gear, maximum line pressure, converter clutch off.

causes.text: Chafed control wire touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid in the valve body assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Limp mode with reverse and one forward gear
No torque converter lock-up, higher fuel consumption

P0967.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0967.summary: Pressure control solenoid B circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, since they have no P0964. For the Saab 9-4X 6T70, where B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch, the module needs 1 s, stores a Type A code and limits the transmission to reverse and 3rd gear at maximum line pressure; GM's 2018 six-speed table uses 0.3 s and one trip.

causes.text: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Dual-clutch gearbox loses the even gears

P0968.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P0968.summary: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Gears that need clutch C are unavailable
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0969.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0969.summary: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve.

causes.text: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve
High resistance in the internal connection to the module

symptoms: Rougher shifts into 4th, 5th, 6th or reverse over time

P0970.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0970.summary: Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches.

causes.text: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly
Chafed control wire touching ground
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Limp mode in reverse and one forward gear

P0971.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0971.summary: Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure.

causes.text: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or loose transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear
Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure
Fault comes and goes with temperature or vibration

P0972.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0972.summary: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code.

causes.text: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage)
Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness
Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Transmission falls back to a fixed default gear

P0973.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0973.summary: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s.

causes.text: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly
Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector
Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip on many vehicles
Limp mode with only a few gears, often reverse plus one forward gear
Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure
Torque converter lockup and manual shifting disabled

P0974.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0974.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker.

causes.text: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, on GM six-speeds only after a second faulty trip
First gear locked out, start-off in a higher gear
Missing or wrong shifts, possibly limp mode

P0975.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0975.summary: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely.

causes.text: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall)
Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B
Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Unexpected shift to neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)
Fixed default gear or harsh shifts

P0976.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0976.summary: Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure.

causes.text: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing
Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly
Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector
Faulty driver in the transmission control module

symptoms: Warning light or stored code, on some GM six-speeds without MIL
Firm shifts due to raised line pressure

P0977.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0977.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high
Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply
Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Limp mode with only reverse and one high forward gear
MIL or transmission warning, depending on calibration

P0978.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0978.summary: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo.

causes.text: Intermittent high resistance at crimped harness terminals (FCA 9-speed)
Open coil of shift solenoid C (Allison-type usage)
Transmission software that predates the manufacturer's fix
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Sudden neutral or default gear while driving

P0979.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0979.summary: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A).

causes.text: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body
Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Rough or delayed shifts involving the affected clutch

P097A.title: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
P097A.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid 1/A
Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Transmission in a fixed default gear

P097B.title: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
P097B.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid 2/B
Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit
Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Default gear operation, some ranges unavailable

P097C.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P097C.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid 3/C
Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid C
Faulty low-side driver in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip
Upper gears unavailable or fixed default gear

P097D.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit/Open
P097D.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid D
Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit
Broken wire in the transmission harness
Faulty driver in the control module

symptoms: Missing gears that depend on solenoid D
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P097E.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit/Open
P097E.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid E
Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame
Broken signal wire to solenoid E
Faulty driver stage in the control module

P097F.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit/Open
P097F.summary: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block.

causes.text: Open coil of shift solenoid F
Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid F
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Gears that need solenoid F unavailable

P0980.title: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0980.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance
Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip
Solenoid C stuck energized, wrong gear or default gear

P0981.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0981.summary: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it.

causes.text: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55)
Transmission software not yet updated by the recall
Solenoid D coil resistance out of range
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Unexpected shift to neutral while driving (FCA 9-speed)

P0982.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P0982.summary: Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s.

causes.text: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly
Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission
Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module

symptoms: MIL on and default gear operation
No engine braking in first or no reverse, depending on gearbox

P0983.title: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P0983.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765.

causes.text: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply
Solenoid D with shorted windings
Conductive contamination between neighbouring pins
Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module

symptoms: Clunk or tie-up feel if the low/reverse clutch applies unintentionally

P0984.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0984.summary: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford checks SSE with P0770, P0985 and P0986 only, GM's documented tables never reach letter E, and even Ferrari's DCT list, which reuses most of its neighbours, skips P0984.

causes.text: Range sensor harness with weak crimps (FCA 9-speed recall)
TCM software below the recall level
Internal transmission fault when the code returns after the update
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Sudden neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed)

P0985.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P0985.summary: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford lists it for SSE on the 5R110W and 6R140 and in its 2020–2023 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries, beside P0770 for an open; for the 6R80 and 6F, whose SSE is the on/off multiplex solenoid, the 2012 text names only P0770.

causes.text: Solenoid E control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid E
Water or fluid in the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module

symptoms: MIL on after the fault is confirmed
All solenoids off, fixed fail-safe gear (Saab/Aisin)
Missing upper gears on Ford gearboxes

P0986.title: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P0986.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985.

causes.text: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin)
Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on, transmission in fail-safe gear
Tie-up or harsh shift if the controlled clutch stays applied

P0987.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
P0987.summary: General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Failed pressure sensor or switch E
Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P0988.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P0988.summary: Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all
Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve
Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit

symptoms: Often no noticeable symptom at first
Shift quality worsens because adaptation stops

P0989.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P0989.summary: Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released.

causes.text: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module
Debris keeping pressure away from the switch
R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve sticking
Low fluid level

symptoms: No warning light, code stored only
Shifts into 4th to 6th or reverse gradually less smooth
Occasional limp mode if the fault persists

P0990.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P0990.summary: Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch.

causes.text: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris
R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised
Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module

symptoms: No warning light, code stored only

P0991.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P0991.summary: The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector
Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker
Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration
Fault in the transmission control module input stage

symptoms: Stored fault, often without warning light

P0992.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P0992.summary: General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found.

causes.text: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch
Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module
Transmission control module input fault

symptoms: Warning light depending on manufacturer calibration
Possible limp mode with a fixed gear

P0993.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P0993.summary: Pressure sensor or switch F is electrically intact, but its reading does not match what the module expects from the commanded clutch state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Sticking clutch regulator valve feeding the switch
Worn or delaminated switch film, debris in the switch
Low or contaminated transmission fluid

P0994.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P0994.summary: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed by debris or damaged film
Clutch circuit not reaching pressure (valve or seal leak)

P0995.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit High
P0995.summary: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays high: with a normally closed switch the contacts stay open, which looks like permanent pressure, or the wire is open or shorted to voltage. No manufacturer documents this use publicly.

causes.text: Open signal wire or unplugged connector
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Switch stuck open inside the valve body module

P0996.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P0996.summary: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F drops out or flickers for short moments without staying low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no transmission with a sixth pressure switch was found: GM's six-speeds end at switch 5 (E), Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses letters B, D and E.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector contact
Debris or delaminated film making the switch chatter
Chafed harness shorting or opening under vibration

symptoms: Stored fault, often without warning light

P0997.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0997.summary: The drive circuit of shift solenoid F works electrically but its measured current or voltage does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code.

causes.text: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Missing or harsh shifts into gears using this solenoid

P0998.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit Low
P0998.summary: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid F. Two makers document it.

causes.text: Solenoid or valve body (control valve) internal fault
Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Transmission control module driver fault

symptoms: Limp mode or loss of a gear range
Harsh engagement or flare when shifting

P0999.title: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit High
P0999.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid F, from a short to voltage or, where the driver uses a pull-up, an open coil or wire. Nissan's bulletin NTB15-037 for the 2012–2017 Versa, Versa Note and Sentra with the RE0F11A CVT names P0999 together with P0998 as shift solenoid F and calls for replacing the control valve rather than the whole CVT when diagnosis confirms the fault.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Open control wire or short to voltage
Connector pin pushed out or corroded

symptoms: Limp mode or loss of a gear range

P099A.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099A.summary: The drive circuit of shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but current or voltage feedback does not fit the command. No manufacturer was found to document this code.

causes.text: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid

P099B.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit Low
P099B.summary: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 service manual for a six-speed automatic uses it for the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with transmission relay voltage at 2 V or more and the solenoid commanded on, the module sets P099B if the actual voltage stays below 3.7 V for 0.5 s.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground in harness or connector
Shorted solenoid inside the valve body
Transmission control module driver fault

symptoms: No reverse or no engine braking in first gear (Mitsubishi)

P099C.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit High
P099C.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid G. Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed uses P099C for an open circuit of the low-reverse brake shift solenoid: with the solenoid commanded off and transmission relay voltage of 2 V or more, a reading of 3.7 V or more for 0.5 s sets the code.

causes.text: Open control wire or connector between module and valve body
Open solenoid coil inside the valve body
Control wire shorted to voltage

symptoms: No reverse or harsh reverse engagement (Mitsubishi)

P099D.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Range/Performance
P099D.summary: Electrical feedback from the drive circuit of shift solenoid H does not fit the command, although no hard short or open is seen. No manufacturer was found to document this code.

causes.text: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High-resistance connector or harness contact
Weak driver stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Harsh or missing shifts involving this solenoid

P099E.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit Low
P099E.summary: Low-voltage fault, typically a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid H. No manufacturer was found to document this code.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Shorted solenoid coil
Transmission control module driver fault

P099F.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit High
P099F.summary: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid H, from a short to voltage or, on pull-up driver designs, an open coil or wire. No manufacturer was found to document this code.

causes.text: Open control wire or connector
Control wire shorted to voltage
Open solenoid coil

P09A0.title: Shift Solenoid G Control Circuit/Open
P09A0.summary: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid G. It is a late addition to J2012: older code lists still show P09A0 to P09FF as reserved.

causes.text: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Open solenoid coil
Pin backed out of the connector housing

P09A1.title: Shift Solenoid H Control Circuit/Open
P09A1.summary: Open circuit or general circuit fault in the drive of shift solenoid H, the eighth shift solenoid. Like P09A0 it is a late J2012 addition that older code lists still show as reserved.

causes.text: Broken control wire or unplugged connector
Open solenoid coil
Pin backed out of the connector housing

P09A2.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B
P09A2.summary: General electrical fault on the second gate select position signal (circuit B) of an automated manual gearbox. The published designs from Isuzu (one select potentiometer) and Aisin AI (one select stroke sensor) show only a single sensor, so it is not documented whether B is a redundant second track of that sensor or a separate sensor.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken signal wire of circuit B near the gearbox
Faulty select sensor, often integrated in the shift and select actuator
Faulty input stage for circuit B in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox shifts slowly or locks out certain gears
Gearbox stays in one gear or neutral

P09A3.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P09A3.summary: Plausibility fault of gate select circuit B: the signal is electrically valid but does not match what the module expects. That could be the reading of circuit A, the learned gate positions, or the target gate the module has commanded, as in the Aisin AI select control that compares actual and target gate.

causes.text: Worn or drifting select sensor, signal B no longer agrees with the reference
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or module replacement
Contact resistance at connector pins distorting signal B
Sluggish or worn select mechanism so the measured gate lags the commanded one

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gate selected or gears refused
Slow, jerky shifting in fallback mode

P09A4.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B Low
P09A4.summary: Set when the gate select signal on circuit B stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Likely causes are a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor short; with potentiometer sensors like the select position sensor in an Isuzu patent, an open signal wire often reads low too.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit B chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal short or broken wiper in the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear changes blocked or limited to a few gears
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A5.title: Gate Select Position Circuit B High
P09A5.summary: Indicates that the gate select signal on circuit B has stayed above its highest valid value for longer than allowed. Typical reasons are a short of the signal wire to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or a defective sensor.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox stays in one gear or in neutral
Limp-home mode with very limited gear choice

P09A6.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C
P09A6.summary: Electrical fault on a third gate select position signal (circuit C) that fits none of the more specific C codes. Public AMT designs show far fewer channels: Aisin AI and Isuzu use one select sensor, and a Mannesmann Sachs patent combines motor encoders with an extra neutral position sensor.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or wet connector at the select sensor or actuator unit
Damaged signal wire of circuit C in the gearbox harness
Faulty sensor supplying signal C
Faulty input stage for circuit C in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P09A7.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P09A7.summary: Rationality fault on gate select circuit C: the value is electrically valid, yet it disagrees with the other select channels, the learned gate positions or the commanded movement. A Mannesmann Sachs patent shows why several select signals can exist: when one sensor fails, the remaining ones still allow controlled positioning before an emergency mode based on stored drive times takes over.

causes.text: Drifting or worn sensor so signal C disagrees with the other channels
Select positions not relearned after repair work on the actuator or gearbox
Loose sensor mounting or magnet shifting the measured position
Contact resistance in the connector of circuit C

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on

P09A8.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C Low
P09A8.summary: The module stores this code when the gate select signal on circuit C remains below its valid range for a calibrated time. Common triggers are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or an internal sensor fault; depending on the sensor type, a broken signal wire can read low as well.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to ground
Sensor supply for circuit C missing or pulled down
Internal short in the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gearbox holds one gear or drops to neutral
Transmission warning message in the instrument cluster

P09A9.title: Gate Select Position Circuit C High
P09A9.summary: Logged when the gate select signal on circuit C sits above its highest plausible value for longer than a calibrated time. Usual suspects are a short to the sensor supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor with an internal fault.

causes.text: Signal wire of circuit C shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open or corroded sensor ground
Internal fault of the sensor delivering signal C
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Limp-home mode, often in a single low gear

P0A00.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0A00.summary: General circuit fault on temperature sensor A in the separate coolant loop that cools the inverter and other drive electronics of a hybrid or electric vehicle. The module flags it when the sensor signal cannot be used at all, without a more specific low, high or plausibility verdict; those cases have their own codes P0A01 to P0A04.

causes.text: Corroded or loose connector at the sensor in the inverter coolant loop
Temperature sensor element failed
Damaged signal or reference wire between sensor and hybrid control module
Fault in the input stage of the hybrid or inverter control module

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning light
Inverter coolant pump or radiator fan running constantly as a precaution

P0A01.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A01.summary: The sensor delivers a value inside its electrical range, but it does not fit the other temperatures in the vehicle. GM uses this code on the 2013 Two-Mode hybrid Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra as a cold-start test: after the vehicle has stood for more than 28,800 s (8 h), the power electronics coolant temperature at power-up may differ from engine coolant temperature by no more than 30 °C, provided engine coolant and intake air agree within 15.75 °C.

causes.text: Sensor characteristic drifted, reading offset against the other temperature sensors
Added resistance at a corroded connector shifting the reading
Low coolant or air pocket at the sensor in the electronics loop
Fault actually in the engine coolant or intake air sensor used for comparison

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips
Often no noticeable change in driving behaviour
Electric drive power limited when the electronics are hot

P0A02.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A02.summary: The signal voltage of the coolant temperature sensor in the electronics loop sits below its valid window. Because the sensor is an NTC thermistor, a low voltage means an implausibly hot reading, typically a short to ground.

causes.text: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the thermistor
Moisture or coolant in the connector bridging signal to ground

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Displayed electronics temperature extremely high although the system is cool
Cooling fans and pump running at full output, drive power limited

P0A03.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0A03.summary: The sensor signal voltage is above its valid window, which for an NTC thermistor reads as an impossibly cold coolant temperature. Typical reasons are an open circuit in the sensor or its wiring, or a short to a voltage source.

causes.text: Connector unplugged, loose or with a pushed-back terminal
Broken signal or ground wire of the sensor
Thermistor element open internally
Signal wire shorted to a voltage supply

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Electronics temperature shown far below ambient
Reduced electric drive power as a safeguard

P0A04.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A04.summary: The temperature signal from the drive electronics coolant loop jumps or drops out for short moments, then returns to normal. Coolant temperature changes slowly, so a sudden step that the physics cannot explain points to a loose contact rather than a real temperature change.

causes.text: Loose or fretting terminal at the sensor or module connector
Partly broken wire that opens under vibration or heat
Sensor with an internal intermittent contact

symptoms: Warning light that appears and disappears
Short, unexplained drops in electric drive power
Stored code with no steady fault on re-test

P0A05.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P0A05.summary: The electric pump that circulates coolant through the inverter, converter and drive motor loop is driven by a control line from the hybrid module. P0A05 means that line shows an open circuit or a fault the driver cannot classify further.

causes.text: Pump connector loose or corroded, often from road splash at the low-mounted pump
Broken control wire between module and pump
Failed electronics or open winding inside the pump
Blown pump fuse or missing supply, so the control input sees no load

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Electric drive power reduced, especially in warm weather or under load
Follow-up inverter overtemperature codes such as P0A93

P0A06.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0A06.summary: The control line of pump A in the drive electronics coolant loop sits at a voltage below what the module expects for the commanded state, usually because the line or the pump input is shorted to ground. Depending on the driver design, the pump then runs uncontrolled or not at all.

causes.text: Control wire chafed against the body and shorted to ground
Internal short at the pump's control input
Water or coolant in the pump connector

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine light
Electronics temperature rising quickly, power limited
Pump silent when commanded on, or running continuously

P0A07.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P0A07.summary: The module measures a voltage on the pump A control line that is higher than the commanded state allows, typically because the line touches a supply wire or the pump input has failed internally. The pump in the inverter and motor cooling loop may then be stuck on or never receive a valid command.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a battery or ignition supply wire
Pump control electronics failed, pulling the input high
Output driver in the control module damaged

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine light
Pump running all the time, even with the vehicle off
Possible power limitation if cooling cannot be confirmed

P0A08.title: DC/DC Converter Status Circuit
P0A08.summary: General fault on the status line through which the DC/DC converter reports its condition to the hybrid control module. The converter replaces the alternator: it steps the traction battery voltage down to charge the 12 V battery.

causes.text: Internal fault in the DC/DC converter reported by its self-diagnosis
Damaged or corroded status line or connector between converter and hybrid control module
Converter overheating due to a fault in the inverter/converter coolant loop
Faulty input stage in the hybrid control module

symptoms: Hybrid system, battery or master warning light on
12 V battery is no longer charged and voltage drops while driving
Electrical consumers fail and the hybrid system may finally shut down

P0A09.title: DC/DC Converter Status Circuit Low
P0A09.summary: The status signal that the DC/DC converter sends to the hybrid control module stays below its expected range, typically from a short to ground, an open line read as low, or a converter that pulls its status output down because of an internal fault. Mitsubishi uses P0A09 on the 2012-2013 i-MiEV for a DC-DC converter fault; its bulletins tie it to a failed on-board charger that blows the high-voltage fuse feeding the converter, after which the 12 V battery and drive battery stop charging.

causes.text: Blown high-voltage fuse feeding the converter, e.g. after an on-board charger failure (Mitsubishi i-MiEV)
DC/DC converter internal fault pulling the status output low
Status line shorted to ground or chafed harness
Faulty input stage in the hybrid/EV control module

symptoms: Power unit, battery or hybrid warning light on
12 V battery not charged, voltage drops
On EVs the drive battery may also stop charging

P0A0A.title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A
P0A0A.summary: The high-voltage interlock loop (HVIL) is a low-voltage signal loop routed through every HV connector, the service disconnect and component covers. If it opens, the control module opens the main contactors so no one can touch live parts.

causes.text: HV connector or service disconnect not fully seated after repair
Spread, bent or corroded interlock pins or damaged connector seals
Interlock wiring chafed or cut
Battery pack control module software fault (Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid 2024-2025)

symptoms: Vehicle will not start or go into ready mode
Check engine and hybrid system warning on
High-voltage system switched off while the 12 V system still works

P0A0B.title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Performance
P0A0B.summary: The interlock loop A responds electrically, but its behaviour does not match what the module expects – for example a loop resistance outside the window, a signal that does not follow the commanded test pattern, or two modules on the same loop disagreeing. Mercedes-Benz logs P0A0B00 in the battery management system, the DC converter and the on-board charger of model line 243 when the vehicle will not start; its listed causes include oxidised interlock pins in the low-voltage connectors, twisted or chafed harnesses and bent pins on HV components.

causes.text: Oxidised interlock pins in low-voltage connectors raising loop resistance
Improperly connected HV connector or bent interlock pins on an HV component
Twisted or chafed interlock harness rubbing on the body
Faulty interlock driver or receiver in a control module

symptoms: High-voltage system warning in the instrument cluster
Several modules store interlock codes at the same time

P0A0C.title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Low
P0A0C.summary: The voltage sensed on interlock loop A is too low while the module drives the loop – typically an opened loop or a short to ground. GM documents it codegenau: in its 2016 HPC2 table P0A0C sets when the sensed interlock voltage stays below 30 % of the 5 V test signal in 2 of 2 samples (12.5 ms each) with the 12 V supply above 10.2 V; it is Type A, so the MIL lights after one trip.

causes.text: HV connector, cover or service disconnect open, interrupting the loop
Interlock wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed at a module or the body
Corroded or pushed-back interlock pins
Faulty interlock source or sense stage in the battery or hybrid module

symptoms: Check engine light (GM Type A) and hybrid/EV warning
No ready mode, electric drive unavailable

P0A0D.title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A High
P0A0D.summary: The voltage sensed on interlock loop A is higher than expected – most often a short to a voltage source, or the loop not being pulled down when the module expects it. GM checks both states: in the 2016 HPC2 table P0A0D sets when the sensed voltage exceeds 24 % of 5 V with the source switched off (5 of 8 samples) or 44 % with it switched on (4 of 6 samples), Type A with MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Service/safety plug not fully inserted or with poor contact (Hyundai Sonata Hybrid)
Interlock wire shorted to a 12 V or reference voltage
Damaged interlock harness or connector after body or battery work
Faulty interlock stage in the battery or hybrid control module

symptoms: No ready mode or ready light blinking
Check engine and charging warning lights on

P0A0E.title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit A Intermittent
P0A0E.summary: The interlock loop A signal drops out or jumps for short moments and then recovers, so the module sees an unstable loop rather than a lasting open or short. Typical are connectors with loose or spread contacts, harness sections that move with the body or drivetrain, and moisture in seals.

causes.text: Loose or spread interlock contacts in an HV or low-voltage connector
Harness section with a broken strand that opens under vibration
Moisture entering through a damaged connector seal
Electrical interference on the interlock line or a weak module input

symptoms: Hybrid/EV warning that appears and disappears
Occasional loss of ready mode or sudden shutdown of electric drive
Intermittent no-start, often after rough roads or rain

P0A0F.title: Engine Failed to Start
P0A0F.summary: The control module commanded an engine start – by the hybrid system or an automatic start/stop restart – but the combustion engine did not reach a self-sustaining run within the allowed attempts. The code describes the result, not the cause.

causes.text: Vacuum leak, e.g. separated purge VSV/PCV hose at the throttle body (Toyota Prius)
Shorted sensor harness pulling down the engine ECU 5 V reference (Kia Niro)
Fuel delivery or ignition fault preventing combustion
Failed automatic restart of a mild hybrid with a cold engine (Audi A6/A7 2019)

symptoms: Check engine light and hybrid or drive system warning
Engine does not start, or runs briefly and stops
Reduced power because the vehicle runs on the battery only

P0A10.title: DC/DC Converter Status Circuit High
P0A10.summary: The status signal from the DC/DC converter to the hybrid control module sits above its valid range, typically because the line is shorted to a voltage source, its ground or pull-down path is open, or the converter drives the output high after an internal failure. The converter supplies the 12 V system from the traction battery, and its self-diagnosis reports problems over this status path.

causes.text: Status line shorted to 12 V or another supply
Open ground or signal return at the converter connector
DC/DC converter internal fault driving the status output high
Faulty input stage in the hybrid control module

symptoms: Hybrid system or battery warning light on
12 V battery voltage falls while driving
Possible shutdown of the hybrid system if the 12 V battery runs flat

P0A11.title: DC/DC Converter Enable Circuit/Open
P0A11.summary: General or open-circuit fault on the enable line with which the hybrid or battery control module tells the DC/DC converter that it may deliver power to the 12 V system. In typical designs a high enable level permits converter output, and a CAN message carries the same permission in parallel, so the two can be cross-checked.

causes.text: Broken enable wire or unplugged connector between control module and converter
Corroded or pushed-out terminal at the converter enable pin
Faulty enable output driver in the control module
Faulty enable input inside the DC/DC converter

symptoms: Battery or charging warning light on
12 V battery is not charged and runs down
Vehicle may lose motive power after a while

P0A12.title: DC/DC Converter Enable Circuit Low
P0A12.summary: The enable line to the DC/DC converter reads low when the control module is commanding it on. Because a low enable level usually means converter output is not permitted, the converter stays off and the 12 V system loses its charging source.

causes.text: Enable wire shorted to ground
Weak or failed enable output driver in the control module
Converter enable input internally shorted

symptoms: Charging or battery warning light on
12 V voltage drops, electrical consumers misbehave
Hybrid system may shut down when the 12 V battery is flat

P0A13.title: DC/DC Converter Enable Circuit High
P0A13.summary: The enable line to the DC/DC converter reads high when the control module expects it low, for example while the converter should be switched off. The usual reasons are a short to battery voltage on the enable wire, a stuck output driver, or a missing pull-down.

causes.text: Enable wire shorted to 12 V or another supply
Enable output driver in the control module stuck on
Open pull-down or ground reference at the converter input

symptoms: Hybrid system or battery warning light on
12 V battery drains while the vehicle is parked
Converter-related functions disabled as a precaution

P0A14.title: Engine Mount A Control Circuit/Open
P0A14.summary: Some vehicles use switchable or active engine mounts that the powertrain or a mount control unit changes between soft and firm, or drives with an actuator against vibration. P0A14 reports an open or undefined fault in the control circuit of mount A.

causes.text: Mount actuator connector loose, corroded or unplugged after engine work
Open coil in the mount actuator or switching solenoid
Wire broken where the harness flexes with engine movement
Fault in the engine or mount control unit output

symptoms: More vibration at idle or during cylinder deactivation
Shudder that feels like a torque converter problem

P0A15.title: Engine Mount A Control Circuit Low
P0A15.summary: The control circuit of switchable or active engine mount A shows a voltage or current below the expected level, which usually points to a short to ground on the line or inside the actuator. Ford uses P0A15 in its 2020 to 2023 gasoline OBD summary for the active mounts: the low-level driver reports the fault and the PCM matures it after about 5 seconds; the partner mount B has P0AB7.

causes.text: Control wire chafed on the engine or subframe and shorted to ground
Shorted coil in the mount actuator or solenoid, often after fluid leakage
Moisture in the mount connector

symptoms: Noticeable vibration at idle or low speed

P0A16.title: Engine Mount A Control Circuit High
P0A16.summary: The module sees a higher voltage on the control circuit of engine mount A than it should for the commanded state, usually a short to a supply line or a failed actuator input. The mount can then no longer be switched or driven as intended.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a battery or ignition supply
Mount actuator or solenoid failed with an open low side
Driver stage in the engine or mount control unit damaged

symptoms: Harsh idle or more engine movement on take-off

P0A17.title: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit
P0A17.summary: Some electric drive units measure the torque on the motor or generator shaft directly, for example with a magnetostrictive sensor inside a hollow motor shaft as described in Honda patents for hybrid drive systems. The control unit uses that value to check the torque it commands.

causes.text: Loose or corroded sensor connector at the drive unit
Damaged sensor wiring between drive unit and control module
Torque sensor or its excitation electronics failed, often only replaceable with the drive unit
Input stage of the hybrid or motor control module faulty

symptoms: Electric drive power limited or electric drive disabled
Higher fuel consumption because the engine runs more often

P0A18.title: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A18.summary: The motor torque sensor delivers an electrically valid signal, but the torque it reports does not match what the control unit expects from the commanded motor current, speed and operating state. Typical checks compare measured and estimated torque or look for an offset when no torque is applied.

causes.text: Sensor offset or gain drifted, reading off against the torque model
Electrical interference on the signal from damaged shielding or ground
Missing or outdated calibration after module or drive unit replacement
Mechanical fault in the drive unit that changes the real torque

symptoms: Engine runs more often, fuel use rises

P0A19.title: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit Low
P0A19.summary: The control unit watches the voltage of a torque sensor that measures load directly on the traction motor shaft, such as the magnetostrictive sensor in a hollow motor shaft shown in a Honda patent. P0A19 sets when the signal stays below its valid window for a calibrated time, typical of a short to ground, a broken supply or an open signal line pulled low.

causes.text: Sensor signal or supply line shorted to ground
Sensor reference or excitation supply missing
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Torque sensor electronics failed, often replaced with the drive unit

symptoms: Reduced electric drive power or electric drive disabled
Engine runs more often, higher fuel consumption

P0A1A.title: Generator Control Module
P0A1A.summary: P0A1A reports a fault of the electronics that control the generator, either inside a hybrid inverter or in a belt starter-generator. Toyota lists P0A1A for the 2010-2015 Prius and 2012-2017 Prius V together with P0A94, P324E and P3004 as a malfunction inside the inverter assembly with converter; the repair can mean replacing the MG ECU, IPM transistors or the whole inverter.

causes.text: Internal failure of the inverter or generator control electronics
Control software fault, fixed by an update where the maker provides one
Supply, ground or bus connection to the module faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or charging warning on
Battery no longer charged, start-stop or hybrid drive unavailable
Vehicle may not reach ready state

P0A1B.title: Drive Motor A Control Module Performance
P0A1B.summary: P0A1B flags a self-test failure of the processor that controls drive motor A, usually inside the inverter. In GM hybrid tables (2016) it sets when the processor fails an inhibit path test at power-down, three or more times, proving it could not take the system to a safe state; in 2011 tables internal SPI, RAM or cache faults in 28 of 32 samples count.

causes.text: Control software fault, several makers resolve it by reprogramming
Internal processor or memory fault in the inverter control board
Weak 12 V supply during start-up or shutdown

symptoms: Loss of drive warning and MIL
Vehicle cannot be driven electrically or not at all
Fault may vanish after a full sleep cycle while the code stays stored

P0A1C.title: Drive Motor B Control Module Performance
P0A1C.summary: P0A1C is the counterpart of P0A1B for the second electric machine, drive motor B, and reports that its control processor is no longer trustworthy. GM hybrid tables use it for the motor control processor B: in 2016 calibrations the code sets when an inhibit path test at power-down fails three or more times, in 2011 calibrations internal processor integrity faults such as SPI, RAM or cache errors are counted.

causes.text: Internal processor or memory fault on the motor B control board
Calibration or software fault in the inverter
Unstable 12 V supply or ground to the inverter electronics

symptoms: Reduced drive power or no electric drive

P0A1D.title: Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module A
P0A1D.summary: The hybrid powertrain control module coordinates engine, motors and battery. P0A1D says this module has reported an internal failure or is no longer working reliably.

causes.text: Internal fault of the hybrid control module
Code stored by a scan tool communication error, not by a real defect
Supply, ground or network fault at the module

P0A1E.title: Starter/Generator Control Module
P0A1E.summary: Mild and full hybrids often start the engine and recharge the battery with a belt-driven starter-generator that has its own control electronics. P0A1E means that controller has reported a fault or works incorrectly.

causes.text: Loose wiring connection at the starter-generator
Starter-generator software fault, fixed by update
Starter-generator with integrated electronics failed

symptoms: Wrench lamp or MIL on, electrical system warning

P0A1F.title: Battery Energy Control Module A Performance
P0A1F.summary: The battery energy control module supervises cell voltages, current and temperatures of the high-voltage pack. P0A1F reports that this module failed its own integrity checks.

causes.text: Module software fault, fixed by a new calibration
Internal hardware fault of the battery control module
Unstable 12 V supply causing module resets

symptoms: MIL or service engine soon light on
Battery or hybrid warning, limited electric operation

P0A20.title: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit High
P0A20.summary: This code covers the upper electrical limit of a torque sensor fitted to the traction motor shaft, for example the magnetostrictive design inside a hollow output shaft described in a Honda patent. The control unit sets P0A20 when the sensor voltage remains above the valid range for a calibrated time, which points to a short to the supply voltage, an open ground return or a sensor output stuck high.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground return
Sensor electronics output stuck high

P0A21.title: Motor Torque Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A21.summary: Here the torque sensor on the traction motor shaft delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. Such shaft sensors, as in the Honda patent with a sensor inside a hollow motor shaft, sit in an area with strong electromagnetic fields and vibration, so loose terminals, chafed wires and interference are the usual suspects.

causes.text: Loose or fretted terminal in the sensor connector
Chafed sensor wiring that shorts briefly under vibration
Damaged shield letting inverter noise into the signal

symptoms: Hybrid warning that appears and disappears

P0A22.title: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit
P0A22.summary: In series or power-split hybrids a separate electric machine runs as generator, driven by the combustion engine. A Honda patent claims a torque sensor inside the hollow shaft of either the traction motor or this generator.

causes.text: Sensor connector at the generator unplugged, loose or corroded
Open circuit in the sensor harness
Generator torque sensor or its electronics failed

symptoms: Reduced battery charging by the engine

P0A23.title: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A23.summary: The generator torque sensor sends an electrically valid voltage, but the torque it reports does not fit the generator current, speed and engine load the control unit knows. Typical checks compare the measured value with a torque model or look for an offset while the generator is idle.

causes.text: Sensor zero point or gain drifted
Electromagnetic interference from the generator or inverter
Contact resistance in the connector skewing the signal

symptoms: Generator output limited, battery charges slowly

P0A24.title: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit Low
P0A24.summary: P0A24 is stored when the voltage from the generator torque sensor stays under its lower diagnostic limit for a calibrated time. Electrically this means the line is pulled toward ground, the sensor supply is missing or the signal wire is broken.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Sensor electronics failed with output stuck low

P0A25.title: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit High
P0A25.summary: With P0A25 the control unit sees the generator torque sensor signal above its permitted upper limit for longer than the calibrated debounce time. The common electrical explanations are a short from the signal line to the supply or battery voltage, an interrupted sensor ground, or a sensor output stuck at its maximum.

causes.text: Signal line shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground
Sensor output stuck high

P0A26.title: Generator Torque Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A26.summary: P0A26 points to short interruptions or jumps in the generator torque sensor signal rather than a constant fault. The control unit counts implausible signal changes or brief out-of-range events and sets the code once a calibrated limit is exceeded.

causes.text: Loose or fretted terminal in the sensor connector
Chafed wiring near the generator housing
Shield or ground damage letting inverter noise in

symptoms: Hybrid warning that comes and goes
Brief drop in charging or system power

P0A27.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Power Off Circuit
P0A27.summary: P0A27 covers the circuit that tells the high-voltage battery to drop off the bus, i.e. the command path that opens the main contactors at key-off, after a fault or after a crash signal.

causes.text: Contactor or its driver does not release when power-off is commanded
Internal fault in the inverter/power unit that controls the contactors (Honda Civic Hybrid)
Damaged wiring or loose terminal on the hardwired power-off line
Crash or emergency shutdown signal stored or still active

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Vehicle will not enter ready mode or shuts down while driving
High-voltage system does not power down after key-off

P0A28.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Power Off Circuit Low
P0A28.summary: The control unit watches the voltage on the line that commands the high-voltage battery to disconnect. P0A28 sets when that signal stays below its valid window for a calibrated time, typical of a short to ground or a lost supply on the line.

causes.text: Power-off signal line shorted to ground
Poor terminal fit or corrosion at the battery or control module connector
Missing supply or blown fuse feeding the power-off circuit
Faulty driver stage in the battery or hybrid control module

symptoms: Vehicle does not reach ready mode
Electric drive disabled, engine runs constantly

P0A29.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Power Off Circuit High
P0A29.summary: P0A29 is stored when the voltage on the hybrid battery power-off line sits above its plausible range for longer than allowed, which points to an open line pulled up internally or a short to a supply voltage. No manufacturer explains P0A29 publicly; GM merely names it as a keyword in a generic bulletin on terminal fit.

causes.text: Open power-off line or unplugged connector
Power-off line shorted to battery voltage
Spread or corroded terminals at the connectors
Faulty input or driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Vehicle does not reach ready mode
High-voltage system stays active after switching off

P0A2A.title: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0A2A.summary: A thermistor in the stator of traction motor A reports winding temperature so the inverter can cut torque before the insulation overheats. P0A2A is the general circuit fault; the failure type sits in the extension byte.

causes.text: Broken or shorted sensor wire between motor and inverter
Loose or corroded connector at the drive unit
Thermistor failed inside the motor or transaxle
Faulty sensor input in the inverter/motor control module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Implausible motor temperature in live data

P0A2B.title: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A2B.summary: This is the rationality check: after a long soak, motor A's temperature should match other temperatures in the drive. GM compares it with the average inverter module temperature on its 2013 two-mode trucks and sets P0A2B, Type B, if they differ by more than 28 °C after at least 360 minutes off; the 2011 table uses 20 °C against coolant and transmission fluid, the 2013 MGU mild hybrid 25 °C.

causes.text: Thermistor drifted out of its resistance curve
Added resistance from a worn or corroded connector (Audi A7 e quattro)
Fault in a reference temperature such as inverter or fluid temperature
Motor cooling problem that makes a real temperature look implausible

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor temperature far off from other temperatures after a cold soak

P0A2C.title: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A2C.summary: The motor A sensor is an NTC thermistor, so its signal voltage falls as the winding heats; Hyundai's Sonata Hybrid bulletin gives about 11 to 13 kOhm at 20 °C for 2014-15 units. P0A2C means the voltage is too low, which the module reads as an impossibly hot motor: GM sets it on 2013 two-mode trucks above 230 °C (near 0 V), Type B, two trips; the 2011 table uses 184 °C, the 2013 MGU mild hybrid 236 °C.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Thermistor internally shorted (often only with transaxle or motor)
Chafed extension harness between drive unit and inverter
Faulty sensor input in the inverter/motor control module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor temperature shows a very high fixed value in live data
Electric drive power reduced or disabled

P0A2D.title: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0A2D.summary: With an NTC thermistor, a high signal voltage stands for a cold motor, and a voltage close to the 5 V pull-up means the circuit is open. GM sets P0A2D on its 2013 two-mode trucks when the reading falls below -40 °C, Type B over two trips; if the fault is already present at start-up it waits until the motor has warmed up under load for at least 1.5 minutes.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire of the motor temperature sensor
Connector unplugged or terminal pushed out, often after drive unit work
Thermistor open inside the motor or transaxle
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor temperature shows about -40 degrees in live data

P0A2E.title: Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A2E.summary: P0A2E flags short jumps or dropouts in the motor A temperature signal that are too brief or too erratic for the low/high checks. Bentley documents it for the Bentayga PHEV and Flying Spur Hybrid 2020-23: the resistance in the sensor crimp changes suddenly at high temperature, and only the sensor has to be replaced, although the engine and gearbox come out to reach it.

causes.text: Worn contacts in a coupling connector of the sensor line (Audi A7 e quattro)
Resistance jumps in the sensor crimp at high temperature (Bentley hybrids)
Chafed or loosely routed sensor wire with intermittent contact

symptoms: Check engine light or high-voltage warning in the cluster
Fault comes and goes, often after hard driving
Gearbox or electric drive warning on some models

P0A2F.title: Drive Motor A Over Temperature
P0A2F.summary: Unlike its siblings, P0A2F reports a real thermal problem: the sensor works, but motor A stays too hot. GM sets it on 2013 two-mode trucks when the temperature exceeds 200 °C and does not fall below the 135 °C reset level, Type B, provided no circuit or plausibility fault is active.

causes.text: Motor cooling failure such as a weak pump, low fluid or blocked cooler
Sustained high load such as towing or long climbs in electric mode
Temperature sensor reading too high while still within range

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
Electric drive power drops sharply or is cut
Engine runs more often to support the drive

P0A30.title: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0A30.summary: P0A30 is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor in the second traction motor (motor B). It is meant for faults the control unit can see on the sensor line but cannot classify as too low, too high or implausible.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or damaged connector between motor B and its control module
Chafed or broken sensor wiring at the drive unit
Thermistor in the motor winding failed (often only replaceable with the motor)
Faulty sensor input in the motor control module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine light
Motor B temperature missing or implausible in live data

P0A31.title: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A31.summary: P0A31 checks whether the motor B temperature reading makes sense, typically after a long rest when all parts should be close to the same temperature. GM compares it with other temperatures: the 2011 tables flag a gap above 20 °C to the average of power-electronics coolant and transmission fluid after 6 h without propulsion (Type A); the 2013 two-mode trucks allow 28 °C against the inverter module after 360 min key-off (Type B, two trips).

causes.text: Motor B thermistor reading drifted out of tolerance
Corroded terminals adding resistance in the sensor circuit
Comparison sensor (inverter, coolant or fluid temperature) is wrong
Uneven cooling of the drive unit, e.g. low fluid level

symptoms: Hybrid warning light after a cold start
Motor B temperature differs clearly from other temperatures after a long rest
Electric drive limited as a precaution

P0A32.title: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0A32.summary: P0A32 means the motor B temperature signal sits below its valid voltage range. GM uses an NTC thermistor, so a voltage near 0 V reads as an impossibly hot winding: the 2011 hybrid tables set it above 184 °C (Type A, one trip), the 2013 two-mode trucks above 230 °C (Type B, two trips).

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Thermistor shorted inside the motor
Chafed harness between drive unit and motor control module
Faulty sensor input in the motor control module

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Motor B temperature shows an extremely high fixed value
Electric drive reduced or switched off

P0A33.title: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0A33.summary: P0A33 is stored when the motor B temperature signal stays above its valid voltage range. With GM's NTC thermistor a voltage near 5 V reads as an impossibly cold motor: GM sets it below -41 °C in the 2011 tables (Type A) and below -40 °C on the 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips).

causes.text: Open sensor circuit or unplugged connector
Spread or corroded terminals at the motor or module connector
Thermistor open inside the motor
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Motor B temperature shows about -40 °C regardless of conditions

P0A34.title: Drive Motor B Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A34.summary: P0A34 covers a motor B temperature signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. A winding temperature cannot change by tens of degrees within milliseconds, so such steps point to a loose contact, a chafed wire or a cracked solder joint.

causes.text: Loose or fretting terminal in the sensor connector
Wire insulation chafed through at a moving harness section
Cracked joint at the thermistor leads inside the motor

symptoms: Hybrid warning that appears and clears on its own
Motor B temperature jumps in live data
Occasional loss of electric drive power

P0A35.title: Drive Motor B Over Temperature
P0A35.summary: Unlike the sensor codes, P0A35 reports that motor B is actually too hot according to a working sensor. GM's 2011 hybrid tables set it above 149 °C (Type A, one trip); the 2013 two-mode trucks use 200 °C, clear it only below 135 °C and run it only while P0A31 is not active (Type B).

causes.text: Electric coolant pump of the drive cooling circuit failed or weak
Low coolant or transmission fluid in the motor cooling path
Radiator fan not running or radiator blocked
Extended high load such as towing or long climbs

symptoms: Noticeable loss of electric drive power
Hybrid system overheat or warning message
Engine runs more often to compensate

P0A36.title: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0A36.summary: P0A36 is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor in the hybrid generator, the machine that is mainly driven by the engine to produce electricity. It covers faults the module detects on the sensor line without classing them as low, high or implausible.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector between generator and its control unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the transaxle
Generator coil thermistor failed (usually replaced with the generator)
Faulty input in the generator control unit

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator output or battery charging restricted
Generator temperature missing or implausible in live data

P0A37.title: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A37.summary: P0A37 tests whether the generator temperature reading is believable. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: once per drive cycle, after at least 5,400 s of soak and with the inverter switched off, the generator W-phase coil temperature is compared with the front motor coil and with the oil temperature.

causes.text: Generator coil sensor reading out of tolerance
Corroded connector or damaged harness in the sensor circuit
Fault in the power drive unit that evaluates the sensor
Comparison sensor (motor coil or oil temperature) reads wrong

symptoms: Hybrid warning after the first start of the day
Generator temperature differs from oil temperature after a long rest

P0A38.title: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0A38.summary: P0A38 means the generator temperature signal has fallen below the range a healthy sensor can produce. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the voltage of the generator W-phase coil sensor is 0.1 V or less for at least 0.5 s while the generator control unit has at least 8 V supply.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Generator coil sensor shorted internally
Damaged connector or harness between generator and power drive unit
Faulty sensor input in the power drive unit

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator temperature shows an implausibly high fixed value
Battery charging by the engine restricted

P0A39.title: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0A39.summary: P0A39 is the high-side counterpart of P0A38: the generator temperature signal stays above the range a working sensor can deliver. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the generator W-phase coil sensor voltage reaches 4.93 V or more for at least 0.5 s.

causes.text: Open sensor circuit or unplugged generator connector
Spread or corroded terminals at the generator or power drive unit
Generator coil sensor open internally
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Generator temperature shows a very low fixed value
Generator output or series mode restricted

P0A3A.title: Generator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A3A.summary: P0A3A flags a generator temperature signal that is interrupted or jumps only briefly. Since the thermal mass of a generator winding rules out sudden steps, such behaviour indicates a contact or wiring problem rather than a real temperature change.

causes.text: Loose or fretting terminal in the generator sensor connector
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Harness chafed against the transaxle housing

symptoms: Hybrid warning that appears now and then
Generator temperature jumps in live data
Occasionally restricted battery charging by the engine

P0A3B.title: Generator A Over Temperature
P0A3B.summary: P0A3B reports that the hybrid generator itself has become too hot, with the temperature sensor working correctly. Mitsubishi documents it as generator coil temperature high on the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the monitor runs continuously and sets the code when the W-phase coil temperature criterion of 199 °C is met for one second.

causes.text: Fault in the oil cooling circuit of the generator (low oil, leak, pump)
Radiator fan not working
Internal generator fault such as damaged winding insulation
Power drive unit commanding excessive generator current

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or overheat message
Reduced charging and power when the engine drives the generator
Battery state of charge drops during driving

P0A3C.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Over Temperature
P0A3C.summary: P0A3C reports overheating of the inverter that powers drive motor A, usually measured at its IGBT power switches. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the front motor control unit reads 166 °C or more at the U-phase upper IGBT for 0.12 s; other switch positions have their own P30xx codes.

causes.text: PCU or inverter radiator damaged or leaking (Honda Accord/Civic Hybrid)
Internal inverter defect such as a cracked solder joint (Honda Civic Hybrid 2012-15)
Low coolant or failed electric pump in the inverter cooling circuit
Radiator fan not running

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
Coolant loss from the inverter circuit

P0A3D.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Over Temperature
P0A3D.summary: P0A3D is the over-temperature code for the inverter feeding drive motor B. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV this is the rear motor control unit, and Mitsubishi sets the code when its IGBT temperature is 156 °C or higher for one second.

causes.text: Electric water pump of the EV cooling circuit failed
Low coolant or air in the EV cooling circuit
Radiator fan not running or radiator blocked
Internal fault in the rear motor and inverter assembly

symptoms: Fault appears after long climbs or high load

P0A3E.title: Generator Inverter Over Temperature
P0A3E.summary: P0A3E reports that the inverter controlling the hybrid generator is too hot. Mitsubishi sets it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV when the generator control unit reads 156 °C or more at the U-phase IGBT for 0.12 s; the other switches report via P30AD to P30B1.

causes.text: PCU radiator punctured or leaking after road debris (Honda Accord/Civic Hybrid)
Low coolant or failed electric pump in the inverter cooling circuit
Radiator fan not running
Internal fault in the power drive unit

symptoms: Several hybrid warning lights at once
Coolant loss or visible damage at the front radiator area

P0A3F.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit
P0A3F.summary: The rotor position of a traction motor is read by a resolver: one excitation coil and two pickup coils that return sine and cosine signals. P0A3F is the basic circuit code for motor A and mostly means the signal is gone.
