causes.text: Spread or poorly seated terminal at the resolver connector (documented on the Chevrolet Bolt)
Open or shorted excitation, sine or cosine wire between motor and inverter
Low 12 V auxiliary battery voltage disturbing the motor control module (Subaru, fixed by reprogramming)
Resolver coil failed inside the motor
Faulty resolver excitation or input stage in the inverter/motor control module

symptoms: Sudden loss of propulsion, sometimes normal again after a restart
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle will not enter ready mode or electric drive is disabled

P0A40.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A40.summary: P0A40 means the resolver of motor A still delivers a signal, but its quality is poor or implausible. GM calls this a degraded signal: the sine or cosine value exceeds 4.0 V, judged within 0.2 to 0.4 s of a 2 s window (Type A, one trip in 2016; Type B, two trips on the 2013 mild hybrid).

causes.text: Rotor position sensor (resolver) delivering a degraded signal, e.g. Audi G713
Worn, loose or contaminated contacts in the resolver connectors (Audi, Bentley)
Sensor wires pinched or misrouted on the gearbox housing after a repair
Faulty resolver evaluation in the inverter/motor control module

symptoms: Drive system fault message in the instrument cluster
Vehicle cannot be started or will not enter ready mode
Electric drive disabled or torque jerks while driving

P0A41.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A41.summary: P0A41 reports that a resolver signal of motor A sits below its permitted range, as happens with a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to ground, a shorted coil or a broken line pulled down by the input circuit. Kia documents it on the 2011-13 Optima Hybrid: an intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp with P0A41 in the motor control unit, traced to internal shorts or poor pin fit in the sub-harness between the hybrid power control unit and the motor, checked against resistance specs.

causes.text: Internal short in the resolver sub-harness between power control unit and motor (Kia Optima Hybrid)
Poor pin fit at the resolver connectors
Shorted resolver coil inside the motor
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control unit

symptoms: Intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp
Code returns after clearing, often with vibration or heat

P0A42.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A42.summary: P0A42 is the counterpart to P0A41: a resolver line of motor A reads above its allowed range. Typical triggers are a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to a supply voltage, or an open coil whose line is pulled up by the bias resistors of the input circuit, which drives the converter into clipping.

causes.text: Resolver wire shorted to a supply voltage inside the sub-harness (Kia Optima Hybrid)
Open sine or cosine line pulled high by the input circuit
Poor pin fit or corrosion at the resolver connectors
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control unit

symptoms: Intermittent MIL or hybrid service lamp
Electric drive disabled or vehicle not ready
Reduced power until the fault clears

P0A43.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A43.summary: P0A43 is set when the motor A resolver signal drops out or jumps only briefly, so that neither a steady low, high nor a lasting loss is confirmed. Stellantis uses it on the Pacifica Hybrid: NHTSA files show P0A43-00 stored in the hybrid control processor next to P0A3F and P0A45, and a 2026 parts review tells dealers to check active bulletins and flash the hybrid control processor before ordering a new power inverter module.

causes.text: Loose or spread terminal in the resolver connector, losing contact under vibration
Hybrid control or inverter software needing an update (Stellantis)
Chafed resolver wiring making intermittent contact
Intermittent fault in the power inverter module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL that comes and goes
Brief loss of propulsion, normal again after restart
Code stored as history without current symptoms

P0A44.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A44.summary: P0A44 reports that the speed derived from the motor A resolver is above the highest speed the motor may run. Mitsubishi uses it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV front motor: set at 15,500 rpm or more for 0.5 s with module supply above 8 V, judged only when the position sensor itself is fault-free; the guided fix after other codes are ruled out is a new front motor.

causes.text: Mechanical fault in the front motor or its drivetrain (Mitsubishi replaces the motor)
Real overspeed from wheel spin or a slipping coupling
Disturbed resolver signal producing a false speed value
Motor control module calculating speed incorrectly

symptoms: Electric drive torque cut during acceleration or high speed
Reduced top speed in limp mode

P0A45.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit
P0A45.summary: P0A45 is the general circuit code for the resolver of the second traction motor (B), usually meaning its signal is missing. GM sets it like P0A3F when sine or cosine amplitude falls below 2.3 V (Type A, one trip).

causes.text: Damaged or faulty frame/body wire harness to the rear motor (Toyota RAV4 Hybrid)
Poor contact at the motor B resolver connector
Resolver or control unit inside the rear motor assembly failed (Mitsubishi)
Hybrid control software needing an update (Stellantis)

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning message
Loss of rear-axle electric drive or all-wheel drive
Reduced power or vehicle not ready

P0A46.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A46.summary: P0A46 reports that the motor B resolver still delivers a signal, but one that is degraded or not plausible. GM uses the same check as P0A40 for its second motor: sine or cosine above 4.0 V, with a failure counted when it persists for 0.2 to 0.4 s of a 2 s window (Type A, one trip in the 2011 and 2016 tables).

causes.text: Resolver of motor B delivering unequal or distorted sine/cosine signals
High contact resistance or moisture in the resolver connector
Fault inside the rear motor assembly incl. bearing damage (Mitsubishi)
Damaged shielding letting inverter noise into the resolver lines

symptoms: Rear or second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Jerky torque delivery before the fault sets

P0A47.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A47.summary: P0A47 means a resolver signal of motor B is below its allowed range, typically from a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a shorted coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Resolver sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Poor pin fit or water ingress at the motor B resolver connector
Shorted resolver coil inside motor B
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

symptoms: Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Fault may come and go with vibration or moisture

P0A48.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A48.summary: P0A48 reports a motor B resolver line reading above its allowed range, for example a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to a supply voltage, or an open coil whose line is pulled up by the input bias circuit until the converter clips. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Resolver line shorted to a supply voltage
Open sine or cosine line pulled high by the input circuit
Corroded or loose terminals at the motor B resolver connector
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

symptoms: Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A49.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A49.summary: P0A49 covers short dropouts or jumps in the motor B resolver signal that are too brief to count as a lasting loss, low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or spread terminal in the motor B resolver connector
Chafed or stretched resolver wiring near the rear axle or subframe
Moisture in the connector causing intermittent leakage
Hybrid control software needing an update

symptoms: Hybrid warning or MIL that comes and goes
Brief loss of second-motor drive, often over bumps
Code stored as history without current symptoms

P0A4A.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A4A.summary: P0A4A reports that the speed calculated from the motor B resolver exceeds the motor's permitted maximum. Mitsubishi uses it for the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: set at 12,500 rpm or more for at least 1 s with supply above 8 V, and only judged once the rear position sensor codes P0A45, P0A46, P0C57, P0C58, P0C61 and P0C62 are ruled out; otherwise the rear motor assembly is replaced, bearing damage being one listed cause.

causes.text: Fault in the rear motor assembly, e.g. damaged bearing or control unit (Mitsubishi)
Real overspeed from rear wheel spin on low grip
Disturbed resolver signal producing a false speed value

symptoms: Rear electric drive shut off, front-wheel drive only

P0A4B.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit
P0A4B.summary: P0A4B covers the resolver that tells the inverter where the generator rotor stands; without a valid angle the generator cannot be commutated. Mitsubishi (Outlander PHEV 2023) runs the check continuously once the generator control unit has at least 8.0 V and sets P0A4B when its internal status flags stay failed for 0.23 s or 0.28 s; low and high signal levels go to separate codes there.

causes.text: Damaged resolver wiring or connector between generator and inverter
False detection in the inverter monitor software (Volvo, fixed by update)
Generator resolver defective
Resolver evaluation in the power drive unit faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or crank in hybrid mode
Electric drive or charging by the generator disabled

P0A4C.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A4C.summary: P0A4C means the generator resolver delivers signals that are electrically present but implausible, so the computed rotor angle cannot be trusted. Mitsubishi documents the exact limits for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the sine or cosine winding voltage must stay between 2.1 and 2.9 V; if either leaves that window for 0.28 s, or an internal status fault persists for 0.31 s, the generator control unit stores P0A4C.

causes.text: Corroded or loose resolver connector
Damaged shielding letting interference onto the sine/cosine lines
Resolver winding drifted out of tolerance
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit

symptoms: Reduced drive power or engine-only operation
Engine start via the generator not possible

P0A4D.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A4D.summary: P0A4D reports a generator resolver signal stuck below its permitted range, as caused by a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a winding short. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted resolver winding inside the generator

symptoms: Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4E.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A4E.summary: P0A4E is set when a generator resolver signal sits above its permitted range, which usually points to an open signal line pulled up by the input circuit or a short to a supply voltage. No manufacturer documents P0A4E publicly.

causes.text: Open resolver signal line or pushed-out terminal
Signal line shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit

symptoms: Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4F.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A4F.summary: P0A4F flags a generator resolver signal that drops out or jumps briefly and then recovers, as opposed to a steady fault. No manufacturer documents P0A4F publicly.

causes.text: Loose or fretting terminals in the resolver connectors
Chafed resolver cable that breaks contact under vibration
Heat-related cracks in wiring or solder joints

symptoms: Hybrid warning that appears and clears again
Short loss of electric drive or jerky power delivery
Fault often linked to bumps or heat

P0A50.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A50.summary: P0A50 says the generator speed derived from its resolver has exceeded the permitted maximum. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: with at least 8.0 V at the generator control unit and the position sensor itself judged healthy, a speed of 15,500 rpm or more lasting 0.5 s stores P0A50, and the repair path ends with replacing the generator.

causes.text: Internal generator fault (Mitsubishi repair path ends with generator replacement)
Mechanical fault in the transaxle or clutch letting the generator overrun
Incorrect speed calculation in the power drive unit

symptoms: Generator shut off, reduced power or engine-only drive

P0A51.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit
P0A51.summary: P0A51 reports a fault in the circuit of the current sensor that measures the phase current of drive motor A. The inverter needs this value for torque control and overcurrent protection.

causes.text: Current sensor in the inverter assembly failed
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted inside the inverter
Evaluation circuit on the motor control board faulty

symptoms: Drive motor A disabled, vehicle may not move or runs on engine only

P0A52.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A52.summary: P0A52 means the current sensor of drive motor A delivers values that are electrically valid but do not fit the operating state. Typical checks compare the reading at zero current with its expected offset, or compare redundant sensors with each other.

causes.text: Sensor offset drifted beyond the compensation range
Control and monitoring sensor disagree due to one degraded sensor
Electrical interference or poor ground on the sensor signal

symptoms: Drive motor A disabled, engine-only operation

P0A53.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A53.summary: P0A53 is stored when the current sensor signal of drive motor A stays below its valid range, typically from a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A53 publicly.

causes.text: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Hall element of the current sensor failed

symptoms: High-voltage system switched off, vehicle may not move

P0A54.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A54.summary: P0A54 signals that the current sensor output of drive motor A sits above its valid range, as caused by an open ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal sensor fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A54 publicly.

causes.text: Open ground of the current sensor
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Internal sensor fault with saturated output

symptoms: Drive motor A disabled or power strongly reduced

P0A55.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit
P0A55.summary: P0A55 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor that measures the current of drive motor B, typically the second traction motor, for example on a rear axle. The inverter needs this signal for torque control and to protect its power switches.

causes.text: Current sensor of drive motor B failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the motor B control board faulty

symptoms: Hybrid or electric drive warning with MIL
Drive motor B disabled, loss of electric all-wheel drive or reduced power

P0A56.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A56.summary: P0A56 means the current sensor of drive motor B delivers electrically valid values that do not match the operating state, for example a zero-current offset outside its band or a reading that disagrees with a redundant sensor. No manufacturer documents P0A56 publicly.

causes.text: Current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Current sensor of drive motor B degraded
Electrical interference on the sensor signal

symptoms: Reduced or missing drive from motor B

P0A57.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A57.summary: P0A57 is set when the signal of the drive motor B current sensor stays below its valid range, usually from a signal line shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A57 publicly.

causes.text: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Hall element of the current sensor failed

symptoms: Drive motor B or the whole high-voltage system switched off

P0A58.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A58.summary: P0A58 reports that the output of the drive motor B current sensor sits above its valid range, for instance from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A58 publicly.

causes.text: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Current sensor with saturated output

symptoms: Drive motor B disabled, reduced power

P0A59.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit
P0A59.summary: P0A59 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor on the hybrid generator, the electric machine driven by the engine that charges the battery and often starts the engine. Its inverter uses the current reading to control generator torque.

causes.text: Generator current sensor failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the generator control board faulty

symptoms: Engine runs constantly or the high-voltage battery is no longer charged
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A5A.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A5A.summary: P0A5A means the generator current sensor delivers values that are electrically valid but implausible, for example a wrong zero offset or phase currents that no longer add up. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5A publicly with criteria.

causes.text: Generator current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Generator current sensor degraded
Control module calibration requiring an update

symptoms: Reduced charging or engine running more often

P0A5B.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A5B.summary: P0A5B indicates that the signal of the generator current sensor stays below its valid range, as caused by a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed sensing element. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5B publicly with criteria.

causes.text: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Sensing element of the generator current sensor failed

symptoms: High-voltage system switched off or battery no longer charged

P0A5C.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A5C.summary: P0A5C means the generator current sensor output lies above its valid range, typically from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or a saturated sensor. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5C publicly with criteria.

causes.text: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Generator current sensor with saturated output

symptoms: Generator disabled, engine start or battery charging affected

P0A5D.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current
P0A5D.summary: P0A5D concerns the current in phase U of drive motor A, as seen by the inverter. Audi documents it on the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro (bulletin 2069917/1): P0A5D00, often with P0A6000 and P0A6300, is stored in the electric drive control module J841, the cluster reads Drive system: fault and the car may not start or drive.

causes.text: High-voltage phase cable or weld joint to drive motor A faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase current sensor in the inverter failed
Internal inverter fault
Winding fault in phase U of drive motor A

symptoms: Drive system fault message and MIL
Vehicle does not start or the drive system cannot be activated

P0A5E.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Low
P0A5E.summary: P0A5E means too little current flows, or is sensed, in phase U of drive motor A, the classic sign of an open phase. GM describes the check for the motor control processor of the 2016 Chevrolet Volt and in its 2018 hybrid tables: with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 900 A2 (2016) or 4,900 A2 (2018), the absolute U current is sampled while the rotor is within 30 degrees of the U phase axis; below 9 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, P0A5E sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Open circuit in the phase U cable, connector or terminal
Phase U current sensor reads zero
Phase U switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in drive motor A

symptoms: Rough or reduced electric drive, possible engine-only operation

P0A5F.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current High
P0A5F.summary: P0A5F reports excessive current in phase U of drive motor A, a condition the inverter treats as overcurrent. Hyundai documents it on the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid (bulletin 17-01-057-1, campaign T2J): coolant leaking inside the traction motor set the Check Engine and hybrid lights with P0A5F, P0A62 or P0A65, often together with the isolation fault P0AA6; drivers noticed weak acceleration and a dead air conditioner.

causes.text: Internal coolant leak in the traction motor causing insulation breakdown (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Shorted winding or phase lead of drive motor A
Inverter power stage fault in phase U
Current sensor falsely reporting overcurrent

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights

P0A60.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current
P0A60.summary: P0A60 covers the current in phase V of drive motor A. Toyota uses it with sub codes: a field report filed with NHTSA describes a 2006 Highlander Hybrid whose master warning lit and which would not move; P0A60 sub code 501 had set first, followed by P0A63, P0A78 and P0AEF, all returning at once after clearing, and the inverter assembly was replaced.

causes.text: Internal fault in the inverter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
High-voltage phase V cable or weld joint faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase V current sensor failed
Winding fault in phase V of drive motor A

symptoms: Master warning or drive system fault message, MIL
Vehicle will not move or start

P0A61.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Low
P0A61.summary: P0A61 indicates that phase V of drive motor A carries, or reports, too little current when it should be near its peak, pointing to an open phase V circuit. GM uses the same peak-axis test as for phase U on the 2016 Chevrolet Volt motor control processor and in its 2018 hybrid tables, here with the rotor within 30 degrees of the V phase axis: inverter above 50 V in normal PWM, squared current command above 900 A2 in 2016 and 4,900 A2 from 2018, a peak phase current under 9 A for 0.4 s within 0.6 s, Type A with MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Open circuit in the phase V cable, connector or terminal
Phase V current sensor reads zero
Phase V switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in drive motor A

P0A62.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current High
P0A62.summary: P0A62 signals overcurrent in phase V of drive motor A. Hyundai lists it in bulletin 17-01-057-1 for the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid next to P0A5F, P0A65 and the isolation fault P0AA6: the bulletin traces them to coolant leaking inside the traction motor and checks the high-voltage insulation first.

causes.text: Coolant inside the traction motor with loss of insulation (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Phase V lead or winding shorted to ground or to another phase
Inverter power stage fault in phase V

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights

P0A63.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current
P0A63.summary: P0A63 concerns the current in phase W of drive motor A. In the Toyota field reports filed with NHTSA it always appears beside P0A60: on a 2006 Highlander Hybrid with sub code 502, after P0A60 sub code 501, together with P0A78 and P0AEF, master warning on and no drive; the inverter assembly was replaced.

causes.text: Internal fault in the inverter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
High-voltage phase W cable or weld joint faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase W current sensor failed

symptoms: Master warning or drive system fault message, MIL
Vehicle will not move or start

P0A64.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Low
P0A64.summary: P0A64 means phase W of drive motor A shows too little current at the moment it should peak, typically an open W lead or a W sensor stuck at zero. GM completes its three-phase sequence with this code on the 2016 Chevrolet Volt motor control processor and in the 2018 hybrid tables: when the rotor sits within 30 degrees of the W phase axis, the inverter runs normal PWM above 50 V and the squared current command exceeds 900 A2 (2016) or 4,900 A2 (2018), a W peak below 9 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window sets P0A64 as Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Open circuit in the phase W cable, connector or terminal
Phase W current sensor reads zero
Phase W switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase W in drive motor A

symptoms: Uneven or reduced electric drive torque

P0A65.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current High
P0A65.summary: P0A65 reports overcurrent in phase W of drive motor A. It is the third phase code in Hyundai bulletin 17-01-057-1 for the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid, campaign T2J: with an internal coolant leak in the traction motor, P0A65, P0A5F or P0A62 set with Check Engine and hybrid lights, often joined by the isolation fault P0AA6.

causes.text: Internal coolant leak in the traction motor (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Phase W lead or winding shorted to ground or to another phase
Inverter power stage fault in phase W
Current sensor falsely reporting overcurrent

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights

P0A66.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current
P0A66.summary: P0A66 is the general fault code for the current in phase U of drive motor B, the second electric machine of a two-motor hybrid or an electric rear-axle motor. No manufacturer documents P0A66 publicly; GM, for instance, only uses the open-phase code P0A67 for this phase.

causes.text: Phase U current sensor of motor B failed (inside the inverter)
Phase U high-voltage cable or terminal between inverter and motor B faulty
Internal fault in the motor B power stage
Winding fault in phase U of drive motor B

symptoms: Motor B switched off, less power or no electric all-wheel drive

P0A67.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Low
P0A67.summary: P0A67 reports that phase U of drive motor B carries too little current at the moment it should peak, which GM interprets as an open circuit in that phase. In the 2016 Chevrolet Volt tables for motor control processor B the test runs while the rotor is within 30 degrees of the U axis, the inverter is above 50 V in normal PWM and the squared current command exceeds 900 A²; a peak below 9 A for 0.4 s within a 0.6 s window sets a Type A fault with MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Open circuit in the phase U cable, connector or terminal of motor B
Phase U switch of the motor B inverter not conducting
Phase U current sensor stuck at zero
Open winding of phase U in drive motor B

symptoms: MIL on the first trip and propulsion system warning
Jerky or weak electric drive, reduced power

P0A68.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current High
P0A68.summary: P0A68 means the current measured in phase U of drive motor B rises above its plausible maximum, either because a real overcurrent flows, for example through damaged insulation, a winding short or a shorted power switch, or because the phase sensor reads too high. No manufacturer documents P0A68 publicly.

causes.text: Winding short or insulation breakdown in phase U of motor B (e.g. coolant ingress)
Shorted power switch in the phase U leg of the inverter
Phase U current sensor reading too high (gain or offset fault)

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL, often with an insulation fault code
Sudden loss of drive from motor B

P0A69.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current
P0A69.summary: P0A69 flags a general fault in the current of phase V of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A69 publicly.

causes.text: Phase V current sensor of motor B failed
Fault on the motor B inverter board or power stage
Phase V high-voltage cable or terminal loose or damaged

symptoms: Reduced power, motor B no longer contributes

P0A6A.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Low
P0A6A.summary: P0A6A is GM's open-circuit test for phase V of drive motor B. The controller checks each phase on its own as the rotor turns; for phase V it looks at the window of 30 degrees either side of the V axis, where the current should be largest.

causes.text: Phase V lead, connector or bolted terminal of motor B open
Phase V switch of the motor B inverter not switching
Phase V current sensor output stuck at zero
Open phase V winding in motor B

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning after the first trip
Vibration or uneven torque from motor B before shutdown

P0A6B.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current High
P0A6B.summary: P0A6B is stored when phase V of drive motor B reports more current than the operating state allows. No manufacturer documents P0A6B publicly.

causes.text: Phase V current sensor gain or offset drifted high
Shorted power switch in the phase V leg
Winding or insulation fault in phase V of motor B

symptoms: Motor B cut out, reduced acceleration

P0A6C.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current
P0A6C.summary: P0A6C covers a general fault in the phase W current of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A6C publicly.

causes.text: Phase W high-voltage lead or terminal to motor B damaged or loose
Phase W current sensor failed
Internal fault of the motor B inverter

symptoms: Loss of electric drive on the axle driven by motor B

P0A6D.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Low
P0A6D.summary: P0A6D completes GM's set of open-phase tests for drive motor B with phase W. Because each phase is only judged while the rotor sits within 30 degrees of its own axis, the code points to W alone rather than to the motor as a whole.

causes.text: Phase W lead or terminal of motor B interrupted
Phase W switch of the inverter not conducting
Phase W current sensor stuck at zero
Open phase W winding in motor B

symptoms: MIL on the first trip with propulsion warning

P0A6E.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current High
P0A6E.summary: P0A6E indicates excessive current, measured or real, in phase W of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A6E publicly.

causes.text: Insulation breakdown or winding short in phase W (moisture, coolant)
Shorted switch in the phase W leg of the inverter
Phase W current sensor reading too high

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning, possibly with an isolation fault
Motor B no longer drives; possible air conditioning shutdown

P0A6F.title: Generator Phase U Current
P0A6F.summary: P0A6F is the general fault code for the phase U current of the hybrid generator, the motor-generator that is mainly driven by the engine, starts it and charges the battery, such as Toyota's MG1 or Hyundai's hybrid starter-generator. No manufacturer documents P0A6F publicly; Toyota's published field reports show generator codes for phases V and W only.

causes.text: Generator phase U current sensor failed
Fault in the generator section of the inverter assembly
Generator phase U cable or terminal faulty

symptoms: Engine cannot be started electrically or battery is no longer charged

P0A70.title: Generator Phase U Current Low
P0A70.summary: P0A70 means phase U of the hybrid generator carries or reports too little current while the generator is loaded, typical of an open phase or a sensor stuck near zero. No manufacturer documents P0A70 publicly.

causes.text: Open circuit in the generator phase U lead or terminal
Generator phase U current sensor stuck near zero
Phase U switch in the generator inverter not conducting

symptoms: Engine runs rough at start or battery charge level keeps dropping

P0A71.title: Generator Phase U Current High
P0A71.summary: P0A71 is set when the current in phase U of the hybrid generator exceeds its permitted level. No manufacturer documents P0A71 publicly.

causes.text: Shorted power switch in the generator phase U leg
Winding or insulation short in generator phase U
Faulty phase U current sensor or its evaluation in the inverter

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shuts down; vehicle may not move or restart

P0A72.title: Generator Phase V Current
P0A72.summary: P0A72 reports a fault in the phase V current of the hybrid generator. Toyota uses it: a field report filed with NHTSA covers a 2006 Highlander Hybrid with the MIL on and P0A72 stored together with P0A75 for generator phase W, P0A60 and P0A63 for drive motor A, and inverter performance codes including P0A78; after checking connector fit and the resistance of the three-phase cables, the inverter/converter assembly was replaced.

causes.text: Internal fault in the inverter/converter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
Generator phase V current sensor failed
Poor pin fit or damaged three-phase cable to the generator

symptoms: MIL and master warning, several hybrid codes at once
Vehicle may not move or enter ready mode

P0A73.title: Generator Phase V Current Low
P0A73.summary: P0A73 indicates that phase V of the hybrid generator delivers or reports too little current under load. No manufacturer documents P0A73 publicly.

causes.text: Generator phase V current sensor reading near zero
Generator phase V lead or terminal open
Phase V switch in the generator inverter not conducting

symptoms: Engine runs more often, battery charge does not recover

P0A74.title: Generator Phase V Current High
P0A74.summary: P0A74 appears when phase V of the hybrid generator shows more current than its limit allows. No manufacturer documents P0A74 publicly.

causes.text: Phase V sensor offset drifted or offset correction failed
Power switch in the generator phase V leg not turning off
Winding or insulation short in generator phase V

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shutdown, possibly no propulsion

P0A75.title: Generator Phase W Current
P0A75.summary: P0A75 stands for a fault in the phase W current of the hybrid generator. Toyota documents it in practice: in a field report from an NHTSA investigation of 2006 Highlander Hybrid inverters, P0A75 appeared next to P0A72, the drive motor phase codes P0A60 and P0A63 and inverter performance codes, and the root cause was inside the inverter/converter, which was replaced.

causes.text: Internal fault in the inverter/converter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
Generator phase W current sensor failed
Generator phase W cable or connector faulty

symptoms: MIL and master warning, usually with other hybrid codes
Vehicle will not become ready or will not move

P0A76.title: Generator Phase W Current Low
P0A76.summary: P0A76 signals that phase W of the hybrid generator conducts or reports too little current while the generator should be producing or absorbing torque. No manufacturer documents P0A76 publicly.

causes.text: Loose terminal, cracked lead or corroded connector in generator phase W
Generator phase W current sensor stuck near zero
Open phase W winding in the generator

symptoms: Engine start harsh or delayed, charging reduced

P0A77.title: Generator Phase W Current High
P0A77.summary: P0A77 is the excess-current code for phase W of the hybrid generator. No manufacturer documents P0A77 publicly.

causes.text: Turn-to-turn short or insulation breakdown in generator phase W
Power switch in the generator phase W leg failed closed
Generator phase W current sensor with excessive gain

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shuts down during charging or engine start

P0A78.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Performance
P0A78.summary: P0A78 means the inverter stage feeding drive motor A has reported a power-switch fault. GM explains the check in its hybrid OBD tables: the IGBT module watches each phase for desaturation, a sign of a short between the upper and lower switch; if that status persists for about 2 ms the code sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: IGBT desaturation or short in the inverter power stage
Power inverter module defective (replaced on Jeep Wrangler 4xe)
Hybrid control software requiring update
Shorted winding or phase cable of drive motor A

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or high-voltage warning
Stop safely warning on some models

P0A79.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Performance
P0A79.summary: P0A79 is the drive motor B counterpart of P0A78: the inverter stage for motor B has detected a power-switch fault. In GM hybrid OBD tables the IGBT module reports a desaturation status on a high or low side switch of any phase; persisting for about 2 ms it sets P0A79 as Type A with MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: IGBT desaturation or short in the motor B power stage
Power inverter module defective
Loose high-voltage cable at the inverter terminal (Pacifica Hybrid)
Hybrid control software requiring update

symptoms: Loss of propulsion in severe cases

P0A7A.title: Generator Inverter Performance
P0A7A.summary: P0A7A reports that the inverter stage driving the generator has signalled a fault, for example overcurrent or a failed power switch. Toyota uses the code across its hybrids and splits it with information codes.

causes.text: Internal generator inverter fault with overcurrent (Toyota information code 122)
Inverter assembly defective
Fault in the generator inside the transaxle
Insufficient inverter cooling stressing the power stage

symptoms: MIL, master warning and Check Hybrid System message
Reduced power or vehicle will not enter ready mode

P0A7B.title: Battery Energy Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P0A7B.summary: P0A7B is a request code: the battery energy control module, which has found an emissions-relevant fault of its own, asks the engine control module to switch on the MIL, and the engine controller stores P0A7B. The actual cause sits in a separate code in the battery module.

causes.text: Emissions-relevant fault stored in the battery energy control module
Air trapped at the battery coolant pump (Corvette E-Ray, with P0E3C)
Frozen power supply relay of the drive motor control module (Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid)

symptoms: Additional codes stored in the battery control module

P0A7C.title: Motor Electronics Over Temperature
P0A7C.summary: P0A7C reports that the electronics controlling the hybrid motors, mainly the inverter, have run hotter than allowed. Ford uses the code on its hybrids and stores it in the PCM.

causes.text: Coolant pump of the motor electronics cooling loop failed
Low coolant or air in the electronics cooling loop
PCM calibration triggering the code without real overheating (Ford Fusion Hybrid)
Blocked electronics radiator or faulty cooling fan

symptoms: Reduced power, especially under high load or heat

P0A7D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack State of Charge Low
P0A7D.summary: The battery controller watches whether the traction or mild-hybrid pack stays inside its usable state-of-charge (SOC) window. GM sets P0A7D (Type B, two trips) when SOC stays below a program threshold (30 % or 10.5 %) for more than half of a drive cycle longer than 50 km, after allowing generator time to recover.

causes.text: Pack discharged by long standing time or repeated crank/no-start attempts
Generator, DC/DC or charging path not replenishing the pack
48 V battery in low-voltage protection state (relays open)
Weak or self-discharging cell modules

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
No electric driving or reduced motor assist
Engine runs longer to recharge the pack
Vehicle may not start or reach ready mode

P0A7E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Over Temperature
P0A7E.summary: The pack controller compares the hottest module temperature with a protection limit. GM sets P0A7E, mostly as Type A (MIL after one trip), when the maximum module temperature exceeds a program limit between about 61 and 73.5 °C, unless a temperature sensor fault is active.

causes.text: Battery cooling fan inoperative or intake/filter clogged
Battery controller software logic (update released by Subaru, Porsche)
Low 12 V system voltage stopping the cooling fan
Aged cells with high internal resistance heating up

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
In rare cases warning with no-start

P0A7F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Deterioration
P0A7F.summary: This is the state-of-health monitor that CARB requires for hybrid storage systems. GM compares the calculated pack power capability with an end-of-life table at mid state of charge and sets P0A7F as Type B (two trips) when it falls short.

causes.text: Pack capacity or power capability lost through ageing
Dust or debris in the battery cooling fan or filter overheating cells
Battery controller software misjudging health (Honda, Mercedes)
Individual weak modules pulling the pack down

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid/IMA warning light
Weak acceleration assist, especially from a stop
Engine runs more often, higher fuel consumption
Shorter electric range on plug-in models

P0A80.title: Replace Hybrid/EV Battery Pack
P0A80.summary: The battery controller has concluded that the pack is at end of life. In GM tables this is a resistance test: the maximum cell or pack resistance, measured from current and voltage swings, exceeds a temperature-dependent end-of-life threshold, and the code sets as Type A after one trip.

causes.text: Cell or module resistance above end-of-life limit
Clogged battery cooling fan or intake filter (Toyota)
Controller software misreading a replaced pack (Honda Accord Hybrid 2018)

symptoms: Check engine and hybrid system warning on
Higher fuel consumption, engine runs more

P0A81.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit/Open
P0A81.summary: The controller watches the output that drives battery cooling fan 1 for an open circuit. In the 2016 GM table the fan is commanded at low duty (under 10 %) and the circuit voltage sits between about 1.6 and 5.85 V instead of being pulled low; 16 failures in 20 samples set it as Type B.

causes.text: Fan motor or its internal electronics open
Loose or corroded fan connector, broken control wire
Blown fan supply fuse
Faulty output stage in the battery control module

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning, often no other complaint
Battery cooling fan does not run when commanded
Reduced hybrid power in hot conditions

P0A82.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Performance/Stuck Off
P0A82.summary: This code covers a fan 1 that is electrically intact but does not deliver the requested cooling, up to standing still. No manufacturer publishes code-exact criteria; CARB requires a functional check of battery cooling where feasible.

causes.text: Dust or debris on fan blades or in the duct
Clogged or covered battery air intake or filter
Worn or seized fan motor bearings
Faulty fan speed feedback signal

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Fan audibly weak or silent under load
Reduced electric assist in warm weather

P0A83.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Stuck On
P0A83.summary: P0A83 means battery cooling fan 1 keeps turning although the controller has switched it off. No manufacturer publicly documents this exact code.

causes.text: Fan control wire shorted to supply voltage
Welded fan relay keeps power applied
Fan's internal speed controller ignores off command
Battery control module output stuck active

symptoms: Battery fan heard running with the vehicle off or idle

P0A84.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit Low
P0A84.summary: The controller detects a short to ground on the control output of battery cooling fan 1. GM tests it while the fan is commanded at low duty: a circuit voltage below about 0.26 V counts as a failure, and 16 fails in 20 samples at 250 ms set a Type B code (MIL after two trips).

causes.text: Fan control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short in the fan's control input
Moisture or corrosion in the fan connector
Defective output stage in the controller

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning after two trips
Battery cooling fan does not follow commands
Reduced hybrid power when the pack gets warm

P0A85.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit High
P0A85.summary: The controller detects a short to voltage on the control output of battery cooling fan 1. GM runs the test while the fan is commanded between 11 % and 100 % duty: a circuit voltage above 9 V counts as a failure, and 16 fails in 20 samples set a Type B code with MIL after two trips.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Fan control input internally open or shorted to its supply
Corroded connector creating leakage to supply

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning after two trips
Battery fan runs constantly or not at all
Possible 12 V battery drain when parked

P0A86.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit
P0A86.summary: The 14 volt power module is the DC/DC converter that feeds the 12 V network of a hybrid or electric vehicle from the high-voltage battery; GM calls it the Accessory Power Module (APM). Current sensor A measures the current flowing through this converter.

causes.text: Current sensor inside the 14 V power module faulty (usually not replaceable separately)
Damaged wiring or corroded connector between module and hybrid controller
Software fault in the module or hybrid controller

symptoms: Hybrid or charging system warning lamp on
Possibly no other noticeable change in driving

P0A87.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A87.summary: This code means the current sensor of the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter, GM: APM) delivers values that are electrically valid but implausible. GM's 2016 eAssist tables (hybrid control processor HPC1) describe a stuck-in-range test: once per key cycle, while the high-voltage contactors are open and then move to precharge, the converter should be off, so the averaged input current must be near zero.

causes.text: Current sensor zero-point drift inside the power module
Converter actually conducting current when it should be off (internal module fault)
Ground or reference fault distorting the sensor signal

symptoms: MIL on after two drive cycles
Possible reduced 12 V charging if the converter is limited

P0A88.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A88.summary: P0A88 reports that the current sensor of the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter feeding the 12 V system) reads too low while the converter should be delivering power. GM documents it for the Accessory Power Module: in the 2013 eAssist tables the input current must stay below 0.5 A for 1.5 s within a 2 s window while calculated output power is 0.25 to 1.5 kW; the 2016 tables use 0.50 A or less in 640 of 800 samples, enabled only when the APM is on, the hood is closed and the 12 V target is reached.

causes.text: Sensor signal shorted to ground or open
Current sensor in the power module failed
Corroded or loose module connector

P0A89.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit High
P0A89.summary: P0A89 is set when the current sensor of the 14 V power module reports more current than the converter can physically carry. GM's eAssist tables show how: in 2013 the APM input current reading had to exceed 22.5 A for 1.5 s while calculated output power was 1.5 kW or less; in 2016 the limit is 45.25 A or more in 200 of 250 samples (about 5 s) with the APM commanded on and 9 to 32 V supply.

causes.text: Sensor signal shorted to supply voltage
Current sensor in the power module failed
Open sensor ground pulling the signal high

symptoms: Converter output limited, 12 V voltage drops

P0A8A.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A8A.summary: P0A8A covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the current sensor in the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter that charges the 12 V battery in hybrids and EVs. The signal is valid most of the time but briefly leaves its range or changes faster than physically possible.

causes.text: Loose or fretted terminals at the module connector
Chafed wiring with intermittent short or open
Intermittent internal fault of the current sensor

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes

P0A8B.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage
P0A8B.summary: The 14 V power module (DC/DC converter) regulates the voltage of the 12 V network in hybrid and electric vehicles. P0A8B is the general code for a fault in the voltage this module produces or senses, without the more specific labels unstable, low, high or performance (P0A8C to P0A8F).

causes.text: Internal fault of the DC/DC converter
Loose or corroded 12 V output cable or ground connection
Weak 12 V battery distorting the system voltage

P0A8C.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage Unstable
P0A8C.summary: P0A8C indicates that the output voltage of the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter supplying the 12 V network of a hybrid or EV, fluctuates beyond what the control strategy accepts instead of settling at its target. Possible reasons include a poor 12 V connection, an aged 12 V battery that no longer buffers the network, or a regulation problem inside the converter.

causes.text: Loose or corroded 12 V battery terminal or ground strap
Aged 12 V battery no longer buffering the network
Unstable regulation inside the DC/DC converter

P0A8D.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage Low
P0A8D.summary: P0A8D reports too low a voltage at the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter feeding the 12 V network). GM uses it in its 2013 eAssist tables as the circuit-low check of the APM low-voltage sensor: if that sensor reads below 1 V for 1.5 s within a 2 s window while ignition voltage is 9 to 32 V, the code sets; it passes again above 1.5 V.

causes.text: Voltage sense line open or shorted to ground
Voltage sensor inside the power module failed
Converter not delivering output (fuse, output cable)

P0A8E.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage High
P0A8E.summary: P0A8E signals too high a voltage at the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter supplying the 12 V side. In GM's 2013 eAssist tables it is the circuit-high check of the APM low-voltage sensor: a reading above 20 V for 1.5 s within a 2 s window, with ignition voltage 9 to 32 V, sets the code, and it passes below 19.5 V.

causes.text: Voltage sense line shorted to a higher potential
Voltage sensor inside the power module failed
Converter regulating its output too high

symptoms: Very bright lights or failing bulbs if overvoltage is real

P0A8F.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Performance
P0A8F.summary: P0A8F means the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter for the 12 V network) does not perform as expected even though its signals are electrically in range. GM's 2013 eAssist tables use it as a correlation test: with the APM commanded on and ignition voltage 9 to 32 V, the APM's own low-voltage reading and the run/crank voltage measured by the controller must agree within 4.5 V.

causes.text: High resistance in 12 V output cable, fuse link or ground
Drifting voltage sensor in the module
Converter unable to hold its target voltage

P0A90.title: Drive Motor A Performance
P0A90.summary: P0A90 reports that electric drive motor A does not behave as commanded. In GM's eAssist mild hybrid the motor/generator is belt-driven from the crankshaft, so GM uses P0A90 to detect a slipping or broken belt: the motor speed is compared with the engine speed.

causes.text: Slipping, worn or broken drive belt on belt-driven motor/generators
Faulty belt tensioner or contamination on the belt
Motor, position sensor or inverter fault in full hybrids

symptoms: Belt squeal or auto-stop/start not working
Reduced electric assist or limp mode

P0A91.title: Drive Motor B Performance
P0A91.summary: P0A91 is set when the second electric drive motor (motor B) of a hybrid or electric vehicle does not deliver the expected speed or torque, although no electrical circuit fault is detected. Motor B exists only on systems with two traction motors, such as power-split or dual-motor layouts.

causes.text: Inverter B fault limiting motor current
Motor position sensor (resolver) signal error
Mechanical damage to motor B or its gearing

P0A92.title: Hybrid Generator Performance
P0A92.summary: P0A92 indicates that the generator of a hybrid system, the electric machine mainly used to convert engine power into electrical energy, does not reach the expected output, speed or torque. CARB requires manufacturers to describe how they monitor the generator so that faults preventing it from working are detected.

causes.text: Hybrid controller or inverter software needing update (documented by FCA)
Inverter phase current sensing fault
Internal generator fault (winding, bearing, position sensor)

symptoms: Reduced charging of the high-voltage battery

P0A93.title: Inverter A Cooling System Performance
P0A93.summary: The power inverter of a hybrid has its own coolant circuit with an electric pump, radiator and fan, separate from engine cooling. P0A93 is set when this circuit does not cool as intended.

causes.text: Electric inverter coolant pump failed or seized
Low coolant or air in the inverter circuit
Pump wiring, fuse or relay fault
Radiator fan not running or radiator blocked

symptoms: Vehicle may not start or may stall

P0A94.title: DC/DC Converter A Performance
P0A94.summary: P0A94 reports that a DC/DC converter in the high-voltage system does not perform as commanded. In Toyota hybrids this is the boost converter inside the inverter assembly, which raises the battery voltage before it reaches the motor inverters.

causes.text: Damaged power transistors in the boost converter / inverter assembly
Thermal stress from insufficient inverter cooling
Outstanding recall or software update not performed

symptoms: MIL, hybrid system and other warning lamps
Fail-safe mode with greatly reduced power
Vehicle may stop and not restart

P0A95.title: High Voltage Fuse A
P0A95.summary: P0A95 means the battery management detects that a fuse in the high-voltage circuit has opened, usually by comparing the voltage before and after the fuse. Several makers document it: Jaguar for the I-PACE battery energy control module, where a shorted high-voltage auxiliary component blows fuses in the junction box and battery module; Porsche for the Taycan as the main high-voltage fuse with a vehicle that will not become ready to drive; Volvo, whose procedure compares the voltage after the fuses with pack voltage; and Audi, which found an intermittent false entry in hard cornering fixed by software.

causes.text: Short circuit in a high-voltage auxiliary component (e.g. compressor, heater)
Fuse opened after overload or ageing
Faulty voltage measurement or software misdetection in the battery control module

symptoms: Vehicle not ready to drive, propulsion warning

P0A96.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit/Open
P0A96.summary: Some packs use two cooling fans; P0A96 reports an open or general fault in the control circuit of the second one. Ford documents it code-exact: on 2005–12 Escape Hybrid and 2006–11 Mariner Hybrid the traction battery control module may store P0A96, often together with P0A81 for fan 1, and the repair is to replace both high-voltage battery fans with a kit (about 3 hours, pack removal included).

causes.text: Fan 2 motor or electronics failed (Ford replaces both fans)
Loose connector or broken wire to fan 2
Blown fan fuse

symptoms: Code found during other diagnosis, often no complaint
Reduced hybrid power in hot conditions

P0A97.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Performance/Stuck Off
P0A97.summary: P0A97 is the fan 2 counterpart of P0A82: the second battery cooling fan is electrically reachable but does not reach its requested speed or does not turn at all. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Dust or debris on fan 2 or in its duct
Worn or seized fan 2 bearings
Blocked air intake to the battery
Faulty speed feedback from fan 2

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Weak airflow from the battery vents
Reduced electric assist in warm weather

P0A98.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Stuck On
P0A98.summary: P0A98 reports that battery cooling fan 2 keeps running after the controller has commanded it off; it mirrors P0A83 for fan 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Welded fan 2 relay
Fan 2 control wire shorted to supply
Fan 2 internal controller ignores off command

symptoms: Battery fan audible after the vehicle is switched off

P0A99.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit Low
P0A99.summary: P0A99 reports a short to ground on the control circuit of the second battery cooling fan. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Ford's two-fan Escape/Mariner Hybrid packs show that a second fan exists (there with P0A96).

causes.text: Fan 2 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in fan 2 control input
Moisture or corrosion in the fan 2 connector

symptoms: Fan 2 does not run when commanded
Reduced hybrid power in hot conditions

P0A9A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit High
P0A9A.summary: P0A9A reports a short to voltage on the control circuit of the second battery cooling fan. No manufacturer publishes this exact code; CARB requires the electronic outputs of battery thermal management to be checked for circuit faults.

causes.text: Fan 2 control wire shorted to supply voltage
Fan 2 control input internally open or shorted to supply
Corroded connector with leakage to supply

symptoms: Fan 2 runs constantly or not at all
Possible 12 V battery drain when parked

P0A9B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0A9B.summary: Temperature sensor A is one of the thermistors the battery controller uses to track cell or module temperature for cooling, charge limits and power limits. P0A9B is the general circuit code for this sensor: the controller finds an electrical fault it does not classify further as low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Open, corroded or loose sensor wiring or connector inside the pack
Failed thermistor on the module or cell sensing board
Battery controller input or software fault

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and check engine light
Reduced electric assist, regeneration or charging power
Battery cooling fan or pump runs more than usual

P0A9C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A9C.summary: This is a plausibility check: the reading of temperature sensor A is compared with the other sensors in the same pack, which should agree within a few degrees. GM sets P0A9C (Type B, two trips) when sensor A deviates from the average of the others by more than 25 °C for 50 of 67 samples (19OBDG02); Two-Mode hybrids use more than 15 °C against each other sensor for 90 of 100 samples, other programs more than 20 °C.

causes.text: Thermistor drifted or poorly seated on its cell or module
High-resistance connection in the sensor circuit shifting the reading
Battery controller calibration causing false sets (GM Volt update)
Genuine local temperature difference from a cooling or cell problem

symptoms: Check engine light after two drive cycles
Reduced hybrid assist or charging power
Message such as battery too cold, plug in to warm (GM Volt)

P0A9D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A9D.summary: Sensor A is an NTC thermistor fed through a pull-up resistor, so the voltage falls as the temperature rises; a short to ground looks like an absurdly hot cell. GM sets P0A9D (Type B, two trips) when the converted value exceeds 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples (19OBDG02); Two-Mode hybrids use above 95 °C while the other sensors read below 70 °C, other programs above 87.5 °C for 1.4 s.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground or chafed inside the pack
Internally shorted thermistor on the sensing board
Moisture or coolant in the sensor connector
Battery controller software causing false sets (GM Volt)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Strongly reduced electric power or no EV mode
Battery cooling running at high speed without reason

P0A9E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0A9E.summary: With the NTC thermistor of sensor A on a pull-up circuit, an open sensor or wire drives the input voltage toward the reference, which the controller reads as an extremely cold cell. GM sets P0A9E (Type B, two trips) when the value falls below -69 °C in 8 of 10 samples (19OBDG02); Two-Mode hybrids flag readings below -45 °C, other programs below -40 °C for 1.4 s.

causes.text: Open sensor wire or unplugged connector inside the pack
Open (failed) thermistor on the sensing board
Signal shorted to the reference voltage
Battery controller software causing false sets (GM Volt)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Battery too cold message although it is not cold
Little or no electric drive and weak regeneration

P0A9F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0A9F.summary: Cell temperature changes slowly, so a reading that jumps back and forth points to the circuit, not the battery. GM monitors this by summing the absolute sample-to-sample change of sensor A over a 10-sample window every 100 ms; if the sum exceeds 10, that window fails, and four failed windows out of five set P0A9F as Type B (two trips) in the 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 19OBDG02).

causes.text: Loose, fretted or corroded pin in the sensor connector
Partly broken sensor wire that opens with vibration or heat
Electrical interference on the sensor line from high-voltage components

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Temporarily reduced hybrid or EV power
Battery temperature value jumps in the scan tool data

P0AA0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Circuit
P0AA0.summary: The positive main contactor is a high-voltage relay that connects the positive pole of the traction battery to the propulsion bus. P0AA0 is the general fault code for this contactor circuit, used when the controller sees a problem it does not split into stuck closed (P0AA1), stuck open (P0AA2) or the control-circuit codes P0AD9 to P0ADC.

causes.text: Positive contactor or battery junction box worn or damaged
Fault in the contactor coil feed or its connector
Weak 12 V supply so the contactor does not pull in reliably

symptoms: Vehicle does not enter ready or propulsion-active mode
Hybrid or EV system warning with check engine light
Possible loss of propulsion while driving

P0AA1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
P0AA1.summary: P0AA1 means the positive main contactor conducts although it should be open, typically because its contacts have welded. GM checks this with all contactors commanded open for over 120 s (or the bus already below 9 % of pack voltage): more than 30 V on the positive bus in 4 of 6 samples sets Type B (two trips, 19OBDG02).

causes.text: Positive contactor contacts welded, e.g. after high current or arcing
Battery or hybrid controller software (GM Volt 2019, Jeep 4xe updates)
Faulty battery disconnect unit (GM Bolt EV bulletin)
Bus voltage sensing error making an open contactor look closed

symptoms: Vehicle will not switch into ready or propulsion-active mode
Check engine light and service high voltage system message
Often stored together with P0AA4 or a slow discharge code such as P0C76

P0AA2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Circuit Stuck Open
P0AA2.summary: P0AA2 means the positive main contactor does not close, or does not conduct, when the controller commands it closed, so the high-voltage bus cannot be energised from the pack. Audi documents it for the 2020-2022 Q5 e quattro and 2021-2022 A7 e quattro plug-in hybrids: the car does not start and the battery management module stores P0AA2 (often with P0AA5).

causes.text: Oxidised contact surfaces after long standing or high humidity (Audi)
Failed battery junction box or burnt contactor
Contactor coil not energised due to wiring or 12 V supply fault

symptoms: Vehicle does not start or reach ready mode
Service high voltage battery or hybrid warning message
Possible sudden loss of propulsion if the contactor opens while driving

P0AA3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Circuit
P0AA3.summary: The negative main contactor switches the negative pole of the traction battery onto the propulsion bus; together with the positive contactor it isolates the pack completely when the car is off. P0AA3 is the general code for this contactor circuit when the fault is not reported more precisely as stuck closed (P0AA4), stuck open (P0AA5) or a control-circuit fault (P0ADD to P0AE0).

causes.text: Negative contactor or battery junction box worn or damaged
Fault in the contactor coil wiring or connector
Battery controller driver or software fault

symptoms: Vehicle does not enter ready mode
Hybrid or EV system warning with check engine light

P0AA4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
P0AA4.summary: P0AA4 reports that the negative main contactor still conducts while it should be open, usually through welded contacts, so the pack is no longer fully isolated on the negative side. GM tests it once all contactors have been commanded open for more than 120 s, or the bus has already decayed below 9 % of pack voltage: over 30 V on the negative bus in 4 of 6 samples at 12.5 ms sets Type B (two trips, 19OBDG02).

causes.text: Negative contactor contacts welded after high current or arcing
Battery or hybrid controller software (GM Volt 2019, Jeep 4xe updates)
Faulty battery disconnect unit (GM Bolt EV bulletin)
Negative bus voltage sensing error

symptoms: Vehicle will not start or switch into ready mode
Check engine light and high voltage system message
Often stored together with P0AA1 or the slow discharge code P0C76

P0AA5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Circuit Stuck Open
P0AA5.summary: P0AA5 is set when the negative main contactor stays open or fails to conduct after the controller has commanded it closed, so the negative side of the high-voltage bus never connects. Audi reports it, alone or with P0AA2, on the 2020-2022 Q5 e quattro and 2021-2022 A7 e quattro plug-in hybrids with a no-start complaint; the stated cause is oxidation of the contact surfaces in the battery junction box after very long standing or extreme humidity.

causes.text: Oxidised contact surfaces after long standing or high humidity (Audi)
Failed battery junction box or burnt negative contactor
Contactor coil not energised due to wiring or 12 V supply fault

symptoms: Vehicle does not start or reach ready mode
Hybrid or high voltage battery warning

P0AA6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage System Isolation Fault
P0AA6.summary: The high-voltage system floats free of the chassis, and an isolation monitor measures the resistance from each HV rail to body ground. P0AA6 sets when that resistance falls below a calibrated limit.

causes.text: Coolant or moisture inside the battery pack, inverter or drive motor
Chafed or crushed orange HV cable shorting to the body
Insulation breakdown in the electric A/C compressor or a motor winding
Electrolyte leakage or contamination inside the battery sections

symptoms: Check engine and hybrid or EV system warning lights
Vehicle will not charge or will not enter ready mode after restart
Stop safely now message or reduced power

P0AA7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Isolation Sensor Circuit
P0AA7.summary: To measure isolation, the battery controller reads the voltage of each HV rail against chassis ground through an isolation sensor circuit and can switch in a known bias resistor. P0AA7 means this measuring circuit itself does not work, so the controller can no longer judge isolation.

causes.text: Failed isolation bias switch or measuring circuit inside the battery controller
Controller software misreading electrical noise (update available on some models)
Open or loose isolation sense lead or connector at the battery

symptoms: Check engine and EV system service warnings
Power reduced or speed limited until the system is switched off and on
Regenerative braking warning on some models

P0AA8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Isolation Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0AA8.summary: The two isolation sensor readings, positive rail to ground and negative rail to ground, should together equal the total pack voltage. P0AA8 is the plausibility check of that relation.

causes.text: Isolation measuring amplifier or reference in the battery controller out of tolerance
Pack voltage sense lead fault making the comparison value wrong
Controller software misreading electrical noise (update available on some models)

symptoms: Check engine and hybrid or EV system warnings
Reduced power or speed limit until restart
Isolation monitoring unavailable, so related faults may go unreported

P0AA9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Isolation Sensor Circuit Low
P0AA9.summary: P0AA9 reports that the isolation sensor signal sits below its valid window, typically because the sense line or the measuring input is pulled toward ground or has lost its supply. GM's 2016 and 2019 tables flag it when the sensor reads under 5 V with the bias switch open in 320 of 400 samples (about 5 s), Type B, two trips; the 2013 GM table uses a negative mid-pack reading under 5 V with contactors closed.

causes.text: Isolation sense line shorted to ground or open input
Failed isolation measuring circuit in the battery controller
Controller software misreading electrical noise (update available on some models)

symptoms: Check engine and EV system warning lights
Reduced power or speed limit on some models

P0AAA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Isolation Sensor Circuit High
P0AAA.summary: P0AAA is the high-side counterpart of P0AA9: the isolation sensor reports a rail-to-ground voltage above anything the pack can produce. GM's tables tie the limit to the pack: over 333 V in the 2016 table and over 416 V in the 2019 table, each in 320 of 400 samples with the bias switch open, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Open ground or reference in the isolation measuring circuit
Failed isolation input stage in the battery controller
Sense lead shorted to another HV potential inside the pack

symptoms: Check engine and hybrid or EV warning lights
Isolation monitoring disabled while the code is active

P0AAB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Isolation Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AAB.summary: P0AAB covers an isolation sensor signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of staying wrong. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM's hybrid tables use only P0AA7 to P0AAA for the measuring circuit.

causes.text: Electrical noise misinterpreted by controller software
Loose or corroded sense connector at the battery controller
Failing isolation measuring circuit inside the controller

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lights that come and go
Occasional power limitation that clears after restart

P0AAC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0AAC.summary: Air-cooled hybrid batteries carry a thermistor in the cooling air path; GM calls sensor A the inlet air sensor. The battery controller uses it to run the fan and to judge cooling.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or damaged sensor connector or wiring at the air duct
Failed air temperature thermistor
Battery controller input or reference voltage fault

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid system warning light
Battery cooling fan runs constantly or at fixed speed
Reduced electric assist in hot conditions

P0AAD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0AAD.summary: P0AAD is the plausibility check for battery air temperature sensor A: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit other temperatures. GM documents two methods.

causes.text: Thermistor drifted or stuck at a plausible value
Sensor displaced from the air stream or duct blocked
Fault in the comparison sensor (outlet air or cell temperature)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light

P0AAE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0AAE.summary: The battery air temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor, so a low signal voltage reads as very hot air. P0AAE sets when the signal stays below the lower limit, usually a short to ground.

causes.text: Sensor signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Thermistor shorted internally
Battery controller input fault

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Battery cooling fan runs at high speed without reason

P0AAF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0AAF.summary: Air temperature sensor A is the thermistor GM places at the cooling air inlet of air-cooled hybrid packs. Being an NTC type, a high signal voltage means the controller sees implausibly cold air, typically from an open wire or a lost ground.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire between sensor and battery controller
Connector at the air inlet duct loose or with pushed-back pin
Thermistor open internally
Battery controller input fault

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Scan tool shows inlet air near -40 °C regardless of weather
Battery fan runs on a fixed default speed

P0AB0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AB0.summary: P0AB0 flags a battery air temperature sensor A signal that jumps faster than real air temperature can change, usually a sign of a loose contact rather than a dead sensor. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's two-mode and 2013 tables for sensor A only list the low, high and plausibility codes.

causes.text: Loose or corroded contact at the inlet air sensor connector
Wire chafed through at the duct, intermittently touching ground
Electrical interference on the sensor line

symptoms: Hybrid warning light that comes and goes
Inlet air reading jumps in live data
Battery fan speed changes without obvious reason

P0AB1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P0AB1.summary: Air temperature sensor B is a second thermistor in the battery cooling air path; in GM's two-mode hybrid tables it is the outlet air sensor behind the modules. P0AB1 is the general circuit code for it, used when the controller sees an electrical fault without sorting it into low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Damaged wiring or poor contact at the outlet air sensor
Air temperature sensor B failed
Battery controller input circuit fault

symptoms: Hybrid or check engine warning light
Battery fan runs on a default setting

P0AB2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0AB2.summary: P0AB2 checks whether air temperature sensor B reads sensibly. GM uses it on the full-size two-mode hybrids, where sensor B measures outlet air: in the 2011 and 2013 tables, with the battery fan commanded on, the outlet air may not be more than 10 °C warmer than the hottest battery module, 90 of 100 samples, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Outlet air thermistor drifted from its characteristic
Sensor displaced from its position in the air duct
Battery module temperature sensor used for comparison reads wrong
Corroded contact adding resistance

symptoms: Hybrid or check engine warning light
Outlet air reads clearly above module temperatures in live data
Usually no change in driving behavior

P0AB3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P0AB3.summary: P0AB3 means the signal of air temperature sensor B sits below its valid range. Because the sensor is an NTC thermistor, a low voltage translates into very hot air, so a short to ground is the usual cause.

causes.text: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Thermistor shorted internally
Moisture or debris bridging the connector pins

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Battery fan runs loud even when the pack is cool

P0AB4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P0AB4.summary: P0AB4 reports a signal from air temperature sensor B above the valid range. For an NTC thermistor that reads as extremely cold air, which points to an open circuit, a broken ground or a disconnected plug.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B
Connector not refitted after battery or duct work
Thermistor open internally

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Outlet air shows about -40 °C in live data

P0AB5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AB5.summary: P0AB5 is set when the signal of battery air temperature sensor B fluctuates in a way real air temperature cannot, typically from an intermittent contact. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's two-mode tables, which use sensor B as the outlet air sensor, list only P0AB2 to P0AB4.

causes.text: Loose or corroded terminal at sensor B
Partly broken wire near the outlet duct
Interference coupled into the sensor line

symptoms: Hybrid warning light that appears intermittently
Outlet air value jumps in live data
No noticeable driving change in most cases

P0AB6.title: Engine Mount B Control Circuit/Open
P0AB6.summary: Some engines sit on switchable or actively driven hydraulic mounts whose solenoid or actuator is energised by the engine controller. P0AB6 reports that the driver output for the second mount (B) sees an open or otherwise faulty circuit.

causes.text: Broken or chafed control wire to the mount actuator
Corroded or loose connector at the mount (splash zone)
Mount solenoid or actuator coil open internally
Output driver in the engine controller defective

symptoms: Noticeable vibration at idle or with cylinder deactivation active
Cylinder deactivation may be suspended on some models

P0AB7.title: Engine Mount B Control Circuit Low
P0AB7.summary: P0AB7 means the engine controller sees the control line of active engine mount B pulled too low, the usual signature of a short to ground or an actuator coil with too little resistance. Ford's 2020-23 gasoline OBD summary lists it among the active-mount checks for bank 2: the output driver flags the fault continuously and the PCM matures it within roughly 5 seconds.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Mount solenoid coil shorted internally
Water ingress in the mount connector

symptoms: Increased vibration felt through seat and steering wheel at idle

P0AB8.title: Engine Mount B Control Circuit High
P0AB8.summary: With P0AB8 the controller finds the control circuit of active engine mount B at too high a level, for example because the line has a short to battery voltage or the driver cannot pull it down. Ford names the code in its 2020-23 gasoline OBD summary as the bank 2 high fault of the active-mount circuit check, which runs continuously and needs about 5 seconds of driver-reported fault before a code is stored.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage circuit
Mount actuator defective
Output driver in the engine controller defective

symptoms: Rougher feel at idle and when pulling away

P0AB9.title: Hybrid/EV System Performance
P0AB9.summary: Despite the broad title, GM uses P0AB9 for one concrete check: a failed engine auto-start or auto-stop in its hybrids, including an engine stall during that process. In the 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables the hybrid controller sets the code when the engine still reports no torque about 15 seconds into an auto-start although more than 20 Nm is commanded, provided fuel level is sufficient and no cam or crank fault is present.
