causes.text: Fuel delivery problem (weak pump, nearly empty tank, clogged filter)
Ignition or injector fault that prevents the engine from firing
Starter-generator or motor unable to spin the engine to start speed
Controller software needing an update

symptoms: Engine hesitates, fails or stalls when restarting at a stop
Auto-stop disabled for the rest of the trip

P0ABA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit
P0ABA.summary: The battery management system measures the total voltage of the high-voltage pack through a dedicated sense circuit and uses it for state of charge, power limits and contactor checks. P0ABA is the general circuit fault for sense circuit A, set when the reading is unusable without being clearly low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Damaged or loose voltage sense lead inside the battery pack
Measurement input of the battery controller defective
Blown sense fuse or failed divider resistor

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid system warning light
Reduced electric assist or EV range
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0ABB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
P0ABB.summary: P0ABB is a plausibility check: the measured pack voltage is within electrical limits but does not agree with what the individual cells add up to. GM documents it in several hybrid tables.

causes.text: Pack voltage measurement drifted (divider or input aging)
Faulty cell voltage tap distorting the cell sum
High-resistance busbar or sense connection

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid system warning light

P0ABC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
P0ABC.summary: P0ABC is stored when the pack voltage sensor reports a value below anything the battery could really have, pointing to a short to ground or a lost sense signal rather than a discharged pack. GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables set it below 4.8 V with system voltage above 10.2 V, after 8 failed samples out of 10 taken every 25 ms, and rate it Type A with MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Sense line shorted to ground or disconnected
Sense fuse or link open so no voltage reaches the input
Battery controller measurement input defective

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on
Vehicle may refuse to enter ready mode
Engine runs continuously, no electric drive

P0ABD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit High
P0ABD.summary: The counterpart to P0ABC: the pack voltage reading is above the highest value the battery could physically reach, which suggests an open reference, a failed divider or a damaged input rather than real overcharging. GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables set P0ABD above 392 V, again with 8 failed samples out of 10 at 25 ms intervals and Type A, so the MIL comes on immediately.

causes.text: Open ground or reference side of the sense circuit
Voltage divider component failed in the battery controller
Battery controller measurement input defective

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on

P0ABE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0ABE.summary: P0ABE flags a pack voltage signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of changing smoothly, as a battery voltage physically would. A loose sense connection or a cracked solder joint inside the pack are the classic triggers.

causes.text: Loose or fretted voltage sense connection
Cracked solder or crimp joint on the sense board
Electrical noise from damaged shielding or ground

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Sudden short drops in electric power

P0ABF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit
P0ABF.summary: The pack current sensor, usually a Hall-effect unit around the main cable, tells the battery controller how much current flows in and out. P0ABF is the general fault of sensor A.

causes.text: Hall current sensor output frozen
Sensor supply, ground or signal wire faulty
Sensor not seated around the conductor after repair

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on
Reduced electric power and erratic charge display

P0AC0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0AC0.summary: P0AC0 belongs to the battery current sensor family, not to battery cooling. It reports a sensor whose reading is electrically valid but implausible.

causes.text: Current sensor zero offset drifted
Unstable sensor supply or reference voltage
Battery controller input fault

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on
State of charge display drifts or jumps

P0AC1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit Low
P0AC1.summary: P0AC1 is set when the output of the pack current sensor falls below the valid window, so that the converted current would be an impossible discharge or charge value. GM documents it in several hybrid tables.

causes.text: Sensor 5 V supply open or shorted
Signal wire shorted to ground
Hall current sensor failed internally

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on
Electric drive limited or vehicle will not go ready

P0AC2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit High
P0AC2.summary: With P0AC2 the current sensor output sits above its valid window, which after conversion would mean an implausibly large current in the opposite direction to P0AC1. GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables set it when the Hall-effect sensor reads above 274.6 A in 8 of 10 samples taken every 25 ms, again as Type A with immediate MIL.

causes.text: Sensor ground open
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V supply or another voltage
Hall current sensor failed internally

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning on
Battery power limited, engine runs more often

P0AC3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AC3.summary: P0AC3 describes a battery current signal that jumps, spikes or drops out in a way real current flow could not explain, typically through a loose connector, a chafed signal wire or interference on the sensor ground. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or corroded current sensor connector
Chafed signal or supply wire with intermittent contact
Interference on sensor ground or shield

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Short drops in electric power while driving

P0AC4.title: Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P0AC4.summary: In many hybrids the hybrid powertrain controller has its own emission-related diagnostics but does not drive the malfunction indicator lamp itself. When it detects such a fault it sends a MIL request to the engine controller, which then stores P0AC4 as a pointer.

causes.text: Emission-related fault stored in the hybrid controller
Request still present because codes were cleared only in the engine controller

symptoms: Check engine light on (caused by the underlying hybrid fault)
Further codes present only in the hybrid controller

P0AC5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P0AC5.summary: Battery temperature sensor B is one of several thermistors that measure cell or module temperature inside the high-voltage pack; GM's Volt bulletin calls it sensor 2 of nine. P0AC5 is the general circuit code for it, used for an electrical fault the controller does not classify as low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Poor contact or damaged wire between sensor B and sensing board
Temperature sensor B failed
Fault in the battery controller input stage

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
Charging may be slower on plug-in models

P0AC6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0AC6.summary: P0AC6 is the plausibility test for battery temperature sensor B: its reading is compared with the other pack sensors. GM documents several calibrations.

causes.text: Sensor B drifted from its characteristic
Controller software flags the sensor falsely (GM Volt bulletin 18-NA-342)
Corroded contact adding resistance in the sensor circuit
Real temperature difference from a weak cell or blocked cooling

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
One sensor reading far off the others in live data
Battery too cold message on the Volt in mild weather

P0AC7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P0AC7.summary: P0AC7 means the voltage of battery temperature sensor B is below its valid range. GM's sensors are NTC thermistors, so a low voltage equals an extremely hot reading, usually from a short to ground.

causes.text: Sensor B signal shorted to ground inside the pack harness
Thermistor shorted internally
Controller software setting the code falsely (Volt bulletin 18-NA-342)
Moisture or coolant at the sensing board connector

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Sensor B shows an implausibly high temperature

P0AC8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P0AC8.summary: P0AC8 reports that battery temperature sensor B delivers a voltage above its valid range, which for an NTC thermistor reads as extreme cold. An open wire, a disconnected sensing board plug or a broken sensor are typical.

causes.text: Open signal or return wire of sensor B
Thermistor open internally
Controller software issue on the Volt (bulletin 18-NA-342)
Signal shorted to the reference voltage

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Battery too cold message although it is not cold
Strongly reduced charging and electric power

P0AC9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AC9.summary: P0AC9 catches a battery temperature sensor B signal that changes erratically. Pack temperatures move slowly because of the large thermal mass, so rapid swings point to a bad connection.

causes.text: Loose terminal or unlatched connector at the sensing board
Partly broken sensor wire inside the pack
Interference from high-voltage switching on the sensor line

symptoms: Hybrid warning light that comes and goes
Sensor B value jumps in live data

P0ACA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P0ACA.summary: Battery temperature sensor C is a further thermistor inside the high-voltage pack, corresponding to sensor 3 in GM's Volt bulletin. P0ACA covers a general electrical fault in its circuit that the controller does not narrow down to low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Poor contact or damaged wire between sensor C and sensing board
Temperature sensor C failed
Fault in the battery controller input stage

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
Further battery sensor codes may be stored

P0ACB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P0ACB.summary: With P0ACB the controller judges battery temperature sensor C implausible: its value deviates too far from what the other pack sensors report. GM applies the same limits as for sensors A and B.

causes.text: Sensor C drifted from its characteristic
Controller software flags the sensor falsely (GM Volt bulletin 18-NA-342)
Corroded terminal adding resistance
Real temperature difference in the module monitored by sensor C

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Sensor C reads clearly off the others after a long soak
Possibly reduced charge and drive power

P0ACC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P0ACC.summary: P0ACC sets when the signal of battery temperature sensor C drops below the valid voltage window. For the NTC sensors GM uses, that equals an impossibly hot reading, most often caused by a short to ground in the pack wiring.

causes.text: Sensor C signal shorted to ground
Thermistor shorted internally
Controller software setting the code falsely (Volt bulletin 18-NA-342)
Moisture at the sensing board connector

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Sensor C shows an implausibly high temperature
Reduced charging and electric drive power

P0ACD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P0ACD.summary: P0ACD indicates that battery temperature sensor C reports a voltage above its plausible range, which an NTC sensor translates into extreme cold. Common reasons are an open circuit, a pin backed out of the sensing board connector or a cracked thermistor.

causes.text: Open signal or return wire of sensor C
Thermistor open or cracked
Controller software issue on the Volt (bulletin 18-NA-342)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Battery too cold message in mild weather
Strongly reduced charging and electric power

P0ACE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0ACE.summary: P0ACE flags erratic behaviour of battery temperature sensor C, meaning the reading jumps faster than the heavy battery mass could ever warm or cool. In GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables the controller sums the absolute changes of the sensor value across a 10-sample window taken every 100 ms; a sum above 10 fails the window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 store the code as Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Loose terminal or unlatched connector at sensor C
Partly broken sensor wire inside the pack
Fault on the battery sensing board affecting several inputs

symptoms: Hybrid warning light that appears intermittently
Sensor C value jumps in live data

P0ACF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit/Open
P0ACF.summary: Air-cooled traction batteries can use several blowers; P0ACF belongs to the third one and means the battery controller sees an open or otherwise invalid control line while it drives fan 3. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15.2.3)(B) requires the electrical inputs and outputs of the battery thermal management to be monitored like other comprehensive components.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at fan 3
Broken control wire between battery controller and fan 3
Fan motor or its built-in driver open internally
Fan output stage in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning light, often with check engine light
Electric drive power reduced when the battery gets warm
No fan noise from the battery area when cooling is expected

P0AD0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Performance/Stuck Off
P0AD0.summary: P0AD0 is a functional fault: the control line of battery fan 3 may be electrically fine, but the blower does not deliver what was commanded, or stays still. Depending on design, the controller compares fan speed feedback with the request, or, as a Honda patent describes, compares the expected battery temperature change for the known cooling capacity with the measured one.

causes.text: Fan intake or duct blocked by dirt, pet hair or objects (often under or beside a seat)
Worn bearings or debris slowing the fan wheel
Speed feedback signal from fan 3 missing or implausible
Weak 12 V supply or poor ground at the fan

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning light
Power or regeneration limited after longer drives or in heat
Battery temperature rises faster than usual

P0AD1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Stuck On
P0AD1.summary: P0AD1 is the counterpart to P0AD0: fan 3 of the traction battery keeps turning although the controller has switched it off or commanded a lower level. A speed feedback or the current in the fan circuit shows that the blower still runs.

causes.text: Fan output stage in battery controller or fan module stuck on
Control wire chafed against a supply voltage
Fan relay contacts welded (relay-switched designs)

symptoms: Battery fan audible after the vehicle is switched off

P0AD2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit Low
P0AD2.summary: P0AD2 reports that the control signal for battery fan 3 is pulled too low, typically a short to ground on the line between battery controller and blower. Such fans are mostly speed-controlled by a PWM duty cycle, as a Toyota patent on battery fan control explains.

causes.text: Control wire chafed through to body ground
Internal short in fan 3 motor or its electronics
Moisture or spilled liquid in the fan connector
Output stage in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning light, often with check engine light
Electric drive power reduced when the battery gets warm
No fan noise from the battery area when cooling is expected

P0AD3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit High
P0AD3.summary: With P0AD3 the battery controller finds the control line of cooling fan 3 at a voltage that is too high for the commanded state, pointing to a short to a supply voltage or a fan input that no longer pulls the line down. No manufacturer publicly documents this code; GM's analogous fan 1 code P0A85 trips when the control voltage exceeds 9 V while the fan is driven, Type B.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to 12 V or another supply
Fan electronics no longer loading the control line
Bent or bridged pins in the fan connector
Battery controller output stage defective

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning light
Fan 3 runs constantly or not at all
Reduced electric power when the battery is warm

P0AD4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Flow System Insufficient Air Flow
P0AD4.summary: P0AD4 is a system-level check of air-cooled traction batteries: the controller concludes that too little air passes the cells, for example because the cell temperatures rise faster than the commanded fan level allows, as a Honda fan diagnosis patent describes. CARB 1968.2 asks for a functional check of the battery cooling performance where feasible.

causes.text: Cabin air intake grille or duct of the battery blocked (bags, clothing, dust, pet hair)
Battery air filter clogged, where fitted
Battery fan running too slowly
Battery controller software sets the code falsely (Ram eTorque, fixed by update)

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Reduced electric assist or start-stop not available
Battery fan runs loud for long periods

P0AD5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Flow Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P0AD5.summary: Some air-cooled battery packs route their cooling air through a motorized flap that switches between cabin air, recirculation or an outlet. P0AD5 means the battery controller finds the drive circuit of this valve A open or otherwise faulty.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at the flap actuator
Broken wire in the actuator harness
Actuator motor winding open
Output stage in battery controller defective

symptoms: Hybrid warning, electric drive may be switched off
Battery temperature not controlled as usual

P0AD6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Flow Valve A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0AD6.summary: P0AD6 flags that the air flow valve A of the battery cooling does not behave as expected: the circuit is intact, but position, travel or the learned end stops do not fit the command. Audi documents exactly this code as P0AD600 on the 2012-15 Q5 hybrid (TSB 2038152): a software error made the battery management module J841 lose the learned end stops of the air supply valve, electric and hybrid drive were disabled, and a software update to version 0543 fixed it.

causes.text: Battery controller software loses learned end stops (Audi Q5 hybrid, fixed by update)
Flap binding from dirt or a deformed duct
Actuator gears or position feedback worn
End stops not relearned after battery or actuator work

symptoms: Hybrid drive system error message in the cluster
Electric and hybrid operation no longer available

P0AD7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Flow Valve A Control Circuit Low
P0AD7.summary: P0AD7 sets when the control circuit of the battery air flow valve A reads too low a voltage, usually a short to ground in the line or actuator. The valve is a motorized flap in the battery cooling duct, as in the Audi Q5 hybrid cooling module, whose bulletin covers the range/performance sibling P0AD6.

causes.text: Actuator control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the flap actuator
Moisture in the actuator connector
Battery controller output stage defective

symptoms: Hybrid warning, electric drive may be switched off
Battery temperature not controlled as usual

P0AD8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Air Flow Valve A Control Circuit High
P0AD8.summary: With P0AD8 the battery controller sees too high a voltage in the drive circuit of air flow valve A, typically a short to a supply voltage or an actuator that no longer draws current. The component is the motorized flap that directs cooling air through an air-cooled traction battery, documented for example in Audi's Q5 hybrid bulletin on the related code P0AD6.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Actuator no longer loading the circuit
Bridged or bent pins in the connector
Battery controller output stage defective

symptoms: Hybrid warning, electric drive may be switched off
Battery temperature not controlled as usual

P0AD9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Control Circuit/Open
P0AD9.summary: The positive main contactor connects the traction battery to the high-voltage bus; its coil is driven by the battery or hybrid controller. P0AD9 covers an open in this coil circuit.

causes.text: Open in the contactor coil or its pigtail inside the battery disconnect unit
Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the battery disconnect unit
Broken control wire in the battery harness
High-side driver in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or start
Hybrid or EV warning light and check engine light

P0ADA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0ADA.summary: P0ADA describes a positive contactor coil circuit that is electrically present but does not behave plausibly: coil current, voltage or response time outside the expected window, for instance due to high resistance or an unstable PWM hold signal. No manufacturer publicly documents this code; GM, which details the positive contactor driver codes P0AD9, P0ADB and P0ADC with Type B logic and sample counters, does not list P0ADA.

causes.text: High resistance in coil wiring or connector (corrosion, fretting)
Contactor coil degraded or partially shorted
Low 12 V supply during contactor closing
Battery controller fault or software

symptoms: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or start
Hybrid or EV warning light and check engine light

P0ADB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Control Circuit Low
P0ADB.summary: P0ADB means the drive circuit of the positive main contactor reads too low, mostly a short to ground. GM uses it widely: 2016-19 tables set it when the control voltage stays under 5.35 V with the contactor commanded on, 13 of 16 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Coil control wire shorted to ground
Contactor coil internally shorted
Battery controller software sets the code (Audi, Dodge bulletins)
Driver stage in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle does not start; multiple warnings in the cluster

P0ADC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Positive Contactor Control Circuit High
P0ADC.summary: P0ADC indicates that the positive contactor drive circuit carries too much voltage for the commanded state, usually a short to battery voltage. In GM's 2016-19 hybrid tables the driver output, with the contactor commanded off, reads between 5.27 and 19.7 V for 40 of 50 samples at 12.5 ms, Type B with two trips.

causes.text: Coil control wire shorted to 12 V
Damaged harness or connector at the battery disconnect unit
Driver stage in the battery controller shorted

symptoms: High-voltage system disabled, vehicle not ready

P0ADD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Control Circuit/Open
P0ADD.summary: The negative main contactor closes the return path of the traction battery; P0ADD reports an open in its coil drive circuit. GM documents the code in parallel to the positive side: tables since model year 2011 detect open load in the HPC2 and store it after two trips; 2016-19 tables evaluate a control voltage between 1.15 and 2.81 V while off, 40 of 50 samples, Type B, and 2019 tables add a coil current check below 194 mA when on.

causes.text: Open in negative contactor coil or its pigtail
Loose or corroded connector at the battery disconnect unit
Broken control wire in the battery harness
Driver in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or start
Hybrid or EV warning light and check engine light

P0ADE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0ADE.summary: P0ADE is set when the coil circuit of the negative main contactor works electrically but its values are implausible, such as coil current or hold voltage out of range or a slow response after the command. No manufacturer publicly documents this code; GM, whose tables cover the negative contactor driver codes P0ADD, P0ADF and P0AE0 in detail, does not use P0ADE.

causes.text: High resistance in coil wiring or connector
Negative contactor coil degraded
Weak 12 V battery during start-up
Battery controller fault or software

symptoms: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or start
Hybrid or EV warning light and check engine light

P0ADF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Control Circuit Low
P0ADF.summary: P0ADF reports that the drive circuit of the negative main contactor is pulled too low, typically a short to ground in the coil line. GM documents the code in its 2016-19 hybrid tables: control voltage below 5.35 V while the contactor is commanded on, 13 of 16 samples at 12.5 ms (20 of 25 in one 2016 group), Type B with two trips, enabled above about 9 to 10 V on the 12 V system.

causes.text: Coil control wire shorted to ground
Negative contactor coil internally shorted
Moisture in the battery disconnect unit connector
Driver in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or start
Hybrid or EV warning light and check engine light

P0AE0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Negative Contactor Control Circuit High
P0AE0.summary: P0AE0 is stored when the negative contactor drive circuit shows too high a voltage for its state, which mostly means a short to battery voltage. GM's 2016-19 hybrid tables set it with the contactor commanded off and the driver output between 5.27 and 19.7 V for 40 of 50 samples at 12.5 ms, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Coil control wire shorted to 12 V
Damaged harness or connector at the battery disconnect unit
Driver stage in the battery controller shorted

symptoms: High-voltage system disabled, vehicle not ready

P0AE1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor Circuit
P0AE1.summary: Before the main contactors close, a precharge contactor routes battery current through a resistor so the inverter capacitors fill slowly instead of drawing a damaging inrush. P0AE1 is the general fault of this precharge path when it is not split into stuck closed (P0AE2), stuck open (P0AE3) or a driver fault (P0AE4 to P0AE7).

causes.text: Defective solder joint in the motor power inverter (Honda IMA)
Precharge contactor or precharge resistor failed
Fault logged by battery controller software after an interrupted charging sequence
Wiring or connector fault in the contactor circuit

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning in the cluster
Vehicle does not become ready to drive

P0AE2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed
P0AE2.summary: P0AE2 means the precharge path conducts although it should be open, for example welded contacts or a precharge switch that no longer turns off. GM's 2011 Volt table checks it once per precharge event: if the bus voltage already exceeds 80 % of pack voltage before precharge begins, the precharge FET is judged stuck closed, 4 of 4 samples, Type A with MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Precharge contactor contacts welded or precharge switch shorted
Battery controller software sets the code falsely (Audi, Stellantis bulletins)
Contactor driver held on by a short to power
Bus voltage not discharged before the next precharge

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
MIL and hybrid or EV warning on
Wrench symbol or service message in the cluster

P0AE3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor Circuit Stuck Open
P0AE3.summary: P0AE3 is set when the precharge path does not conduct after it has been commanded closed, so the bus voltage fails to rise and the main contactors are not allowed to close. GM documents several cases: preliminary information PIC6165A for the 2016-17 Chevrolet Volt describes a rare P0AE3 in cool weather right after a completed charge, without driveability effects; parts should not be replaced, a new calibration followed, and the MIL goes out after three clean drive cycles.

causes.text: Battery controller calibration sets the code under certain conditions (GM Volt, Audi)
Precharge contactor contacts burnt or coil not pulling in
Precharge resistor or its fuse open
Internal fault in the battery disconnect unit

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
MIL or service engine soon light on
No battery charge level shown after switching on

P0AE4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor A Control Circuit/Open
P0AE4.summary: P0AE4 concerns the circuit that drives the coil of precharge contactor A, not its contacts. GM uses it in many hybrid and EV tables, with changing logic: the 2016 and 2019 OBDG02 tables look for an open high-side driver circuit, a control voltage between 1.15 and 2.81 V while commanded off, 40 of 50 samples at 12.5 ms, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Open control wire or loose connector at the contactor coil
Precharge contactor coil open internally
Control wire shorted to 12 V (GM 2011 and 2019 logic)
Driver stage in the battery or hybrid controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
MIL and hybrid or EV warning on

P0AE5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0AE5.summary: P0AE5 reports that the precharge function works electrically but does not deliver the expected result, so the controller judges the circuit implausible. Ford documents it in special service message SSM 47129: 2013-18 C-MAX and Fusion Hybrid and Energi models and the MKZ Hybrid may not start, with P0AE5 stored in the battery energy control module.

causes.text: High-voltage consumer with low internal resistance (DC/DC converter, coolant heater, A/C compressor)
Precharge resistor degraded or wrong value
Precharge contactor responding slowly or with high contact resistance

symptoms: Vehicle does not start or become ready
Red warning triangle or hybrid warning in the cluster
Possible additional codes from the faulty high-voltage consumer

P0AE6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor A Control Circuit Low
P0AE6.summary: P0AE6 means the control line of precharge contactor A is pulled too low, usually a short to ground. GM documents it in several programs.

causes.text: Control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Precharge contactor coil shorted internally
Open circuit on low-side driven designs (GM eAssist)
Driver stage in the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Engine start or electric drive unavailable

P0AE7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor A Control Circuit High
P0AE7.summary: P0AE7 is stored when the control line of precharge contactor A carries too much voltage for its commanded state, typically a short to the 12 V supply. In GM's 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables the high-side driver output reads between 5.27 and 19.7 V while the contactor is commanded off, 40 of 50 samples at 12.5 ms, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to 12 V supply
Driver stage stuck on in the battery controller
Outdated battery controller calibration

symptoms: Vehicle may not start or become ready

P0AE8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P0AE8.summary: Battery temperature sensor D is a further thermistor inside the high-voltage pack; GM's Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the matching codes as temperature sensor 4 of nine. P0AE8 is the general circuit code for it, used when the controller finds an electrical fault without classifying it as low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Poor contact or damaged wire between sensor D and sensing board
Temperature sensor D failed
Fault in the battery controller input stage

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
Further battery sensor codes may be stored

P0AE9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P0AE9.summary: P0AE9 is the plausibility check for battery temperature sensor D, GM's sensor 4: its reading is compared with the other pack sensors. In GM's 2016 and 2019 tables it fails when the value is more than 25 °C away from the average of the others in 50 of 67 samples; the two-mode hybrid tables of 2011 and 2013 use more than 15 °C in 90 of 100; the eAssist table 13OBDG05C allows 8.55 °C after a long module off time; GM's 2018 table uses 20 °C for 5 s within 6.7 s.

causes.text: Outdated controller software (GM Volt, bulletin 18-NA-342)
Temperature sensor D drifting out of tolerance
Genuine local temperature difference in one battery module
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips
Battery Too Cold message despite mild weather (Volt)
Reduced charge and electric drive power

P0AEA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P0AEA.summary: P0AEA means the voltage of battery temperature sensor D is below its valid range. GM uses NTC thermistors with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a low voltage reads as an extremely hot cell, usually from a short to ground.

causes.text: Sensor D signal wire shorted to ground
Temperature sensor D internally shorted
Outdated controller software (GM Volt, bulletin 18-NA-342)
Moisture or damage on the battery sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips
Charge and drive power strongly limited
Battery cooling running more than usual

P0AEB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P0AEB.summary: P0AEB reports that battery temperature sensor D delivers a voltage above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensors this reads as extreme cold, pointing to an open wire, a backed-out pin at the sensing board or a cracked thermistor.

causes.text: Open circuit or unplugged connector at sensor D
Outdated controller software (GM Volt, bulletin 18-NA-342)
Temperature sensor D open internally

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips

P0AEC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AEC.summary: P0AEC flags erratic behaviour of battery temperature sensor D: the reading jumps faster than the heavy battery mass could ever warm or cool. GM documents the method in its 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables.

causes.text: Loose terminal or connector not fully latched at sensor D
Partly broken or chafed sensor wire
Fault on the battery sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips, may go out again
Jumping battery temperature in live data

P0AED.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0AED.summary: The inverter of an electric drive motor carries thermistors near its power switches so the controller can derate before the IGBTs overheat. In GM's hybrid tables, inverter temperature sensor A is the phase U sensor of the inverter for motor A.

causes.text: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp

P0AEE.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0AEE.summary: P0AEE checks whether inverter temperature sensor A reads sensibly. GM's 2016 to 2019 tables compare it after a cold soak with an average temperature of the vehicle; more than 20 °C apart sets Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Controller software error (Audi Q5/A7 e quattro bulletin)
Inverter temperature sensor A drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module (e.g. Honda MPI solder joints)
Uneven inverter cooling after soak

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often without drivability change
Vehicle may not start in hybrid mode

P0AEF.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0AEF.summary: P0AEF means the signal of inverter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. GM describes it as an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a low voltage reads as an impossibly hot inverter, usually a short to ground or an internal sensor fault.

causes.text: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Electric drive power cut back strongly
Vehicle may not start (Jeep Compass PHEV)

P0AF0.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0AF0.summary: P0AF0 reports a signal from inverter temperature sensor A above its valid range, which for an NTC sensor reads as an extremely cold inverter: open wire, lost ground or a broken sensor. GM's 2016 to 2019 hybrid tables set it below -50 °C for 2.6 of 3.65 s, but only after at least 90 s of inverter warm-up at 20 Nm or more, so a really cold car does not trigger it; Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Motor control unit software (Kia Sorento Hybrid 2025)
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Traction motor noise or inoperative A/C (Kia)

P0AF1.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AF1.summary: P0AF1 is meant for an inverter temperature sensor A signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing permanently. Inverter heat sinks are liquid-cooled and change temperature smoothly, so sudden steps point to a contact problem or an internal fault in the sensing circuit.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Electrical interference on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0AF2.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P0AF2.summary: Inverter temperature sensor B is, in GM's hybrid tables, the phase U thermistor of the second inverter, the one that drives motor B in two-motor systems. P0AF2 is its general circuit code for an electrical fault that the controller does not narrow down to low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive or generator power
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

P0AF3.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0AF3.summary: P0AF3 is the plausibility test for inverter temperature sensor B, the phase U sensor of GM's motor B inverter. In the 2016 to 2019 tables the sensor is compared after a cold soak with a calculated average vehicle temperature; a difference above 20 °C sets the code, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Inverter temperature sensor B drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module
Uneven inverter coolant flow after soak

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips
Further inverter temperature codes may be stored

P0AF4.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P0AF4.summary: P0AF4 reports a signal of inverter temperature sensor B below the valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up, so a low voltage reads as an inverter far hotter than possible, usually from a short to ground or an internal sensor fault in the motor B inverter.

causes.text: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning

P0AF5.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P0AF5.summary: P0AF5 means inverter temperature sensor B delivers a voltage above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor that equals an implausibly cold inverter, so an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked thermistor is likely.

causes.text: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two trips
Implausibly cold inverter temperature in live data

P0AF6.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0AF6.summary: P0AF6 targets an inverter temperature sensor B signal that jumps or drops out briefly. Since the heat sink of the motor B inverter is liquid-cooled and warms or cools gradually, abrupt changes in the reading indicate a contact problem or an intermittent fault in the sensing circuit rather than real temperature.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Electrical interference on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief reductions of motor B power
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0AF7.title: 14 Volt Power Module Internal Temperature Too High
P0AF7.summary: The 14 V power module is the DC/DC converter that feeds the 12 V network from the high-voltage battery in hybrids and EVs. P0AF7 reports that its internal temperature has exceeded the protection limit, a real overheat rather than a sensor circuit fault.

causes.text: Restricted cooling, weak coolant pump or failed cooling fan
Sustained high 12 V load or weak 12 V battery
Internal fault of the DC/DC converter

symptoms: Warning lamp or 12 V charging warning

P0AF8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage
P0AF8.summary: P0AF8 compares the battery pack voltage reported by the battery controller with an independent measurement on the high-voltage bus. GM calls it system voltage correlation: with the contactors closed, the 2019 tables fail it when the pack reading differs from the inverter bus voltage by more than 13.95 V, or from the charger bus voltage by more than 14.95 V, 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms, Type A.

causes.text: Loose or arcing high-voltage battery cable connection
Pack or bus voltage sensing circuit inaccurate
Low 12 V supply or loose 12 V power fuse affecting the measuring modules
High resistance in a pack fuse or main contactor

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning on
Battery saver or low battery message
Intermittent no crank or reduced hybrid power

P0AF9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage Unstable
P0AF9.summary: P0AF9 is meant for a traction battery voltage that fluctuates more than load changes can explain, for example through a loose terminal, an intermittent contactor or a cell group that collapses under load. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM, for instance, covers system voltage with P0AF8 (correlation), P0AFA and P0AFB (low and high), and reports uneven cell groups as P0BBE pack voltage variation, which bulletin 19-NA-117 ties to degraded cells in the Volt and ELR.

causes.text: Loose high-voltage terminal or busbar connection
Degraded cell group collapsing under load
Main contactor with intermittent contact

symptoms: Code may come and go without lasting symptoms

P0AFA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage Low
P0AFA.summary: P0AFA protects the traction battery from deep discharge: the pack voltage, or in some versions any cell voltage, has fallen below a temperature-dependent limit. GM's 2016 and 2019 tables set it after 320 of 400 samples (about 10 s) for the pack or 112 of 140 for a cell, Type A, and latch it so that only a technician command can clear it.

causes.text: Degraded or self-discharging cell groups
Pack drained by repeated failed engine starts or long standing
Open high-voltage fuse or manual disconnect
Loose or high-resistance ground on 48 V systems

symptoms: Vehicle does not start; restart blocked while the code is latched
Reduced or lost propulsion before the no-start

P0AFB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage High
P0AFB.summary: P0AFB guards against overcharging: the pack voltage, or a single cell, exceeds a temperature-dependent upper limit. GM's 2016 and 2019 tables use 320 of 400 samples (about 10 s) for the pack and 112 of 140 for a cell, Type A, and latch the code until a technician clears it by command; the 2011 Volt table also uses Type A.

causes.text: Loose or arcing battery cable causing voltage spikes
Control unit software allows overvoltage (Mercedes 48 V bulletins)
Cell imbalance so that one cell overcharges
Faulty voltage sensing reporting too high a value

symptoms: Possible no crank on mild hybrids

P0AFC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Sensor Module
P0AFC.summary: Some hybrid packs carry a separate sensor module that measures block voltages and passes them to the battery controller; Toyota calls it the battery voltage sensor or battery smart unit. P0AFC reports a fault of this module itself, such as a failed self-check or disturbed data transfer.

causes.text: Radio interference from an aftermarket antenna near the battery (Toyota Camry Hybrid)
Battery voltage sensor module internally defective
Supply or communication wiring of the sensor module faulty

symptoms: MIL and check hybrid system warning on
Code may return when the radio transmitter is used

P0AFD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Temperature Too Low
P0AFD.summary: P0AFD indicates that the traction battery is colder than its permitted operating range. At very low temperatures cell resistance rises and charging risks lithium plating, so the controller restricts or blocks charging and discharging.

causes.text: Vehicle parked unplugged in extreme cold
Battery heater or coolant heater not working
Temperature sensor reading too cold (sensor or software)

symptoms: Battery too cold message in the cluster
Reduced electric power or electric drive unavailable
Charging slow or not possible until the pack warms up

P0AFE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Voltage Too Low for Voltage Step Up Conversion
P0AFE.summary: Many hybrids raise the battery voltage with a step-up (boost) converter before it reaches the inverters; Toyota's second-generation Hybrid Synergy Drive, for example, boosts a pack of around 200 V to 500 V or more. The converter needs a minimum input voltage to reach its target without excessive current.

causes.text: Pack deeply discharged or weak under load
High-resistance connection between battery and converter
Converter input voltage measured too low

symptoms: Engine runs more often than usual

P0AFF.title: System Voltage Too Low for Voltage Step Down Conversion
P0AFF.summary: A step-down (buck) DC/DC converter, often called the accessory power module, supplies the 12 V system from the high-voltage or 48 V bus. To regulate its output it needs an input voltage above a minimum.

causes.text: High-voltage or 48 V bus voltage too low (discharged pack, open contactor)
High-resistance input connection or fuse of the DC/DC converter
DC/DC converter internal measuring fault

symptoms: Battery or charging system warning light
12 V battery discharges, electrical consumers fail

P0B00.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current
P0B00.summary: P0B00 is the general fault for phase U of the three-phase motor that drives the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump, the pump that keeps line pressure while the engine is stopped. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or unlatched phase U connection at the pump motor
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty (shunt or phase sensor)
Power stage of phase U in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase U of the pump motor

symptoms: Engine auto-stop disabled or no electric drive mode
Delayed engagement or harsh restart after a stop

P0B01.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current Low
P0B01.summary: P0B01 means the pump inverter sees almost no current in phase U of the auxiliary fluid pump motor, typically an open phase. GM documents the check for the Volt motor control processor (2016) and its hybrid tables of 2018 and 2019: with the drive state in Run, the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 5 A2 (2016) or 14.97 A2 (2018), the peak current on the U axis is compared while the rotor is within 30 degrees of it; below 1 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, the code sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase U lead or terminal of the pump motor cable
Phase U switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in the pump motor

symptoms: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Propulsion Power Reduced or Vehicle Speed Limited message

P0B02.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current High
P0B02.summary: P0B02 reports excessive current in phase U of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor, an overcurrent condition that the pump inverter must cut off to protect its switches. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Phase U lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase U of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled
Harsh or delayed engagement after an engine stop

P0B03.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current
P0B03.summary: P0B03 covers a general current fault in phase V of the brushless motor of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump. No manufacturer publicly describes a monitor for it.

causes.text: Poor contact in the phase V lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase V power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase V of the pump motor

symptoms: Engine auto-stop or electric mode no longer available

P0B04.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current Low
P0B04.summary: P0B04 indicates that phase V of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries too little current, usually because the phase is open somewhere between inverter and winding. GM tests it on the Volt (2016) and in the 2018 and 2019 hybrid tables like its U and W siblings: in Run, with normal PWM, more than 50 V on the inverter and a minimum squared current command, the V current is sampled while the rotor sits within 30 degrees of the V axis.

causes.text: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase V lead or terminal
Phase V switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in the pump motor

symptoms: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Reduced propulsion power or limited vehicle speed

P0B05.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current High
P0B05.summary: P0B05 flags overcurrent in phase V of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publicly documents this specific code.

causes.text: Phase V lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump seized or contaminated, motor draws excess current
Pump restart logic in the inverter software causing overcurrent
Shorted turns in phase V of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Loss of propulsion or no-start in severe cases

P0B06.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current
P0B06.summary: P0B06 is the general current fault for phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publishes a monitor description for this exact code.

causes.text: Poor contact in the phase W lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase W power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase W of the pump motor

symptoms: Engine keeps running at stops, no auto-stop

P0B07.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current Low
P0B07.summary: P0B07 means phase W of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries less current than commanded, the typical sign of an open W path. GM uses it on the Volt and later hybrids: below 1 A peak W-axis current for 0.4 s of 0.6 s, with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V, sets a Type A fault.

causes.text: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase W lead or terminal
Outdated inverter software (Cadillac CT6 plug-in, service update 18199)
Open winding of phase W in the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon light
Loss of propulsion, vehicle shutdown or no-start

P0B08.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current High
P0B08.summary: P0B08 is set when the current in phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor rises above the permitted limit. No manufacturer documents this exact code in public sources.

causes.text: Phase W lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase W of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled

P0B09.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0B09.summary: P0B09 concerns the power feed of auxiliary pump A's motor: the controller sees no valid supply voltage, usually because the circuit is open. GM documents it for its 2012-13 eAssist mild hybrids (BAS Plus): the hardware input reports an out-of-range voltage flag on the auxiliary pump circuit, enabled with ignition voltage above 9 V; failing for at least 0.375 s within a 1.2 s sample sets P0B09 as Type B, MIL after two trips.

causes.text: Blown fuse or open relay in the pump supply
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the pump connector
Poor ground connection of the pump motor
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

symptoms: Shift flare or delayed drive engagement on restart

P0B0A.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0B0A.summary: P0B0A means the supply voltage measured at the motor of auxiliary pump A is lower than expected while the pump should be running. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's eAssist tables only cover the open-circuit case as P0B09.

causes.text: Corroded terminal or high resistance in the pump feed or ground
Weak 12 V battery or poor charging
DC/DC converter or alternator output too low (hybrid)
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

symptoms: Jerky drive-off after an engine stop

P0B0B.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0B0B.summary: P0B0B reports a supply voltage at the motor of auxiliary pump A that is above the expected range. Subaru documents it on the 2014-15 XV Crosstrek Hybrid (bulletin 16-94-15R), together with P172A: a leaking O-ring at the electric oil pump relief valve can let CVT fluid into the pump motor.

causes.text: CVT fluid entering the pump motor via a leaking relief valve O-ring (Subaru XV Crosstrek Hybrid)
Supply circuit shorted to a higher voltage source
Oil pump inverter or its voltage sensing faulty

symptoms: Warning lamp on, hybrid or CVT function restricted
Possibly P0C79 stored at the same time

P0B0C.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Hydraulic Leakage
P0B0C.summary: P0B0C says the circuit fed by auxiliary pump A loses pressure through a leak, so the pump cannot hold the demanded pressure. Stellantis documents it as P0B0C 7A for the 2023-26 Jeep Avenger and 2026 Compass with hybrid dual-clutch transmission outside the US (TSB 21-061-26): an internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston causes jerking and power loss and may stop the engine from restarting after a stop; with P07E4 or P07E6 present and more than 5 km on the clock, the piston or the transmission is replaced.

causes.text: Internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston (Jeep Avenger/Compass hybrid DCT)
Worn seal or valve leaking inside the hydraulic circuit
External leak and low transmission fluid level
Internal wear of the auxiliary pump

symptoms: Jerking and loss of power while driving
Engine fails to restart after a stop
Transmission warning, possibly with P07E4 or P07E6

P0B0D.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Control Module
P0B0D.summary: P0B0D is an internal fault of the module that drives the auxiliary pump motor. GM documents it for the auxiliary transmission pump controller (ATPC) in its 2011 and 2014 hybrid tables and for the 2016 Cadillac ELR: it checks processor integrity, such as SPI hardware faults or a wrong seed and key between processors, with more than 9.5 V supply; 28 failures out of 32 samples in a 6.25 ms loop, detected within about 200 ms, set a Type A fault.

causes.text: Electric pump with integrated control electronics failed (Jeep 4xe 8P75PH)
Processor or memory fault inside the pump control module
Supply voltage dips or poor ground at the module

symptoms: Possibly lost communication with the pump module (U0287)

P0B0E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit
P0B0E.summary: Many packs measure current with two channels or two sensors so the controller can cross-check them; sensor B is the second channel next to sensor A (P0ABF to P0AC3). P0B0E is its general circuit code.

causes.text: Signal or ground wire of channel B damaged or connector loose
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective
Sensor supply voltage faulty
Battery ECU input defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric assist

P0B0F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B0F.summary: P0B0F flags a current sensor B signal that is electrically in range but implausible, for example an offset at zero current or a value that does not match the other measurement. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Current sensor B offset drift or ageing
Ground offset or high resistance in the sensor wiring
Sensor displaced on the busbar or magnetic interference

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL possible
State of charge jumps or drifts

P0B10.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Low
P0B10.summary: P0B10 means the output of current sensor B lies below its valid range. GM uses a dual-range Hall sensor whose channel B covers small currents with high resolution: the 2019 battery energy control module table sets P0B10 when this fine current reads below -24 A (ADC count under 82) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the 2011 Volt table uses -23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip.

causes.text: Sensor B signal line shorted to ground
5 V supply of the current sensor missing
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery charge and discharge power limited
Engine runs more often, fuel use rises

P0B11.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit High
P0B11.summary: P0B11 is set when current sensor B delivers a signal above its valid range. In GM's dual-range design, channel B is the fine channel for small currents: the 2019 battery energy control module table fails it above +24 A (ADC count over 4013) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and the 2011 Volt table above +23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip.

causes.text: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply or 12 V
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric driving

P0B12.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B12.summary: P0B12 covers a current sensor B signal that jumps or drops out in a way real current cannot, typically from a loose connector, a chafed signal wire or noise on the sensor ground. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Loose connector or poor terminal contact at the current sensor
Chafed signal or ground wire
Electrical noise on the sensor ground

P0B13.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A/B Correlation
P0B13.summary: P0B13 compares the two pack current readings, sensor A and sensor B, and sets when they disagree. On the Chevrolet Volt GM pairs a coarse and a fine channel: the code fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, for example 10 s within a 12.5 s window (2016) or 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms (2019), Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Battery controller software fault, fixed by update (Audi, GM)
Disturbance from an external charging station during charging
Offset drift of one of the two current channels
Internal communication fault between switching unit and current sensor

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Red battery or Service High Voltage message, request to stop safely
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B14.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B14.summary: SAE J2012 reserves up to four pack voltage measurements, A to D; voltage sense B is the second one. P0B14 is its general circuit code: the battery controller sees an electrical fault on this input, typically an open or implausible raw signal.

causes.text: Voltage sense lead or its fuse open inside the pack
Sense connector at the battery controller loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B15.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B15.summary: P0B15 marks pack voltage measurement B as electrically valid but implausible: the value lies within the sensor range yet does not match a reference, typically the sum of the cell voltages or another pack measurement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel B
Faulty cell voltage acquisition distorts the reference sum
Increased contact resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B16.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B16.summary: P0B16 sets when pack voltage measurement B reports a value below its plausible minimum, usually an electrical cause such as a sense lead shorted to ground or an open input that pulls the reading down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Sense lead of channel B shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B17.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B17.summary: P0B17 means pack voltage measurement B reads above its plausible maximum. Mercedes-Benz uses this exact code on the eSprinter 907: inaccurate BMS measurements can store P0B171C, voltage sensor B in the high-voltage battery module shorted to positive with the value out of range, together with P0ABD00 for sensor A.

causes.text: BMS measurement inaccuracy, fixed by software update (Mercedes eSprinter)
Sense lead of channel B shorted to a higher potential
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B18.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B18.summary: P0B18 reports that pack voltage measurement B jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. The controller detects implausibly fast changes or short signal losses that disappear again, so the fault often shows up as a history code.

causes.text: Loose or corroded sense connector
Sense lead chafed, intermittent contact
Battery controller software misinterprets transients

symptoms: Warning appears and disappears, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B19.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B19.summary: Voltage sense C is the third of up to four pack voltage measurements defined in SAE J2012. P0B19 is its general circuit code and sets when the battery controller finds this input electrically unusable, for instance open or without a valid raw value.

causes.text: Voltage sense lead C or its fuse open
Sense connector loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B1A.summary: P0B1A flags pack voltage measurement C as in range but not believable. The controller compares it with a reference, usually the sum of the cell voltages or another pack voltage reading, and sets the code when the difference stays too large.

causes.text: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel C
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Increased resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B1B.summary: P0B1B sets when pack voltage measurement C delivers a reading below its plausible lower limit. Typical electrical causes are a sense lead shorted to ground, an open fuse or resistor in the sense path, or a defective controller input.

causes.text: Sense lead of channel C shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B1C.summary: P0B1C reports that pack voltage measurement C reads above its plausible upper limit. Usually the measurement path is at fault, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a defective controller input or a software error in the evaluation, rather than a real overvoltage of the pack.

causes.text: Sense lead of channel C shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B1D.summary: P0B1D stands for an unsteady pack voltage measurement C: the signal jumps, drops out for moments or changes faster than a real battery voltage can. Because the fault often clears itself, it is frequently found only as a stored code.

causes.text: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact
Controller software misinterprets transients

symptoms: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B1E.summary: Voltage sense D is the fourth and last pack voltage measurement in the SAE J2012 scheme. P0B1E is its general circuit code: the battery controller treats this input as electrically faulty, for example open or without a usable raw signal.

causes.text: Voltage sense lead D or its fuse open
Sense connector loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
P0B1F.summary: P0B1F says pack voltage measurement D is electrically present but disagrees with what the controller expects, typically the sum of cell voltages or a parallel pack measurement. It is a plausibility fault, not an open or shorted circuit.

causes.text: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel D
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Increased resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B20.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
P0B20.summary: P0B20 sets when pack voltage measurement D falls below its plausible minimum. The cause is usually electrical: a sense lead shorted to ground, an interrupted fuse or resistor in the measurement path, or a damaged controller input.

causes.text: Sense lead of channel D shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B21.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit High
P0B21.summary: P0B21 means pack voltage measurement D reports more than its plausible maximum. As with the other high codes, the measurement path is the main suspect, for example a sense lead shorted to a higher potential, a faulty input stage or an evaluation error in software, not an actual overcharged pack.

causes.text: Sense lead of channel D shorted to a higher potential
Evaluation error in battery controller software
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B22.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B22.summary: P0B22 completes the voltage sense D series and reports an intermittent or erratic pack voltage measurement D: the reading jumps, drops out briefly or changes implausibly fast, then recovers. Current code lists title it this way; the older label Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit does not belong to this number.

causes.text: Loose or corroded sense connector or terminal
Chafed sense lead with intermittent contact
Controller software misinterprets transients

symptoms: Warning comes and goes, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B23.title: Hybrid/EV Battery A Voltage
P0B23.summary: P0B23 is the general fault for the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A, the first of up to four sub-batteries or energy stores (A to D) that the battery controller evaluates separately; which physical unit carries the letter is up to the manufacturer. The code says that the measured voltage of this unit no longer fits the expected value, without the finer split into unstable (P0B24), low (P0B25) or high (P0B26).

causes.text: Weak or failing cells or module in battery A
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery A
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B24.title: Hybrid/EV Battery A Voltage Unstable
P0B24.summary: P0B24 reports that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is unstable: it swings or jumps more than the battery controller accepts instead of staying steadily too low or too high (P0B25, P0B26). Stellantis lists P0B24-00 with MIL on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe, together with pack voltage variation, cell balancing and state-of-health codes; the cure is new software for the battery pack control module or, on the 2025 Wrangler, for the hybrid control processor.

causes.text: Battery controller software (Jeep 4xe BPCM/HCP, Ford BECM updates)
Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery A
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery A

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent

P0B25.title: Hybrid/EV Battery A Voltage Low
P0B25.summary: P0B25 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A drops below the window the controller expects. Bentley uses it in two different systems.

causes.text: Internal fault of the energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Aged or unbalanced cells pulling the unit voltage down
Deep discharge after long standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B26.title: Hybrid/EV Battery A Voltage High
P0B26.summary: P0B26 means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery A is above the permitted value. Bentley documents it in the 48 V Dynamic Ride system of the Continental GT and Flying Spur, stored in address 0021 with symptom code 28672; the prescribed repair is replacing the super capacitor.

causes.text: Failing energy store, e.g. Bentley 48 V super capacitor
Cell group charged too high, balancing not effective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Bentley Dynamic Ride fault warning, roll control inactive
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on

P0B27.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage
P0B27.summary: P0B27 is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery B, the second separately monitored sub-battery or energy store. It covers a voltage that does not match expectation without saying whether it is unstable (P0B28), too low (P0B29) or too high (P0B2A).

causes.text: Weak or failing cells or module in battery B
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery B
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B28.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage Unstable
P0B28.summary: P0B28 flags an unstable voltage of hybrid/EV battery B: the reading fluctuates beyond what the battery controller tolerates. Stellantis documents it with P0B28-00 on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe: the MIL is on, and the bulletin warns that after 49 days with this MIL lit the vehicle is no longer allowed to start.

causes.text: Battery pack control module software (Jeep 4xe update)
Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery B
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery B

symptoms: Start inhibited after a long period with the MIL lit (Jeep 4xe: 49 days)
Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent

P0B29.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage Low
P0B29.summary: P0B29 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B stays below the range the controller expects for the present state of charge and load. It is the low counterpart to P0B2A; fluctuating readings belong to P0B28 and the general fault to P0B27.

causes.text: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery B
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage High
P0B2A.summary: P0B2A is stored when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery B rises above its permitted upper limit. It mirrors P0B29 (too low), while P0B28 covers fluctuation and P0B27 the general fault.

causes.text: Cell group in battery B charged too high, balancing ineffective
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads
Battery controller software fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage
P0B2B.summary: P0B2B is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery C, the third sub-battery or energy store that a controller can monitor on its own. It signals an implausible voltage of this unit without the detail given by P0B2C (unstable), P0B2D (low) or P0B2E (high).

causes.text: Weak or failing cells or module in battery C
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery C
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage Unstable
P0B2C.summary: P0B2C indicates that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is unstable, meaning it changes faster or further than plausible for the current load, while a steady deviation would set P0B2D or P0B2E. No manufacturer documents P0B2C publicly.

causes.text: Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery C
Battery controller software (pattern known from P0B24/P0B28)
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery C

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage Low
P0B2D.summary: P0B2D means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is too low compared with what the controller expects. High readings of the same unit are P0B2E, fluctuating ones P0B2C.

causes.text: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery C
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B2E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage High
P0B2E.summary: P0B2E is set when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C exceeds its upper limit. It pairs with P0B2D for undervoltage; P0B2C covers unstable readings and P0B2B the general fault.

causes.text: Cell group in battery C charged too high, balancing ineffective
Drifting voltage measurement channel or sense lead fault
Battery controller software fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on

P0B2F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery D Voltage
P0B2F.summary: P0B2F is the general voltage fault of hybrid/EV battery D, the fourth and last sub-battery in this code family. The controller reports with it that the voltage of unit D is implausible, without specifying unstable (P0B30), low (P0B31) or high (P0B32).

causes.text: Weak or failing cells or module in battery D
Fault in the voltage sense leads or connectors of battery D
Battery controller software or internal measurement fault

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B30.title: Hybrid/EV Battery D Voltage Unstable
P0B30.summary: P0B30 reports an unstable voltage of hybrid/EV battery D: the measured value fluctuates beyond the limit the controller allows. It differs from P0B31 and P0B32, which stand for a lasting low or high voltage, and from the general fault P0B2F.

causes.text: Loose busbar, terminal or sense contact in battery D
Battery controller software (pattern known from P0B24/P0B28)
Cell with rising internal resistance in battery D
