symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Warning comes and goes, fault often stored as intermittent
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B31.title: Hybrid/EV Battery D Voltage Low
P0B31.summary: P0B31 is stored when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery D stays below the expected range. High voltage of the same unit sets P0B32, fluctuation P0B30 and an unspecified deviation P0B2F.

causes.text: Aged cells with lost capacity in battery D
Deep discharge or self-discharge after standstill
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B32.title: Hybrid/EV Battery D Voltage High
P0B32.summary: P0B32 sets when the voltage of hybrid/EV battery D goes above its permitted maximum. It is the high counterpart of P0B31; P0B30 covers unstable readings and P0B2F the general fault.

causes.text: Cell group in battery D charged too high, balancing ineffective
Defective module in battery D
Voltage measurement fault in the controller or sense leads

symptoms: Hybrid/EV system or high-voltage battery warning on
Battery power limited, less electric drive or assist

P0B33.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit
P0B33.summary: The high-voltage service disconnect is the removable plug, usually fused, that splits the traction battery for safe servicing. A low-voltage detection loop runs through the plug, and the battery controller reads it to know whether the plug is seated; patents from Ford and Lear describe this loop, which opens before the main contacts part.

causes.text: Service disconnect plug not fully seated or locked after service
Chafed, open or shorted detection loop wiring between plug base and battery controller
Corroded or spread terminals in the plug or its base
Battery controller input fault

symptoms: Vehicle does not enter ready mode or will not start
High-voltage system warning and MIL on

P0B34.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit Performance
P0B34.summary: P0B34 covers a plausibility fault of the service disconnect detection: the signal is electrically within limits but does not match what the controller expects, for example a plug reported as removed while the high-voltage bus still shows voltage, or a state that changes without a matching event. Audi lists P0B3400 in the controller at address 008C of the 2025 Q5 e-hybrid, together with U029A00 and U059B00, and asks technicians to log the case in its pending service database; no threshold is published.

causes.text: Battery controller software fault (Audi case under investigation)
Loose plug or worn contacts giving an implausible detection state
Increased resistance in the detection loop
Communication fault between battery controller and other modules

symptoms: No ready mode or charging interrupted
Related network codes stored at the same time

P0B35.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit Low
P0B35.summary: P0B35 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays below its lower limit. Where the loop is coded with a resistor in the plug, as in a Lear patent, a reading near zero typically points to a short to ground in the loop wiring; the exact meaning depends on how the manufacturer powers the input.

causes.text: Detection loop wire chafed and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the plug base bridging to ground
Coding element in the plug shorted
Battery controller input stage fault

symptoms: No ready mode or stall with a stop-safely message

P0B36.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit High
P0B36.summary: P0B36 sets when the service disconnect detection signal stays above its upper limit. With a pulled-up input this usually means a short to a voltage source or a missing coding element in the plug; on some designs an open loop also reads high, so manufacturers separate it with P0B37 only where they can tell the cases apart.

causes.text: Detection loop wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open loop or missing contact read as high signal
Wrong or damaged service disconnect plug without proper coding
Battery controller input stage fault

P0B37.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Open
P0B37.summary: P0B37 means the controller sees the service disconnect as open, either because the plug is really removed or because its detection loop is broken. Ford uses the code in the battery energy control module of the 2013-2016 C-Max Energi: bulletins SSM 46108 and TSB 17-0015 describe intermittent stalls or no crank with a Stop Safely Now message and MIL, stored with U3012 and, in another module, the interlock code P0A0A.

causes.text: Low-voltage interlock wiring chafed with intermittent short to ground (Ford C-Max)
Service disconnect plug removed, loose or not locked
Open terminal in the plug base or interlock connector
Battery energy control module fault

symptoms: Stop Safely Now message and MIL
High-voltage interlock code stored in another module

P0B38.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P0B38.summary: Hybrid and electric drives cool the inverter and motor electronics with electric coolant pumps; J2012 numbers them A, B and C. P0B38 sets when the controller detects an open or general fault in the control line of pump B, typically by checking the driver output for missing load current.

causes.text: Pump connector loose, corroded or terminal pushed out
Open control wire between controller and pump
Pump electronics or motor failed open
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system or coolant warning, MIL on
Reduced electric drive power when electronics get hot
Pump not running audibly after switch-on

P0B39.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P0B39.summary: P0B39 sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B is lower than the controller expects, usually a short to ground on the command line or a pump input that pulls the line down. On a low-side switched or PWM line the module sees the voltage stuck low while it commands the pump off.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground, often chafed at brackets
Pump electronics pulling the control input low
Coolant or water in the pump connector
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump runs permanently or not at all, depending on circuit design
Power limitation at high load or heat

P0B3A.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P0B3A.summary: P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Pump control input open so the line floats high
Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump cannot be switched off or on as commanded
Reduced electric power when the inverter heats up

P0B3B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
P0B3B.summary: Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A.

causes.text: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E)
Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda)
Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: MIL or powertrain warning, Stop Safely Now message possible
Fail-safe EV mode with limited speed and sudden loss of power

P0B3C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
P0B3C.summary: P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Reduced electric range or no electric drive
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B3D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
P0B3D.summary: P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active.

causes.text: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B3E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
P0B3E.summary: P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA)
Open sense line letting the input float high
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: MIL on, possibly without noticeable drivability change

P0B3F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B3F.summary: P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly.

causes.text: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B40.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B40.summary: P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Wrench indicator or MIL, Stop Safely Now message possible

P0B41.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B41.summary: P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage above 10.2 V.

causes.text: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B42.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B42.summary: P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present.

causes.text: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: Vehicle behaves as if running on the engine only

P0B43.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B43.summary: P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first.

causes.text: Open sense line letting the input float high
Battery controller software misreading the channel
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

P0B44.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B44.summary: P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly.

causes.text: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B45.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B45.summary: Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel.

causes.text: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C
Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
Powertrain warning (wrench) and Stop Safely Now message

P0B46.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B46.summary: With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. GM's 2019 tables run the test in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2: whenever the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V in one direction, channel C has to follow; if it stays frozen in 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms, the code sets, Type A.

causes.text: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value
High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal

symptoms: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
Reduced electric power or hybrid assist
Contactor or precharge codes stored at the same time (Pacifica)

P0B47.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B47.summary: P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations.

causes.text: Sense lines of channel C shorted to each other or to a neighbouring tap
Failed measuring input in the battery monitoring module
Loose or corroded block connector shared by blocks 3 and 4 (GM two-mode)

symptoms: Electric drive or engine start-stop no longer available

P0B48.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B48.summary: No healthy lithium-ion cell reaches 4.8 V, which is why GM's battery energy control module treats a channel C reading of 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window as a sensing fault and stores P0B48, Type A, one trip. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids the threshold is scaled to a nickel-metal hydride block: block 3 above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Channel C sense line touching a tap of higher potential
Failed measuring input or reference in the monitoring electronics
Monitoring software fault, check for controller updates

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning

P0B49.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B49.summary: P0B49 is reserved for a channel C signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing for good. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses the other four channel C codes, has no erratic test for it in its published tables.

causes.text: Loose crimp or connector on the channel C sense line
Cracked solder joint on the cell monitoring board
Electrical noise from the inverter coupling into the sense line

symptoms: Warning light that appears and disappears
Occasional short loss of electric drive power

P0B4A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B4A.summary: P0B4A is the open-circuit code of cell sense channel D, the fourth measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics. GM checks it in the battery energy control module with the same open sense line logic as the other channels: a gap of 1.3 V or more between adjacent cells, under 36 mV on a cell being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at a bus bar, for 0.6 s, Type A.

causes.text: Open channel D sense tap or connector (code set alone)
Faulty BECM flexible printed circuit affecting several channels (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: No start or vehicle will not go into ready mode
Several sense channel codes stored together

P0B4B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
P0B4B.summary: How the plausibility of channel D is judged depends on the pack. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids the battery pack control module multiplies block 4 by 20 and compares it with the pack voltage; a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets P0B4B, Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Outdated battery controller software (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Block or cell voltage measurement drifting away from the pack voltage
Measuring input of channel D frozen at a constant value

symptoms: Limited hybrid assist or electric range

P0B4C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
P0B4C.summary: From the driver's seat P0B4C looks like a battery problem: the hybrid warning comes on and electric power is cut back. Technically it is a measuring fault on cell channel D, whose reading has fallen below what even a deeply discharged cell would show.

causes.text: Short between channel D sense line and a neighbouring line
Defective input on the cell monitoring module
Corroded tap shared by blocks 4 and 5 (GM two-mode)

symptoms: Electric power and regeneration cut back
Engine runs more often than usual

P0B4D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit High
P0B4D.summary: P0B4D sets when cell sense channel D reports more voltage than the cell or block behind it can deliver. GM's limits are 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s on lithium-ion packs (battery energy control module, Type A, one trip) and above 23 V for block 4 of the 2012 two-mode hybrids (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips).

causes.text: Channel D sense lead contacting a tap of higher potential
Damaged measuring input in the monitoring electronics
Moisture or contamination on the monitoring board creating leakage paths

symptoms: Charging power limited or charging refused

P0B4E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B4E.summary: P0B4E completes the five-code set of cell channel D. Where P0B4A means a lasting open circuit, P0B4B a frozen or implausible value and P0B4C or P0B4D a reading beyond fixed limits, this code is meant for short, irregular dropouts and spikes.

causes.text: Connector or tap losing contact under vibration
Solder joint or crimp cracked by thermal cycling

symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads
Fault not reproducible during workshop test

P0B4F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit
P0B4F.summary: Cell sense channel E is the fifth measuring path between the battery cells and the monitoring electronics; P0B4F means the controller sees it as electrically open. Ford's experience shows how serious this can be: on 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids P0B4F appears among up to fourteen open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C with a no-start condition, and the bulletin prescribes replacing the high-voltage battery.

causes.text: Broken channel E sense lead, splice or bus bar contact
Internal failure of the high-voltage battery (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)

symptoms: Stop Safely Now message while driving

P0B50.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Range/Performance
P0B50.summary: On the 2020 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid P0B50 is called Voltage Sense 5 Circuit Performance and rarely comes alone: the FCA bulletin lists it with the other sense channels, contactor stuck codes, a long precharge time and wake-up circuit faults, all cured by updating the battery pack control module. Some owners also notice that scheduled charging fails because the pack does not wake up.

causes.text: Battery pack control module software, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel E reading frozen in the measuring chip
Block voltage measurement drifting from pack voltage (GM two-mode)

symptoms: Premature oil change or fuel refresh message (Pacifica)

P0B51.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Low
P0B51.summary: P0B51 tells that cell sense channel E reads near zero. GM's battery energy control module only runs this check under clear conditions: the module is in run, crank or accessory mode, the second protection self-test is not running, and no slave communication, open sense line, balancing or internal performance fault is active.

causes.text: Channel E sense line shorted to its neighbour
Faulty input on the cell monitoring slave board
Pin backed out of the monitoring harness connector

P0B52.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit High
P0B52.summary: The threshold behind P0B52 is chosen so that only a measurement error can reach it. A lithium-ion cell is fully charged at roughly 4.2 V, yet GM's battery energy control module waits for 4.8 V or more on channel E, for 1.4 s within 2 s, before storing the code as Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Channel E sense line contacting a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the monitoring module

symptoms: Charging stops early or is refused

P0B53.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B53.summary: P0B53 belongs to cell sense channel E and describes a signal that is sometimes fine and sometimes not. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at the channel E tap or connector
Chafed sense lead touching briefly under movement
Marginal component on the monitoring board

symptoms: Brief loss of electric power while driving

P0B54.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit
P0B54.summary: Ford's 2024 special service message for the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit is the most instructive case for P0B54: vehicles built up to 9 December 2023 could store this and the other open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B5E, show the wrench light, refuse to start or charge, or display Stop Safely Now, and the cause was an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable rather than the cells. The 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV shows the same code with a battery replacement as remedy.

causes.text: Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit built to Dec 2023)
Open channel F tap or splice
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B55.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Range/Performance
P0B55.summary: P0B55 is the plausibility code of cell channel F: the signal exists and lies inside its range, yet it does not move like the rest of the pack. On the 2016 Chevrolet Volt the vehicle integration control module checks whether channel F moves in the same direction as the average cell voltage, failing it after 7 seconds in an 8 second window, Type A; GM's 2019 tables use 35 failures in 40 samples of 100 ms.

causes.text: Battery controller software, fixed by update (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel F measuring input stuck or slow to respond
Increased resistance in the channel F tap or connector

P0B56.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Low
P0B56.summary: The GM two-mode hybrids of 2012, Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra, show a detail of P0B56 that lithium-ion packs lack. Their nickel-metal hydride pack is read in blocks, channel F being block 6, and the battery pack control module sets the code only when block 6 and block 7 both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, two trips; a shared sense wire between the blocks is the obvious suspect then.

causes.text: Fault in the sense wire shared by blocks 6 and 7 (GM two-mode)
Channel F sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Failed input on the cell monitoring electronics

symptoms: Hybrid system warning, MIL after the second drive (two-mode)
Engine runs continuously, no electric launch

P0B57.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit High
P0B57.summary: P0B57 stands for an implausibly high value on cell sense channel F, as opposed to P0B56 for an implausibly low one and P0B55 for a frozen value. GM uses fixed upper limits: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems (Type A, one trip), and above 23 V for block 6 in the 2012 two-mode trucks (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips).

causes.text: Channel F sense lead touching a higher potential
Measuring input or reference fault in the module

P0B58.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B58.summary: P0B58 is reserved for an erratic signal on cell sense channel F, and the honest state is short: no manufacturer documents this code publicly. The neighbouring codes are well covered; Ford and GM use the open circuit code P0B54, GM and Chrysler the range code P0B55, GM the fixed low and high limits.

causes.text: Sense tap of channel F loosening under vibration
Damaged section of the flexible sense circuit

symptoms: Sporadic warning depending on road or temperature

P0B59.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit
P0B59.summary: Voltage sense G is the seventh cell measuring channel; how many cells or groups it covers depends on how the manufacturer splits the pack among monitoring chips. P0B59 is its open-circuit code.

causes.text: Open channel G tap, splice or bus bar contact
Intermittent BECM flexible circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

P0B5A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5A.summary: P0B5A asks whether cell channel G behaves like a real cell. GM answers that question in three ways across its programmes.

causes.text: Channel G measuring input frozen or drifting
Block 7 reading out of line with pack voltage (GM two-mode)
Monitoring software issue, check for updates

P0B5B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Low
P0B5B.summary: When P0B5B appears, the battery controller has seen cell sense channel G at a level no usable cell would show, and it shuts down or restricts electric operation to stay on the safe side. GM documents the trigger for its lithium-ion systems as cell voltage G at or below 0.2 V for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, with the test held off while communication, open line or balancing faults are active.

causes.text: Channel G sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Damaged or backed-out pin in the monitoring connector
Failed measuring input on the monitoring module

P0B5C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit High
P0B5C.summary: P0B5C marks an out-of-range high reading on cell sense channel G. For a technician the quickest plausibility check is arithmetic: the sum of all cell or block readings should match the pack voltage, so a single channel that reads far too high while the total stays normal is a sensing fault.

causes.text: Channel G sense lead touching a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the module
Contamination or moisture on the monitoring board

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0B5D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B5D.summary: P0B5D is the J2012 code for an unsteady signal on cell sense channel G, a reading that flickers or drops out for moments without staying beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents P0B5D publicly.

causes.text: Marginal contact at the channel G tap or connector
Sense harness under strain, losing contact with pack movement

symptoms: Warning that disappears after restart and returns

P0B5E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit
P0B5E.summary: P0B5E flags a broken measuring path on voltage sense H, the eighth cell tap channel read by the battery monitoring electronics. In GM's 2019 tables the battery energy control module runs an open sense line test within a 0.6 s window: neighbouring cells diverging by 1.3 V or more, a cell under 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a bus bar splice) sets it as Type A.

causes.text: Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable at the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit 2023)
Open cell tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel H
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator and Stop Safely Now message
Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive

P0B5F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5F.summary: With P0B5F the channel H wiring is intact, but the value it delivers does not fit the rest of the battery. GM runs two quite different plausibility tests.

causes.text: Block or cell voltage input for channel H drifting away from the true value
Measuring chip input stuck at a constant value
Faulty pack voltage reference distorting the comparison

P0B60.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Low
P0B60.summary: P0B60 means channel H reports less voltage than any healthy cell or block could hold, so the measurement itself is suspect. GM publishes three variants.

causes.text: Channel H sense lead shorted to ground or to the next lower tap
Failed measuring input on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel H actually collapsed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Electric drive power limited or switched off

P0B61.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit High
P0B61.summary: A lithium-ion cell cannot sit much above about 4.2 V, so when channel H reads 4.8 V or more the GM battery energy control module concludes the sense circuit is wrong and stores P0B61 after 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets the same code at more than 4.65 V on the cell sense line in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, while the 2012 two-mode hybrids treat H as nickel-metal hydride block 8 and only object above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Channel H sense lead in contact with a higher cell tap
Lost reference connection letting the measuring input float
Internal fault of the cell monitoring chip

P0B62.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B62.summary: P0B62 describes a channel H signal that jumps or cuts out for moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at the channel H connector or flexible circuit
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
Inverter noise coupling into the sense line

symptoms: Warning appears occasionally and clears after a restart

P0B63.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit
P0B63.summary: Channel I is the ninth sense input of the battery monitoring chain, and P0B63 reports that its circuit is open. GM shows how differently this can be detected.

causes.text: Broken channel I sense wire, crimp or cell tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Corroded or loose connector at the cell monitoring board

symptoms: Vehicle will not start or enter ready mode
Service hybrid or EV system warning

P0B64.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Range/Performance
P0B64.summary: P0B64 is a rationality fault: channel I is connected and reads a believable number, yet it does not move with the other cells. GM's 2016 Chevrolet Volt compares the movement of each cell with the average; if channel I does not follow when the average moves by more than 0.022 V, 7 out of 8 seconds fail the check, Type A.

causes.text: Channel I measuring input frozen at a constant value
Battery controller software misjudging the channel
High-resistance cell tap damping the signal

symptoms: Reduced hybrid assist or electric range

P0B65.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Low
P0B65.summary: The 2012 GM two-mode hybrids show a detail worth knowing for P0B65: their battery pack control module only declares channel I, nickel-metal hydride block 9, too low when block 9 and its neighbour block 10 both read under 2 V, and only after 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms; the fault is Type B and needs two trips. A single weak block alone therefore does not set it.

causes.text: Channel I sense lead shorted to ground or a lower tap
Connector fault affecting adjacent blocks 9 and 10 (two-mode)
Failed measuring input in the battery controller

symptoms: Engine runs more often, electric assist reduced

P0B66.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High
P0B66.summary: When channel I claims a voltage above what its cell or block can physically reach, the controller stores P0B66. The thresholds GM publishes depend on chemistry and architecture: lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module set it at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2012 two-mode trucks, which measure nickel-metal hydride block 9 rather than single cells, above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Channel I lead touching a higher-potential tap
Open reference or ground of the measuring chip
Genuinely overcharged cell after a charging control fault

P0B67.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B67.summary: SAE J2012 reserves P0B67 for an unsteady signal on channel I, meaning readings that spike, drop and recover. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the GM tables that define the other four channel I codes includes an erratic test.

causes.text: Sense contact on channel I opening under vibration or heat
Corroded terminal in the module connector

symptoms: Sporadic warning without a reproducible pattern

P0B68.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit
P0B68.summary: For owners of a 2019 or 2020 Ford Fusion plug-in hybrid, P0B68 is best known from bulletin 23-2039: the car will not start, the battery energy control module stores one or more open sense line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C, and the prescribed repair is a complete high-voltage traction battery. Technically the code says that the tenth measuring channel, J, has lost its connection to the cells.

causes.text: Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Open sense wire or cell tap on channel J
Bad bus bar or splice connection near channel J

symptoms: No start, vehicle does not become ready
Hybrid system warning on the cluster

P0B69.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Range/Performance
P0B69.summary: P0B69 is set when channel J is electrically present but its readings do not behave plausibly. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid explains the logic most clearly: once the average cell voltage moves by more than 0.045 V, the cell under test must move in the same direction and by at least half as much; 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Channel J input reacting too little to real voltage changes
Corroded or high-resistance cell tap
Calibration error in the battery controller

P0B6A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Low
P0B6A.summary: A reading of almost zero on channel J points to the measurement, not to the cell, and that is what P0B6A records. In GM's lithium-ion systems (2016 and 2019 tables) the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A.

causes.text: Channel J lead chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell on channel J internally shorted

P0B6B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High
P0B6B.summary: On GM's 2012 two-mode hybrid trucks the battery is divided into 20 nickel-metal hydride blocks, and channel J is block 10. The battery pack control module samples it every 100 ms while the 12 V supply is between 9 and 18 V; if block 10 reports more than 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, P0B6B is stored as Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second trip.

causes.text: Channel J lead shorted to a higher block or cell tap
Faulty measuring input in the battery pack control module

symptoms: MIL after the second drive (Type B systems)

P0B6C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B6C.summary: No manufacturer documents P0B6C publicly. The code stands for a channel J signal that is unstable, with brief jumps or dropouts, as opposed to the steady faults covered by P0B68 to P0B6B.

causes.text: Marginal contact in the channel J harness or connector
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring electronics

P0B6D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit
P0B6D.summary: P0B6D marks an open circuit on voltage sense K, the eleventh cell measuring channel. GM has used the code since its first published hybrid tables: in 2011 the open-line test already checked bus bar voltages, flagging more than 0.7 V.

causes.text: Loose or corroded bus bar connection at the channel K tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Broken sense wire between cells and monitoring board

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning with MIL

P0B6E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance
P0B6E.summary: In a nickel-metal hydride pack with 20 equal blocks, twenty times one block voltage should roughly equal the whole pack voltage. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids use exactly this for P0B6E, assigned to block 11: the battery pack control module checks blocks 11 and 12, and if both scaled values deviate from the pack voltage sensor by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is set, Type B.

causes.text: Block or cell voltage measurement of channel K out of calibration
Pack voltage sensor reading off, distorting the comparison
Measuring input stuck at one value

symptoms: Less electric assist, more engine running

P0B6F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Low
P0B6F.summary: GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid, the eAssist system in table 13OBDG05C, gives P0B6F a simple rule: if the cell sense line for channel K measures below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples at 200 ms while the 12 V supply is above 8.8 V, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. Since a lithium-ion cell in use never falls that low, the value must come from a short or a failed input.

causes.text: Channel K sense line shorted to ground or a lower tap
Failed measuring input in the battery interface module
Blown protective element in the sense line

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL after the second trip
Auto stop and electric assist disabled

P0B70.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit High
P0B70.summary: P0B70 says that cell voltage K reads too high to be genuine. GM's 2019 battery energy control module sets it at 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault with immediate MIL, and only when no communication loss, open sense line or internal module fault takes precedence.

causes.text: Channel K lead in contact with a higher tap
Floating measuring input after loss of its lower reference
Cell monitoring chip fault

P0B71.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B71.summary: P0B71 belongs to the unsteady fault type: the channel K reading flickers or drops out momentarily without staying beyond a fixed limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Fretting corrosion on channel K connector terminals
Sense harness under strain losing contact with movement

symptoms: Occasional short loss of electric power

P0B72.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit
P0B72.summary: P0B72 reports an open circuit on voltage sense L, the twelfth channel. One detail sets it apart from its neighbours: GM's 2011 hybrid tables list every open sense line code from P0B3B upward except P0B72 (and P0B90), so the early system did not use it, while L's range, low and high codes were present.

causes.text: Open sense lead, crimp or cell tap on channel L
Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
High-resistance splice or bus bar joint

symptoms: No start or no ready mode

P0B73.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance
P0B73.summary: Channel L delivers a value, but P0B73 tells you that the value is not credible. GM checks this in three ways.

causes.text: Channel L input not following real cell voltage changes
Battery controller software or calibration issue
Corroded cell tap slowing the signal

P0B74.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Low
P0B74.summary: P0B74 is set when channel L reads implausibly low. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where L is nickel-metal hydride block 12 of 20, the battery pack control module needs both block 12 and block 13 under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples before it stores the code as Type B; no battery control module fault P0A1F may be active.

causes.text: Channel L sense lead shorted to a lower potential
Defective measuring input in the battery controller
Cell or block on channel L actually failed

P0B75.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit High
P0B75.summary: With P0B75 the battery controller rejects channel L because it reads above any value a real cell or block can reach. GM's lithium-ion systems in the 2016 Volt and the 2019 tables set it at 4.8 V or more over 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Channel L lead touching a higher tap
Floating measuring input after an open reference line
Real overvoltage of the cell after a charging fault

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0B76.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B76.summary: P0B76 closes the channel L group and covers an erratic signal: values that jump or vanish briefly while the circuit otherwise works. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, the only maker with public tables for L, defines open, plausibility, low and high tests for this channel but no erratic test, and the Ford bulletins name only the open-circuit code P0B72.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at the channel L cell tap
Fatigued sense harness wire
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

symptoms: Warning clears after restart and comes back

P0B77.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit
P0B77.summary: P0B77 flags an open or high-resistance tap on voltage sense M, the thirteenth cell channel. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases: adjacent cells differing by 1.3 V or more, a balancing gate reading below 36 mV, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice).

causes.text: Open or corroded tap of sense lead M at the cell connector
Fault inside the traction battery (Ford Fusion PHEV TSB 23-2039)
High resistance at a splice or busbar joint in the sense path
Defective cell monitoring board input

symptoms: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not start or go into ready mode

P0B78.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Range/Performance
P0B78.summary: With P0B78 the controller doubts the reading of channel M rather than its wiring. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor watches for a frozen value: whenever the average of all cells moves by more than 0.022 V, cell M must follow by at least 0.005 V in the same direction, and 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set a Type A fault.

causes.text: Measuring channel M stuck at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Block 13 voltage drifting from the pack on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL on, often without noticeable driving change

P0B79.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Low
P0B79.summary: P0B79 means that the voltage reported for sense M is too low to be real. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 set it at 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, and only while no open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead is reported by P0B77 first.

causes.text: Sense lead M shorted to ground or a lower cell potential
Failed measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel M actually collapsed

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message

P0B7A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit High
P0B7A.summary: A reading on channel M above what any healthy cell can deliver produces P0B7A. For lithium-ion packs GM sets the line at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window and treats it as Type A, illuminating the MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Sense lead M in contact with a higher cell potential
Measuring input of channel M reading high
Real overvoltage of the cell after a balancing fault

symptoms: MIL on from the first trip (GM lithium-ion, Type A)

P0B7B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B7B.summary: P0B7B is reserved for a sense M signal that flickers: short dropouts or jumps while the circuit is otherwise intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Loose crimp or connector at the channel M tap
Chafed wire in the cell sense harness
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

symptoms: Hybrid warning appearing and clearing again

P0B7C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit
P0B7C.summary: Voltage sense N, the fourteenth channel, reports a broken or high-resistance sense lead with P0B7C. It is the last code in Ford's TSB 23-2039: 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that fail to start with any open-circuit code from P0B3B up to P0B7C get a replacement traction battery; the bulletin names no channel beyond N.

causes.text: Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Sense lead N broken or with excessive resistance
Fault on the cell monitoring board

symptoms: No start or vehicle does not become ready
MIL and stop-safely or service message

P0B7D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Range/Performance
P0B7D.summary: P0B7D concerns a channel N value that stays inside its limits yet does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2016 tables show how the same check is tuned per vehicle: the Chevrolet Volt fails when cell N does not move with the average for 7 of 8 seconds, while the Cadillac ELR counts 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms once the average shifts by more than 0.006 V; both are Type A.

causes.text: Channel N value not tracking the other cells
Outdated battery controller calibration
Block 14 or 15 voltage mismatch on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: Shorter electric range or less assist

P0B7E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Low
P0B7E.summary: P0B7E sets when channel N reads below the lower plausibility limit. GM's 2016 program with a separate battery sense module uses less than 0.20 V and needs 14 failures in 18 samples, about 1.8 s at 100 ms each, before a Type A fault; the open-circuit test must not be failing at the same time.

causes.text: Sense lead N shorted to a lower potential
Damaged input stage in the sense module
Deeply discharged or failed cell on channel N

symptoms: MIL from the first trip on lithium-ion GM systems
Combustion engine does not shut off at standstill

P0B7F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit High
P0B7F.summary: Channel N reporting more voltage than a cell can hold leads to P0B7F. GM uses three thresholds depending on the system: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s on most lithium-ion battery controllers, above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples on the 2016 program with a separate sense module, both Type A, and above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, Type B.

causes.text: Sense lead N touching a higher potential
Drifted measuring input in the battery controller
Real overvoltage of the cell on channel N

symptoms: MIL and warning in the instrument cluster

P0B80.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B80.summary: P0B80 describes an unsteady channel N signal: the voltage drops out or jumps for moments, then looks normal again. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Contact at the N tap opening under vibration
Fretting corrosion in the sense harness connector
Solder joint cracking with temperature cycles

P0B81.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit
P0B81.summary: P0B81 stands for an open sense lead on channel O, the fifteenth cell tap. GM has used it from the start: the 2011 Volt battery tables already list P0B81 among the open sense line codes and detect, among other cases, a busbar connection voltage above 0.7 V.

causes.text: Loose or high-resistance busbar joint at the O tap
Broken sense wire O in the battery harness
Faulty cell sense module

symptoms: Reduced power or no electric drive

P0B82.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Range/Performance
P0B82.summary: P0B82 is a plausibility verdict on channel O. GM's 2016 program with a battery sense module asks cell O to trend at least 0.002 V in the direction of the average whenever the average moves by more than 0.022 V; 35 failed evaluations out of 40 set a Type A code.

causes.text: Channel O reading frozen in the monitoring electronics
Battery controller software fault
Rising resistance in the O sense tap distorting the reading

symptoms: State of charge display jumps or is inaccurate

P0B83.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Low
P0B83.summary: P0B83 reports that channel O reads implausibly low. It is not the same as an open lead: GM's lithium-ion controllers run this check only while no open sense line fault is present, so a broken wire shows as P0B81 instead.

causes.text: Short in the O sense path towards ground or a lower cell
Monitoring input reading low
Dead cell or NiMH block 15

P0B84.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High
P0B84.summary: P0B84 is stored when channel O sits above the upper limit of a credible cell voltage. For GM lithium-ion packs that limit is 4.8 V, held 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A; the 2016 program with a separate sense module tolerates up to 4.90 V and counts 14 failures in 18 samples, also Type A.

causes.text: Sense lead O shorted to a higher cell tap
Monitoring input of channel O reading too high
Cell overcharged because balancing failed

P0B85.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B85.summary: P0B85 would mark a channel O signal that is present but unsteady, with spikes or brief gaps. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; even GM, whose public tables cover channel O in detail from 2011 onward, defines only the open, rationality, low and high tests for it.

causes.text: Loose busbar screw changing contact resistance at tap O
Moisture or corrosion in the sense harness connector
Cracked joint on the monitoring board

P0B86.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit
P0B86.summary: P0B86 belongs to channel P, the sixteenth sense lead, and indicates that this lead has lost its connection to the cell. Comparing GM's tables shows how the timing evolved: the 2016 Volt battery controller decides within 0.6 s, the 2019 version waits 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window; both use the 1.3 V adjacent-cell, 36 mV balancing gate and splice criteria and are Type A.

causes.text: Sense lead P open at the cell tap or connector
Excessive resistance in the sense line (corrosion, loose screw)
Defective input of the sense module

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system fault message
Vehicle runs only on the engine or with reduced power

P0B87.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Range/Performance
P0B87.summary: P0B87 says channel P is delivering numbers that do not fit the rest of the battery. On GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid the cell under test must move at least 50 percent as far as the average cell voltage; if not, 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, i.e.

causes.text: Measuring electronics for channel P out of tolerance
Software or calibration of the battery controller
NiMH block 16 or 17 out of balance with the pack

symptoms: MIL after two trips on Type B systems
Engine start-stop or electric assist less frequent

P0B88.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Low
P0B88.summary: A too-low value on sense P, the sixteenth channel, is what P0B88 records. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it at a cell sense line below 1.4 V for 7 of 10 samples, sampled every 200 ms and only with the 12 V battery above 8.8 V; it rates the fault Type B.

causes.text: Lead P shorted to a lower potential or chassis
Defective input in the battery interface module
Weak cell or NiMH block 16

P0B89.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit High
P0B89.summary: P0B89 covers the opposite case to P0B88: the voltage reported on channel P is above the plausible range. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids assign P to NiMH block 16 and set the code when the block exceeds 23 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, provided no battery controller fault P0A1F is active.

causes.text: Lead P in contact with a higher cell tap
Input fault in the cell monitoring electronics
Genuine overvoltage of the cell or block

P0B8A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8A.summary: P0B8A is the erratic-signal member of the channel P group. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it: GM describes open, rationality, low and high diagnostics for sense P in its 2016 and 2019 tables, but none for an intermittent signal, and the Ford bulletins stop at channel N.

causes.text: Fatigued wire at a bend of the sense harness
Connector losing contact as the pack warms up
Sporadic fault in the cell monitoring chip

symptoms: Warning lamp that goes out again
Occasional engine start without demand on hybrids

P0B8B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit
P0B8B.summary: P0B8B marks an open circuit on voltage sense Q, the seventeenth channel. In GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid tables Q is the first channel whose open test is blocked by code P1B37 instead of P1B36, which suggests it sits in the next measuring group of the battery interface module; the criterion stays lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Sense lead Q open between cell tap and module
Loose or corroded connector at the second measuring group
Fault in the battery interface module

P0B8C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Range/Performance
P0B8C.summary: P0B8C is set when channel Q reports a voltage that fails the plausibility test against the other cells or the pack. On GM's 2012 two-mode trucks Q is NiMH block 17; the battery pack control module takes block 17 and block 18, multiplies each by twenty and compares with the measured pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B.

causes.text: Monitoring electronics misreading channel Q
Outdated battery controller software
Block 17 or 18 voltage deviating on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL with little change in driving

P0B8D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Low
P0B8D.summary: P0B8D reports a voltage on sense Q below the lowest credible cell value. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers in the 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the 2016 program with a separate sense module 0.20 V with 14 of 18 samples.

causes.text: Short in the Q sense path to a lower potential
Sense module input reading low
Cell or block 17 deeply discharged

symptoms: Engine runs more often on hybrids

P0B8E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit High
P0B8E.summary: Channel Q reporting an implausibly high voltage sets P0B8E. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where Q is NiMH block 17, the limit is 23 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, checked only while the 12 V system lies between 9 and 18 V.

causes.text: Damaged harness letting lead Q touch the next tap
Measuring input of channel Q reading high
Real cell overvoltage after a balancing failure

P0B8F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8F.summary: P0B8F closes the channel Q group and stands for a sense Q signal that is erratic rather than absent or out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Cracked crimp at the channel Q tap
Damaged flexible circuit between cells and monitoring board
Cold solder joint at the measuring chip

symptoms: Power briefly reduced, normal after restart

P0B90.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit
P0B90.summary: P0B90 is stored when the battery controller concludes that the tap of sense R, the eighteenth cell channel, is open or too resistive. GM's 2019 battery energy control module runs seven cases for it: neighbouring cells 1.3 V or more apart, a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate is on, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice).

causes.text: Loose, corroded or broken tap of sense lead R
Excessive resistance at a splice or busbar joint feeding channel R
Faulty measuring or balancing input on the cell monitoring board

symptoms: MIL with service hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode

P0B91.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Range/Performance
P0B91.summary: Here the wiring of sense R is intact, but its value does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor demands that cell R moves at least 0.005 V in the same direction whenever the cell average shifts by more than 0.022 V; 35 failures out of 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault.

causes.text: Measuring channel R reporting a stuck value
Outdated battery controller or hybrid processor software
Block 18 or 19 voltage drifting on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL on, vehicle often drives normally
Less electric assist or regenerative braking

P0B92.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Low
P0B92.summary: P0B92 stands for an implausibly low reading on sense R. In GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 the limit is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A; the test is suspended while an open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead appears as P0B90 rather than P0B92.

causes.text: Sense lead R chafed through and touching ground or a lower cell
Failed input for channel R on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel R genuinely collapsed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system message

P0B93.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit High
P0B93.summary: A reading on sense R above anything a healthy cell could produce sets P0B93. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 use 4.8 V or more, held 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault.

causes.text: Sense lead R in contact with a higher cell potential
Damaged measuring input for channel R
Cell on channel R actually overcharged

P0B94.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B94.summary: No manufacturer documents P0B94 publicly. The code is reserved for a sense R signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing steadily.

causes.text: Crimp or terminal of lead R opening under vibration
Hairline crack in the flexible circuit carrying channel R
Moisture or contamination in the monitoring board connector

symptoms: Warning appears and disappears between trips
Short power reductions, normal after restart

P0B95.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit
P0B95.summary: P0B95 reports that the sense S lead, channel nineteen, no longer connects its cell reliably to the monitoring electronics. GM programmes with a separate battery sensor module (16OBDG02) measure this directly: after each normal reading the balancing gates switch in a test pattern, current flows through the sense wires and the voltage drop is turned into a line resistance.

causes.text: High resistance in sense lead S from corrosion or a loose terminal
Sense lead S broken at the cell connector
Defective input of the battery sensor module for channel S

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0B96.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Range/Performance
P0B96.summary: P0B96 is a plausibility code: the voltage of sense S looks electrically valid but fails to track the rest of the pack. GM's eAssist mild hybrid requires cell S to move at least half as much as the other cells once the average changes by more than 0.045 V, judged over 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms, Type B.

causes.text: Measuring channel S frozen or lagging behind the other cells
Battery controller calibration requiring a software update
Block 19 or 20 out of step with the pack on two-mode NiMH batteries

symptoms: MIL with little or no change in driving

P0B97.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Low
P0B97.summary: With P0B97 the controller sees sense S pulled close to zero. In the 2012 two-mode trucks, where S is the nickel-metal hydride block 19, the battery pack control module only sets it when block 19 and block 20 are both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V.

causes.text: Sense lead S shorted to ground or to the next lower cell
Defective channel S input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel S actually discharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning message
Restricted power, engine may run more often on hybrids

P0B98.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit High
P0B98.summary: P0B98 marks a sense S value that is too high to be a cell voltage. The thresholds vary with the battery chemistry and controller: GM's 2016 Volt and 2019 battery controllers flag 4.8 V or more after 1.4 s in 2 s (Type A), the 16OBDG02 programme 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples (Type A), and the eAssist mild hybrid more than 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V (Type B).

causes.text: Sense lead S shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring chip reading channel S incorrectly
Real overvoltage of the cell or block on channel S

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid system message

P0B99.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B99.summary: P0B99 is the erratic variant within the sense S group. A public manufacturer description does not exist.

causes.text: Fretting corrosion on the terminal of sense lead S
Cracked solder joint for channel S on the monitoring board
Harness chafing that only shorts under movement

symptoms: Sporadic hybrid warning without a pattern
Code often stored as history, hard to reproduce

P0B9A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit
P0B9A.summary: P0B9A is the open-circuit code for sense T, the twentieth cell channel. GM uses it only on lithium-ion packs.

causes.text: Open sense lead T at the cell tab or connector
Poor busbar or splice joint in the channel T path
Monitoring board input for channel T failed

symptoms: MIL, hybrid or EV system warning

P0B9B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Range/Performance
P0B9B.summary: On the 2012 two-mode trucks sense T is block 20, the last of their twenty nickel-metal hydride blocks, and P0B9B shows how GM handles the missing neighbour: block 20 alone is multiplied by twenty and compared with the pack voltage, and a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets the code as Type B. All other channels there use a pair of blocks.

causes.text: Channel T measurement stuck or sluggish
Block 20 voltage diverging from pack voltage on two-mode NiMH packs
Faulty pack voltage reference used for the comparison

symptoms: Hybrid assist or EV range slightly reduced

P0B9C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Low
P0B9C.summary: P0B9C signals that sense T reads too low. On the 2012 two-mode trucks this is block 20, and because no block 21 exists the low test there looks at block 20 alone: below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, while channels R and S each need their upper neighbour to read low as well.

causes.text: Sense lead T shorted to ground or a lower potential
Weak or discharged NiMH block 20 on two-mode packs
Failed measuring input for channel T

symptoms: Reduced power, engine may not shut off on hybrids

P0B9D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit High
P0B9D.summary: If sense T reports more voltage than its cell can hold, the battery controller stores P0B9D. GM documents it on several systems.

causes.text: Sense lead T shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring input for channel T drifting high
Cell or block T genuinely overcharged

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message

P0B9E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B9E.summary: P0B9E would describe a sense T signal that flickers. It lacks any public manufacturer documentation.

causes.text: Loose or spread terminal in the channel T connector
Connection that opens with temperature changes
Electrical interference coupling into sense lead T

symptoms: Occasional brief loss of electric drive

P0B9F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit
P0B9F.summary: P0B9F covers an open or high-resistance sense U lead, channel twenty-one. From U onward the 2012 two-mode trucks drop out, as their pack has only twenty blocks, so this code is a lithium-ion matter at GM.

causes.text: Sense lead U interrupted or detached from its cell
Corroded terminal raising the resistance of lead U
Fault in the balancing circuit used for the channel U test

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
No start or ready mode on some vehicles

P0BA0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Range/Performance
P0BA0.summary: P0BA0 tells the technician that channel U gives a number, but the number does not move with the pack. GM checks this rationality only on lithium-ion systems, since the two-mode NiMH trucks end at block 20.

causes.text: Measuring channel U holding a fixed value
Software or calibration issue in the battery controller
Cell U behaving differently from its neighbours due to ageing

P0BA1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Low
P0BA1.summary: P0BA1 is stored when sense U reads close to zero. GM's lithium-ion controllers of the 2016 Volt and ELR and of 2019 treat 0.2 V or less over 1.4 s in a 2 s window as a Type A fault, provided no open sense line, lost slave communication or balancing fault is already active.

causes.text: Sense lead U shorted towards ground or a lower cell
Dead measuring input for channel U
Cell U internally shorted or deeply discharged

symptoms: MIL and EV or hybrid system warning

P0BA2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit High
P0BA2.summary: P0BA2 flags an excessive voltage on channel U. GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses the lowest threshold of the documented systems: above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V, Type B.

causes.text: Sense lead U in contact with a higher potential
Measuring IC misreading channel U
Cell U actually overcharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0BA3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BA3.summary: Within the sense U group, P0BA3 is the slot for a signal that is present but unsteady. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM, the only maker whose tables cover channel U in detail, uses P0B9F to P0BA2 and nothing more.

causes.text: Fatigued crimp on sense lead U
Loose fastener at the busbar tap of channel U
Vibration damage to the flexible printed circuit

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes

P0BA4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit
P0BA4.summary: P0BA4 reports an open or poorly connected sense V lead, the twenty-second channel and the last before W begins at P0BA9. GM's 2019 battery energy control module recognises it through seven cases, including 1.3 V between neighbouring cells, less than 36 mV with the balancing gate on and splice voltages above 0.1 or 0.5 V, with 0.8 s of failure in 1.6 s, Type A.

causes.text: Broken or unplugged sense lead V
High-resistance splice or busbar joint on channel V
Cell monitoring board fault on channel V

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not become ready to drive

P0BA5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Range/Performance
P0BA5.summary: P0BA5 describes a sense V value that stays within limits but fails a rationality check against the other cells. GM's 16OBDG02 programme demands a trend of at least 0.002 V in the same direction as the average whenever that average moves more than 0.022 V, with 35 failures in 40 evaluations giving Type A.

causes.text: Channel V reading stuck while other cells move
Battery controller firmware needing reprogramming
Aged cell V responding differently to load

P0BA6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Low
P0BA6.summary: A sense V reading that collapses towards zero produces P0BA6. The threshold depends on the system: GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses under 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples with at least 8.8 V on the 12 V side, Type B, while GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 go down to 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A.

causes.text: Sense lead V shorted to ground or a lower cell
Monitoring board input for channel V failed
Cell V genuinely collapsed

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Power limited, restart may be refused

P0BA7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit High
P0BA7.summary: P0BA7 is the high-voltage plausibility code for channel V. The battery controller compares the measured value against a ceiling no healthy cell should reach: 4.8 V for 1.4 s within 2 s in GM's 2016 Volt and ELR and in the 2019 battery energy control module (Type A), 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples of 100 ms in the 16OBDG02 programme (Type A), and 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples in the eAssist mild hybrid (Type B).

causes.text: Sense lead V touching a higher cell tab or busbar
Measuring chip with faulty reference reading channel V high
Cell V really overcharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0BA8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BA8.summary: P0BA8 completes the five codes of channel V and is meant for an unstable rather than a failed sense V signal. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it.

causes.text: Contact of lead V lost intermittently under vibration
Joint on channel V opening with thermal cycling
Corroded connector pin for channel V

symptoms: Fault not reproducible during short workshop test

P0BA9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit
P0BA9.summary: P0BA9 opens the W group, the twenty-third cell voltage channel, and flags a sense lead that is open or badly connected. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases, ranging from a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate of that cell is switched on to at least 1.3 V between neighbouring cells and splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at busbar joints; 0.8 s of failure within 1.6 s sets it as Type A.

causes.text: Broken, chafed or unplugged sense lead W
High-resistance busbar or splice joint at channel W
Failed input on the cell monitoring board for W

symptoms: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode

P0BAA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Range/Performance
P0BAA.summary: Here the W reading is not missing but implausible: it fails to follow the rest of the pack. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 watches for the average cell voltage to move more than 0.022 V between samples and then expects channel W to trend at least 0.005 V in the same direction; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault.

causes.text: Measuring input for W frozen at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Cell W reacting differently to load because of ageing

symptoms: Warning lamp with little change in driving
Possibly limited regeneration or electric assist

P0BAB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Low
P0BAB.summary: A W channel reading at or near zero sets P0BAB. How low is too low depends on the battery: GM's lithium-ion modules of 2016 and 2019 react to 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, and the 16OBDG02 programme to under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples at 100 ms.

causes.text: Sense lead W shorted to a lower cell potential
Measuring input for W on the monitoring board failed
Cell W deeply discharged or internally shorted

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning and MIL

P0BAC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit High
P0BAC.summary: P0BAC is the upper counterpart to P0BAB: channel W reports more voltage than a single cell can plausibly hold. GM sets the limit at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the 2011 and 2016 Volt battery modules, which makes it a one-trip fault.

causes.text: Sense lead W in contact with a higher cell potential
Monitoring board input for W reading too high
Cell W actually overcharged after a balancing fault

P0BAD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BAD.summary: P0BAD is reserved for a W signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing outright. No manufacturer documents the code publicly.

causes.text: Loose or fretting connector pin on lead W
Crimp on lead W opening with temperature changes
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board input W

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes

P0BAE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit
P0BAE.summary: Channel X, number twenty-four, starts with P0BAE, the open-lead code. The first-generation Volt of 2011 already detected it through several cases: two neighbouring readings more than 1 V apart, a busbar sense voltage above 0.7 V combined with an implausible cell voltage, or adjacent cells differing by more than 0.5 V on a shared supply line.

causes.text: Sense lead X broken or disconnected
Loose busbar fastener at the X sensing point
Sense harness X damaged during earlier battery work

symptoms: MIL and service message for the high-voltage system
Vehicle may stay out of ready mode

P0BAF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Range/Performance
P0BAF.summary: P0BAF covers a sense X signal that is electrically present yet does not behave like a real cell. For model year 2016 GM documents two versions in the same booklet.

causes.text: Sense X value stuck while the pack voltage changes
Calibration of the battery controller requiring reprogramming
Cell X with deviating internal resistance

symptoms: Reduced electric range in some cases

P0BB0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Low
P0BB0.summary: When channel X reads too low, P0BB0 is stored. In GM's eAssist mild hybrid the battery interface module sets it below 1.4 V in seven of ten samples at 200 ms, provided the 12 V system is above 8.8 V and the group fault P1B38 is not active, as a two-trip Type B fault.

causes.text: Short between sense lead X and a lower potential
Defective measuring channel X in the monitoring electronics
Cell X collapsed or internally shorted

P0BB1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit High
P0BB1.summary: P0BB1 means the battery controller sees too much voltage on sense X. In GM's 2019 battery energy control module the threshold is 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, and the code is Type A, so the MIL comes on in the first trip.

causes.text: Sense lead X shorted to the next higher cell
Measuring input X drifting high
Cell X genuinely over voltage

P0BB2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BB2.summary: Of the five X codes, P0BB2 is the only one without any public manufacturer description. It is intended for a sense X signal that flickers, drops out briefly or jumps between values.

causes.text: Contact on lead X opening under vibration
Moisture or corrosion in the X sense connector
Harness X chafing against the module housing

P0BB3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit
P0BB3.summary: P0BB3 reports that the sense lead of channel Y, the twenty-fifth cell group, is no longer properly connected. GM's 16OBDG02 programme does not wait for odd voltages but calculates the resistance of the sense line and fails it above 30.00 in seven of nine samples, which is a one-trip Type A fault; the unit is missing in the table.

causes.text: Open circuit in sense lead Y
Corroded or loose terminal raising line resistance at Y
Cell monitoring slave board fault on input Y

symptoms: Vehicle may not start in electric mode

P0BB4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Range/Performance
P0BB4.summary: P0BB4 is a plausibility code: the controller compares how the Y reading changes over time with the behaviour of all other cells. In the 16OBDG02 programme a sample counts as failed when the pack average moves by more than 0.022 V but Y has not trended at least 0.002 V the same way; 35 such results in 40 evaluations set a one-trip Type A fault.

causes.text: Analogue input Y frozen at one value
Battery controller software fault
Weak cell Y with sluggish voltage response

P0BB5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Low
P0BB5.summary: P0BB5 stands for a sense Y voltage below the plausible minimum. GM's 2016 Volt module and the 2019 battery energy control module both use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window and flag it as Type A.

causes.text: Pinched sense wire Y shorting to a lower potential
Failed measuring channel Y
Cell Y severely discharged

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning with MIL

P0BB6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit High
P0BB6.summary: The battery controller logs P0BB6 when the Y channel climbs above a level no healthy cell reaches. GM's first Volt of 2011 put that limit at 4.8 V or more, 1.4 s within 2 s, with the MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Sense input Y bridged to the next cell potential
Defective input Y on the monitoring board
Overcharged cell Y after a balancing problem

P0BB7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BB7.summary: P0BB7 would describe an unstable sense Y signal, one that is mostly correct but drops out or jumps from time to time. No manufacturer publishes a monitor for it.

causes.text: Intermittent contact in the Y sense connector
Crimp or weld on lead Y opening when hot
Hairline crack in a solder joint of input Y

symptoms: Warning lamp appears now and then

P0BB8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit
