P0BB8.summary: P0BB8 is the open-circuit code of channel Z, the twenty-sixth and last cell channel with a generic P0 code. GM packs with more channels continue with manufacturer codes, for example P1B28 for the circuit of AA in the 2019 tables.

causes.text: Sense lead Z interrupted
Excessive resistance at the splice or busbar of Z
Monitoring electronics input Z defective

symptoms: MIL and stop or service warning for the drive system

P0BB9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Range/Performance
P0BB9.summary: With P0BB9 the controller says that sense Z does not track the pack: the value is within limits, but it stays still or moves the wrong way while the other cells change. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 enables the comparison once the system voltage is above 10.20 V and the average cell voltage shifts by more than 0.022 V, then demands a trend of at least 0.005 V on Z; 35 failures in 40 samples are Type A.

causes.text: Z reading static despite changing pack voltage
Monitoring board or controller calibration fault
Cell Z with abnormal charge and discharge behaviour

P0BBA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Low
P0BBA.summary: P0BBA is stored when the voltage measured on channel Z falls below the lower limit. In the 16OBDG02 programme the hybrid processor checks Z every 100 ms and fails it below 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples, a Type A fault, but only with a system voltage above 10.20 V and no open-circuit fault on the cell.

causes.text: Short in the Z sense wiring or connector
Failed channel Z on the monitoring board
Voltage collapse of cell Z

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0BBB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit High
P0BBB.summary: If the Z channel shows a cell voltage above the upper limit, the controller sets P0BBB. The 2016 Volt battery module uses 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, and checks first that the cell monitoring slave is communicating and no open sense line is reported.

causes.text: Sense lead Z shorted towards the higher neighbour cell
Faulty measuring input Z
Cell Z overcharged

P0BBC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BBC.summary: P0BBC closes the generic block of 26 cell voltage channels from A to Z; after it J2012 moves on to pack-level codes such as P0BBD and P0BBE. The code is meant for a Z signal that is unstable rather than absent.

causes.text: Intermittent contact on sense lead Z
Joint at channel Z opening with heat cycling
Corrosion in the Z sense connector

symptoms: Occasional brief loss of electric drive power

P0BBD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Variation Exceeded Limit
P0BBD.summary: P0BBD means the spread between cells or blocks of the pack has grown beyond what the controller accepts. GM used it on the two-mode hybrids, where a difference of more than 1.5 V between adjacent block voltages in three of three samples at 1 s, with battery current above 0.2 A, set a Type B fault labelled as end-of-life deviation.

causes.text: Cells or modules with increased self-discharge or capacity loss
Controller software or cell capacity adaptation needing an update
Aged battery pack at end of life
Cell balancing unable to equalise the pack

symptoms: Reduced propulsion power and capped state of charge
Drive system cannot be activated in severe cases

P0BBE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Variation
P0BBE.summary: P0BBE watches the gap between the highest and the lowest cell voltage in the pack. GM's first-generation Volt sets it when that difference exceeds 0.3 V in 50 of 245 samples taken every 100 ms, provided the cell voltage rationality fault is not active; it is a one-trip Type A fault.

causes.text: Cells drifted apart beyond what balancing can correct
Battery pack control module software needing an update
Defective or aged high-voltage battery pack
Faulty cell voltage measurement simulating a spread

P0BBF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0BBF.summary: Air-cooled hybrid packs draw cooling air through a 12 V blower that is fed through a fuse and often a relay; the controller watches the voltage reaching the fan, and Toyota even uses that measured supply voltage to correct the fan duty. P0BBF means this feed is open or missing while the fan should be powered.

causes.text: Blown fuse in the battery fan feed
Fan relay contacts not closing or relay coil open
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the fan connector

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan silent when it should run
Reduced electric assist in hot weather or under load

P0BC0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0BC0.summary: P0BC0 reports that the voltage feeding the battery cooling fan is lower than expected while the fan is switched on. A short to ground downstream of the fuse, a corroded connector or a relay with burnt contacts drops the voltage, so the fan turns slowly or not at all.

causes.text: Fan supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Burnt fan relay contacts or corroded terminals causing voltage drop
Weak 12 V auxiliary battery or poor ground
Seizing fan motor pulling excessive current

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan runs slowly or noticeably weaker
Reduced electric assist when the pack is warm

P0BC1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0BC1.summary: P0BC1 flags voltage on the battery fan feed when there should be none, or more than expected. GM documents it for the battery pack control module of its Two-Mode hybrid SUVs and pickups (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra; 2012 and 2013 tables) as a welded fan relay: with the fan commanded off, a fan monitor voltage of at least 0.9 V in 10 of 20 samples at 100 ms sets it, provided the 12 V system is between 9 and 18 V and no fan circuit code (P0A81) is active.

causes.text: Fan relay contacts welded closed
Fan feed shorted to a constant battery voltage wire
Relay control output in the module stuck on

symptoms: Battery fan keeps running after the vehicle is switched off

P0BC2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit
P0BC2.summary: Battery temperature sensor E is the fifth thermistor in the high-voltage pack; GM's Chevrolet Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the E codes as temperature sensor 5 of nine. P0BC2 is the general circuit code, used when the controller detects an electrical fault without classing it as low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector of sensor E at the sensing board
Failed thermistor E
Faulty input on the battery sensing board or module

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Battery cooling running more than usual

P0BC3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Range/Performance
P0BC3.summary: P0BC3 is the plausibility check for battery temperature sensor E, GM's sensor 5: its reading is compared with the other pack sensors, which should agree closely. GM's 2016 hybrid table fails it when E is more than 25 °C away from the average of the others in 50 of 67 samples; the 2018 CT6 plug-in table more than 20 °C for 5 s within 6.7 s; the eAssist mild hybrid (13OBDG05C) allows only 8.55 °C, and only after the module has been off for more than six hours.

causes.text: Sensor E drifting or poorly seated on its cell group
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)
Real local hot spot from a weak cell group or blocked airflow

symptoms: Battery too cold or reduced power message

P0BC4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Low
P0BC4.summary: Sensor E is an NTC thermistor with a pull-up resistor, so its voltage falls as it gets hotter; a short to ground therefore looks like an extremely hot cell group. GM's 2016 table sets P0BC4 when the converted value exceeds 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples; the 2011 Volt table and GM's 2019 battery module table use above 87.5 °C for 1.4 s within 2 s; the eAssist mild hybrid flags a sense voltage under 0.3 V, about 90 °C, in 7 of 10 samples.

causes.text: Sensor E signal wire shorted to ground inside the pack
Internally shorted thermistor E
Moisture or contamination on the sensing board

symptoms: Implausibly high temperature for sensor E on the scan tool
Reduced power and battery fan or cooling at full speed

P0BC5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit High
P0BC5.summary: P0BC5 reports that battery temperature sensor E delivers a voltage above its valid range. With GM's NTC sensors that reads as extreme cold, pointing to an open wire, a backed-out pin at the sensing board or a cracked thermistor.

causes.text: Open sensor E wire or backed-out pin at the sensing board
Cracked or open thermistor E
Module software misreading in the cold (GM Volt, reprogramming)

symptoms: Battery too cold, plug in to warm message

P0BC6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BC6.summary: P0BC6 flags erratic behaviour of battery temperature sensor E: the reading jumps far faster than the heavy battery mass could warm or cool. GM documents the method in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 18OBDG02).

causes.text: Loose terminal or unlatched connector of sensor E
Cracked or chafed sensor wire breaking contact intermittently
Sensing board fault affecting several temperature inputs

symptoms: Sensor E value jumping on the scan tool

P0BC7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit/Open
P0BC7.summary: Many battery cooling fans report their actual speed back to the controller as a pulse signal; Toyota patents describe a rotation sensor on the fan motor whose measured speed is compared with the target. P0BC7 means this feedback line for fan 1 is open or carries no usable signal.

causes.text: Open feedback wire or loose pin at the fan connector
Failed speed sensor or electronics inside the fan unit
Faulty feedback input in the controlling module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Reduced electric assist or charging power
Fan audible even though the code reports no feedback

P0BC8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Range/Performance
P0BC8.summary: P0BC8 compares the speed fed back by battery cooling fan 1 with what the controller commanded. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables run two checks.

causes.text: Dust-clogged impeller, blocked intake or worn fan bearing
Fan keeps running while commanded off (stuck drive or relay)
Fan electronics reporting a wrong speed

symptoms: Weak airflow or unusual fan noise from the battery intake
Reduced electric assist when the pack warms up

P0BC9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit Low
P0BC9.summary: P0BC9 means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly low while the fan is running. GM evaluates the feedback as a frequency: in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables the code counts a failure when the frequency stays below 8 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Fan seized, blocked or without power
Feedback wire shorted to ground or interrupted
Failed speed sensor inside the fan unit

symptoms: No airflow from the battery cooling fan
Reduced power when the battery gets warm

P0BCA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit High
P0BCA.summary: P0BCA means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly high. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables count a failure when the feedback frequency exceeds 290 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Electrical noise on the feedback line from poor routing or a bad ground
Feedback wire shorted to voltage or another signal
Fan electronics sending an invalid speed signal

symptoms: Implausible fan speed reading on the scan tool

P0BCB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BCB.summary: P0BCB flags a speed feedback from battery cooling fan 1 that drops out or jumps in a way no rotating fan can, typically a loose contact in the feedback line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables, which watch the same pulse feedback, list only performance, low and high (P0BC8, P0BC9, P0BCA).

causes.text: Loose or corroded terminal in the feedback circuit
Chafed harness near the fan or battery case
Intermittent fault in the fan's speed sensor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL, sometimes coming and going
Fan speed reading jumping on the scan tool

P0BCC.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0BCC.summary: In a two-machine hybrid one inverter feeds the traction motor and a second one the generator, the machine that is mainly driven by the engine to charge the battery or start it. Its power switches carry thermistors so the controller can cut current before they overheat.

causes.text: Fault of the sensor or its circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Software fault in the inverter or hybrid control module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced generator output and battery charging
Engine runs more often or hybrid mode limited

P0BCD.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0BCD.summary: P0BCD flags a generator inverter temperature sensor A whose signal is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state, for example a value stuck at one temperature or far from the other temperatures after a long soak. Ford documents this exact code: on 2020 Lincoln Aviator 3.0L hybrids built up to 18 July 2020, P0BCD stored in the inverter system controller (SOBDMC) lights the MIL and is caused by software; the fix is reprogramming that module.

causes.text: Inverter controller software (Ford SSM 49120, Lincoln Aviator 2020)
Sensor drifting or stuck at one value
Uneven inverter coolant flow distorting the comparison

symptoms: Often no noticeable change in driving

P0BCE.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0BCE.summary: P0BCE means the signal of generator inverter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. Inverter thermistors are usually NTC types with a pull-up resistor, as GM's tables describe for the drive motor inverter sensors: a short to ground or a shorted element pulls the voltage down, which the controller reads as an impossibly hot inverter.

causes.text: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Battery charge drops, engine runs more

P0BCF.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0BCF.summary: P0BCF reports a signal from generator inverter temperature sensor A above its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor and pull-up, an open circuit, a lost sensor ground or a cracked element drives the voltage up, which reads as an extremely cold inverter.

causes.text: Open sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BD0.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BD0.summary: P0BD0 is reserved for a generator inverter temperature sensor A signal that jumps or briefly drops out instead of failing for good. A liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature slowly, so sudden steps point to a contact problem or to interference: a Hitachi patent on inverter systems explains that the small sensor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit and has to be filtered statistically.

causes.text: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter connector
Intermittent fault inside the inverter assembly
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief drops in generator or hybrid power
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BD1.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P0BD1.summary: Which thermistor is called sensor C depends on the maker. In GM's hybrid tables it is the second sensor of the motor A inverter: the phase V sensor in the 2016 to 2019 tables, labelled temperature sensor 2 in the Volt and ELR.

causes.text: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp

P0BD2.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P0BD2.summary: P0BD2 checks whether inverter temperature sensor C, GM's second sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the other temperatures after a cold soak. More than 20 °C apart sets it: Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt; Type A in a 2019 table; Type A on the 2011 Volt and 2016 ELR, compared with coolant and transmission temperature after 6 h off.

causes.text: Inverter module software (GM bulletin 18-NA-064, Bolt EV/Ampera-e)
Sticking thermostat in the power electronics coolant hose (Porsche Cayenne S E-Hybrid)
Inverter temperature sensor C drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often without drivability change
Red hybrid warning in the cluster (Porsche)

P0BD3.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P0BD3.summary: P0BD3 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor C, the phase V sensor of GM's motor A inverter, is below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground reads as an impossibly hot inverter.

causes.text: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning

P0BD4.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P0BD4.summary: P0BD4 reports a voltage from inverter temperature sensor C above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor this is an implausibly cold inverter, typically caused by an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked element.

causes.text: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BD5.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BD5.summary: P0BD5 is meant for an inverter temperature sensor C signal that jumps or drops out for short moments. Because the heat sink of a liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature smoothly, sudden steps point to a contact fault or to interference; a Hitachi patent explains that the small thermistor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit.

causes.text: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BD6.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P0BD6.summary: Sensor D is, in GM's hybrid tables, the second thermistor of the motor B inverter, the counterpart of sensor C in the motor A inverter: phase V in the 2016 to 2019 tables, temperature sensor 2 of inverter B on the Volt. Other makers assign the letter differently.

causes.text: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive or generator power
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

P0BD7.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P0BD7.summary: P0BD7 is the plausibility check for inverter temperature sensor D, GM's second sensor in the motor B inverter. After a cold soak its reading is compared with an average vehicle temperature; more than 20 °C apart sets the code, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt and Type A in a 2019 table.

causes.text: Inverter temperature sensor D drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module
Uneven inverter coolant flow after soak

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often after two trips
Further inverter temperature codes may be stored

P0BD8.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P0BD8.summary: P0BD8 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor D is below its valid range; with an NTC thermistor and pull-up that reads as an extremely hot inverter, usually from a short to ground or an internal sensor fault. GM sets it above 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt, above 159 °C, Type A, in a 2019 table, above 130 °C, Type A, on the 2011 Volt and above 125 °C, two trips, in the 2012 table.

causes.text: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter (Jeep Compass PHEV bulletin)
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Vehicle does not start, Electric Traction System Fault (Jeep)

P0BD9.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P0BD9.summary: P0BD9 means inverter temperature sensor D delivers a voltage above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor in the motor B inverter that equals an implausibly cold inverter, so an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked thermistor is likely.

causes.text: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Reduced motor B power and regeneration
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BDA.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BDA.summary: P0BDA covers an inverter temperature sensor D signal that changes in steps or drops out briefly. Real temperatures of a liquid-cooled inverter move smoothly, so such jumps suggest a contact problem or interference from the high-voltage switching, which a Hitachi patent on inverter systems names as a typical disturbance of the small sensor signal.

causes.text: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BDB.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit
P0BDB.summary: Which thermistor counts as inverter temperature sensor E is set by the manufacturer. In GM's hybrid tables it is the third sensor of the motor A inverter (PIM sensor #3), assigned to phase W in the 2016 to 2019 tables.

causes.text: Internal fault of the thermistor or its circuit inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Further inverter temperature codes stored at the same time

P0BDC.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Range/Performance
P0BDC.summary: P0BDC checks whether inverter temperature sensor E, GM's phase W sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the vehicle after a long stand. The 2016 and 2018 tables compare it after a cold soak with a calculated average temperature; more than 20 °C apart for 0.525 of 0.625 s sets Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Phase W thermistor drifting out of tolerance
Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period
Failing power inverter module (replace only with P0AC4 per GM PIC6303A)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two drives, often without any drivability change
Code found during inspection without customer complaint

P0BDD.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Low
P0BDD.summary: P0BDD reports that the signal of inverter temperature sensor E, the phase W thermistor of GM's motor A inverter, sits below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground appears as an impossibly hot inverter.

causes.text: Shorted thermistor or signal line inside the power inverter module
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Drive motor A power strongly limited

P0BDE.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit High
P0BDE.summary: P0BDE means the signal of inverter temperature sensor E is above its valid range. For GM's NTC thermistor with pull-up that reads as an extremely cold phase W in the motor A inverter, typically an open circuit, lost reference ground or a failed sensor.

causes.text: Open thermistor or broken connection inside the power inverter module
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced electric drive power once the inverter has warmed up

P0BDF.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BDF.summary: P0BDF flags an unstable signal from inverter temperature sensor E: the reading jumps or drops out briefly instead of staying out of range, typically from a loose connector, a cracked solder joint or an ageing thermistor. In GM's hybrid tables sensor E is the phase W sensor of the motor A inverter, but GM does not list this erratic code; no manufacturer documents P0BDF publicly.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or vibrating connector at the inverter
Cracked solder joint on the inverter sensing board
Ageing thermistor with unstable resistance

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive power

P0BE0.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit
P0BE0.summary: Sensor F is, in GM's hybrid tables, the third thermistor of the motor B inverter (inverter B sensor #3), the counterpart of sensor E in the motor A inverter; the 2016 to 2019 tables assign it to phase W. Other makers may use the letter differently.

causes.text: Internal fault of the thermistor or its circuit inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

P0BE1.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Range/Performance
P0BE1.summary: P0BE1 is the plausibility check of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. After the car has stood long enough, its reading must match a reference: in the 2016 and 2018 tables a calculated average after cold soak, with more than 20 °C difference for 0.525 of 0.625 s setting Type B over two trips, Type A in a 2019 table.

causes.text: Phase W thermistor of inverter B drifting out of tolerance
Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period
Failing power inverter module (replace only with P0AC4 per GM PIC6303A)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two drives, usually without drivability change
Code found during inspection without customer complaint

P0BE2.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Low
P0BE2.summary: P0BE2 is set when the voltage from inverter temperature sensor F, the phase W thermistor in GM's motor B inverter, drops below the valid window. Because GM pairs an NTC element with a pull-up resistor, a short to ground is converted into a temperature far above anything the inverter can survive.

causes.text: Shorted thermistor or signal line inside the power inverter module
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Power of drive motor B strongly limited
Engine runs more often in hybrid operation

P0BE3.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit High
P0BE3.summary: P0BE3 is the high-signal fault of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. With an NTC element and pull-up, an open circuit or a sensor that has lost ground drives the voltage up, which the controller reads as an implausibly cold inverter.

causes.text: Open thermistor or broken connection inside the power inverter module
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B once warmed up

P0BE4.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BE4.summary: P0BE4 stands for brief dropouts or jumps in the signal of inverter temperature sensor F, which GM's hybrid tables place at phase W of the motor B inverter. The reading returns to normal between events, which separates it from the steady low and high faults P0BE2 and P0BE3.

causes.text: Loose, corroded or vibrating connector at the inverter
Cracked solder joint on the inverter sensing board
Ageing thermistor with unstable resistance

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Occasional power reduction of drive motor B

P0BE5.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0BE5.summary: The inverter of drive motor A measures the current in each motor phase with a current sensor; the controller needs these values for torque control and overcurrent protection. P0BE5 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor, used for an electrical fault that is not classed as offset, low or high.

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BE6.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BE6.summary: GM uses P0BE6 as the offset check of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter. At every start, while no current flows, the controller learns the sensor's zero offset; if it exceeds 30 A (2011 Volt and 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B) or 35 A (2019 table, Type A), the code sets.

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase U current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BE7.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BE7.summary: P0BE7 means the output of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter has fallen below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and compares it with a limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, both Type A; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for these sensors.

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A

P0BE8.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BE8.summary: P0BE8 is the high-side counterpart of P0BE7: the phase U current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. GM's tables set it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A, one trip; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; above 700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; and above 440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table.

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BE9.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BE9.summary: P0BE9 covers a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter, meaning an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to an offset, low or high condition. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BEA.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEA.summary: P0BEA is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM implements it as an offset test: with no current flowing at start-up, the learned zero point must stay within 30 A (2011 Volt, 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B, with P0BEB/P0BEC not active) or 35 A (2019 table, Type A, after a 0.4 s delay).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase V current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BEB.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEB.summary: P0BEB reports that the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. GM compares the converted current with a lower limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019 table), Type A, one trip; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks.

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BEC.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BEC.summary: P0BEC is set when the phase V current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. In GM's tables the limit is above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt with PWM output disabled; and above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks.

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BED.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BED.summary: P0BED is the general circuit code of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor A inverter, for an electrical fault outside the offset, low and high categories. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's hybrid tables from the 2011 Volt to 2019, including the BAS Plus (eAssist) system, use P0BEE, P0BEF and P0BF0 instead.

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or assist from drive motor A

P0BEE.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEE.summary: P0BEE checks the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the sensor offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A (2011 Volt and 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B) or above 35 A (2019 table, Type A).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase W current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BEF.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEF.summary: P0BEF indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table.

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A

P0BF0.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF0.summary: P0BF0 is the high-signal fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM sets it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, Type A, one trip; above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; above 440 A, Type B, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for this sensor family.

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BF1.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF1.summary: On hybrids with two electric machines, the inverter of drive motor B carries its own set of phase current sensors, which the motor control processor uses for torque control and to protect the power switches. P0BF1 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor of motor B, meant for an electrical fault that is not classified as offset, low or high.

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BF2.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF2.summary: GM runs P0BF2 as the offset test of the phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter. Each time the vehicle is started, while no current flows through the motor, the controller learns the sensor's zero point and compares it with a limit: 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, after 0.1 s), 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, power stage open, P0BF3/P0BF4 not active) and 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, after 0.4 s).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase U current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BF3.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF3.summary: P0BF3 is stored when the phase U current sensor of the motor B inverter reports a value below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and sets the code below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips), and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip).

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BF4.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF4.summary: P0BF4 is the upper-limit counterpart of P0BF3 for the phase U current sensor of drive motor B. GM's thresholds: above 800 A on the 2011 Volt, checked with PWM output disabled (Type A); above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips); above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip).

causes.text: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Further inverter or phase current codes stored

P0BF5.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF5.summary: P0BF5 stands for a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF6.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF6.summary: P0BF6 is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, implemented by GM as a zero offset test. The offset is learned at every start with no current through the motor and must stay within 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, P0BEB/P0BEC not active, as printed in the table) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, 0.1 s), within 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and within 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, 0.4 s).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase V current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BF7.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF7.summary: P0BF7 reports that the phase V current sensor of the motor B inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. In GM's hybrid tables the converted current must fall below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) or below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) and 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), both Type A.

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BF8.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF8.summary: P0BF8 sets when the phase V current sensor of drive motor B reports more current than its valid range allows. GM uses above 800 A on the 2011 Volt with the PWM output disabled (Type A), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip).

causes.text: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF9.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF9.summary: P0BF9 is reserved for a general circuit fault of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor B inverter, outside the offset, low and high categories that have their own codes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's tables from the 2011 Volt through 2019, and Jeep's 2020 Renegade and Compass PHEV bulletins, refer only to the specific siblings, chiefly P0BFA.

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFA.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BFA.summary: P0BFA checks the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, power stage open), above 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, only with P0BFB/P0BFC inactive), above 30 A after 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and above 35 A after 0.4 s in a 2019 table (both Type A).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase W current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)

P0BFB.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BFB.summary: P0BFB indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples at 10.4 ms), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip).

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFC.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BFC.summary: P0BFC is the signal-high fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter. GM sets it above 800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A).

causes.text: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BFD.title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFD.summary: In a three-phase motor without a neutral connection the three phase currents must add up to roughly zero. P0BFD checks this for drive motor A: if the absolute sum of the U, V and W readings exceeds a limit, at least one sensor is wrong.

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
One motor A phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BFE.title: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFE.summary: P0BFE applies the phase balance test to drive motor B: the controller adds the U, V and W current readings, which should cancel out, and sets the code when the absolute sum stays above a limit. GM uses 156 A on the 2011 Volt and 110 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type A, one trip, main relay closed) and 110 A for 0.0032 of 0.0038 s in the 2016 and 2019 tables (Type A).

causes.text: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
One motor B phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BFF.title: Drive Motor A Current
P0BFF.summary: P0BFF is the general code for the current flowing through drive motor A, the electric machine the manufacturer labels A. It covers a current fault that is not classed as too low (P0C00) or too high (P0C01).

causes.text: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase cable joint between inverter and motor A
Fault in the motor A inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor A
Motor control software fault

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric drive power or limp mode
Other drive motor A current or phase codes stored

P0C00.title: Drive Motor A Current Low
P0C00.summary: P0C00 reports that the current of drive motor A is lower than the controller expects for the commanded torque, the counterpart of P0C01 (current high). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM and Stellantis use only P0C01 from this group.

causes.text: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection at motor A or the inverter
Inverter power stage for motor A not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor A

symptoms: Weak or missing electric drive torque
Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Vehicle runs on the engine only or in limp mode

P0C01.title: Drive Motor A Current High
P0C01.summary: P0C01 is the overcurrent check of drive motor A, meant to protect the inverter's IGBTs. GM sets it when any phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt, 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 tables, or 396 A on eAssist; since 2016 a too negative d-axis current (about -540 to -310 A, depending on stator temperature) also counts.

causes.text: Damaged or improperly torqued three-phase cable joints (Stellantis S2608000006)
Damaged stator winding of motor A (GM PIP5246)
Outdated hybrid control software (Jeep TSB 08-144-23)
Failing power switch or current measurement in the inverter

symptoms: Reduced propulsion or engine unavailable message
Rough running or loud noise from the motor generator

P0C02.title: Drive Motor B Current
P0C02.summary: P0C02 is the general current code for drive motor B, the second electric machine, such as the second motor of a two-motor hybrid or the rear motor of an electric all-wheel-drive system. It applies to a current fault that is neither classed as low (P0C03) nor high (P0C04).

causes.text: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase connection of motor B
Fault in the motor B inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor B

symptoms: Hybrid or electric drive warning lamp
Reduced power or loss of all-wheel drive

P0C03.title: Drive Motor B Current Low
P0C03.summary: P0C03 indicates that drive motor B draws less current than the controller expects for the requested torque. It is the low counterpart of P0C04 and the motor B twin of P0C00.

causes.text: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection of motor B
Inverter power stage for motor B not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor B

symptoms: Weak or missing torque from motor B
Warning lamp for the hybrid or electric drive

P0C04.title: Drive Motor B Current High
P0C04.summary: P0C04 is the overcurrent check of drive motor B and protects the IGBTs of its inverter. GM flags it when the highest phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt or 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 hybrid tables; the newer tables also fail a d-axis current below a stator-temperature curve of roughly -556 to -315 A.

causes.text: Cross-threaded or loose three-phase cable bolts with metal debris (Stellantis S2608000006)
Shorted or damaged stator winding of motor B
Failing power switch or current measurement in the motor B inverter

symptoms: Limp mode with red wrench or malfunction lamp
Sudden loss of electric drive power

P0C05.title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C05.summary: P0C05 detects an open or missing phase between the inverter and drive motor A. GM checks each phase as the rotor passes its axis: if the peak phase axis current stays below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees of that axis and over 35 V on the inverter, about 200 failed samples set the code.

causes.text: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor A
Software fault, cured by update (Jeep TSB 08-144-23)
Internal fault of the motor generator unit or open stator winding
One-off event that does not return after clearing (Volvo TJ 36863)

symptoms: Propulsion system performance message or warning lamp
Loss of 12 V charging or noise from the motor generator on mild hybrids

P0C06.title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C06.summary: P0C06 belongs to the phase circuit group of drive motor A and reports that a U, V or W phase line sits too low, typically a short to the negative high-voltage rail or to chassis ground. P0C05 covers an open or missing phase, P0C07 the opposite high state.

causes.text: Phase cable or winding shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing

symptoms: Electric drive shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time

P0C07.title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C07.summary: P0C07 is the high member of the drive motor A phase circuit group: a U, V or W phase line reads higher than it should, most likely through a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a power switch that stays on. Its siblings are P0C05 for an open phase and P0C06 for a phase pulled low.

causes.text: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Phase cable shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on

symptoms: Immediate shutdown of electric drive with warning lamp

P0C08.title: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C08.summary: P0C08 is the open-phase check for drive motor B, the motor B twin of P0C05. GM runs it on the 2011 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks: each phase is checked as the rotor passes its axis, and a phase axis current below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees and over 35 V on the inverter, counts as a miss.

causes.text: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor B
Open stator winding in drive motor B
Inverter stage for motor B not conducting

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Engine running more often than usual

P0C09.title: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C09.summary: P0C09 marks a U, V or W phase line of drive motor B that is pulled low, for example by a short to the negative high-voltage rail, to ground or by a power switch that conducts when it should not. It is the motor B twin of P0C06; the siblings P0C08 and P0C0A cover an open phase and a phase stuck high.

causes.text: Phase cable or winding of motor B shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing

symptoms: Motor B shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time

P0C0A.title: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C0A.summary: P0C0A reports that a phase line of drive motor B reads too high, typically a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a high-side power switch that stays on. It mirrors P0C07 for motor A and completes the motor B trio with P0C08 (open) and P0C09 (low).

causes.text: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Phase cable of motor B shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on

symptoms: Immediate shutdown of motor B with warning lamp
Reduced performance or loss of electric all-wheel drive

P0C0B.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit/Open
P0C0B.summary: P0C0B flags a lost or interrupted supply inside the motor A inverter. GM reads it from the IGBT module status: when the gate drive supply falls below its threshold, the module reports a bias fault; on eAssist the 5 V rail below 3.5 to 4.3 V or the 15 V rail below 10.4 to 12.6 V counts, with run/crank above 7 V.

causes.text: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor A inverter
Low 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground to the inverter control board
Open high-voltage feed to the inverter, e.g. in a belt starter-alternator (Mercedes LI15.40-P-077947)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Electric drive or motor generator unavailable
Engine cannot be started, only electric driving possible (Mercedes P3 hybrids)

P0C0C.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit Low
P0C0C.summary: P0C0C reports that the supply voltage of the motor A inverter is present but too low, while P0C0B covers a lost or open supply and P0C0D a supply that is too high. Which supply is meant depends on the maker: GM ties its sibling P0C0B to the gate-drive supply of the IGBTs, Mercedes to the high-voltage feed.

causes.text: Internal fault of the drive power electronics (Audi TSB 2081725)
Weak 12 V supply, poor ground or high-resistance connector at the inverter
Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output

symptoms: Red high-voltage system warning asking to stop safely
Loss of drive power or vehicle will not get ready to drive

P0C0D.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Power Supply Circuit High
P0C0D.summary: P0C0D reports that the supply of the motor A inverter is above its permitted range, while P0C0B stands for a lost or open supply and P0C0C for a supply that is too low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.

causes.text: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor A inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or a charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced or no electric propulsion from motor A
Engine runs more often or the vehicle enters limp mode

P0C0E.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit/Open
P0C0E.summary: P0C0E is the motor B counterpart of P0C0B: the inverter for the second motor has lost the supply of its gate-drive board. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks.

causes.text: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor B inverter
Weak 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground at the inverter control board
Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion message, motor B unavailable
Engine runs continuously instead of electric driving

P0C0F.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit Low
P0C0F.summary: P0C0F means the supply of the motor B inverter is present but below its permitted range. P0C0E covers a lost or open supply, P0C10 a supply that is too high, and P0C0C is the same fault on motor A.

causes.text: Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output feeding the inverter electronics
Corroded connector or poor ground raising resistance in the inverter supply
Failing internal gate-drive power supply in the motor B inverter

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Fault appears mainly with low 12 V voltage, e.g. after standing

P0C10.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Power Supply Circuit High
P0C10.summary: P0C10 flags a supply of the motor B inverter that is above its permitted range. Its siblings are P0C0E for a lost or open supply and P0C0F for a low one; P0C0D is the motor A version.

causes.text: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor B inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or an external charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Vehicle limited to engine or reduced-power operation

P0C11.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase U Over Temperature
P0C11.summary: P0C11 is a protective code: the temperature sensor at phase U of the motor A inverter reads a valid but excessive value. GM uses it across its hybrids.

causes.text: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed or weak electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged power electronics radiator or inoperative cooling fan
Sustained heavy load such as towing uphill in high ambient heat

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often with a hybrid system overheat message
Reduced propulsion power until the inverter cools down
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs continuously

P0C12.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase V Over Temperature
P0C12.summary: P0C12 sets when the inverter for motor A measures an excessive temperature at phase V while its sensor itself is plausible. In GM's 2011 Volt table that is PIM sensor C above 98 °C; the two-mode trucks of 2012 use 88 °C with an 85 °C reset, the 2016 Volt 126 °C for 1.2 s out of 2 s and the 2016 ELR 102.5 °C, all Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Low coolant level or trapped air in the inverter cooling loop
Inoperative electric coolant pump of the power electronics
Blocked low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Degraded thermal contact or failing power stage inside the inverter

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Propulsion power reduced, especially under load or in hot weather
Hybrid system overheat or service message

P0C13.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Phase W Over Temperature
P0C13.summary: P0C13 covers phase W of the motor A inverter: the controller sees a credible sensor reading that exceeds the overtemperature limit. GM's 2011 Volt uses PIM sensor E with 98 °C, the 2012 two-mode trucks 88 °C, the 2016 and 2018 tables 126 °C for 1.2 s within a 2 s window and the 2019 table 128 °C for 1.5 s, always Type A, one trip, so the MIL comes on at once.

causes.text: Coolant loss or air pocket in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump for the inverter stopped or running slow
Debris on the low-temperature radiator or cooling fan not running

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp immediately after the fault
Engine runs more often, little or no electric driving

P0C14.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase U Over Temperature
P0C14.summary: P0C14 is the motor B counterpart of P0C11: phase U of the second inverter has become too hot while its temperature sensor reads plausibly. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks.

causes.text: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Long periods of high load on motor B, e.g. towing or steep climbs

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion power, especially under load

P0C15.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase V Over Temperature
P0C15.summary: P0C15 reports overtemperature at phase V of the motor B inverter, based on a sensor reading that is valid but above the limit. GM applies it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks: PIM sensor D above 98 °C on the 2011 Volt, 88 °C on the 2012 trucks, 102.5 °C on the 2016 ELR, 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s on the 2016 Volt and in the 2018 table, every time Type A with one trip.

causes.text: Coolant loss or air in the inverter cooling loop
Electric coolant pump of the power electronics not working
Blocked radiator for the power electronics or fan failure
Poor heat transfer or ageing power stage inside the inverter

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion until the inverter has cooled
Engine runs more often than usual

P0C16.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Phase W Over Temperature
P0C16.summary: P0C16 is set by the motor B inverter when phase W runs too hot and the temperature sensor itself shows no fault. GM's tables give PIM sensor F above 98 °C for the 2011 Volt, above 88 °C with an 85 °C reset for the 2012 two-mode trucks, and 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s for the 2016 Volt, with 1.5 s in the 2019 table; each is Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump of the inverter failed or blocked
Dirty low-temperature radiator or inoperative fan

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion, notably at high load or high ambient temperature

P0C17.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Not Learned
P0C17.summary: P0C17 means the controller has no valid learned offset for the resolver of motor A, which it needs to align rotor position with the stator field. GM runs the learn at key-off and sets the code if it fails without a stored value: motor speed above 50 rpm, DC voltage below 192 V (200 V on the 2016 Volt), phase current below 15 A or a learn time over 1.4 s.

causes.text: Offset learn not performed after replacing the inverter, motor or resolver
High voltage not reaching the inverter during the learn, e.g. contactor or HV cable fault
Loose three-phase ring terminals after a repair
Damaged motor stator winding (GM 21-NA-218)

symptoms: Engine starts and stalls or will not start after a repair
Malfunction indicator lamp with reduced propulsion message

P0C18.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Not Learned
P0C18.summary: P0C18 is the motor B version of P0C17: the resolver offset of the second motor has not been learned and no valid earlier value is stored. GM performs the learn at key-off; it fails if motor speed exceeds 50 rpm, DC voltage stays below 192 V, phase current stays below 15 A or the learn takes longer than 1.4 s.

causes.text: Offset learn not completed after replacing the inverter, motor B or its resolver
No high voltage at the drive motor control module, e.g. contactor fault or disconnected HV cable
Control module needs reprogramming to enable a wide position sensor learn

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after a repair or module programming
Reduced propulsion or vehicle will not enter ready mode
Motor B unavailable for driving or charging

P0C19.title: Drive Motor A Torque Delivered Performance
P0C19.summary: P0C19 is a plausibility check: the torque that motor A actually delivers, calculated by the motor control processor, does not follow the slewed torque command. GM sets it when the difference exceeds 123 Nm for 0.1875 s within 0.2 s on the 2016 and 2018 tables, Type A, one trip; eAssist uses 36 Nm as Type B, two trips.

causes.text: Outdated power inverter module software (Stellantis 08-059-25, 08-231-24)
Implausible rotor position signal from the motor A resolver or its wiring
Faulty phase current sensing distorting the calculated torque
Internal fault of the inverter power stage or motor winding

symptoms: Electric drive shuts off and the engine takes over
Engine stop-start no longer works or a service hybrid system warning appears

P0C1A.title: Drive Motor B Torque Delivered Performance
P0C1A.summary: P0C1A compares the torque command for motor B with the torque the motor control processor calculates as actually delivered. GM's 2016, 2018 and 2019 tables set it when the difference exceeds 132 Nm for 0.1875 s in a 0.2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only while listed resolver and motor control faults are inactive.

causes.text: Short in the internal transmission wiring connector (Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid 21-008-23)
Implausible rotor position signal from the motor B resolver
Hybrid control or inverter module software requiring an update
Faulty phase current sensing for motor B

symptoms: Vehicle in limp mode with reduced propulsion
Hybrid system warning, engine runs more often

P0C1B.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Too High
P0C1B.summary: P0C1B is a protection code: the electronics that drive the auxiliary transmission fluid pump measure a valid but excessive internal temperature. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: High transmission fluid temperature from heavy load, towing or a weak fluid cooler
Pump running against high resistance (binding, clogged filter) and heating its driver
Poor heat transfer from the module (mounting, contamination) or internal module fault

symptoms: Transmission or hybrid warning, MIL depending on manufacturer
Harsh engagement when driving off after a stop

P0C1C.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0C1C.summary: P0C1C is the general circuit fault of the temperature sensor inside the auxiliary pump control module, used when the signal is invalid without fitting the low, high or range checks. No manufacturer documents it publicly.

causes.text: Temperature sensor or its measuring circuit on the module board faulty
Unstable supply or ground of the pump module distorting the sensor reading
Moisture or fluid inside the module housing

P0C1D.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0C1D.summary: P0C1D means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers an electrically valid value that does not fit the other temperatures in the vehicle. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Board temperature sensor drifted or measuring circuit out of tolerance
Reference value wrong because the transmission fluid or coolant temperature sensor is faulty
Internal fault of the pump control module

P0C1E.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0C1E.summary: P0C1E reports that the signal voltage of the module's internal temperature sensor is below its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor, low voltage corresponds to a very high temperature, so a short to ground looks like an overheated board.

causes.text: Board temperature sensor or its signal path shorted to ground inside the module
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Fluid or moisture on the module board

symptoms: Pump switched off as if overheated, auto-stop unavailable

P0C1F.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0C1F.summary: P0C1F means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers a voltage above its valid range, which for an NTC thermistor reads as an implausibly cold board and usually indicates an open sensor path. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Board temperature sensor open or its solder joint cracked
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Ground offset at the pump module shifting the sensor voltage

symptoms: Start-stop restricted, pump in protective mode

P0C20.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0C20.summary: P0C20 means at least one of the three motor phases of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump carries no current, typically an open lead, terminal or winding. GM uses it in the pump controller of the Chevrolet Volt (2011-15 tables) and the 2016 Cadillac ELR: with the inverter in Run, high voltage above 35 V and the rotor within 30 degrees of a phase axis, the peak current of that phase is checked; below 1 A for 200 counts sets the code, Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Motor connector of the pump not fully seated, or loose phase terminal
Open phase lead between pump inverter and motor
Power switch of one phase in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding in the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon message
Reduced propulsion or no electric drive mode

P0C21.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0C21.summary: P0C21 reports a low condition on the phase U, V or W circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, usually a phase lead shorted to ground or a voltage at a phase terminal that stays below what the inverter commands. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Phase lead chafed through and shorted to ground or the transmission case
Transmission fluid or water in the motor connector creating a leakage path
Low-side switch or phase sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Motor winding shorted to the stator core

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump off, no engine auto-stop

P0C22.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0C22.summary: P0C22 reports a high condition on the U-V-W phase circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, for example a phase lead shorted to the supply or a phase voltage that stays high while the inverter should pull it down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Phase lead shorted to supply voltage or to another phase
High-side switch of the pump inverter stuck conducting
Phase current sensing in the inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in the pump motor winding

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or transmission warning
Pump shuts down, harsh engagement after stops

P0C23.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit/Open
P0C23.summary: P0C23 is set by the controlling module, usually the PCM, TCM or hybrid controller, when the circuit to the auxiliary pump control module is open. J2012 does not name the line further; in practice it is the command or enable wire.

causes.text: Open command or enable wire between controller and pump module
Pushed-out or corroded terminal at the pump module or controller connector
Input stage of the pump control module faulty

symptoms: Harsh engagement after an engine stop

P0C24.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit Low
P0C24.summary: P0C24 means the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module is held low, typically a short to ground on the command line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Command wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed at the transmission case
Fluid or corrosion in the pump connector pulling the line low
Output stage in the PCM/TCM or input of the pump module faulty

P0C25.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Circuit High
P0C25.summary: P0C25 reports that the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module sits high, for instance a command wire shorted to battery voltage or an output that cannot pull the line down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Command wire shorted to battery or another supply voltage
Output stage in the PCM/TCM stuck high
Input stage of the pump control module faulty

symptoms: Pump runs continuously or start-stop is disabled

P0C26.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current
P0C26.summary: P0C26 is the general motor current fault of auxiliary pump A: the current drawn does not match what the commanded operating point should need, without clearly being too low or too high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Low or aerated transmission fluid at the pump intake
Pump binding or contaminated, changing the motor load
Current sensing in the pump driver implausible
Outdated control software of the pump or controlling module

P0C27.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current Low
P0C27.summary: P0C27 means motor A of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump draws less current than expected, a sign that the pump is not loaded, for example because it sucks air or turns without delivering. Ford documents it twice.

causes.text: Air entering the pump supply tube (Ford 6F35, new tube with check ball)
Calibration of PCM and hybrid module (Ford Fusion/C-Max Energi)
Low transmission fluid level letting the pump draw air
High resistance or open circuit in the pump motor wiring

symptoms: Harsh transmission engagement after a start-stop event

P0C28.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Current High
P0C28.summary: P0C28 is the overcurrent protection of auxiliary pump motor A. GM uses it on Volt, ELR and later hybrids: the inverter trips when any of the U, V or W phases exceeds 35 A, in 2016 within about 4 ms of a 62 ms window, or when the d-axis current falls below a stator temperature limit, Type A, MIL on the first trip.

causes.text: Pump control software faulty (Cadillac CT6 update 18199, Ford Energi TSB 18-2282)
Pump seized, contaminated or running against blocked flow
Short between motor phases or to ground
Current sensing or power stage in the pump inverter faulty

symptoms: Auxiliary pump shuts down, no auto-stop or electric mode

P0C29.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Driver Circuit Performance
P0C29.summary: P0C29 means the driver stage of auxiliary pump A does not behave as commanded, for instance the pump does not reach its target or the activation is reported as implausible. Volkswagen Group documents it on the 7-speed DSG 0GC (DQ381): VW lists P0C29 for the 2018 Golf R as implausible activation of auxiliary hydraulic pump 1 (V475), often with clutch and gear actuator codes as consequences; Audi's bulletin for the 2017-18 A3, A3 Cabriolet and S3 with gearbox dated up to 26 September 2017 calls for replacing the auxiliary hydraulic pump when only P0C29 remains.

causes.text: Auxiliary hydraulic pump V475 of early production faulty (VW/Audi 0GC)
Poor contact at the pump electrical connection
Transmission control software not updated per service action

symptoms: Gearbox Malfunction warning in the instrument cluster
Consequential clutch or gear actuator codes, limp mode

P0C2A.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Stalled
P0C2A.summary: P0C2A means motor A of the auxiliary pump is commanded but does not turn, or turns far slower than required. Ford documents it in TSB 17-2056 for the 2016 F-150 2.7L with start-stop built from 1 May 2016: with the fluid above 38 °C the technician commands the pump through the PCM at duty cycles from 20 to 90 percent; if it runs, the PCM gets new software, if not, the auxiliary pump is replaced.

causes.text: Auxiliary pump seized or jammed by debris (Ford F-150 2.7L replaces the pump)
PCM calibration causing false stall detection (Ford TSB 17-2056)
Very cold, thick fluid or wrong fluid type raising drag
Open phase so the motor cannot develop torque

symptoms: Start-stop inactive, harsh engagement after stops

P0C2B.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal
P0C2B.summary: P0C2B concerns the status signal the auxiliary pump control module sends back to the controlling module. GM uses it on the Two-Mode hybrid trucks and SUVs (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra, 2ML70): the hybrid controller expects a complete fault status message from the pump controller every 1.5 s; if it is missing or incomplete for 9.75 s with the vehicle in Run or Crank, the code sets as Type B, MIL after two trips.

causes.text: Wiring or terminal tension fault between hybrid controller and pump control module
Early pump control module (GM date code 089-11 or older)
Key held in crank for a long time during a no-start

symptoms: Bumps, lulls or surges around auto-stops

P0C2C.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal Range/Performance
