P0C2C.summary: P0C2C means the feedback signal from the auxiliary pump control module is present and electrically valid but does not make sense, for example a reported speed or status that contradicts the command. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Electronics of the pump module reporting wrong status or speed
Intermittent contact on the feedback line distorting the signal
Pump not following the command mechanically, so feedback and command differ

symptoms: Reduced propulsion power or no start-stop

P0C2D.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal Low
P0C2D.summary: P0C2D reports that the feedback signal from the electric transmission fluid pump module stays low, below its valid range. GM documents it for the 2021-23 Chevrolet Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV in bulletin 21-NA-148: the driver sees Propulsion Power is Reduced and a Service Vehicle Soon lamp, with P0C2D, P2797 or P2798 stored.

causes.text: Faulty solder joints in the electric transmission fluid pump (Chevrolet Bolt, GM 21-NA-148)
Feedback line shorted to ground
Corroded or loose pump connector

P0C2E.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Module Feedback Signal High
P0C2E.summary: P0C2E means the feedback line from the auxiliary pump control module sits above its valid range, for example shorted to supply voltage or no longer pulled down by the module. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.

causes.text: Feedback line shorted to supply voltage
Output stage of the pump control module no longer switching
Lost ground at the pump module letting the line float high

symptoms: MIL or Service Vehicle Soon lamp

P0C2F.title: Internal Control Module Drive Motor/Generator - Engine Speed Sensor Performance
P0C2F.summary: P0C2F is an internal plausibility check of the hybrid control processor: the engine speed it reads through its own sensor path must match other speed information. In GM's Two-Mode truck tables (12OBDG06, 13OBDG06) the HCP compares its SPI-sensed engine speed with the calculated transmission input speed and with the engine speed received over CAN; a deviation beyond 250 rpm above 1500 rpm, with a wider band at lower speed, in 160 of 320 samples sets it as Type A, MIL after one trip.

causes.text: Control module software flagging the comparison falsely (Ford Mach-E, fixed by reprogramming)
Speed signals disagree because of a faulty input or a disturbed CAN signal
Internal fault of the hybrid control module

symptoms: One pedal drive or regenerative functions switched off (Ford Mach-E)
Reduced hybrid assist or limited power

P0C30.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack State of Charge High
P0C30.summary: P0C30 is the counterpart of P0A7D: the battery controller finds that the state of charge of the high-voltage pack stays above its usable window. CARB requires hybrid OBD to flag a state of charge that can no longer be kept inside the manufacturer's range.

causes.text: Wrong SOC estimate from a drifting pack current or voltage measurement
Battery or hybrid control software not drawing the charge down as intended
Electric assist blocked by another fault, so the pack cannot discharge

symptoms: Changed brake pedal feel and higher fuel consumption

P0C31.title: Inverter B Cooling System Performance
P0C31.summary: P0C31 reports that the cooling circuit of a second power inverter does not remove heat as expected; inverter A has its own code, P0A93. Vehicles with two separately cooled power electronics units, for example a front and a rear drive unit, need this second code.

causes.text: Low coolant level or air trapped in the inverter B circuit
Weak or failed electric coolant pump of the circuit
Clogged radiator or inoperative cooling fan

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Reduced drive power, especially under load or in heat
Coolant level low in the electronics reservoir

P0C32.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Cooling System A Performance
P0C32.summary: P0C32 is the functional check of the battery thermal system that CARB asks for. GM tunes it per vehicle: the 2012 Volt (12OBDG01A) fails it when the average pack temperature stays above 40 °C in active cooling or below −17 °C in active heating, after 4200 s or 9000 s, Type A, one trip.

causes.text: Battery cooling fan stopping at low 12 V system voltage (GM eAssist)
Low coolant, air or a weak pump in a liquid-cooled pack circuit
Blocked cooling air intake or ducts of an air-cooled pack
Failed pack heater or chiller valve

symptoms: Charging system or battery warning message (eAssist)

P0C33.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit
P0C33.summary: Battery temperature sensor F is the sixth thermistor in the high-voltage pack; GM's Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the F codes under temperature sensor 6 of nine. P0C33 is the general circuit code for an electrical fault the controller does not classify as low, high or erratic.

causes.text: Loose or corroded connector of sensor F at the sensing board
Failed thermistor F
Faulty input on the battery sensing board or module

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Battery cooling running more than usual

P0C34.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit Range/Performance
P0C34.summary: P0C34 checks whether sensor F, GM's sensor 6, agrees with the rest of the pack. The controller compares its reading with the average of the other battery temperature sensors.

causes.text: Sensor F drifting or poorly seated on its cell group
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)
Real local temperature difference from a weak cell group or uneven cooling

symptoms: Battery too cold or reduced power message

P0C35.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit Low
P0C35.summary: Sensor F is an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so its voltage drops as temperature rises; a short to ground looks like an extremely hot cell group. Low refers to the signal, not to the temperature.

causes.text: Sensor F signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internally shorted thermistor F
Faulty input on the battery sensing board

symptoms: Battery cooling running at high speed
Strongly reduced charge and drive power

P0C36.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit High
P0C36.summary: P0C36 means the voltage from battery temperature sensor F sits above its valid range. With GM's NTC thermistor and pull-up, an open circuit, a broken wire or an unplugged connector pulls the input up and reads as an impossibly cold cell group.

causes.text: Open circuit or unlatched connector of sensor F
Thermistor F open internally
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)

symptoms: Battery too cold, plug in to warm message

P0C37.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0C37.summary: P0C37 targets a sensor F signal that jumps instead of following the slow temperature change of a heavy battery. GM documents the logic in its 2016 to 2018 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 17OBDG02, 18OBDG02): every 100 ms the controller adds up the absolute changes of the sensor value over a window of 10 samples; a sum above 10 fails the window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 set the code as Type B, two trips, with system voltage above 10.2 V and no communication fault active.

causes.text: Loose terminal or connector of sensor F not fully latched after pack work
Cracked sensor wire with intermittent contact
Faulty battery sensing board, often with several sensors affected

symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads

P0C38.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0C38.summary: The DC/DC converter steps the high-voltage battery down to the 12 V system and replaces the alternator in hybrids and EVs. Its power stage carries temperature sensors so the controller can derate before the semiconductors overheat.

causes.text: Control unit software misjudging the sensor after long parking (Hyundai Palisade Hybrid)
Fault in the circuit of sensor A inside the converter or power control unit
Internal fault of the DC/DC converter requiring replacement

symptoms: 12 V charging reduced or switched off
Code appearing after the car has stood for a long time

P0C39.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
P0C39.summary: P0C39 is the plausibility check of DC/DC converter temperature sensor A: its reading lies within the electrical range but does not fit the converter's operating state or a second sensor. FCA uses it on the 2021 Ram 1500 with the 3.6 litre eTorque mild hybrid, where the code is called temperature sensor 1 performance.

causes.text: Outdated hybrid control software (Ram 1500 eTorque, bulletin 08-037-21)
Sensor A drifting or with poor thermal contact to the power stage
Uneven cooling of the converter making the readings disagree

symptoms: MIL, after one trip with updated Ram software
Mild hybrid assist or 12 V supply reduced

P0C3A.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor A Low
P0C3A.summary: P0C3A means the signal of DC/DC converter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. Low refers to the signal voltage: with an NTC thermistor and pull-up, as GM uses for its hybrid temperature sensors, a short to ground or a failed element reads as extreme heat.

causes.text: Sensor A signal shorted to ground inside the converter or its harness
Shorted temperature element A, usually requiring converter replacement
Converter really overheated due to a cooling fault

symptoms: 12 V battery warning, system voltage dropping

P0C3B.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor A High
P0C3B.summary: P0C3B reports a signal from DC/DC converter temperature sensor A above its valid range, typically a short to positive or an open circuit pulled up by the input. Mercedes-Benz documents it on series 243 (EQB) and 465 (G-Class, including the electric G 580): information LI54.10-P-079533 describes P0C3B00 as a short circuit to positive of temperature sensor A, stored together with P0E9700, P0E5400 and P0C4000 after faulty wake-up behaviour of the converter.

causes.text: Faulty wake-up behaviour of the converter putting it into an error state (Mercedes 243/465)
Open circuit or short to positive in the sensor A circuit
Internal defect of the DC/DC converter

symptoms: Red 12 V battery warning in the cluster
White or yellow high-voltage system warning
12 V battery no longer charged while driving

P0C3C.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P0C3C.summary: P0C3C covers a signal from DC/DC converter temperature sensor A that drops out or jumps for short moments while staying mostly within range. The heat sink of a converter warms and cools slowly, so fast jumps point to the signal path rather than to real temperature changes.

causes.text: Loose terminal or moisture at the converter connector
Harness damaged by vibration with intermittent contact
Intermittent fault inside the converter

P0C3D.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P0C3D.summary: P0C3D is the general circuit code for the second temperature sensor of the DC/DC converter, which turns high-voltage battery power into 12 V supply. Converters with two sensors watch separate parts of the power stage or cross-check one sensor against the other.

causes.text: Connector or wiring fault in the sensor B circuit
Failed temperature element B inside the converter
Converter or hybrid control software misjudging the sensor

P0C3E.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor B Range/Performance
P0C3E.summary: P0C3E flags DC/DC converter temperature sensor B as electrically valid but implausible, for instance when it disagrees with sensor A or with what the converter load should produce. FCA uses it on the 2021 Ram 1500 with the 3.6 litre eTorque mild hybrid under the name temperature sensor 2 performance.

causes.text: Outdated hybrid control software (Ram 1500 eTorque, bulletin 08-037-21)
Sensor B drifting or with poor thermal contact
Uneven converter cooling making sensors A and B disagree

symptoms: MIL, after one trip with updated Ram software
Mild hybrid assist or 12 V supply reduced

P0C3F.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor B Low
P0C3F.summary: The ECM detects a low fault on the dc/dc converter temperature sensor b. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Internal sensor short

P0C40.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor B High
P0C40.summary: The ECM detects a high fault on the dc/dc converter temperature sensor b. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to B+
Open sensor

P0C41.title: DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic
P0C41.summary: The ECM detects a intermittent/erratic fault on the dc/dc converter temperature sensor b. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

causes.text: Sensor connector not seated
Noisy ground reference
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0C42.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0C42.summary: The ECM detects a circuit fault on the hybrid/ev battery pack coolant temperature sensor a circuit. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

causes.text: Sensor failed
Wiring or connector fault
Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0C43.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

causes.text: Sensor characteristic drifted

symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode

P0C44.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0C44.summary: The ECM detects a low fault on the hybrid/ev battery pack coolant temperature sensor a circuit. Reading cannot be used reliably for control.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground

P0C45.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High

P0C47.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P0C47.summary: The HV battery pack coolant pump A reports a control circuit/open condition. Battery thermal management may be impaired.

causes.text: Open in pump control wire
Open pump motor
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Reduced power output or limp mode
Charging may fail or be slowed

P0C48.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0C48.summary: The HV battery pack coolant pump A reports a control circuit low condition. Battery thermal management may be impaired.

causes.text: Wire shorted to ground

P0C4B.summary: The HV battery pack coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit/open condition. Battery thermal management may be impaired.

causes.text: Open in supply wire

P0C4C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0C4C.summary: The HV battery pack coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit low condition. Battery thermal management may be impaired.

P0C4D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0C4D.summary: The HV battery pack coolant pump A reports a supply voltage circuit high condition. Battery thermal management may be impaired.

causes.text: Wire shorted to higher voltage

P0C4E.title: Drive Motor A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P0C4E.summary: The required adaptation offset for drive motor A position sensor exceeds the calibrated learning window. Sensor or rotor mechanism out of nominal range.

causes.text: Sensor reference drifted

P0C4F.title: Drive Motor B Position Exceeded Learning Limit

P0C50.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A Circuit

causes.text: Position sensor failed

P0FFF.title: Reserved Powertrain Fault
P0FFF.summary: Manufacturer-specific reserved code in the SAE generic range used as catch-all for hybrid system faults that do not map to a more specific defined code. Should be diagnosed using the freeze frame data and any additional manufacturer codes.

causes.text: Unspecified hybrid system fault

P2000.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2000.summary: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 1 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

causes.text: Sulphur poisoning from high-sulphur fuel — desulphation regeneration not running
Thermal aging of washcoat after high-temperature exposure
Downstream NOx sensor reading drifts

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2001.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P2001.summary: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 2 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

causes.text: Sulphur poisoning
Thermal aging of washcoat

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2002.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2002.summary: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted from runaway regeneration
Differential pressure sensor drift
Leak around DPF housing

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2003.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P2003.summary: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2004.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.summary: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

causes.text: Carbon buildup blocks flap travel
IMRC actuator or vacuum motor failed
Linkage rod broken or disconnected

P2005.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2005.summary: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

causes.text: Carbon buildup blocks flap travel
IMRC actuator failed on bank 2
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2006.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2006.summary: The IMRC flap on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position and cannot open at higher rpm. Top-end power suffers because the runner is restricted, and the engine may breathe poorly above mid-range.

causes.text: Carbon deposits seize flap closed
Actuator stuck or vacuum line collapsed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2007.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2007.summary: Bank 2 counterpart to P2006. The IMRC flap on bank 2 cannot return to the open position and chokes intake flow at higher rpm.

causes.text: Carbon deposits seize flap closed on bank 2
Bank 2 actuator stuck
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2008.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Open (Bank 1)
P2008.summary: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC solenoid for bank 1. No control current flows when the runner is commanded to switch, leaving the flap in its default position.

causes.text: Solenoid coil open
Connector unplugged or corroded
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2009.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2009.summary: The IMRC solenoid drive line for bank 1 reads below the lower threshold — short to ground or a failed driver stage. The runner cannot be switched on demand.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to ground
Solenoid internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P200A.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 1)
P200A.summary: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 1 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

causes.text: Carbon buildup restricts flap travel
Actuator weak or vacuum supply low
Linkage worn — play between actuator and flap

P200B.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 2)
P200B.summary: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

causes.text: Carbon buildup

P200C.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P200C.summary: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 1 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

causes.text: Excessive soot load triggers runaway regeneration
Post-injection over-fueling during regeneration
DPF temperature sensor reading drifts high

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P200D.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P200D.summary: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 2 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

causes.text: Runaway regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P200E.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P200E.summary: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 1 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

causes.text: Persistent misfire dumps unburned fuel into the cat
Sustained rich mixture from leaking injector or fuel pressure regulator
Catalyst temperature sensor drifts high

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P200F.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P200F.summary: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 2 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

causes.text: Misfire dumps fuel into cat

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2010.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2010.summary: Drive voltage at the IMRC solenoid on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or an open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to supply
ECU driver stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2011.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)

Connector corroded — high resistance contact
Actuator solenoid winding open

P2012.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)

causes.text: Short to ground in driver line
Actuator winding shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2013.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit High (Bank 2)

causes.text: Short to B+ in driver line

P2014.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
P2014.summary: The position feedback signal of the IMRC flap on bank 1 is missing or implausible. Without feedback, the ECU cannot verify that the commanded runner position has been reached.

causes.text: Position sensor failed
Signal wire broken

P2015.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 1)

causes.text: Connector clip worn — intermittent contact
Flap sticking due to carbon
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2016.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2016.summary: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads below the lower limit. Usually a short to ground on the signal wire or a failed sensor.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2017.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor ground open

P2018.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Open (Bank 2)

P2029.title: Fuel Fired Heater Disabled

Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P20DF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P20DF.summary: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P20E0.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E0.summary: The pressure in the SCR reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line is below the calibrated minimum. Without sufficient pressure the dosing module cannot atomise reagent properly, leading to NOx exceedence.

causes.text: Worn DEF pump
Leak in DEF line
Clogged DEF filter

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E1.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E1.summary: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line pressure stays below the demanded value during dosing. The dosing system needs a stable supply pressure to inject metered amounts; without it the system cannot meet NOx targets.

causes.text: Reductant pump worn or weak
Leak in pressure line
Inline filter clogged

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E2.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E2.summary: The reductant line pressure exceeds the upper limit. A blocked return path, a stuck pump or a faulty pressure sensor are common causes; over-pressure can damage the dosing valve and the pump head.

causes.text: Return line blocked or frozen
Pressure sensor reads high
Dosing valve stuck closed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E3.summary: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.text: One EGT sensor drifts
Exhaust leak between the two sensor positions

P20E4.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E4.summary: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes.text: One EGT sensor drifts

P20E5.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P20E5.summary: EGT sensors 1 and 3 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real temperature gradient that exceeds the calibrated map (e.g. from a leaking exhaust joint between the two locations).

causes.text: One EGT sensor drifts

P20E6.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
P20E6.summary: The DEF system air-assist pressure is below the required threshold — pump weak, line leak, or pressure-control valve stuck open.

causes.text: Air pump weak
Leak in air line

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E7.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
P20E7.summary: The DEF system air-assist pressure exceeds the upper threshold — pressure-control valve stuck closed or air pump runaway.

causes.text: Pressure control valve stuck closed
Air pump does not regulate

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E8.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E8.summary: Pressure in the AdBlue/DEF supply line is below the target. Usually a failing reductant pump, a clogged filter, frozen lines, or a leak in the pressurised circuit.

causes.text: Reductant pump weak or failed
Reductant filter clogged with crystals
Leak in pressurised reductant line

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20E9.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E9.summary: Manufacturer-specific variant of the reductant over-pressure condition. The pressure exceeds the upper threshold during a defined operating window; on some platforms used in addition to P20E2 to flag a different test path.

causes.text: Return line blocked or frozen
Pressure sensor reads high

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EA.title: Reductant Pump Control Circuit Open
P20EA.summary: The control circuit to the reductant (DEF) dosing pump is open — no current flow detected. Without pump pressure no AdBlue reaches the SCR catalyst and NOx reduction stops.

causes.text: Pump motor open
Connector unplugged or corroded
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EB.title: Reductant Reservoir Heater "A" Control Circuit
P20EB.summary: A general electrical fault on the reductant tank heater "A" control circuit. AdBlue freezes at -11 C, so the tank heater must work for cold-start dosing.

causes.text: Heater element failed
Wiring open or connector loose

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EC.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck Off
P20EC.summary: The reductant tank heater "A" does not heat when commanded on. Either a failed element or a stuck-off driver in the dosing module.

causes.text: Heater element open
Heater driver stuck off
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20ED.title: Reductant Heater "A" Control Stuck On
P20ED.summary: The reductant tank heater "A" stays energised even when not commanded — usually a shorted driver stage. Continuous heating wastes current and can overheat the heater element.

causes.text: Heater driver shorted on
Heater line shorted to positive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20EE.title: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.summary: The SCR catalyst on bank 1 is no longer reducing NOx to the level the ECU expects, even with proper reductant dosing and quality. Often the result of catalyst poisoning by sulphur or hydrocarbons, thermal aging, or a leak between the upstream and downstream NOx sensors.

causes.text: SCR catalyst aged or poisoned
NOx sensor drift
Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream NOx sensors

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20EF.title: Reductant Injection Valve Performance
P20EF.summary: The SCR reductant injection valve does not deliver the commanded amount of reagent. Causes include clogging by urea crystals, electrical faults or incorrect spray pattern.

causes.text: Urea crystals in dosing valve
Electrical fault in dosing valve

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F0.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F0.summary: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

causes.text: Runaway DPF regeneration upstream
Temperature sensor drift high

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F1.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F1.summary: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

causes.text: Runaway regeneration upstream

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F2.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.summary: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: SCR catalyst thermally aged
Catalyst poisoning from sulphur or oil ash

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F3.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.summary: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Pre-catalyst thermally aged

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P20F4.title: Reductant Consumption Too Low
P20F4.summary: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is below the model expectation — typically a clogged dosing nozzle, weak pump, or leak between pump and injector that recirculates DEF back to the tank.

causes.text: Dosing nozzle clogged with crystallised DEF
Pump weak — flow under target

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F5.title: Reductant Consumption Too High
P20F5.summary: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is above the model expectation — typically a leaking injector seat, leaking line fitting, or a pressure-control valve that vents constantly to the tank.

causes.text: Injector seat leaks DEF into exhaust
Cracked line or fitting

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F6.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.summary: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.text: Valve seat eroded or contaminated
Valve plunger seized open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F7.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P20F7.summary: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes.text: Valve seat eroded or contaminated
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20F8.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.summary: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 1 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

causes.text: Solenoid winding ageing — resistance climbing

P20F9.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.summary: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

causes.text: Solenoid winding ageing

P20FA.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P20FA.summary: The control line driving DEF pump B is open. On large engines or dual-tank systems a second pump (B) supplements pump A; with B offline the system loses redundancy.

causes.text: Pump motor winding open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FB.title: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.summary: DEF pump B receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely.

causes.text: Pump head crystallised — motor seized
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FC.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.summary: DEF pump B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FD.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.summary: DEF pump B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FE.title: Reductant Metering Unit 1 Performance
P20FE.summary: The first DEF metering unit (the integrated module that combines pump, filter, level sensor, and dosing valve) is electrically OK but does not deliver the expected pressure or flow during operation.

causes.text: Metering unit aged or partially clogged

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P20FF.title: Reductant Control Module Performance
P20FF.summary: The dedicated SCR/reductant control module reports an internal performance fault — failed self-tests, watchdog resets, or calibration mismatch. Frequently a forerunner of total module failure.

causes.text: Internal module fault
Calibration mismatch after software update
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2100.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
P2100.summary: The drive-by-wire throttle motor circuit is open — no current flow detected. The ECU loses authority over the throttle plate and forces a limp-home with reduced power.

causes.text: Throttle motor failed
Connector loose or corroded
Wiring break to throttle body

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2101.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.summary: The throttle motor responds, but its actual position does not track the commanded position within tolerance. Often a dirty throttle bore where the plate sticks, or a worn motor.

causes.text: Throttle bore coked, plate sticks
Throttle motor worn
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2102.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.summary: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is below the lower limit. Typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage in the ECU.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to ground
Throttle motor internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2103.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.summary: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to supply
Throttle motor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2104.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Idle
P2104.summary: The ECU has detected a fault severe enough that it forces the throttle actuator to the idle stop. The driver loses pedal authority — only idle is available until the underlying TAC fault clears.

causes.text: Severe upstream TAC fault
Throttle position signal invalid

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2105.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.summary: The TAC monitor commanded an engine shutdown because throttle authority can no longer be guaranteed safely. The most aggressive TAC limp mode — used when both throttle position sensors disagree or the motor is uncontrollable.

causes.text: TPS1 and TPS2 disagree beyond limit
Throttle motor not controllable

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2106.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited Power
P2106.summary: The TAC monitor restricts maximum throttle opening as a safety response to a TAC fault. The vehicle can still be driven, but accelerator pedal travel is capped.

causes.text: Underlying TAC fault triggers limit
Pedal position sensor signal implausible

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2107.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Internal Processor
P2107.summary: The internal processor or watchdog of the throttle actuator control module reports an internal fault. Communication between the TAC monitor core and the main ECU core has failed plausibility — typical for a defective ECU.

causes.text: ECU internal processor fault
ECU software flash corrupted
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2108.title: Throttle Actuator Control Module Performance
P2108.summary: Self-tests within the TAC module fail their performance criteria — for example RAM/ROM checks or analog reference voltages drift. Indicates an aging ECU rather than a wiring fault.

causes.text: ECU internal performance fault
ECU connector pins corroded
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2109.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.summary: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor A signal at the closed-throttle stop does not match the learned minimum value. The mechanical or electrical zero reference of the throttle has drifted out of the expected range, often after cleaning, replacement or wear.

causes.text: Carbon deposits on throttle plate
Throttle position sensor drift
Idle/throttle relearn not performed

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.summary: The drive circuit of throttle actuator motor B is open. Throttle B is the secondary throttle on engines with two throttle bodies — typically used for tumble flap or charge-motion control.

causes.text: Motor winding open
Open wire to motor
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.summary: Throttle actuator B motor responds electrically but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically high-resistance brushes, partial winding fault, or a sticky throttle bore.

causes.text: Motor brushes worn
Carbon buildup at throttle plate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.summary: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.summary: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210E.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.summary: The redundant throttle or accelerator pedal position channels C and F disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire systems compare two or three independent channels to detect a faulty potentiometer track.

causes.text: One potentiometer track worn — voltage drift
Water in pedal connector

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P210F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.summary: Throttle B control has detected an unsafe condition and forced an RPM limit. Common protective response when motor current, throttle position feedback, or supply voltage on the B path is out of spec.

causes.text: Protection mode triggered by paired throttle-B fault

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2110.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited RPM
P2110.summary: The TAC monitor caps engine speed at a fixed limp-home rpm because it can no longer trust the throttle response. Driver may notice a hard rev limit well below redline.

causes.text: Underlying TAC fault triggers rpm cap
Throttle response time out of spec

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2111.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
P2111.summary: The throttle plate cannot be commanded back to the closed/idle position. Idle speed runs high or the engine cannot decelerate properly — safety-critical fault that usually triggers immediate limp mode.

causes.text: Throttle plate seized open
Return spring broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2112.title: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Closed
P2112.summary: The throttle plate cannot be commanded open. The engine stays at idle or stalls under load.

causes.text: Throttle plate seized closed
Throttle motor seized or gear broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2113.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Limited RPM
P2113.summary: The throttle actuator control has detected a fault and limits engine speed to a defined emergency value. The vehicle stays drivable but with severely reduced power until the underlying fault is cleared.

causes.text: Underlying throttle actuator fault
Pedal/throttle correlation fault

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2114.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Below Limit RPM
P2114.summary: The throttle actuator system has dropped engine speed below the normal limp limit because of a more serious fault. The engine may run only at idle or stall.

causes.text: Severe throttle actuator fault
TPS signal lost

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2115.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.summary: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor A is outside the expected range during the ECU self-check. The signal at fully closed throttle does not match the stored reference, indicating a mechanical or sensor issue.

causes.text: Throttle plate sticking due to carbon
Internal sensor fault

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2116.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.summary: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor B does not match the learned reference during ECU self-test. Sensor B is the redundant channel used to cross-check sensor A.

causes.text: Carbon deposits affecting throttle motion
Internal sensor B fault

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2117.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.summary: The minimum stop signal from throttle/pedal position sensor C is out of specification during initialization. Used on systems with three redundant sensor channels for safety-critical drive-by-wire control.

causes.text: Internal pedal sensor fault
Corroded connector pins

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2118.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.summary: The current draw of the throttle motor lies outside the expected range — either much higher (binding plate) or much lower (worn brushes, open winding) than calibrated.

causes.text: Plate binding from carbon
Motor windings aged or open
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2119.title: Throttle Closed Position Performance
P2119.summary: When commanded to idle, the throttle plate does not reach the calibrated closed position. Often a coked throttle bore preventing the plate from seating fully.

causes.text: Throttle bore coked at closed-position stop
Plate or stop misadjusted after service

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.summary: Throttle B is mechanically stuck open — typically carbon buildup or a broken return spring on the secondary throttle plate.

causes.text: Carbon buildup holds plate open
Return spring broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.summary: Throttle B is mechanically stuck closed — carbon buildup or a seized bearing on the secondary throttle.

causes.text: Carbon buildup holds plate closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.summary: Throttle B motor current draw does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction.

causes.text: High friction in throttle bore
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.summary: The throttle B body itself does not respond as commanded — position feedback is plausible but does not track the setpoint within the calibrated time window.

causes.text: Throttle body aged or contaminated
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211E.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.summary: The processor monitoring throttle B inside the throttle/PCM has reported a self-test failure — RAM check, ROM check, or watchdog timeout.

causes.text: Internal processor fault
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
Supply voltage outside specification

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P211F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.summary: The throttle control module on the B path reports general performance issues — internal fault, communication mismatch, or calibration drift.

causes.text: Internal module fault
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
Supply voltage outside specification

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2120.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit
P2120.summary: A general electrical fault on the "C" channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor. Drive-by-wire pedals carry two or three redundant tracks; "C" is the third channel.

causes.text: Pedal sensor track C failed
Signal wire open

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Range/Performance
P2121.summary: The "C" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the other channels or the operating point.

causes.text: Sensor track C worn
Correlation with tracks A/B lost
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low
P2122.summary: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.text: Pedal sensor track worn
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High
P2123.summary: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Low
P2124.summary: The "C" channel signal is below the lower threshold — usually a short to ground or an open signal wire.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Signal wire open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2125.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit High
P2125.summary: The "C" channel signal is above the upper threshold — typically a short to positive or an open ground.

causes.text: Signal shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2126.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "C" Circuit Intermittent
P2126.summary: The "C" channel produces an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a worn track inside the pedal sensor.

causes.text: Connector intermittent
Track C worn at common pedal angle
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2127.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low

P2175.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P2175.summary: Sustained low air-flow condition detected — slower than P2174 but persistent. Restricted air filter, dirty MAF, or partially-stuck throttle.

causes.text: Air filter heavily restricted
MAF sensor contaminated

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2176.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.summary: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Idle relearn procedure not completed

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2177.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 1
P2177.summary: Fuel trim values on bank 1 indicate a lean condition during off-idle operation. The ECU has to add significant fuel correction to maintain stoichiometric mixture above idle.

causes.text: Vacuum leak under load
Low fuel pressure / weak pump
Contaminated MAF sensor

P2178.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 1
P2178.summary: Bank 1 fuel trim shows a strong rich correction during off-idle operation. The ECU is forced to subtract fuel to keep the mixture near stoichiometric.

causes.text: Leaking fuel injector
Excessive fuel pressure
Stuck-open purge valve

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2179.title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 2
P2179.summary: Fuel trims on bank 2 show a lean deviation during off-idle operating conditions. Causes are similar to bank 1 but isolated to the second cylinder bank.

causes.text: Vacuum leak on bank 2
Low fuel pressure

P217A.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P217A.summary: The supply rail to injector group G is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders.

causes.text: Open supply wire or blown fuse
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P217B.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P217B.summary: The supply voltage feeding injector group G has dropped below the lower limit. The injectors in this group lose drive voltage and may stop firing, so the cylinders they serve run lean or cut out.

causes.text: Fuse, relay, or wiring fault on supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P217C.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit High
P217C.summary: The supply voltage on injector group G is above the upper limit. Overvoltage on the group-G supply can mis-time or damage the injectors.

causes.text: Charging system overvoltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P217D.title: Fuel Injector Group H Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P217D.summary: The supply rail to injector group H is open, so none of the injectors in this group can fire. The affected cylinders produce no power and the engine runs rough or on reduced cylinders.

Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder

P2180.title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 2
P2180.summary: Bank 2 fuel trim shows a rich shift during off-idle conditions. The ECU subtracts fuel to maintain proper combustion.

causes.text: Leaking injector on bank 2
Excessive fuel pressure

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2181.title: Cooling System Performance
P2181.summary: The engine cooling system does not reach or maintain the expected temperature within the diagnostic window — usually a stuck-open thermostat, but also a low coolant level or a stuck cooling fan that overcools the engine.

causes.text: Thermostat stuck open
Coolant level low
Cooling fan stuck on

P2182.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
P2182.summary: A general electrical fault is reported on engine coolant temperature sensor 2 — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor 2 is typically at the radiator outlet or as redundancy on the second cylinder bank.

causes.text: Sensor failed
Harness fault

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2183.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P2183.summary: ECT sensor 2 reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response, stuck reading, or value does not track ECT 1 across a warm-up.

causes.text: Sensor drifts over service life
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2184.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2184.summary: ECT sensor 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2185.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
P2185.summary: The second coolant temperature sensor (often radiator-outlet or cylinder-head bank) reports a voltage above the upper threshold — typically an open signal wire or a sensor with infinite resistance.

causes.text: Sensor element open
Signal wire open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2186.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2186.summary: The second coolant temperature sensor reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Sensor element shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P2187.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P2187.summary: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

causes.text: Vacuum leak (intake gasket, brake booster, hoses)
PCV valve stuck open

P2188.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P2188.summary: Fuel trim on bank 1 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.

causes.text: Leaking injector at idle
Purge valve stuck open

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2189.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P2189.summary: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the lean limit only at idle, while trim returns to normal at higher load. This pattern strongly indicates a vacuum leak — leaks become a larger fraction of total airflow at idle and so dominate the trim, but disappear into background noise above idle.

causes.text: Vacuum leak on bank 2
PCV valve stuck open

P218A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P218A.summary: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Idle relearn procedure not completed

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P218B.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit
P218B.summary: A general electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit signal B — used by anti-theft, immobiliser, or transmission to forbid throttle/fuel until released.

causes.text: Inhibit signal lost

P218C.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Range/Performance
P218C.summary: Throttle/fuel inhibit B signal reads in range but plausibility fails — does not assert/release as expected.

causes.text: Inhibit logic mismatch
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P218D.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Low
P218D.summary: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P218E.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit High
P218E.summary: Throttle/fuel inhibit B line stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P218F.title: Reductant No Flow Detected
P218F.summary: The DEF dosing system commands flow but the pressure or flow sensor reports no actual delivery — typically a fully blocked dosing nozzle, a frozen line, or a dead pump.

causes.text: Dosing line or nozzle fully blocked
Pump dead
Line frozen at very low ambient temperature

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2190.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P2190.summary: Fuel trim on bank 2 hits the rich limit only at idle. Often a leaking injector dribbling fuel at low load, a sticky purge valve dumping fuel vapour, or fuel pressure regulator that fails to relieve pressure when intake vacuum is high.

causes.text: Leaking injector at idle on bank 2
Purge valve stuck open

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2191.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2191.summary: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

causes.text: Fuel pump weak under load
Fuel filter clogged
MAF reads low at high airflow

P2192.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2192.summary: Bank 1 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.

causes.text: Fuel pressure too high
MAF reads low under load
Coolant temperature sensor stuck cold

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2193.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2193.summary: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the lean limit only at higher engine load. Pattern points to a fuel-supply restriction — failing fuel pump, blocked filter, or weak injectors — rather than a vacuum leak (which would dominate at idle).

causes.text: Fuel pump weak under load
Fuel filter clogged

P2194.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2194.summary: Bank 2 fuel trim hits the rich limit only at higher load. Often excessive fuel pressure, a stuck-closed MAF reading low, or coolant temperature signal stuck cold causing over-fuelling.

causes.text: Fuel pressure too high

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2195.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2195.summary: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

causes.text: Upstream sensor failed stuck lean
Sensor heater slow to warm up

P2196.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2196.summary: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 returns a constant rich signal under deceleration fuel cut-off where lean is expected. Often a contaminated sensor (silicone, oil, coolant) or short to ground that pulls the signal high in some sensor types.

causes.text: Upstream sensor contaminated
Upstream sensor failed stuck rich

P2197.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2197.summary: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 returns a constant lean signal during conditions where rich content is expected (for example after a deceleration fuel cut-off recovery). Usually a sensor that has lost its rich-side response or a slow heater warm-up.

causes.text: Upstream sensor failed stuck lean

causes.text: Injector clogged or leaking
