P21F4.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F4.summary: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

causes.text: Vacuum leak
Port injectors clogged
Fuel pressure low

P21F5.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F5.summary: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

causes.text: Port injectors leaking
Fuel pressure high

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P21F6.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F6.summary: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition outside idle. On dual-injection systems (port + direct) the secondary loop trims port injection independently from the main loop.

causes.text: Vacuum leak or injector clog

P21F7.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F7.summary: The secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a rich condition outside idle.

causes.text: Injectors leaking

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P21F8.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F8.summary: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 1. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.

causes.text: Vacuum leak — most visible at idle

P21F9.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F9.summary: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

causes.text: Injectors leak at low duty cycle

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P21FA.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FA.summary: Secondary fuel control loop B reports a lean condition at idle on bank 2. Idle is sensitive to vacuum leaks since manifold flow is low.

causes.text: Vacuum leak on bank 2 intake

P21FB.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FB.summary: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at idle on bank 2. Idle rich often means injectors that leak at low duty cycle.

causes.text: Injectors leak on bank 2

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P21FC.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FC.summary: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 1 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.

causes.text: Fuel pressure drops under load
Charge-air leak after turbo

P21FD.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FD.summary: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1): the fuel-trim control is correcting for an over-rich mixture in this operating range.

causes.text: Fuel pressure regulator stuck high

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P21FE.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FE.summary: Secondary fuel control loop B on bank 2 reports a lean condition at higher load. Lean at high load typically points at fuel pressure shortfall, restricted injectors, or charge-air leak.

causes.text: Fuel or charge-air problem on bank 2

P21FF.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FF.summary: The secondary fuel control loop B reports a rich condition at higher load on bank 2. Rich at high load typically points to a stuck-closed return on the fuel pressure regulator or over-delivering injectors.

causes.text: Injectors over-deliver on bank 2

symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust on acceleration
Smell of unburned fuel, fouled spark plugs

P2200.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1)
P2200.summary: The NOx sensor on bank 1 — typically upstream of the SCR catalyst — does not communicate or sends an invalid signal. NOx sensors are smart sensors with their own controller on the CAN bus; faults often involve heater failure or bus dropout.

causes.text: NOx sensor failed
Sensor wiring or CAN harness open

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2201.title: NOx Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2201.summary: The bank 1 NOx sensor reports values outside the plausibility window against modeled NOx and the downstream sensor. Often slow response from contamination by oil ash or coolant.

causes.text: NOx sensor aged — slow response
Sensor element contaminated
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2202.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2202.summary: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is below the lower limit. Either short to ground on the analog return, sensor failed at low end, or pump cell stuck.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor failed low
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2203.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2203.summary: The NOx sensor signal on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground, or a sensor that failed high. SCR control runs in default mode.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor failed high
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2204.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P2204.summary: The bank 1 NOx sensor signal drops out intermittently. Typical cause is a marginal connector, harness chafing near hot exhaust components, or thermal-cycling solder joints inside the smart sensor.

causes.text: Connector intermittent contact
Harness chafed near exhaust
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2205.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1)
P2205.summary: The heater inside the bank 1 NOx sensor cannot be controlled — open, short, or failed driver. Without proper heater operation the sensor never reaches its operating temperature and reports invalid data.

causes.text: Heater element open
Heater short to supply or ground

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2206.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
P2206.summary: A general electrical fault on the bank 2 NOx sensor circuit. NOx sensors are smart sensors with a CAN/LIN interface; this code typically indicates that the sensor module no longer responds.

causes.text: NOx sensor module failed
Wiring open or connector loose

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2207.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2207.summary: The bank 2 NOx sensor returns values outside the expected range for the operating point — for example a non-zero reading at engine off or unchanged values during load changes.

causes.text: Sensor drift due to ageing
Sensor contaminated with soot or condensate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2208.title: NOx Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 2)
P2208.summary: A general electrical fault on the heater of the bank 2 NOx sensor. NOx sensors must reach roughly 800 C to measure correctly; without heater current the sensor never enters its operating range.

causes.text: Heater element failed
Heater wiring open or connector loose

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2209.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2209.summary: The heater feedback (sense) line on the bank 2 NOx sensor reports values outside the expected window — heating is happening but the temperature does not match the model.

causes.text: Heater element ageing, resistance drift
Sensor module failed
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220A.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220A.summary: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

causes.text: Fuse, harness break, or short

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220B.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220B.summary: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

causes.text: Supply rail fault

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220C.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P220C.summary: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

causes.text: Supply rail fault

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220D.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P220D.summary: The supply voltage rail to the NOx sensor on bank 2 sensor 2 is faulty — typically a fuse, harness break, or short. NOx sensors need a clean stable supply for the heater and the wide-band measurement cell.

causes.text: Supply rail fault

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220E.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220E.summary: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.

causes.text: Heater element ageing
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P220F.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220F.summary: The heater control loop for the NOx sensor at bank 1 sensor 2 reports off-spec behaviour — heater current draw or response time outside the calibrated range. NOx sensors only operate above ~600 °C, so heater control is critical.

causes.text: Heater element ageing

Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P225E.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225E.summary: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously high for too long — biased upward or stuck. Common after sensor poisoning by silicon, sulphur, or oil ash.

causes.text: Sensor poisoned
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P225F.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225F.summary: The NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 reads suspiciously low for too long — biased downward or stuck. Common after sensor element ageing, condensate damage from cold start, or wiring fault that pulls the signal down.

causes.text: Sensor aged
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2260.title: Secondary Air Injection System Control B Circuit High
P2260.summary: AIR system control B drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2261.title: Turbo/Super Charger Bypass Valve Mechanical
P2261.summary: The ECU detects a mechanical fault in the turbocharger or supercharger bypass valve. The valve does not open or close as commanded, causing boost-pressure errors and reduced engine response.

causes.text: Stuck bypass valve
Leak in vacuum/pressure actuator

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2262.title: Turbo Boost Pressure Not Detected - Mechanical
P2262.summary: The ECU does not detect any meaningful boost pressure increase under load even though the turbocharger is commanded. Likely a mechanical defect in the turbo, charge-air piping or wastegate.

causes.text: Charge pipe loose or split
Turbocharger mechanical damage
Wastegate stuck open

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2263.title: Turbo/Super Charger Boost System Performance
P2263.summary: Boost pressure does not match the requested target during normal operation. The deviation between commanded and measured boost exceeds the calibrated tolerance, often due to leaks, sticking actuators or sensor errors.

causes.text: Charge-air leak
VNT vanes sticking with soot
Boost pressure sensor drift

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2264.title: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit
P2264.summary: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the diesel water-in-fuel sensor circuit. Until repaired, water contamination in the fuel filter cannot be detected, risking damage to the high-pressure pump and injectors.

causes.text: Defective water-in-fuel sensor
Wiring or connector fault

P2265.title: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2265.summary: The ECU detects that the water-in-fuel sensor signal is implausible compared to operating conditions. The reading does not change as expected during fuel filter purge or warm-up.

causes.text: Sensor drift or contamination
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2266.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Low
P2266.summary: The water-in-fuel sensor at the diesel fuel filter reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The sensor warns the driver to drain the filter when condensate accumulates.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2267.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit High
P2267.summary: Water-in-fuel sensor reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Open signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2268.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2268.summary: Water-in-fuel sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P2269.title: Water in Fuel Condition - Sensor A
P2269.summary: The water-in-fuel sensor at fuel filter A has detected water above the warning threshold. The fuel filter must be drained; running the engine on water-contaminated diesel can damage the high-pressure pump and injectors.

causes.text: Condensate accumulated in filter — drain required

P226A.title: Water in Fuel Lamp Control Circuit
P226A.summary: A general electrical fault on the drive line for the dashboard water-in-fuel warning lamp.

causes.text: Lamp drive failed

P226B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Boost Pressure Too High - Mechanical
P226B.summary: Boost pressure on turbo A exceeds the upper threshold and the cause is mechanical (wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck closed) rather than electrical drive fault.

causes.text: Wastegate or VGT stuck closed

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P226C.title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response
P226C.summary: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.text: VGT vanes stiff or worn

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P226D.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 1)
P226D.summary: The DPF substrate on bank 1 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.

causes.text: Substrate cracked or melted from runaway regen
Substrate removed by tampering

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P226E.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 2)
P226E.summary: The DPF substrate on bank 2 has been detected as cracked, melted, or removed. Differential pressure across the filter is too low for the measured exhaust flow — the soot trap no longer works.

causes.text: Substrate cracked, melted, or removed

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P226F.title: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response
P226F.summary: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.text: VGT vanes stiff or worn

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2270.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2270.summary: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

causes.text: Downstream sensor failed stuck lean
Exhaust leak after catalyst

P2271.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2271.summary: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

causes.text: Downstream sensor failed stuck rich
Downstream sensor contaminated

P2272.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2272.summary: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant lean signal during a forced-rich command from the ECU. Suggests either a sensor that has lost its rich-side response, or a catalyst that is so degraded that no rich exhaust reaches the downstream sensor (cross-check P0420).

causes.text: Downstream sensor failed stuck lean
Exhaust leak after catalyst

P2273.title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2273.summary: The downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2 reports a constant rich signal during a forced-lean command. Suggests a failed downstream sensor or a sensor contaminated by oil/coolant from upstream engine wear.

causes.text: Downstream sensor failed stuck rich

P2274.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2274.summary: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Sensor aged or contaminated

P2275.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2275.summary: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 3): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue

P2276.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2276.summary: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a lean reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment.

causes.text: Sensor aged

P2277.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2277.summary: O2 sensor at bank 2 sensor 3 reports a rich reading suspiciously stable for too long. Sensor 3 is typically downstream of the second catalyst on systems with three-stage aftertreatment; sensor coated with carbon or fuel residue is the typical cause.

causes.text: Sensor coated

P2278.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 3 / Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2278.summary: The PCM detects that the O2 sensor signals from bank 1 sensor 3 and bank 2 sensor 3 are swapped — typically a wiring crossover after sensor replacement.

causes.text: Wiring crossover after sensor replacement

P2279.title: Intake Air System Leak
P2279.summary: The ECU has detected a discrepancy between commanded throttle/intake conditions and the resulting MAP/MAF that points to unmetered air entering after the throttle body. On turbocharged engines this often means a cracked or disconnected boost pipe between turbo and intake; on naturally aspirated engines, a hole in the intake manifold or hose.

causes.text: Boost pipe disconnected or cracked
Intake hose split

P227A.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit
P227A.summary: A general electrical fault on barometric pressure sensor C — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor measures atmospheric pressure for altitude compensation; sensor C is a redundant or secondary unit.

causes.text: Sensor failed

P227B.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P227B.summary: Barometric sensor C reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P227C.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
P227C.summary: Barometric sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P227D.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit High
P227D.summary: Barometric sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Open signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P227E.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P227E.summary: Barometric sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P227F.title: Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 2)
P227F.summary: Restriction or leak detected in the intake plumbing between the air filter and the mass-air-flow sensor on bank 2 — typically a cracked intake boot or torn filter element.

causes.text: Cracked intake boot

P2280.title: Air Flow Restriction / Air Filter Restriction
P2280.summary: The ECU detects an excessive intake restriction. Either the air filter is heavily clogged or an obstruction in the intake duct is reducing airflow below the expected level.

causes.text: Clogged air filter element
Foreign object in intake

P2281.title: Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
P2281.summary: The ECU detects unmetered air entering between the mass airflow sensor and the throttle body. The actual airflow into the engine is greater than what the MAF measures, leading to lean conditions.

causes.text: Cracked or torn intake hose
Loose hose clamp

P2282.title: Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
P2282.summary: The ECU detects unmetered air entering downstream of the throttle body. Typical sources are leaking intake-manifold gaskets, vacuum hoses or PCV components.

causes.text: Leaking intake manifold gasket
Cracked vacuum hose

P2283.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2283.summary: A general electrical fault on the injector control pressure (ICP) sensor — used on HEUI (Hydraulically actuated Electronically controlled Unit Injector) systems on heavy-duty diesel engines such as the Ford Powerstroke 6.0/7.3 and Caterpillar engines. ICP measures the high-pressure oil that actuates the injectors.

causes.text: Sensor failed

P2284.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2284.summary: The injector control pressure (ICP) sensor on HEUI diesel systems reports a value that does not match expected operating range or commanded pressure. Affects fuel injection timing and quantity.

causes.text: ICP sensor drift
Leak in high-pressure oil system
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2285.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2285.summary: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is below the calibrated minimum. The signal indicates either a short to ground or a sensor that has lost its supply.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Open 5 V supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2286.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2286.summary: The voltage of the injector control pressure sensor is above the calibrated maximum. Likely a short to supply voltage or an open ground in the sensor circuit.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Open ground wire
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2287.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Intermittent
P2287.summary: The injector control pressure sensor signal is intermittently lost or out of range. Often caused by intermittent wiring faults or a failing sensor that drops out under vibration or temperature.

causes.text: Intermittent connector contact
Sensor failing under load
Harness routed against vibrating component

P2288.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High
P2288.summary: ICP is above the upper threshold during operation. Typically the injection pressure regulator (IPR) is stuck closed or the high-pressure oil pump runs above target.

causes.text: IPR stuck closed

P2289.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
P2289.summary: ICP remains above threshold after engine shutdown — pressure does not bleed off as expected, indicating a stuck check valve or sensor offset error.

causes.text: Check valve stuck

P228A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228A.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Pressure runaway

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P228B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228B.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Pressure runaway

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P228C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P228C.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Regulator leaks or pump weak

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P228D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P228D.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Return path blocked or pump runaway

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P228E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P228E.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low: the adaptive learning value has reached its lower limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Long-term wear of regulator

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P228F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P228F.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High: the adaptive learning value has reached its upper limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Long-term drift upward

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2290.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low
P2290.summary: ICP is below the lower threshold — typically IPR stuck open, leaking high-pressure oil rail, or weak HP oil pump.

causes.text: IPR stuck open
HP oil pump weak

P2291.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P2291.summary: During cranking, ICP does not build up enough to fire injectors. Typical no-start condition on HEUI engines from a stuck-open IPR or weak HP oil pump.

causes.text: HP oil rail does not pressurise

P2292.title: Injector Control Pressure Erratic
P2292.summary: ICP signal is unstable or jumps — connector or sensor issue, or air in the high-pressure oil rail. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

causes.text: Air in HP oil rail
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P2293.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Performance
P2293.summary: The high-pressure fuel pressure regulator (volume control or pressure control valve on a direct-injection rail) is not maintaining commanded pressure. Often the rail-pressure sensor reading drifts away from the setpoint under load.

causes.text: Pressure regulator worn or sticking
High-pressure pump weak
Rail pressure sensor drift

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2294.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit
P2294.summary: Electrical fault on the control line to the high-pressure fuel pressure regulator solenoid. Without a working drive signal the rail cannot maintain pressure and the engine may not start or runs in limp-home.

causes.text: Regulator solenoid open or shorted
Wiring break to regulator

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2295.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit Low
P2295.summary: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is below the lower limit. On common-rail diesels and direct-injection petrol engines this affects high-pressure fuel control directly.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to ground
Solenoid coil internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2296.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Control Circuit High
P2296.summary: Drive voltage to the second fuel pressure regulator solenoid is above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. The driver protection trips, regulator falls back to default.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to supply
ECU driver stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2297.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2297.summary: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

causes.text: Sensor slow or coated

P2298.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2298.summary: During engine deceleration with closed throttle (DFCO), the O2 sensor on bank 2 sensor 1 should swing fully lean as the manifold fills with fresh air. Code is set when the swing does not happen — usually a slow or coated sensor.

causes.text: Sensor slow or coated

P2299.title: Brake Pedal Position / Accelerator Pedal Position Correlation
P2299.summary: The ECU detects simultaneous brake and accelerator activation beyond a permitted threshold. Modern brake-throttle override safety logic forces idle in this state — usually triggered by a stuck brake light switch or a faulty pedal sensor.

causes.text: Brake light switch stuck on
Accelerator pedal sensor drift

P229A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P229A.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Regulator leaks or pump weak

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P229B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P229B.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Return path blocked or pump runaway

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P229C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P229C.summary: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low: the adaptive learning value has reached its lower limit, so the ECU can no longer compensate. This controls fuel-rail pressure.

causes.text: Long-term wear of regulator

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P229D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P229D.summary: The adaptive learning offset for fuel pressure regulator B has reached the upper limit. Long-term drift upward indicates progressive wear of the regulator or a return path that is becoming restricted.

causes.text: Long-term drift upward

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P229E.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P229E.summary: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

causes.text: Sensor element failed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P229F.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P229F.summary: The downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 (after the SCR catalyst) returns implausible NOx readings during operation. Either the sensor is degraded or upstream chemistry is abnormal.

causes.text: NOx sensor aging
Low SCR efficiency
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A0.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A0.summary: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A1.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A1.summary: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes.text: Open signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A2.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A2.summary: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.

causes.text: Intermittent connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A3.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A3.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control circuit is open. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Heater winding open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A4.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A4.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A5.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A5.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A6.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A6.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): an electrical fault is present in the circuit. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Sense circuit failed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A7.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A7.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Sense circuit drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A8.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A8.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is below the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22A9.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A9.summary: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the signal voltage is above the expected range. The NOx sensor heater brings the sensor to operating temperature; a fault delays accurate NOx readings used for SCR control.

causes.text: Open signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22AA.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AA.summary: The feedback line that monitors the NOx sensor heater current draw on bank 1 sensor 2 jumps or drops out intermittently — connector loose or chafed wire near the exhaust heat zone.

causes.text: Intermittent connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P22AB.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AB.summary: The positive (sourcing) side of the O2 sensor pumping current control circuit on bank 1 sensor 2 is open. Wide-band O2 sensors regulate oxygen concentration in a reference chamber by pumping current; the positive line is open here.

causes.text: Open positive current line
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22AC.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AC.summary: O2 positive current line on bank 1 sensor 2 stuck low — short to ground. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

causes.text: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

Short-trip operation - exhaust never reaches operating temperature
Exhaust heater or heat-management strategy not active

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2300.title: Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low

causes.text: Internal coil short
Primary wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

Open primary winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2302.title: Ignition Coil A Secondary Circuit

Coil secondary winding failure

Coil secondary failure

Partial misfire from ignition or fuel-side defect

P233C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit High

causes.text: Control line shorted to battery or supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P233D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Open
P233D.summary: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is open. Without supply the regulator cannot operate and the ECU cannot maintain rail pressure on this stage; sets when the controller sees no current flow even with the solenoid commanded on.

causes.text: Supply line open or relay defective
Fuse for regulator B supply blown
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P233E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low
P233E.summary: The supply line that powers the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B is below the expected voltage with the regulator commanded active - typically a high-resistance feed, partial short to ground or weak relay contact.

causes.text: Supply feed has high contact resistance
Partial short to ground on supply line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P233F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High
P233F.summary: Same as P233D but with the supply line shorted to a higher potential than expected, so the ECU measures more voltage on the regulator B feed than the commanded level allows.

causes.text: Supply line shorted to a higher voltage rail
Supply relay contact welded closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2340.title: Cylinder 5 Above Knock Threshold
P2340.summary: The knock-sensor evaluation reports cylinder 5 above the knock threshold over a sustained window. The ECU retards ignition for that cylinder; persistent knock indicates poor fuel quality, carbon deposits or cooling issues.

causes.text: Low octane or contaminated fuel
Carbon deposits raise compression locally
Local cooling issue at cylinder 5

P2341.title: Cylinder 6 Above Knock Threshold
P2341.summary: Same condition as P2340 but on cylinder 6 — sustained knock above the threshold with retarded ignition correction.

causes.text: Low octane or contaminated fuel
Carbon deposits raise compression locally

P2342.title: Cylinder 7 Above Knock Threshold

causes.text: Low octane or contaminated fuel
Carbon deposits raise compression locally

P2343.title: Cylinder 8 Above Knock Threshold

causes.text: Low octane or contaminated fuel
Carbon deposits raise compression locally

P2344.title: Cylinder 9 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold

causes.text: Persistent knocking on cylinder 9 (low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, hot spot)
Sensor or wiring biased high by short or moisture
Mechanical knock from bearings, piston pin or wrong torque

P2345.title: Cylinder 10 Above Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor Threshold

causes.text: Persistent knocking on cylinder 10

Connector loose or oxidised

Sensor element drifted
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2370.title: Fuel Volume Regulator B Control Circuit Open
P2370.summary: An open circuit is detected on the control line for the second fuel volume regulator (B) used on twin high-pressure-pump diesel systems. Without this regulator the high-pressure pump cannot meter fuel for its assigned cylinder bank, leading to rail-pressure faults and limp-home behaviour.

causes.text: Open in harness or connector to regulator B
Regulator solenoid winding open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

causes.text: Regulator stem sticking due to debris or wear
High-pressure pump wear changes regulator response

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake
