P23DD.title: Cylinder 4 Fuel Heater Control Circuit Open
P23DD.summary: Per-cylinder fuel heaters (used on some heavy-duty diesels for cold-start atomisation) on cylinder 4 have an open control circuit.

causes.text: Open in heater or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23DE.title: Cylinder 4 Fuel Heater Control Circuit High
P23DE.summary: Same as P23D2 on cylinder 4. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23DF.title: Cylinder 4 Fuel Heater Control Circuit Low
P23DF.summary: Same as P23D3 on cylinder 4. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P23E0.title: Cylinder 4 Fuel Heater Performance
P23E0.summary: Cylinder 4 fuel heater is electrically intact yet does not deliver the expected heat - aged element or contact resistance high.

causes.text: Heater element aged

P23E1.title: EGR C Control Circuit Open
P23E1.summary: A general open-circuit fault on the third EGR valve C control - typically a third EGR loop in heavy-duty engines or specific Euro-7 systems.

causes.text: Open in valve or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P23E2.title: EGR C Control Circuit Performance
P23E2.summary: Same as P23E1 with the actuator electrically intact but not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: EGR valve C sticking due to soot

P23E3.title: EGR C Control Circuit Low
P23E3.summary: Same as P23E1 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P23E4.title: EGR C Control Circuit High
P23E4.summary: Same as P23E1 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P23E5.title: EGR C Control Stuck Open
P23E5.summary: EGR valve C is stuck in the open position - exhaust gas continuously dilutes intake air, reducing power and risking misfires at idle.

causes.text: Valve stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23E6.title: EGR C Control Stuck Closed
P23E6.summary: Same as P23E5 with valve C stuck closed - no EGR through this stage; NOx emissions rise. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P23E7.title: EGR C Flow Insufficient Detected
P23E7.summary: Same as P049B on EGR loop C. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: EGR cooler C clogged with soot

P23E8.title: EGR C Flow Excessive Detected
P23E8.summary: Same as P049C on EGR loop C. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: EGR valve C sticking open

P23E9.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2
P23E9.summary: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2: the circuit is open. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.text: Open in output wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23EA.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 2
P23EA.summary: Same as P23E9 with the output shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23EB.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 2
P23EB.summary: Same as P23E9 with the output shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23EC.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 1
P23EC.summary: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 1: the circuit is open. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.text: Open in output wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23ED.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 1
P23ED.summary: Same as P23EA on cam B bank 1. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23EE.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 1
P23EE.summary: Same as P23EB on cam B bank 1. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23EF.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2
P23EF.summary: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Open Bank 2: the circuit is open. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

causes.text: Open in output wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23F0.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 2
P23F0.summary: Same as P23EA on cam B bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23F1.title: Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 2
P23F1.summary: Same as P23EB on cam B bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Output line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P23F2.title: Cylinder 1 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F2.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 1 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 1 has drifted in flow rate

P23F3.title: Cylinder 2 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F3.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 2 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 2 has drifted in flow rate

P23F4.title: Cylinder 3 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F4.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 3 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 3 has drifted in flow rate

P23F5.title: Cylinder 4 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F5.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 4 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 4 has drifted in flow rate

P23F6.title: Cylinder 5 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F6.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 5 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 5 has drifted in flow rate

P23F7.title: Cylinder 6 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F7.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 6 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 6 has drifted in flow rate

P23F8.title: Cylinder 7 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F8.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 7 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 7 has drifted in flow rate

P23F9.title: Cylinder 8 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23F9.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 8 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 8 has drifted in flow rate

P23FA.title: Cylinder 9 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FA.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 9 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 9 has drifted in flow rate

P23FB.title: Cylinder 10 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FB.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 10 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 10 has drifted in flow rate

P23FC.title: Cylinder 11 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FC.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 11 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 11 has drifted in flow rate

P23FD.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FD.summary: On dual-injector systems (typical for some heavy-duty diesels and some petrol/gas bi-fuel applications) the secondary injector B at cylinder 12 cannot keep its mixture in balance with the rest of the bank.

causes.text: Injector B for cylinder 12 has drifted in flow rate

P23FE.title: Bank 1 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FE.summary: The secondary fuel system B on bank 1 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 1 is biased by an offset on the B system.

causes.text: Secondary fuel system has drifted

P23FF.title: Bank 2 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FF.summary: The secondary fuel system B on bank 2 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 2 is biased by an offset on the B system.

causes.text: Secondary fuel system has drifted

P2400.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.summary: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.

causes.text: Leak detection pump failed
Wiring open to pump
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2401.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.summary: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to ground
Pump internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2402.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.summary: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to supply
Pump ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2403.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
P2403.summary: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.

causes.text: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2404.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2404.summary: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.

causes.text: Pump diaphragm worn
Reed switch intermittent
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2405.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
P2405.summary: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Sense line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2406.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
P2406.summary: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Sense line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2407.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2407.summary: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.

causes.text: Pump diaphragm worn
Sense wiring high resistance
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2408.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2408.summary: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.

causes.text: Cap switch worn
Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2409.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P2409.summary: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

causes.text: Contact drifted or dirty

P240A.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
P240A.summary: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.

causes.text: Open in heater or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240B.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
P240B.summary: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240C.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
P240C.summary: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240D.title: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
P240D.summary: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes.text: Hose or fitting leak

P240E.title: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
P240E.summary: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes.text: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak

P240F.title: EGR Slow Response
P240F.summary: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

causes.text: EGR valve or cooler sticky

P2410.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Stuck
P2410.summary: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

causes.text: Cap switch stuck mechanically
Connector corroded

P2411.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2411.summary: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

causes.text: Signal wire open
Cap switch failed

P2412.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2412.summary: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P2413.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
P2413.summary: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

causes.text: Carbon buildup in EGR passages
Sticking EGR valve
EGR differential pressure sensor fault

P2414.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2414.summary: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

causes.text: Sensing element fouled

P2415.title: EVAP Switching Valve Circuit Open
P2415.summary: The ECU detects an open circuit on the EVAP switching valve drive line. The valve cannot be commanded between its purge and isolation positions.

causes.text: Valve coil open
Drive line open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2416.title: EVAP Switching Valve Performance
P2416.summary: The EVAP switching valve responds electrically but does not produce the expected pressure change. Often a stuck valve seat or a torn diaphragm.

causes.text: Valve seat stuck
Diaphragm torn

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2417.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2417.summary: The EVAP switching valve cannot reach the open position. Purge flow is blocked and the EVAP system cannot vent the canister.

causes.text: Valve seat stuck closed
Valve internals corroded
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2418.title: EVAP Switching Valve Control Circuit Performance
P2418.summary: The evaporative switching valve — used on multi-path EVAP systems to route purge or pressure-test flow — does not respond as expected. Self-test fails because tank pressure does not change in the calibrated direction.

causes.text: Switching valve failed
EVAP line blocked or kinked

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2419.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Open
P2419.summary: The EVAP switching valve cannot close. Tank pressure cannot be isolated for the leak detection test, and purge routing may bypass the canister.

causes.text: Valve stuck open mechanically
Drive circuit always energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P241A.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241A.summary: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

causes.text: Harness swapped during repair

P241B.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241B.summary: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

causes.text: Harness swapped during repair

P241C.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
P241C.summary: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.

causes.text: Ice in throttle bore

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P241D.title: SCR Inducement Forced Engine Shutdown
P241D.summary: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.

causes.text: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241E.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
P241E.summary: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241F.title: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
P241F.summary: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.

causes.text: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled

P2420.title: EVAP Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2420.summary: The EVAP switching valve cannot open when commanded. Purge or test flow cannot reach the appropriate path and the leak monitor aborts.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed mechanically
Drive circuit open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2421.title: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Open
P2421.summary: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.

causes.text: Vent valve mechanically stuck open
Dust/debris preventing valve seat
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2422.title: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.summary: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues.

causes.text: Vent valve seized closed
Drive circuit open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2423.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P2423.summary: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.

causes.text: Catalyst aging / thermal damage
Oxygen sensor drift

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2424.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
P2424.summary: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.

causes.text: Catalyst adsorber aged

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2425.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
P2425.summary: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.

causes.text: Open in valve or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2426.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
P2426.summary: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2427.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit High
P2427.summary: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2428.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
P2428.summary: An EGT sensor on bank 1 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

causes.text: DPF blocked or active regeneration

P2429.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2
P2429.summary: An EGT sensor on bank 2 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

causes.text: DPF blocked or active regeneration

P242A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242A.summary: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

causes.text: Open in sensor or wiring

P242B.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242B.summary: Same as P242A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes.text: Sensor element drifted

P242C.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242C.summary: Same as P242A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P242D.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242D.summary: Same as P242A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P242E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242E.summary: Same as P242A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P242F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 1
P242F.summary: The diesel particulate filter on bank 1 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

causes.text: DPF full of ash

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2430.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P2430.summary: A general circuit fault on the secondary air injection (AIR) system flow or pressure sensor on bank 1 - the sensor that verifies air pump flow during cold-start enrichment compensation.

causes.text: Open in sensor or wiring

P2431.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2431.summary: The ECU detects a general fault in the secondary air injection system air flow or pressure sensor circuit. The diagnostic cannot verify proper SAI operation.

causes.text: Defective SAI sensor
SAI sensor wiring fault

P2432.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2432.summary: The signal of the SAI air flow or pressure sensor is implausible during operation. The reading does not change as expected when the air pump is commanded.

causes.text: Clogged SAI passages
SAI sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2433.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P2433.summary: Same as P2430 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2434.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1
P2434.summary: Same as P2430 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P2435.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P2435.summary: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

causes.text: Open in sensor or wiring

P2436.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2
P2436.summary: Same as P2430 on bank 2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes.text: Sensor element drifted

P2437.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P2437.summary: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2438.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P2438.summary: Same as P2433 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2439.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2
P2439.summary: Same as P2434 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P243A.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 2
P243A.summary: The diesel particulate filter on bank 2 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

causes.text: DPF full of ash

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243B.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
P243B.summary: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: DPF heavily clogged

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243C.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency Bank 2
P243C.summary: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.

causes.text: Short-trip operation

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243D.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration Bank 2
P243D.summary: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.

causes.text: Regeneration too slow

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2
P243E.summary: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Regeneration aborted before completion

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
P243F.summary: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.text: Soot loading critical

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2440.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.summary: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.text: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2441.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.summary: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.text: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Vacuum control line leak
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2442.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.summary: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.text: Switching valve stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2443.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2443.summary: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.text: Switching valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2444.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2444.summary: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

causes.text: Pump seized by corrosion
Pump relay failed
Pump fuse blown

P2445.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2445.summary: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.

causes.text: Pump relay stuck closed
Drive line shorted to supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2446.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
P2446.summary: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.text: Pump seized from condensate corrosion
Relay failed open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2447.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
P2447.summary: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.

causes.text: Relay stuck closed
Driver stage shorted on
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2448.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
P2448.summary: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

causes.text: AIR switching valve stuck open

P2449.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
P2449.summary: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

causes.text: AIR switching valve stuck open

P244A.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
P244A.summary: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.

causes.text: Cracked or missing DPF substrate
Leak in pressure sensing line

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244B.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
P244B.summary: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.

causes.text: Sensor zero-point drift

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244C.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244C.summary: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held.

causes.text: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244D.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244D.summary: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.

causes.text: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244E.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
P244E.summary: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held.

causes.text: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244F.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2

causes.text: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2450.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck
P2450.summary: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.

causes.text: Mechanical failure of valve
Contamination preventing motion

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2451.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2451.summary: The EVAP switching valve - which directs vapor flow between purge and leak-detection paths - is stuck in the closed position. The diagnostic cycle cannot complete.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2452.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2452.summary: A general electrical fault on the DPF differential-pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid pressure reading the ECU cannot estimate soot load and may inhibit regeneration.

causes.text: DPF pressure sensor failed
Sensor sample hoses clogged with soot

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2453.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2453.summary: The DPF differential-pressure sensor produces a value that is electrically valid but does not match expectations — for example a non-zero reading with engine off or no change between idle and load.

causes.text: Sample hoses clogged or kinked
Sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2454.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2454.summary: Voltage on the DPF differential-pressure sensor signal line is below the lower threshold. Typically a short to ground or an open in the supply line.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Reference voltage line open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2455.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2455.summary: Voltage on the DPF pressure sensor line exceeds the upper threshold. Usually a short to supply or an open ground on the sensor.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2456.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2456.summary: The DPF differential-pressure sensor delivers an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a chafed wiring section that breaks contact during temperature or vibration.

causes.text: Connector intermittent
Wiring chafed against bracket
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2457.title: EGR Cooler Performance
P2457.summary: The EGR cooler does not lower exhaust gas temperature as expected — typically internal coolant fouling, a partial blockage, or a cracked cooler that mixes coolant with exhaust gas.

causes.text: Cooler internally clogged with soot
Cooler cracked, coolant entering exhaust

P2458.title: DPF Regeneration Duration
P2458.summary: The DPF regeneration cycle takes longer than the calibrated maximum. The ECU sets this code when the soot load is not being burned off within the expected window — common after many short trips or with degraded post-injection.

causes.text: Heavy soot load, short trips
Post-injection insufficient

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2459.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
P2459.summary: Active DPF regenerations are being requested more often than the calibration window allows. Indicates that soot accumulates faster than the filter can burn it off — typically due to short-trip use, leaking injectors, or excessive engine oil consumption.

causes.text: Predominantly short-trip operation
Leaking injector raises soot output
High engine oil consumption (turbo seals, valve stems)

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P245A.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Open Bank 1
P245A.summary: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 - routes EGR around the cooler during cold-start to keep cabin and engine warm-up fast - has an open control circuit.

causes.text: Open in valve or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P245B.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1
P245B.summary: Same as P245A with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded position. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Bypass valve sticking due to soot

P245C.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P245C.summary: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

Harness chafing through insulation

P245D.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit High Bank 1
P245D.summary: Same as P245A with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply

Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P245E.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P245E.summary: A general circuit fault on the secondary differential pressure sensor B across the DPF - measures backpressure for the regeneration strategy.

causes.text: Open in sensor or wiring

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P245F.title: Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2460.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited Power
P2460.summary: The DPF restriction has reached a level that forces the ECU to limit engine power. The driver must allow a forced regeneration or have the filter serviced before normal power is restored.

causes.text: Heavy soot load, regenerations skipped
Ash loaded near service interval

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2461.title: DPF Restriction — Forced Limited
P2461.summary: The DPF restriction has reached the limit defined for forced limited operation. Vehicle behaviour depends on the manufacturer — usually a hard torque cap with a service warning.

causes.text: Heavy soot load, regenerations skipped
Ash loaded near service interval

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2462.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation
P2462.summary: The DPF differential pressure sensor reports a backpressure rise consistent with excessive soot accumulation. The filter cannot regenerate fast enough, eventually causing limp mode.

causes.text: Repeated failed regeneration cycles
Heavily clogged DPF

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2463.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction — Soot Accumulation
P2463.summary: The estimated soot mass in the DPF has crossed the upper limit and the ECU could not complete a regeneration to bring it back down. Very common on cars used on short trips.

causes.text: DPF heavily loaded after multiple aborted regenerations

Differential pressure sensor reading drifted high

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2464.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High
P2464.summary: The differential pressure across the DPF exceeds the calibrated upper threshold during operation. Indicates severe blockage of the filter element.

Blocked pressure sensing line

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24D9.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P24D9.summary: Same as P24D5 with intermittent or erratic signal. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P24DA.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1
P24DA.summary: The PM sensor on bank 1 cannot acquire a valid exhaust sample - probe fouled, exhaust path obstructed at sensor, or sensor seal leaking.

causes.text: Sensing element fouled

P24DB.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
P24DB.summary: The secondary reductant purge valve B - which clears AdBlue from injector and lines at shutdown to prevent crystallisation - has an open control circuit.

causes.text: Open in valve or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DC.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Performance
P24DC.summary: Same as P24DB with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded purge flow. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Purge valve sticking

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DD.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P24DD.summary: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to ground. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DE.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P24DE.summary: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to supply. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.text: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24DF.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Open
P24DF.summary: Purge valve B is mechanically stuck open - AdBlue lines drain continuously, dosing pressure cannot build.

causes.text: Valve stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24E0.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P24E0.summary: Same as P24DF with valve B stuck closed - AdBlue cannot be cleared at shutdown, risk of crystallisation in injector and lines.

causes.text: Valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24E1.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit
P24E1.summary: A general circuit fault on the NH3 (ammonia) sensor - measures ammonia slip downstream of the SCR catalyst to detect AdBlue overdose.

causes.text: Open in sensor or wiring

P24E2.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24E2.summary: Same as P24E1 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes.text: Sensor element drifted

P24E3.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Low
P24E3.summary: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P24E4.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit High
P24E4.summary: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24E5.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P24E5.summary: The ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR catalyst delivers an intermittent or erratic signal. The ECM expects a smooth voltage proportional to ammonia concentration in the tailpipe — sudden jumps, dropouts or noise mean the wiring, connector or sensing element is failing.

causes.text: Corroded or loose sensor connector
Chafed or vibrating harness near the exhaust
Aged ceramic sensor element drifting under heat cycles

P24E6.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit/Open
P24E6.summary: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia. The ECM detects an open in the heater control circuit — no current flows when the heater should be active, so the sensor never reaches its working point and SCR closed-loop control is suspended.

causes.text: Burnt-out heater winding inside the sensor
Broken wire or unplugged connector
Failed heater driver stage in the dosing module

P24E7.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Low
P24E7.summary: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range. Either the wiring is shorted to ground or the heater driver in the SCR/dosing module is stuck low.

causes.text: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Internal short across the heater element
Low-side driver pulled down in the control module

P24E8.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit High
P24E8.summary: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range. Typically a short to battery voltage or a heater driver stuck high — duty-cycle control is lost, the heater either runs continuously or not at all, and the sensor element risks overheating before the ECM disables it.

causes.text: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage
High-side driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24E9.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Performance
P24E9.summary: The heater of the NH3 slip sensor is electrically intact, but the warm-up profile or steady-state temperature feedback does not match the ECM model. The sensor takes too long to reach operating temperature or drifts away from setpoint, so SCR closed-loop control is delayed or held off.

causes.text: Aged heater with increased resistance
Poor thermal contact between heater and sensing cell

P24EA.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit
P24EA.summary: The supply rail that powers the NH3 slip sensor electronics (typically 5 V or 12 V from the dosing/SCR module) is out of tolerance. Without a stable supply the sensor cannot deliver a valid ammonia reading, and the ECM disables the closed-loop SCR strategy.

causes.text: Open or shorted supply wire
Failing supply rail inside the dosing module

P24EB.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24EB.summary: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage drops below the lower limit. Usually a partial short to ground in the supply line, an undersized ground path with high resistance, or an internal supply collapse in the SCR/dosing module.

causes.text: Supply line shorted to ground
High-resistance ground at the SCR module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24EC.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P24EC.summary: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage rises above the upper limit. Either the supply is shorted to battery voltage or an internal regulator in the dosing module has failed open.

causes.text: Supply line shorted to battery voltage
Failed voltage regulator in the dosing module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24ED.title: NH3 Sensor Calibration Memory
P24ED.summary: The NH3 slip sensor stores its individual calibration coefficients in non-volatile memory (EEPROM/flash). The ECM cannot read valid calibration values — either checksum fails, the memory is empty after replacement, or communication with the sensor electronics is broken.

causes.text: New sensor installed but not coded/learned to the ECM
Corrupted calibration memory after voltage drop
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P24EE.title: NH3 Sensor Processor Performance
P24EE.summary: The microcontroller inside the smart NH3 slip sensor reports an internal performance fault — failed self-test, watchdog reset, or out-of-range plausibility checks. The sensor cannot guarantee its output value, the ECM marks the channel invalid and disables SCR closed-loop control on this branch.

causes.text: Internal processor or firmware fault
Brown-out from supply voltage dips
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P24EF.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit/Open
P24EF.summary: The wake-up line that brings a sleeping ECU back from low-power mode is open. Many networks use a dedicated hardware wake-up wire (door-latch trigger, terminal 15, CAN wake-up) so modules can stay asleep with the ignition off.

causes.text: Broken wake-up wire or unplugged connector
Failed wake-up input stage in the module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P24F0.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Low
P24F0.summary: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal. The module either keeps waking up unnecessarily and drains the battery, or it cannot distinguish a real wake event from the stuck low level.

causes.text: Wake-up wire shorted to ground
Door, hood or terminal switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24F1.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit High
P24F1.summary: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage. The module sees a permanent wake-up request, never enters sleep mode and drains the battery while parked.

causes.text: Wake-up wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24F2.title: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
P24F2.summary: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature. The ECM compares them and detects an implausible delta.

causes.text: One sensor drifting outside tolerance
Residual heat in the charge-air cooler after a hot soak

P24F3.title: Reductant Tank Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P24F3.summary: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient). The ECM detects an implausible spread, which usually means one of the two sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or has a heat source nearby that the plausibility model does not account for.

causes.text: One temperature sensor drifting outside tolerance
Recently active reductant tank heater warming the tank above ambient

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F4.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P24F4.summary: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load. Aged ceramic cells, soot deposits or condensation inside the sensor protective tube slow the diffusion of NOx to the measuring element.

causes.text: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed
Soot clogging the protective tube

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F5.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P24F5.summary: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level. Same failure mechanism as the upstream sensor — aged element, soot or condensate — but post-catalyst the consequence is a degraded SCR conversion-efficiency monitor.

causes.text: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed
Soot clogging the protective tube

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
P24F6.summary: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event. The ECM detects the valve stuck open — pressure or flow does not build up against a closed valve, so the dosing line cannot be charged.

causes.text: Mechanically stuck open valve from soot or coking
Broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
P24F7.summary: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed. The ECM commands purge but the line is not cleared, leaving residual fluid that can foul nozzles or freeze in cold weather.

causes.text: Stuck closed by deposits or seized armature
Open coil — valve never opens
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
P24F8.summary: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve. The ECM cannot drive the valve coil according to plausibility checks — open, short or unexpected feedback voltage.

causes.text: Open or shorted control wire
Failed driver stage in the dosing module

P24F9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
P24F9.summary: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model. Typical for solenoids losing magnetic strength after long thermal cycling, or armatures with increased friction from coking.

causes.text: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Coked armature with increased friction
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P24FA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
P24FA.summary: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver. The valve is energised continuously when it should be off, or the diagnostic feedback voltage is pulled below threshold.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Failed low-side driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
P24FB.summary: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open ground or open coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FC.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P24FC.summary: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement. The driver reports current or junction temperature above the safe limit and disables itself.

causes.text: Partial short across the heater element
Driver overheating due to poor cooling on the module

P24FD.title: Particulate Filter A Incorrect
P24FD.summary: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application. Common after a non-OEM aftermarket DPF or a wrong-application replacement.

causes.text: Incorrect or non-OEM DPF installed
Coding mismatch after part replacement

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24FE.title: SCR Catalyst Incorrect
P24FE.summary: The ECM identifies the installed SCR catalyst as the wrong part — NOx conversion efficiency, NH3 storage capacity or coded part-number do not match the expected application. Typical after fitting a non-OEM SCR brick or after a coding error following replacement.

causes.text: Incorrect or non-OEM SCR catalyst installed
Coding mismatch after part replacement

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P24FF.title: Reductant Temperature Too High
P24FF.summary: The temperature of the AdBlue/DEF in the dosing system exceeds the safe limit — risk of thermal decomposition (NH3/biuret formation) and clogged dosing nozzles. Often caused by a stuck-on tank heater, a stalled coolant return or proximity to a hot exhaust component.

causes.text: Tank heater stuck on
Heat soak from exhaust or engine bay

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P2500.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit Low
P2500.summary: The L-terminal feedback line from the alternator (charging warning lamp circuit) reads below the lower limit. The lamp may stay on, and battery voltage may drift if regulation feedback is also affected.

causes.text: L-terminal shorted to ground
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2501.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit High
P2501.summary: The L-terminal feedback from the alternator reads above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. Charging diagnostics cannot run cleanly.

causes.text: L-terminal shorted to supply
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2502.title: Charging System Voltage
P2502.summary: The ECU detects an out-of-range charging system voltage without specifying high or low. Indicates a generic charging fault that requires further sub-code investigation.

causes.text: Alternator output fault
Voltage regulator fault

P2503.title: Charging System Voltage Low
P2503.summary: The ECU detects that battery voltage during operation stays below the regulated target. The alternator output is insufficient to maintain charge under load, eventually leading to battery depletion.

causes.text: Weak alternator output
Faulty voltage regulator
Slipping drive belt

P2504.title: Charging System Voltage High
P2504.summary: The ECU detects a battery voltage above the regulated upper limit. The voltage regulator is not limiting alternator output, risking damage to electronic modules and battery overcharge.

causes.text: Faulty voltage regulator
Poor alternator ground

P2505.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
P2505.summary: The ECM/PCM monitors the main switched battery feed (typically terminal 15 / ignition-switched supply via the main relay). A general fault is reported — either the input is missing entirely or it does not match the expected timing relative to ignition state.

causes.text: Failed main relay
Blown fuse on the ECM power feed
Corroded connector pin at the ECM

P2506.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
P2506.summary: The switched-battery input to the ECM/PCM is present, but the level or transient behaviour is out of plausibility — sagging during cranking, slow ramp-up after main-relay close, or noisy. Often caused by aged main relay contacts or a weak battery feed under load.

causes.text: Aged main relay contacts with rising contact resistance
Weak battery sagging during crank
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2507.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Low
P2507.summary: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads below threshold while the ignition is on. Either the main relay does not close, the supply wire is broken or shorted to ground, or the battery is too low.

causes.text: Main relay does not pull in
Open supply wire
Severely discharged battery

P2508.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal High
P2508.summary: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads above the upper threshold. Most often caused by a charging system overvoltage (failed alternator regulator) or wrong jump-start procedure.

causes.text: Alternator regulator overvoltage
Improper external power source or jump-start

P2509.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
P2509.summary: The ECU detects sporadic interruptions of its supply voltage. The fault is set when supply drops below a threshold for short periods, often during cranking or due to a poor connection.

causes.text: Poor battery cable connection
Intermittent main relay
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P250A.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit
P250A.summary: General electrical fault on the engine oil level sensor circuit. The ECM cannot read a plausible level signal (analog level, ultrasonic or capacitive sender).

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the oil pan

P250B.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P250B.summary: The oil level sensor is electrically intact, but the level reading is implausible — for example a constant value across drives, jumps that cannot match real oil consumption, or readings outside the design range. Often a contaminated or aged float/ultrasonic sender.

causes.text: Aged or contaminated sender
Foaming oil under high RPM masking the level
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P250C.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Low
P250C.summary: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit, typically a short to ground or an open at the reference end of the sender. The ECM treats the input as invalid and ignores oil-low warnings until the circuit is repaired.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sender shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P250D.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit High
P250D.summary: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit, typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return. Pegged at maximum, the ECM cannot distinguish full from invalid and disables the level monitor.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P250E.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P250E.summary: The oil level signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually loose contacts, vibration cracks at the sender or oil sloshing on bumpy roads. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when the noise pattern exceeds the diagnostic limits.

causes.text: Loose or oil-soaked connector
Cracked sender housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P250F.title: Engine Oil Level Too Low
P250F.summary: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks bearing damage and oil-pump cavitation, so the ECM sets a critical warning, may reduce torque and asks the driver to add oil immediately.

causes.text: High oil consumption between services
External oil leak
Missed top-up since last service

P2510.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2510.summary: The voltage reported on the main power relay sense line for the engine controller does not match expectation. The ECU may shut down too early or stay awake too long, draining the battery.

causes.text: Main relay contacts pitted
Sense wiring corroded
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2511.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P2511.summary: The sense (feedback) line that lets the ECM verify the main power relay has actually closed shows intermittent dropouts. The ECM expects to see battery voltage on this line whenever the relay is energised — short losses suggest aged contacts, vibration or chafed wiring.

causes.text: Aged main relay contacts
Chafed sense wire shorting intermittently
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2512.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit/Open
P2512.summary: The Event Data Recorder (EDR / black box) request line — used by the ECM or restraint module to trigger the EDR to capture pre-crash data — is open. The ECM cannot trigger an event capture, so any subsequent crash event would not be recorded reliably.

causes.text: Open request wire or unplugged module
Failed input stage in the EDR
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2513.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit Low
P2513.summary: The EDR request line reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees a constant request (which it cannot service) or cannot pulse the line high to fire a real event capture.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2514.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit High
P2514.summary: The EDR request line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line back low to release the request, so the EDR may either ignore further requests or sit in a permanent triggered state.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2515.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2515.summary: General electrical fault in the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. Sensor B usually monitors the low-side or compressor-suction pressure (in addition to high-side sensor A).

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P2516.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2516.summary: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B is electrically intact, but its reading does not match the system model — for example pressures that do not fall when the compressor is off, do not change with ambient temperature, or contradict pressure sensor A. Often a refrigerant charge issue or a contaminated sensor.

causes.text: Low refrigerant charge
Contaminated or aged sensor diaphragm
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2517.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2517.summary: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads below the lower limit. Either a short to ground in the signal wire, an open reference voltage at the sensor, or an internal short.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2518.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2518.summary: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or an overpressure event briefly pegging the sensor.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2519.title: A/C Request A Circuit
P2519.summary: General electrical fault on the A/C compressor request input A. This input tells the ECM that the HVAC controller wants the A/C compressor engaged.

causes.text: Open or shorted A/C request wire
HVAC module not transmitting the request

P251A.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit/Open
P251A.summary: The Power Take-Off (PTO) enable switch input to the ECM is open. PTO is used on trucks and work vehicles to drive auxiliary equipment from the engine — without a valid enable signal the ECM refuses to enter PTO operating mode, idle speed control changes do not apply.

causes.text: Open switch wire or unplugged switch
Failed PTO enable switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P251B.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit Low
P251B.summary: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently closed switch. The ECM either sees PTO enabled when the operator has not requested it, or cannot release the PTO mode after work.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P251C.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit High
P251C.summary: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the input low, so the switch state is unreadable and PTO mode is locked out for safety.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P251D.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit/Open
P251D.summary: The PTO engine-shutdown command line is open. This safety input lets a connected work attachment (or operator switch) request an immediate engine shutdown — for example when an interlock is opened on a stationary aerial work platform.

causes.text: Broken shutdown wire or unplugged work attachment
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
