P251E.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit Low
P251E.summary: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted shutdown request. The ECM may treat this as an active shutdown command and refuse to start or keep the engine running while in PTO mode.

causes.text: Shutdown wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P251F.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit High
P251F.summary: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line low to acknowledge a shutdown request, so the operator-side safety chain is effectively disabled.

causes.text: Shutdown wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2520.title: A/C Request A Circuit Low
P2520.summary: The A/C compressor request input A reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees A/C demanded all the time (cannot release idle-up, raises fuel use) or cannot distinguish a real request from the stuck low level.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2521.title: A/C Request A Circuit High
P2521.summary: The A/C request input A reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the line low to read switch state, so the A/C compressor request is treated as invalid and the clutch stays disengaged.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2522.title: A/C Request B Circuit
P2522.summary: General electrical fault on the second A/C request input B. Many vehicles have two HVAC zones, a rear evaporator request, or a redundant request line — input B carries that signal.

causes.text: Open or shorted A/C request wire B
HVAC module not transmitting request B

P2523.title: A/C Request B Circuit Low
P2523.summary: The A/C request input B reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted request. Same effect as input A stuck low, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2524.title: A/C Request B Circuit High
P2524.summary: The A/C request input B reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the switch state, request B is treated as invalid.

causes.text: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2525.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2525.summary: General electrical fault on the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit. The reservoir stores manifold or pump-generated vacuum for systems like brake booster, EGR actuators or HVAC dampers.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P2526.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2526.summary: The vacuum reservoir pressure sensor is electrically intact, but the reading does not match the model — vacuum that does not build up after pump activation, does not bleed off when consumers draw, or stays at one value. Often a partly clogged hose, a leaking reservoir or an aged sensor.

causes.text: Leaking reservoir or vacuum line
Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2527.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2527.summary: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — usually a short to ground or open reference. The ECM disables vacuum pump control until the input recovers.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2528.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2528.summary: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — usually a short to reference voltage or open signal return. ECM disables vacuum pump control to avoid overshooting.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2529.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2529.summary: The sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — loose connector, vibration, or chafed harness. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when noise exceeds limits.

causes.text: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P252A.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit
P252A.summary: General electrical fault on the engine oil quality sensor — typically a capacitive/dielectric sensor that estimates oil aging from permittivity, viscosity proxies and conductivity. With no valid reading the dynamic service-interval algorithm falls back to the fixed-interval default.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor electrode after long use

P252B.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P252B.summary: The oil quality sensor is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — for example permittivity that does not change after an oil change, or shifts inconsistent with km/h driven. Often a contaminated electrode or oil that does not fit the sensor calibration.

causes.text: Contaminated sensor electrode
Oil grade outside the sensor calibration range
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P252C.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P252C.summary: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — typically a short to ground in the signal line or an internal short across the sensor electrode.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P252D.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
P252D.summary: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P252E.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P252E.summary: The oil quality sensor signal jumps or drops out — usually a loose connector at the oil pan, an oil-soaked harness or vibration cracks at the sensor housing.

causes.text: Loose oil-soaked connector
Cracked sensor housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P252F.title: Engine Oil Level Too High
P252F.summary: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass. Overfilling raises foaming, blow-by and crankcase pressure — and on diesels with regen-by-injection, fuel dilution can drive the level up by itself.

causes.text: Overfilled at last service
Fuel dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration
Coolant intrusion (head gasket / cooler)

P2530.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit
P2530.summary: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the ignition switch run position input. The signal indicating that the ignition is in the run position is missing or implausible.

causes.text: Faulty ignition switch contacts
Wiring or connector fault

P2531.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit Low
P2531.summary: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck low — short to ground or a permanently closed contact. The ECM cannot tell when the operator releases the switch from Run, so accessory and crank logic gets confused.

causes.text: Run input wire shorted to ground
Switch contact stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2532.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit High
P2532.summary: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect when the operator turns the switch back to off/accessory, so module sleep and accessory power timeouts do not work correctly.

causes.text: Run input wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2533.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P2533.summary: General electrical fault on the ignition switch On/Start (terminal 50 / crank) input. The ECM uses this signal to know when the starter is energised — without it the ECM cannot raise fuel and timing for cranking, the engine struggles to start or stalls right after.

causes.text: Open or shorted On/Start wire

P2534.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P2534.summary: The On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see crank request when the key is at rest, blocking accessory functions or causing unexpected starter cut-off logic.

causes.text: On/Start wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2535.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P2535.summary: The On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the crank state, modules dependent on this signal are unable to time their wake-up correctly.

causes.text: On/Start wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2536.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit
P2536.summary: General electrical fault on the ignition switch accessory (terminal 75 / ACC) input. ACC tells the ECM that radio, fans, accessory loads should be powered without the engine running.

causes.text: Open or shorted ACC wire

P2537.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit Low
P2537.summary: The ACC input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see ACC active continuously and refuse to enter sleep, draining the battery.

causes.text: ACC wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2538.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit High
P2538.summary: The ACC input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot detect when the operator releases the switch from ACC, accessory power timeouts do not work.

causes.text: ACC wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2539.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2539.summary: General electrical fault on the low-pressure fuel system sensor — typically the lift-pump or pre-supply pressure sensor that monitors the rail feeding the high-pressure pump. With no valid reading, the ECM cannot verify that lift pressure is sufficient for HP-pump intake.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element

P253A.title: PTO Sense Circuit/Open
P253A.summary: The PTO sense (engagement feedback) line is open. This input tells the ECM whether the PTO clutch or driveline is actually engaged after a request — it closes the loop on the PTO enable command.

causes.text: Open sense wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P253B.title: PTO Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P253B.summary: The PTO sense circuit is electrically intact, but the engagement feedback does not match the command. The ECM requests engage and sees no engaged feedback (or vice versa) within the expected time window — drive-line slip, sticky clutch, or a mis-adjusted limit switch.

causes.text: Sticky or worn PTO clutch
Mis-adjusted limit switch
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P253C.title: PTO Sense Circuit Low
P253C.summary: The PTO sense input reads stuck low — short to ground or limit switch stuck closed. The ECM may see PTO continuously engaged.

causes.text: Sense wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P253D.title: PTO Sense Circuit High
P253D.summary: The PTO sense input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect engagement.

causes.text: Sense wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P253E.title: PTO Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P253E.summary: The PTO sense signal jumps or drops out — usually loose connectors, a chattering limit switch, or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.text: Loose connector
Chattering limit switch
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P253F.title: Engine Oil Deteriorated
P253F.summary: The oil quality monitor concludes that the engine oil has reached the end of its useful life — based on permittivity, soot content, fuel dilution and total operating hours. The ECM requests an oil change before the next regen cycle to prevent accelerated bearing wear.

causes.text: Service interval exceeded
High DPF regeneration load with fuel dilution

P2540.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2540.summary: The ECU detects a general fault in the low-pressure fuel system pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid signal the ECU cannot verify lift-pump pressure or fuel rail pre-pressure.

causes.text: Defective low-pressure sensor
Wiring or connector fault

P2541.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2541.summary: The signal of the low-pressure fuel sensor does not match the expected value during operation. Pressure does not rise as expected when the lift pump is commanded.

causes.text: Sensor drift
Clogged fuel filter
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2542.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High
P2542.summary: The low-pressure fuel system sensor signal voltage is above the upper limit. Either a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or a sensor reading pegged high after an internal failure.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2543.title: Power Demand Signal Circuit
P2543.summary: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the power demand input signal used to coordinate accessory loads (e.g. AC compressor, alternator load).

causes.text: Open signal wire
Fault in requesting module

P2544.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A
P2544.summary: The ECU detects an invalid torque-management request signal A from another control unit (e.g. transmission, ESP, ABS) on the CAN bus.

causes.text: CAN communication error
Fault in requesting module

P2545.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Range/Performance
P2545.summary: The ECM receives torque-management requests from other modules (TCM during shifts, ABS/ESC during traction events, hybrid controller). Input A is electrically intact but its values do not match the system model — out-of-range steps, jumps, or persistent values that other modules cannot confirm.

causes.text: Requesting module sending invalid values
Communication bus corruption between modules
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2546.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Low
P2546.summary: Torque management input A reads stuck low — analog short to ground or message stuck at minimum value. The ECM cannot trust the request and falls back to a safe default.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
CAN message stuck at minimum value

P2547.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A High
P2547.summary: Torque management input A reads stuck high — analog short to reference voltage or message stuck at maximum value. The ECM rejects the request to avoid running unintended high-torque commands.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
CAN message stuck at maximum value

P2548.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B
P2548.summary: General electrical fault on the second torque-management request input B. Used when more than one module needs to request torque adjustments — typically TCM on input A and ABS/ESC on input B, or chassis vs powertrain.

causes.text: Open or shorted wire / invalid CAN message

P2549.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Range/Performance
P2549.summary: Input B is electrically intact but the values are implausible — same failure mode as the A-side performance fault, applied to the second torque-management channel.

causes.text: Requesting module sending invalid values
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P254A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit/Open
P254A.summary: The PTO speed-selector switch 1 input is open. This switch lets the operator pick a preset PTO operating speed (idle, 800, 1200 rpm, etc.).

causes.text: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P254B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Range/Performance
P254B.summary: The selector input is electrically intact but the value is implausible — multiple positions asserted at once, or a value that cannot map to any of the configured speed presets. Often a sticky multi-position switch or a contaminated rotary contact.

causes.text: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P254C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Low
P254C.summary: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P254D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit High
P254D.summary: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P254E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P254E.summary: The PTO speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.text: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P254F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit
P254F.summary: General electrical fault on the engine hood (bonnet) switch circuit. The hood switch tells the body controller and (on hybrids) the high-voltage system that the hood is open — used for security, alarm and HV-safety interlock.

causes.text: Open or shorted hood-switch wire
Aged switch with corroded contacts

P2550.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Low
P2550.summary: Torque management input B reads stuck low — short to ground or message at minimum. ECM rejects the request, only A-side is used.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground

P2551.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B High
P2551.summary: Torque management input B reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or message at maximum. ECM rejects the request to avoid unintended high-torque commands.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage

P2552.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit
P2552.summary: General electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit input A. This input lets external safety functions (immobilizer, hybrid HV interlock, anti-theft) override the throttle or cut fuel delivery.

causes.text: Open or shorted inhibit wire

P2553.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Range/Performance
P2553.summary: The throttle/fuel inhibit A signal is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the immobilizer reports OK, or de-asserted while a hybrid HV interlock is active. The ECM cannot trust the signal.

causes.text: Requesting module sending an inconsistent value
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2554.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Low
P2554.summary: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted. ECM may treat it as continuous inhibit and refuse normal operation.

causes.text: Inhibit wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2555.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit High
P2555.summary: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. ECM cannot read the inhibit state and falls back to the safe default.

causes.text: Inhibit wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2556.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2556.summary: General electrical fault on the engine coolant level sensor/switch circuit. Many vehicles use a simple float-switch in the expansion tank, others use a continuous-level analog sensor.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the expansion tank

P2557.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2557.summary: The coolant level sensor is electrically intact, but the readings are implausible — for example a level that does not move at all over many drive cycles, or jumps that cannot match real coolant loss. Often a stuck float, contaminated electrode or air-locked sensor.

causes.text: Stuck float
Trapped air around the sensor
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2558.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P2558.summary: Coolant level sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P2559.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P2559.summary: Coolant level sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P255A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit/Open
P255A.summary: The second PTO speed-selector switch input is open. Switch 2 typically encodes a binary or multi-bit code together with switch 1 — together they select one of several preset PTO speeds.

causes.text: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P255B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Range/Performance
P255B.summary: PTO speed selector switch 2 is electrically intact but its value does not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted, or values that do not map to any preset.

causes.text: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P255C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Low
P255C.summary: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P255D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit High
P255D.summary: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P255E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P255E.summary: PTO speed selector 2 signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes.text: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P255F.title: A/C Request A Circuit Range/Performance
P255F.summary: The A/C request input A is electrically intact, but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the HVAC controller reports off, toggling rapidly, or sustained while compressor pressures cannot support it. The ECM disables A/C clutch engagement until the input becomes plausible.

causes.text: HVAC module sending inconsistent request
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2560.title: Engine Coolant Level Low
P2560.summary: The coolant level monitor reports the engine coolant below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks overheating, head warping and head-gasket failure.

causes.text: External coolant leak (hose, radiator, water pump)
Missed top-up since last service
Head gasket leaking coolant into combustion

P2561.title: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2561.summary: The A/C / HVAC control module has requested the ECM to illuminate the malfunction indicator (MIL) because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is stored in the HVAC module — this code only signals that the ECM has honoured the request.

causes.text: Internal fault in the HVAC module — read its DTCs

P2562.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit
P2562.summary: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor A — the feedback sensor on the wastegate or VGT actuator (often a contactless Hall sensor). Without valid position feedback the ECM cannot close the loop on boost control and falls back to open-loop duty cycle.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element after thermal cycling

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2563.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
P2563.summary: The position feedback sensor on the variable-geometry or wastegate turbocharger actuator is not communicating or is implausible. Without position feedback, boost control runs in default mode and power is reduced.

causes.text: Position sensor failed
Wiring open or chafed near turbo

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2564.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P2564.summary: Position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open reference voltage at the sensor.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2565.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit High
P2565.summary: Position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage in the signal line or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2566.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Range/Performance
P2566.summary: The turbocharger actuator position sensor reports a value, but it does not track commanded vane or wastegate position within tolerance. Often a sticky VTG mechanism due to soot.

causes.text: VTG vanes coked, sticky
Actuator linkage worn
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2567.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2567.summary: The turbocharger position sensor signal is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at zero stop.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor failed low
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2568.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
P2568.summary: The turbocharger position sensor signal is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground or sensor failed high.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor failed high
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2569.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P2569.summary: Direct Ozone Reduction (DOR) catalysts are coated radiator surfaces or dedicated catalysts that decompose tropospheric ozone passing over the radiator — used for low-emissions vehicles. The temperature sensor monitoring the DOR brick reads stuck low — short to ground or sensor short.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P256A.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P256A.summary: The idle-speed selector input is open. On commercial vehicles this switch lets the operator pick a fast-idle setpoint (for example to keep auxiliary loads supplied).

causes.text: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256B.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P256B.summary: The idle-speed selector input is electrically intact but the value does not match a valid preset — multiple positions or a non-mappable value. Often a sticky multi-position switch.

causes.text: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256C.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P256C.summary: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256D.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P256D.summary: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256E.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P256E.summary: The idle-speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Idle speed too high, too low, or unstable
Possible stalling at idle or after cold start

P256F.title: A/C Request B Circuit Range/Performance
P256F.summary: A/C request input B is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — same failure mode as the input A performance fault, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes.text: HVAC module sending inconsistent request B
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

P2570.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2570.summary: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Without a valid temperature the ECM cannot enable the DOR efficiency monitor.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2571.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2571.summary: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator pack.

causes.text: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2572.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit
P2572.summary: General electrical fault on the DOR catalyst deterioration sensor circuit. This sensor estimates the remaining ozone-conversion capacity of the DOR coating — coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by salt or grime, or thermally aged.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2573.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2573.summary: The DOR deterioration sensor is electrically intact but its readings drift or do not match the model — for example a deterioration value that does not move with km/h driven, or moves implausibly fast.

causes.text: Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2574.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Low
P2574.summary: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2575.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit High
P2575.summary: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2576.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2576.summary: The DOR deterioration sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator.

causes.text: Loose connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2577.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
P2577.summary: The DOR catalyst no longer reduces tropospheric ozone with the required efficiency, based on the deterioration sensor and operating-time model. Coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by road salt and grime, or thermally aged after many heat cycles.

causes.text: DOR coating worn off the radiator
Coating contaminated by salt and grime

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2578.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit
P2578.summary: General electrical fault on the turbocharger/supercharger shaft speed sensor A — a high-frequency Hall or eddy-current sensor on the compressor shaft. The ECM uses turbo speed for overspeed protection (typically 200,000+ rpm) and for closed-loop boost on VGT systems.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring
Aged sensor with reduced output amplitude

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2579.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2579.summary: Turbo speed sensor A is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the model — for example a speed that does not climb when boost rises, drifts away from the air-mass-flow estimate, or jumps. Often blade-fouling, a contaminated sensor tip or aged element.

causes.text: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P257A.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit/Open
P257A.summary: The control circuit that drives the vacuum reservoir control valve (or vacuum pump motor) is open. The ECM cannot energise the actuator, so vacuum is no longer maintained on demand and consumers like brake booster, EGR or HVAC dampers may run out of vacuum.

causes.text: Open control wire
Failed driver in the control module
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P257B.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit Low
P257B.summary: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The actuator may be energised continuously when it should be off.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P257C.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit High
P257C.summary: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve/motor.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P257D.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P257D.summary: The hood switch is electrically intact, but its state is implausible — for example reporting hood-open while vehicle speed is rising, or rapid toggles. Usually a worn switch with high contact bounce or a misaligned hood actuator.

causes.text: Worn switch with contact bounce
Misaligned hood actuator
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P257E.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Low
P257E.summary: The hood switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed switch. The body controller may treat the hood as permanently open and refuse to arm the alarm or close the HV interlock.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P257F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit High
P257F.summary: The hood switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The body controller cannot detect when the hood is opened.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2580.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P2580.summary: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open supply.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Open supply at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2581.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P2581.summary: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2582.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2582.summary: Turbo speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist on the sensor tip, or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes.text: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Chafed harness near the turbo
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2583.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
P2583.summary: General fault on the radar/lidar/camera distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise control. On systems with a single sensor or three sensors with a center unit, this code refers to the central sensor — without it, ACC distance control is disabled and the system falls back to plain cruise.

causes.text: Dirty sensor surface (radar emblem / camera lens)
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact
Failed sensor module

P2584.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2584.summary: The fuel additive control module — typical for diesel cars with a separate Eolys/Cerine additive tank that aids DPF regeneration — has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is in the additive module itself.

causes.text: Internal fault in the fuel additive module — read its DTCs

P2585.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Warning Lamp Request
P2585.summary: The fuel additive control module asks for the additive-low warning lamp to be illuminated — the additive tank (Eolys/Cerine, used to lower DPF regen temperature) is approaching empty or has reached a service threshold. Continued driving without refilling will eventually disable DPF regeneration.

causes.text: Additive tank low — service refill required

P2586.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit
P2586.summary: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor B — second position sensor on the same actuator (redundant Hall) or on a second turbo (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). With B invalid the ECM cannot cross-check actuator A and falls back to limited boost control.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2587.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2587.summary: Position sensor B is electrically intact, but the reading does not track sensor A or the actuator-command model. Often a misaligned redundant sensor or aged element on a second turbo.

causes.text: Sensor mounting misaligned after service
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2588.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P2588.summary: Position sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference. Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2589.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit High
P2589.summary: Position sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P258A.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A/Open
P258A.summary: The control circuit driving the electric vacuum pump (used to maintain brake-booster vacuum on direct-injection or hybrid powertrains where the engine is not always running) is open. The ECM cannot run the pump on demand — booster vacuum drops, pedal feel hardens, brake assist may be reduced.

causes.text: Open control wire to the pump
Failed driver in the control module

P258B.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P258B.summary: The vacuum pump control circuit is electrically intact, but the pump response does not match the model — pump runs longer than expected to reach setpoint, current draw rises (mechanically tight) or vacuum does not build at all. Aged motor brushes, dry vanes or a leaking line are typical causes.

causes.text: Aged motor brushes or dry vanes
Leaking vacuum line
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P258C.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Low
P258C.summary: The electric vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The pump may run continuously, drawing current and overheating, until the ECM disables the channel.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground

P258D.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A High
P258D.summary: The vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. The driver cannot pull the line low to start the pump.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open pump motor winding

P258E.title: PTO Enable Switch Performance
P258E.summary: The PTO enable switch is electrically intact but its state does not match operating conditions — for example asserted while the vehicle is rolling above the PTO speed limit, or asserted/de-asserted in fast succession. The ECM rejects the request to avoid unsafe PTO engagement.

causes.text: Switch contact bounce
Switch operated while vehicle is moving

P258F.title: Torque Management Request Output Signal
P258F.summary: The ECM/PCM produces a torque-management output signal for downstream consumers (TCM during shifts, hybrid module, transfer case) and detects a fault on this output — open, short, or feedback voltage outside expected range. Without it, downstream modules cannot synchronise their behaviour with the engine.

causes.text: Open or shorted output line
Downstream consumer not loading the line

P2590.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2590.summary: Position sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration on the actuator, oil mist contamination or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes.text: Vibration-induced chafing of the harness
Oil mist on the sensor
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2591.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Left
P2591.summary: General fault on the left-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Multi-sensor radar arrays use left/center/right sensors for wider field-of-view and lane discrimination — without left, ACC may degrade to single-target tracking.

causes.text: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact

P2592.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Right
P2592.summary: General fault on the right-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Same role as the left sensor but covering the right field-of-view.

causes.text: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact

P2593.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2593.summary: General electrical fault on the second turbocharger speed sensor B — used on twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage installations to read the second compressor shaft speed. Same role as sensor A on the second turbo.

causes.text: Open or shorted wiring

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2594.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2594.summary: Turbo speed sensor B is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the boost or air-mass model — same failure mode as sensor A performance fault, applied to the second turbo.

causes.text: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2595.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2595.summary: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2596.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P2596.summary: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes.text: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2597.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2597.summary: Turbo speed sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist or chafed wiring at the second turbo.

causes.text: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P2598.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck Low
P2598.summary: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the low end of its travel even when the actuator is commanded to move. Either the actuator is mechanically stuck closed (wastegate jammed shut, VGT vanes seized at minimum opening) or the sensor itself is pegged low.

causes.text: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end
Sensor pegged low

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P2599.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck High
P2599.summary: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the high end of its travel — actuator stuck open (wastegate held wide open, VGT vanes seized at maximum opening) or sensor pegged high. Boost suffers — typically underboost on VGT, overboost-protection-off on wastegate.

causes.text: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259A.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck Low
P259A.summary: Same condition as the A-side stuck-low fault, but on the second sensor / second turbo. Position sensor B reads stuck near the low end while the actuator is commanded.

causes.text: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259B.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck High
P259B.summary: Same as the A-side stuck-high fault, applied to sensor B / turbo B. Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259C.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger A Boost Control
P259C.summary: After start-up the boost-control loop on turbo A takes longer than the calibration limit to transition from open-loop to closed-loop control. Typically a slow-warming actuator (VGT vanes carbonised), a sluggish position sensor or a leaky pneumatic actuator that cannot follow setpoints quickly enough.

causes.text: Carbonised VGT vanes
Leaky pneumatic actuator

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger B Boost Control
P259D.summary: Same condition as the turbo A excessive-warm-up fault, applied to the second turbo. Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Carbonised VGT vanes

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259E.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P259E.summary: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the low end of its travel for too long — the closed-loop controller is saturated against the lower stop trying to reach the boost setpoint. Indicates either a leak (wastegate held closed but boost still escapes) or commanded boost above what the engine can produce.

causes.text: Boost leak in the charge-air path
Failing turbocharger that cannot produce target boost

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P259F.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At High Limit
P259F.summary: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the high end of its travel — the controller is saturated against the upper stop trying to bleed off boost. Indicates either a wastegate stuck closed, oversized turbo for the calibration, or commanded boost limits being exceeded by ambient conditions (cold dense air).

causes.text: Wastegate stuck closed

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A0.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P25A0.summary: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.text: Boost leak in the charge-air path

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A1.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit
P25A1.summary: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes.text: Wastegate stuck closed

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25A2.title: Brake System Control Module A Requested MIL Illumination
P25A2.summary: The primary brake system control module (ABS/ESC/iBooster) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side — for example a regenerative braking fault on a hybrid that affects driveline torque flow. The original fault is in the brake module.

causes.text: Internal fault in the brake module — read its DTCs

P25A3.title: Engine Hood Open
P25A3.summary: After plausibility checks the body controller has concluded that the engine hood is genuinely open while the vehicle is operating. Used to suspend HV operation on hybrids/EVs (HV interlock), block remote engine start, and trigger the alarm if armed.

causes.text: Hood not properly latched
Failed hood latch sensor

P25A4.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit
P25A4.summary: General electrical fault on the fuel mode select switch — used on bi-fuel vehicles (CNG/LPG/H2/gasoline) so the driver can pick the active fuel. With the input invalid, the ECM falls back to the default fuel and disables operator-selectable switching.

causes.text: Open or shorted switch wire

P25A5.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Performance
P25A5.summary: The fuel mode select switch is electrically intact, but its state does not match operating conditions — switched to gas while gas tank is empty, or fast toggling. The ECM rejects the request to avoid stalling.

causes.text: Switch contact bounce

P25A6.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Low
P25A6.summary: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25A7.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit High
P25A7.summary: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25A8.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25A8.summary: Fuel mode switch signal jumps or drops out — worn contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Worn switch contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component

P25A9.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit/Open
P25A9.summary: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit is open. Modern engines with under-piston oil jets switch them on under high load to cool the piston crown — controlled by a solenoid valve in the oil gallery.

causes.text: Open control wire to the solenoid
Open solenoid coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P25AA.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Low
P25AA.summary: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The jets may be enabled continuously, raising oil pump load and lowering oil pressure to other consumers.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25AB.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit High
P25AB.summary: Control circuit stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25AC.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P25AC.summary: The control circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid valve does not open when commanded — confirmed by oil-pressure or oil-temperature feedback that does not change after the activation pulse. Piston cooling does not engage under high load — risk of piston-crown overheating and ring-land cracks.

causes.text: Solenoid stuck closed by oil sludge
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P25AD.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Stuck On
P25AD.summary: The piston cooling solenoid does not close when commanded off — jets remain active when not needed. Oil pressure to top-end consumers may sag, and warm-up takes longer because the cooling jets remove heat from the pistons during cold start.

causes.text: Solenoid stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P25AE.title: Piston Cooling Oil Pressure Too Low
P25AE.summary: With the piston-cooling jets commanded on, the dedicated oil-pressure sensor in that gallery reads below the safe threshold. Insufficient flow to the jets means real piston cooling is not happening — the ECM warns the driver and may reduce torque to protect the pistons.

causes.text: Low engine oil level
Sludge-clogged oil gallery
Worn oil pump

P25AF.title: Coolant Temperature Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P25AF.summary: A dedicated coolant-temperature control module (used on engines with electric coolant pumps and electronic thermostats to keep the cylinder head and block at independent setpoints) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. Original fault is in that module.

causes.text: Internal fault — read the module DTCs

P25B0.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Stuck
P25B0.summary: Fuel level sensor A (typically the float in the main fuel tank section) reports a value that does not change over a long driving distance — the float is mechanically stuck against the tank wall, baffle or pump module. Without level changes the EVAP monitor cannot run and remaining-range estimates are wrong.

causes.text: Stuck float
Bent float arm catching the tank wall

P25B1.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Stuck
P25B1.summary: Same condition as sensor A stuck, applied to the second fuel level sensor B. Saddle tanks (often AWD vehicles) and large trucks use two sensors — one per tank chamber — averaged for total level.

causes.text: Stuck float

P25B2.title: Fuel Level Sensor A or B Stuck
P25B2.summary: The ECM detects that one of the two level sensors is stuck but cannot identify which from the available signals — for example because the saddle-tank algorithm sees implausible delta only intermittently. Both sensors should be inspected.

causes.text: One stuck float — inspect both

P25B3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Open
P25B3.summary: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck open. Exhaust gas bypasses the turbine even at low load — turbo cannot reach target speed, boost is permanently low and the engine feels asthmatic.

causes.text: Seized wastegate linkage
Broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Closed
P25B4.summary: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck closed. The turbo cannot bleed off exhaust at high load — boost overshoots the setpoint, risking overboost cut-off and damage to the turbo bearing.

causes.text: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Seized linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Open
P25B5.summary: Same as wastegate A stuck open, applied to the second wastegate (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Seized wastegate linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B6.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Closed
P25B6.summary: Same as wastegate A stuck closed, applied to the second wastegate. Boost control tracks commanded vs.

causes.text: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25B7.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P25B7.summary: General electrical fault on the auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input. Used on commercial vehicles or upfit applications where a second ignition switch (in a sleeper cab, work platform or crew compartment) can crank the engine.

causes.text: Open or shorted wire

P25B8.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P25B8.summary: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25B9.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P25B9.summary: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25BA.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit/Open
P25BA.summary: The DPF/SCR forced-regeneration request switch — used on commercial vehicles to let the operator force a parked regeneration when the automatic regen has been postponed too often — is open. The ECM cannot honour an operator request for forced regen.

causes.text: Open switch wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P25BB.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit Low
P25BB.summary: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. The ECM may see a constant regen request which it cannot service while the vehicle is moving.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P25BC.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit High
P25BC.summary: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P25BD.title: Unmetered Fuel - Forced Engine Shutdown
P25BD.summary: The engine controller commanded a forced shutdown after detecting unmetered fuel reaching the combustion chambers. Common on diesels with leaking turbo seals or cracked intercoolers that drip oil into the intake — the engine then runs on the oil and can overspeed.

causes.text: Turbocharger oil seal leak feeds engine oil into the intake
Oil collected in the intercooler is sucked into the engine on load
Failed PCV / crankcase breather floods intake with oil mist

P25BE.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit / Open
P25BE.summary: The controller cannot drive the alternative-fuel disable line that switches a bi-fuel vehicle (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) back to gasoline. An open detected on the control side blocks the safety shutoff for the gas system.

causes.text: Broken wire or corroded connector on the disable control line
Open coil in the alt-fuel disable relay
Output driver in the alt-fuel control module faulty

P25BF.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit High
P25BF.summary: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is above the expected window. Often a short to battery upstream of the relay or a stuck-on driver in the control module.

causes.text: Disable control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Output driver stuck on inside the control module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C0.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit Low
P25C0.summary: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a failed driver pulling the line low.

causes.text: Disable control wire shorted to ground
Low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C1.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit
P25C1.summary: The feedback signal that confirms the alt-fuel disable command was carried out is missing or out of range. The fuel system cannot verify that the gas circuit is shut.

causes.text: Open feedback wire between relay and control module
Feedback contact in the disable relay corroded or stuck

P25C2.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit High
P25C2.summary: The disable feedback signal sits above its valid window. Typical cause is a short to battery on the feedback wire or a failed pull-up in the input stage.

causes.text: Feedback wire shorted to a B+ supply
Pull-up resistor in the input stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C3.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit Low
P25C3.summary: The disable feedback signal sits below its valid window. Usually a short to ground or an open pull-up that lets the input float low.

causes.text: Feedback wire shorted to ground
Open pull-up resistor in the controller input
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25C4.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P25C4.summary: The temperature sensor monitoring the electric brake booster (iBooster, eBooster) returns no usable signal. Without temperature feedback the controller derates booster assist to protect the motor.

causes.text: Open sensor element or broken sensor wire
Corroded connector on the booster sensor pigtail

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C5.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P25C5.summary: The booster temperature sensor reading is implausible relative to commanded assist or coolant temperature. The signal moves too slowly, sticks, or never reaches expected values during operation.

causes.text: Sensor drift or contamination on the temperature element
Sensor not seated properly against the booster motor housing
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C6.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P25C6.summary: The booster temperature signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Typical causes are a shorted sensor element or a short to ground in the harness.

causes.text: Internal short in the sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C7.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P25C7.summary: The booster temperature signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to a 5 V reference in the harness.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C8.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25C8.summary: The booster temperature signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during vibration or thermal expansion.

causes.text: Sensor connector not fully seated or pin tension lost
Harness chafed against booster housing or pedal bracket
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25C9.title: Brake System Control Module B Requested MIL Illumination
P25C9.summary: A second brake system control module (typically the redundant secondary unit on by-wire or AV-grade brake systems) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.text: Active DTC stored in the secondary brake module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P25CA.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25CA.summary: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.text: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CB.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25CB.summary: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CC.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25CC.summary: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CD.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25CD.summary: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.text: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CE.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25CE.summary: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25CF.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25CF.summary: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D0.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25D0.summary: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.text: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D1.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25D1.summary: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D2.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25D2.summary: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D3.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25D3.summary: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes.text: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D4.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25D4.summary: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D5.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25D5.summary: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25D6.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop Performance
P25D6.summary: During self-calibration of the exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A, the position sensor never reached the expected mechanical stop. The controller cannot zero the position reference, so commanded openings will be inaccurate.

causes.text: Soot or carbon deposits prevent valve from reaching the stop
Worn linkage between actuator and valve flap
Position sensor not aligned with valve shaft

P25D7.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit
P25D7.summary: A third fuel level sensor (C) used on multi-tank trucks, dual-saddle SUVs, or auxiliary fuel systems returns no usable signal. Without it, calculated fuel level and EVAP monitor enabling will be off.

causes.text: Open sender resistor or broken float
Corroded tank pump module connector

P25D8.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Performance
P25D8.summary: The third fuel level sensor reading does not change as expected with consumption or refuelling. Float may be sticking, or the resistor track has localised wear.

causes.text: Float arm stuck on baffle or fuel pump module
Worn spot on the resistor track at common fill level

P25D9.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P25D9.summary: The third fuel level sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sender or a short to ground in the harness.

causes.text: Internal short in the sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DA.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit High
P25DA.summary: The third fuel level sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sender or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.text: Open sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P25DB.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P25DB.summary: The third fuel level sensor signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during driving vibration.

causes.text: Tank module connector not fully seated
Harness chafed near tank straps
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P25DC.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Stuck
P25DC.summary: The third fuel level sensor reads a constant value across known consumption or refuelling events. Float arm or resistor wiper is mechanically stuck.

causes.text: Float arm jammed against tank wall, baffle or pump module
Resistor wiper seized by varnish from old fuel

P25DD.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25DD.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.text: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DE.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25DE.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.text: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25DF.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25DF.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.text: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E0.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
