P25E0.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.text: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E1.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E1.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.text: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E2.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E2.summary: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.text: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E3.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25E3.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.text: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E4.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25E4.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.text: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E5.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25E5.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.text: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E6.title: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E6.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes.text: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E7.title: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E7.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes.text: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E8.title: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E8.summary: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes.text: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P25E9.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Open
P25E9.summary: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not close. The supercharger stays disengaged so boost from this stage is unavailable, which limits torque and may also affect cooling pump drives shared with the same belt.

causes.text: Open electromagnetic clutch coil
Worn friction surfaces leave the air gap too large to attract
Corroded armature plate stuck open

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EA.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Stuck Closed
P25EA.summary: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not open. The supercharger remains coupled at all loads, increasing parasitic loss and fuel consumption when boost is not needed.

causes.text: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Failed pulley bearing welds clutch surfaces

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EB.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Range/Performance
P25EB.summary: The supercharger clutch control current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Either coil resistance has drifted or the driver feedback is implausible.

causes.text: Coil resistance increased due to thermal damage
High-resistance contact in the clutch connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EC.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit Low
P25EC.summary: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted clutch coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25ED.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch Circuit High
P25ED.summary: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open coil that lets the driver float high.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25EE.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B / Open
P25EE.summary: The controller cannot drive the secondary electric vacuum pump (B). Brake servo or HVAC actuators that depend on engine vacuum may not get enough vacuum during low-load operation or with engine off in stop-start mode.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding or worn brushes
Broken control wire between ECU and pump

P25EF.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P25EF.summary: The secondary vacuum pump does not produce the expected vacuum within the commanded run time. Leak in the pump line or worn pump diaphragm reduces output.

causes.text: Worn diaphragm or vanes inside the pump
Cracked vacuum hose or loose connection
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P25F0.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Low
P25F0.summary: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor winding

P25F1.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B High
P25F1.summary: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor that lets the driver float high.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open motor winding or worn brushes

P25F2.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit
P25F2.summary: A third boost pressure sensor (C) used on twin-stage or sequential boost systems returns no usable signal. Without it, boost control of the third stage runs open-loop or is disabled.

causes.text: Open sensor element or broken signal wire
Corroded connector at sensor pigtail

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P25F3.summary: The third boost pressure sensor reading is implausible compared with manifold pressure or commanded boost. Either drift, leak in the sensing line, or contamination on the sensor diaphragm.

causes.text: Sensor drift after thermal aging
Sensing hose blocked by oil residue
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Low
P25F4.summary: The third boost pressure sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor element or a short to ground.

causes.text: Internal short in the sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit High
P25F5.summary: The third boost pressure sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25F6.title: AIR System B
P25F6.summary: A general fault in the second secondary air injection (AIR) circuit. Detected by the O2 sensors which expect a lean swing during cold-start AIR pump operation but do not see one.

causes.text: Failed AIR pump motor or impeller
Check valve seized by exhaust soot
Corroded or cracked air injection pipe

P25F7.title: AIR System B Incorrect Flow Detected
P25F7.summary: The second AIR system delivers measurably more or less air than expected. Often a partially blocked pipe, a worn pump, or a leak between pump and check valve.

causes.text: Air pipe partially blocked by carbon
Worn pump impeller reduces flow
Leak between pump and check valve

P25F8.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit
P25F8.summary: A third bypass (recirculation or wastegate) valve used in three-stage charging systems is not responding to control commands. Boost balancing across stages can no longer be achieved.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil
Open or shorted wiring to the valve

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25F9.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P25F9.summary: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P25FA.summary: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FB.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P25FB.summary: The third bypass valve current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Drifted coil resistance or high-resistance contact in the connector.

causes.text: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
High-resistance contact in the valve connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Charging may not start or interrupts

P25FC.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C - Mechanical
P25FC.summary: The third bypass valve is mechanically jammed. Solenoid is energised correctly but the valve flap or disc does not move as expected.

causes.text: Carbon buildup blocks the valve flap
Actuator linkage seized by corrosion

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FD.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Temperature Too High
P25FD.summary: The third bypass valve has reached over-temperature. Either coil duty cycle is too high for too long, or cooling air flow around the valve is restricted.

causes.text: Sustained high duty cycle from charge balancing strategy
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Possible blue or black smoke from exhaust
Whistling or hissing sound from intake

P25FE.title: Supercharger Disconnect Clutch
P25FE.summary: A general performance fault in the supercharger disconnect clutch. Engagement or release is slow, sticky, or out of tolerance without a clear electrical-side cause.

causes.text: Worn friction surfaces or air gap drift
Oil or debris on the clutch face

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P25FF.title: Electrical System Voltage Stabilizer Control Module Performance
P25FF.summary: The voltage stabiliser module (DC/DC converter for stop-start engine cranking events) does not maintain the regulated 12 V output during high transient loads. Sensitive electronics may reset during cranking.

causes.text: Aged smoothing capacitors lose capacitance
Battery condition causes input voltage to drop too far
Internal fault in the converter switching stage

P2600.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit / Open
P2600.summary: The controller cannot drive the electric coolant pump A control line. Without circulation, engine and aftertreatment can overheat or warm up incorrectly.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P2601.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2601.summary: The electric coolant pump A is commanded on but does not run. Coolant temperature climbs faster than expected with no flow detected.

causes.text: Pump motor seized by debris or sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2602.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Open
P2602.summary: The ECU detects an open circuit on the electric coolant pump control line. Without pump control the engine cannot actively manage warm-up and cool-down phases.

causes.text: Pump motor open
Drive line open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2603.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P2603.summary: The electric coolant pump drive line reads below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to ground
Driver stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2604.title: Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P2604.summary: The electric coolant pump drive line reads above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or a stuck-on driver stage.

causes.text: Drive line shorted to positive
Driver stage shorted on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2605.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit / Open
P2605.summary: The controller cannot drive the secondary intake air heater (heater grid B) used on diesel engines for cold-start support. The grid stays cold so cold-start emissions and white smoke increase.

causes.text: Open heater grid element
Failed heater relay or open coil

P2606.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Range/Performance
P2606.summary: The secondary intake air heater current does not match expected resistance. Either the grid is partially open or the relay contacts have high resistance.

causes.text: Partial element failure raises grid resistance
Burned relay contacts
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2607.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Low
P2607.summary: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted relay coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2608.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit High
P2608.summary: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open relay coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2609.title: Intake Air Heater System Performance
P2609.summary: The intake air heater system did not raise intake temperature by the expected amount during cold-start support. Suggests low current draw, poor connection to the grid, or a failed temperature feedback path.

causes.text: High-resistance battery feed to the heater
Intake air temperature sensor reads with offset

P260A.title: PTO Control Circuit / Open
P260A.summary: The controller cannot drive the power take-off (PTO) engagement line on commercial vehicles. The PTO will not engage even when commanded by the body controller or operator switch.

causes.text: Open coil in the PTO engagement solenoid
Broken wire to the PTO solenoid

P260B.title: PTO Control Circuit Low
P260B.summary: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260C.title: PTO Control Circuit High
P260C.summary: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260D.title: PTO Engaged Lamp Control Circuit
P260D.summary: The dashboard PTO engaged lamp control circuit is faulty. Driver may not see whether the PTO is currently driving an external accessory.

causes.text: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire between cluster and ECU

P260E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Lamp Control Circuit
P260E.summary: The DPF regeneration warning lamp circuit is faulty. The driver may not be alerted to a required highway run that supports passive regeneration.

causes.text: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire to the cluster

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P260F.title: EVAP System Monitoring Processor Performance
P260F.summary: The dedicated EVAP monitoring processor (often a small auxiliary CPU inside the engine controller or a separate module) does not pass its self-test or runs out of step with the main monitor logic.

causes.text: Internal fault in the monitoring processor
Software memory corruption
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2610.title: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
P2610.summary: The engine controller's internal soak-time/engine-off timer fails its plausibility check — for example readings claim instant cool-down or never-cooled. Cold-start enrichment, EVAP and catalyst monitors depend on this timer; a fault freezes those readiness monitors.

causes.text: ECU internal timer fault
Keep-alive memory power intermittent

P2611.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2611.summary: The A/C refrigerant distribution valve A (used to switch refrigerant flow between front and rear evaporators or between cabin and battery cooling on EVs) cannot be driven by the controller.

causes.text: Open coil in the valve solenoid
Broken control wire

P2612.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2612.summary: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the valve solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2613.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit High
P2613.summary: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2614.title: Camshaft Position Output Circuit/Open
P2614.summary: The camshaft position output signal sent from the ECU to other modules is interrupted. Other systems that rely on the cam reference (e.g.

causes.text: Open output wiring
Internal ECU output driver fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2615.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 1
P2615.summary: The buffered camshaft A position output that the engine controller sends to other modules (transmission, body, ignition module) is below the expected level on bank 1. Other modules cannot use the cam phase reference for synchronisation.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2616.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 1
P2616.summary: The buffered camshaft A position output is above the expected level on bank 1. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Power loss especially in mid-rpm range

P2617.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit / Open
P2617.summary: The buffered crankshaft position output that the engine controller sends to ignition modules and the transmission cannot drive its line. Open detected on the output side.

causes.text: Open wire between ECU and downstream module
Output buffer internally open

P2618.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit Low
P2618.summary: The buffered crankshaft position output is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground on the output line or a failed buffer.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to ground
Buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2619.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit High
P2619.summary: The buffered crankshaft position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261A.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P261A.summary: The controller cannot drive the second electric coolant pump (B). Often used for aftertreatment, turbo cool-down, or hybrid battery loops — fault stops circulation in that loop.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P261B.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P261B.summary: The second electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run. Cooling demand of the connected loop is not satisfied.

causes.text: Pump motor seized by sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261C.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P261C.summary: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Motor winding short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261D.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P261D.summary: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261E.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Stuck On
P261E.summary: The second coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.text: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261F.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Stuck On
P261F.summary: The first coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.text: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2620.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit
P2620.summary: A general electrical fault on the ECU output that broadcasts the throttle position signal to other modules — for example to the transmission control or hybrid drive controller.

causes.text: Output wire open or shorted
ECU output stage failed

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2621.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit Low
P2621.summary: The buffered throttle position output that the engine controller sends to the transmission and body modules is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or a failed output stage.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2622.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit High
P2622.summary: The buffered throttle position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.text: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P2623.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit / Open
P2623.summary: The Injector Control Pressure (ICP) regulator on hydraulically actuated injectors (HEUI diesel) or the high-pressure regulator on common-rail systems cannot be driven. Injection pressure cannot be controlled, engine may not start.

causes.text: Open coil in the pressure regulator
Broken control wire

P2624.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit Low
P2624.summary: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted regulator coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2625.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit High
P2625.summary: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open regulator coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2626.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2626.summary: The ECU detects an open in the pumping current trim circuit of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1 sensor 1. Without trim correction, the lambda value reported by the sensor is not accurate.

causes.text: Trim wire open
Internal sensor fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P2627.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2627.summary: On a wide-band (broadband) O2 sensor, the trim resistor circuit that calibrates the pumping current is reading low on bank 1 sensor 1. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.text: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2628.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2628.summary: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 1 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing offsets that the controller cannot compensate.

causes.text: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2629.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit / Open Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2629.summary: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 is open. Air-fuel feedback for bank 2 cannot be calibrated, fuel control runs degraded.

causes.text: Open calibration trim resistor
Open sensor connector pin

P262A.title: Fuel Injector - Pilot Injection Not Learned
P262A.summary: The pilot (pre) injection learning routine on a common-rail diesel did not complete successfully. Without learned pilot quantity, combustion noise increases and NOx may rise.

causes.text: Injector flow drift outside learning window
Unstable rail pressure during learning cycle

symptoms: Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P262B.title: Control Module Power Off Timer Performance
P262B.summary: The internal power-down timer of the engine controller does not run as expected. The module either stays awake too long after key-off (battery drain) or shuts down too early (no aftertreatment cool-down or learn-write).

causes.text: Intermittent main relay opens early
Software timer counter corrupted

P262C.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit / Open
P262C.summary: The 5 V reference G output that the engine controller supplies to a group of sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail will report invalid readings.

causes.text: Open wire on the reference rail
Open inside the ECU reference output

P262D.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Low
P262D.summary: The 5 V reference G voltage is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or excessive load from a downstream sensor pulling the rail down.

causes.text: Reference wire shorted to ground
Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262E.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit High
P262E.summary: The 5 V reference G voltage is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an internal regulator failure.

causes.text: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Internal 5 V regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262F.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Range/Performance
P262F.summary: The 5 V reference G voltage is within range but unstable or offset against expected. Loose ground or marginal regulator load.

causes.text: High-resistance ground for the reference rail
One sensor draws excessive current and shifts the rail
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2630.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2630.summary: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads low. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.text: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2631.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2631.summary: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, the controller cannot compensate the offset.

causes.text: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2632.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P2632.summary: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel pump (B). Common on dual-tank trucks, GDI lift-pump systems, or alt-fuel installations — fault stops fuel delivery from this stage.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding
Failed pump relay

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2633.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit Low
P2633.summary: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2634.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit High
P2634.summary: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2635.title: Fuel Pump A Low Flow / Performance
P2635.summary: The ECU detects insufficient fuel flow from fuel pump A. Either the pump is worn out, the supply line is restricted, or the pressure regulator does not allow proper flow.

causes.text: Worn fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter
Pressure regulator fault

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2636.title: Fuel Pump B Low Flow/Performance
P2636.summary: The second fuel pump runs but does not deliver expected volume or pressure. Worn pump, restricted filter, or leaking pressure regulator.

causes.text: Worn impeller reduces volumetric efficiency
Restricted in-tank or in-line fuel filter
Pressure regulator leaks back to tank

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P2637.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A
P2637.summary: The torque feedback signal A from the transmission or other torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot reduce torque on shift requests, which can cause harsh shifts.

causes.text: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2638.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
P2638.summary: The torque feedback signal A is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.text: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2639.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Low
P2639.summary: The torque feedback signal A reads below its valid range. Either the source reports a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.text: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P263A.title: MIL Control Circuit Low
P263A.summary: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted bulb driver.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Bulb driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263B.title: MIL Control Circuit High
P263B.summary: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open lamp.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Burnt-out MIL bulb
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263C.title: Glow Plug Control Driver Performance
P263C.summary: The glow plug control driver does not respond to commands within tolerance. Cold-start glow function is degraded so cold starting can be delayed and white smoke increases.

causes.text: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Current feedback loop noisy

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263D.title: Reductant Heater Driver Performance
P263D.summary: The reductant (AdBlue) tank or line heater driver does not switch as expected. AdBlue may freeze in cold weather, blocking SCR dosing.

causes.text: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Heater element resistance drifted out of range

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P263E.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Over Temperature
P263E.summary: The first glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.text: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Over Temperature
P263F.summary: The second glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.text: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P2640.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A High
P2640.summary: The torque feedback signal A reads above its valid range. Source module sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.text: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2641.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B
P2641.summary: The torque feedback signal B from a second torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot coordinate torque reduction with this user.

causes.text: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2642.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Range/Performance
P2642.summary: The torque feedback signal B is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.text: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2643.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Low
P2643.summary: The torque feedback signal B reads below its valid range. Source sends a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.text: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P2644.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B High
P2644.summary: The torque feedback signal B reads above its valid range. Source sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.text: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2645.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2645.summary: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 1 (used in cylinder deactivation systems such as VTEC, AFM, MDS). The valve lift mode cannot be switched.

causes.text: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire

P2646.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2646.summary: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 1 is commanded to engage (high lift or all-cylinder mode) but does not switch. Engine stays in low-lift or deactivated mode under load, causing reduced power.

causes.text: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2647.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2647.summary: On variable valve lift systems (e.g. Honda VTEC) the ECU detects that the bank 1 rocker arm actuator is stuck in the engaged (high lift) position.

causes.text: Insufficient oil pressure / level
Stuck VVL solenoid
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2648.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2648.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2649.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2649.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264A.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P264A.summary: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of valve lift cannot verify the state.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector

P264B.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P264B.summary: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes on bank 1. Sensor drift or mechanical wear leaves the signal between expected values.

causes.text: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P264C.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P264C.summary: The position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor or short to ground in the harness.

causes.text: Internal short in sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264D.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P264D.summary: The position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264E.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P264E.summary: The position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire in the harness.

causes.text: Sensor connector not fully seated
Harness chafed against valve cover or cam carrier
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P264F.title: Engine Serial Number Not Programmed or Incompatible
P264F.summary: The engine controller cannot read a valid engine serial number from its non-volatile memory, or the stored value does not match the expected pattern. Calibration sets keyed to the serial number cannot be applied.

causes.text: Replacement ECU not programmed at install
Non-volatile memory corruption

P2650.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2650.summary: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 1. The second valve lift mode cannot be commanded.

causes.text: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire

P2651.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2651.summary: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift or cylinder mode under load.

causes.text: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2652.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2652.summary: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 stays in the activated state when commanded off. Engine cannot return to the alternate lift or cylinder mode.

causes.text: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2653.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2653.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2654.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2654.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2655.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2655.summary: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 2. The valve lift mode cannot be switched on this bank.

causes.text: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire

P2656.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2656.summary: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift mode under load on this bank.

causes.text: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2657.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2657.summary: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes.text: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2658.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2658.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2659.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2659.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265A.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P265A.summary: The position sensor that confirms the B rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector

P265B.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P265B.summary: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator B on bank 1.

causes.text: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P265C.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P265C.summary: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Internal short in sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265D.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P265D.summary: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P265E.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P265E.summary: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire.

causes.text: Sensor connector not fully seated
Harness chafed against valve cover
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P265F.title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit Range/Performance
P265F.summary: The variable-displacement A/C compressor control valve does not respond to commands within tolerance. Refrigerant flow regulation is degraded so cabin temperature varies or efficiency drops.

causes.text: Control valve spool sticky from oil residue
Solenoid coil resistance drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2660.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2660.summary: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 2.

causes.text: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire

P2661.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2661.summary: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch.

causes.text: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2662.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2662.summary: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes.text: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2663.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2663.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2664.title: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2664.summary: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2665.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit / Open
P2665.summary: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel shutoff valve. Engine cannot be commanded off through this path during a safety event.

causes.text: Open coil in shutoff valve
Broken control wire

P2666.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Low
P2666.summary: Voltage on the secondary fuel shutoff valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2667.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit High
P2667.summary: Voltage on the secondary fuel shutoff valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2668.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit
P2668.summary: The fuel mode indicator lamp circuit (showing whether a bi-fuel vehicle currently runs on gasoline or alternative fuel) is faulty. Driver may not know the active fuel.

causes.text: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire to the cluster

P2669.title: Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit / Open
P2669.summary: The second power feed used to supply actuators (relays, solenoids, motor drivers) is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.

causes.text: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P266A.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P266A.summary: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 2 returns no usable signal.

causes.text: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector

P266B.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P266B.summary: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator A on bank 2.

causes.text: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

Broken return spring

P26C1.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Range/Performance
P26C1.summary: The fourth coolant bypass valve responds to commands but the resulting coolant temperature behaviour is not as expected.

causes.text: Valve partially stuck by sediment
Weak return spring fails to close fully
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P26C2.title: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve D Stuck Closed
P26C2.summary: The fourth coolant bypass valve is stuck closed.

causes.text: Valve seized closed by debris
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26C3.title: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Sensor Performance
P26C3.summary: The internal transmission range sensor inside the control module (used for redundancy on shift-by-wire systems) does not match the external sensor reading.

causes.text: Internal sensor drift
External range sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26C4.title: Internal Control Module Clutch Pedal Performance
P26C4.summary: The internal clutch pedal interpretation logic in the control module does not match the external clutch switch state. Manual transmission start interlock or stop-start enable can misbehave.

causes.text: External clutch switch drift
Signal corruption between switch and ECU

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26C5.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P26C5.summary: The controller cannot drive the exhaust flow control valve A (used for exhaust acoustics, EGR boost, or aftertreatment heating).

causes.text: Open coil in valve solenoid
Broken control wire

P26C6.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit Low
P26C6.summary: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is below the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C7.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Circuit High
P26C7.summary: Voltage on the exhaust flow control valve A control line is above the expected window. The exhaust control valve modulates exhaust backpressure or routing (EGR feed, sound, regen support); a malfunction shifts torque mapping and may trigger limp mode.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26C8.title: Chassis Control Module 1 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C8.summary: A chassis control module (typically active suspension, AWD coupling, or steering controller) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.text: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26C9.title: Chassis Control Module 2 Requested MIL Illumination
P26C9.summary: A second chassis control module has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes.text: Active DTC stored in the chassis module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request

P26CA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit / Open
P26CA.summary: The controller cannot drive the main electric coolant pump. Without flow the engine and aftertreatment will overheat under load.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P26CB.title: Engine Coolant Pump Performance/Stuck Off
P26CB.summary: The main electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run.

causes.text: Pump motor seized by sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26CC.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P26CC.summary: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Motor winding short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CD.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P26CD.summary: Voltage on the engine coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26CE.title: Engine Coolant Pump Overspeed/Air In System
P26CE.summary: The coolant pump speed feedback is higher than the commanded value with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.text: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26CF.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage
P26CF.summary: The integrated controller of the smart coolant pump reports a system voltage out of operating range.

causes.text: Weak battery sags voltage under pump load
Alternator output out of regulation

P26D0.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage Low
P26D0.summary: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage below operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.text: Weak battery sags voltage under load
Alternator output below regulation point

P26D1.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module System Voltage High
P26D1.summary: The smart coolant pump module reports the system voltage above operating range. Pump output is reduced or disabled to protect the module.

causes.text: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Load dump transient after disconnecting a heavy load

P26D2.title: Engine Coolant Pump Control Module Over Temperature
P26D2.summary: The smart coolant pump controller has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow.

causes.text: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
Cabin heater weak or excessively hot
Possible long warm-up time or hard cold start

P26D3.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit
P26D3.summary: The dedicated supply voltage line to the coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

causes.text: Blown fuse on supply line
High-resistance contact in supply harness

P26D4.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P26D4.summary: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is below operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: High-resistance battery feed
Weak battery sags under pump current
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D5.title: Engine Coolant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P26D5.summary: The dedicated supply voltage to the coolant pump module is above operating range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Alternator regulator failed to limit output
Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26D6.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit / Open
P26D6.summary: The mechanical clutch on a belt-driven coolant pump (used to disengage the pump for fast warm-up) cannot be driven. Pump always engaged so warm-up takes longer.

causes.text: Open coil in clutch solenoid
Broken control wire

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D7.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Performance/Stuck Off
P26D7.summary: The coolant pump clutch is commanded on but does not engage. Coolant flow is missing under load, leading to overheating.

causes.text: Worn friction surfaces enlarge air gap
Weak solenoid magnetic force
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D8.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Stuck On
P26D8.summary: The coolant pump clutch remains engaged when commanded off. Pump runs continuously, slowing warm-up and increasing parasitic load.

causes.text: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26D9.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit Low
P26D9.summary: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26DA.title: Engine Coolant Pump Clutch Control Circuit High
P26DA.summary: Voltage on the coolant pump clutch control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P26DB.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit / Open
P26DB.summary: The active engine sound generator A (Active Sound Design or AVAS — Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System for EV/hybrid) cannot be driven. EV pedestrian warning sound or sport-mode engine sound is missing.

causes.text: Open output stage in the sound amplifier
Broken control wire to amplifier

P26DC.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Low
P26DC.summary: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Amplifier input stage short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DD.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit High
P26DD.summary: Voltage on the sound generator A control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Amplifier input stage open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26DE.title: Engine Sound Control A Circuit Performance
P26DE.summary: The sound generator A circuit responds to commands but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected. Speaker damage or feedback path noise.

causes.text: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted
Feedback microphone drifts

P26DF.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit / Open
P26DF.summary: The 5 V supply rail D for sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail report invalid readings.

causes.text: Open wire on the supply rail
Open inside the ECU regulator output

P26E0.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit Low
P26E0.summary: The 5 V supply rail D is below the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Reference wire shorted to ground
Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E1.title: Sensor Power Supply D Circuit High
P26E1.summary: The 5 V supply rail D is above the expected level. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Internal 5 V regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E2.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Low
P26E2.summary: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Bulb driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E3.title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit High
P26E3.summary: Voltage on the fuel mode indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Burnt-out indicator bulb
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E4.title: Starter Relay B Circuit
P26E4.summary: The control circuit for the secondary starter relay (used on twin-starter heavy diesels or stop-start systems with a dedicated stop-start starter) returns no usable signal.

causes.text: Open coil in the relay
Broken control wire

P26E5.title: Starter Relay B Circuit Low
P26E5.summary: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E6.title: Starter Relay B Circuit High
P26E6.summary: Voltage on the secondary starter relay control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E7.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit / Open
P26E7.summary: The fourth actuator supply rail is open. All loads on this rail are powerless and report follow-on faults.

causes.text: Blown fuse on the supply rail
Broken supply wire from main relay

P26E8.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit Low
P26E8.summary: The fourth actuator supply rail is below the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Load on the rail shorted to ground
Battery condition causes voltage to drop
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26E9.title: Actuator Supply Voltage D Circuit High
P26E9.summary: The fourth actuator supply rail is above the expected voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Alternator regulator failure
Wiring shorted to a higher-voltage circuit
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EA.title: Fuel Pump Control Module B
P26EA.summary: A general fault in the second fuel pump control module (smart pump controller, separate from the ECU). Internal self-test failed or communication with the ECU is degraded.

causes.text: Internal fault in the pump module
Bus communication errors with ECU

symptoms: Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm

P26EB.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module System Voltage
P26EB.summary: The alternative fuel control module reports a system voltage out of operating range. CNG, LPG, or hydrogen fuelling can be disabled until voltage is in spec.

causes.text: Weak battery sags voltage under load
Alternator output out of regulation

P26EC.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit / Open
P26EC.summary: The second active sound generator (B) cannot be driven.

causes.text: Open output stage in the sound amplifier
Broken control wire to amplifier

P26ED.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Low
P26ED.summary: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is below the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Amplifier input stage short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EE.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit High
P26EE.summary: Voltage on the sound generator B control line is above the expected window. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Amplifier input stage open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26EF.title: Engine Sound Control B Circuit Performance
P26EF.summary: The sound generator B circuit responds but the resulting acoustic feedback is not as expected.

causes.text: Speaker cone damaged or coil shorted
Feedback microphone drifts

P26F0.title: Starter Relay A Stuck On
P26F0.summary: The first starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.text: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
ECU output driver stuck on
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F1.title: Starter Relay A Stuck Off
P26F1.summary: The first starter relay does not close when commanded on. Starter motor cannot crank, the engine will not start.

causes.text: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Open relay coil
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F2.title: Starter Relay B Stuck On
P26F2.summary: The second starter relay stays closed when commanded off. Starter motor B remains engaged after the engine is running, which can destroy the starter pinion or ring gear.

causes.text: Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current
ECU output driver stuck on
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F3.title: Starter Relay B Stuck Off
P26F3.summary: The second starter relay does not close when commanded on. The associated starter motor cannot crank.

causes.text: Burned relay contacts no longer make contact
Open relay coil
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26F4.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit / Open
P26F4.summary: The controller cannot drive the third electric coolant pump. Cooling demand of the connected loop (often hybrid power electronics or battery cooling) is not satisfied.

causes.text: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P26F5.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit Low
P26F5.summary: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F6.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit High
P26F6.summary: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.text: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F7.title: Coolant Pump C Supply Voltage Circuit
P26F7.summary: The dedicated supply voltage line to the third coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

causes.text: Blown fuse on supply line
High-resistance contact in supply harness

P26F8.title: Coolant Pump C Stuck/Stalled
P26F8.summary: The third coolant pump is commanded on but the rotor does not turn. Sediment, frozen coolant, or a foreign object jams the impeller.

causes.text: Impeller jammed by sediment or debris
Pump motor seized by bearing failure

P26F9.title: Coolant Pump C Control Module Overtemperature
P26F9.summary: The smart controller of the third coolant pump has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow around the pump electronics.

causes.text: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel around pump blocked by debris

P26FA.title: Coolant Pump C Overspeed/Air in System
P26FA.summary: The third coolant pump speed feedback is higher than commanded with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.text: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26FB.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 1
P26FB.summary: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, which slows engine warm-up and can degrade cold-start emissions.

causes.text: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FC.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 2
P26FC.summary: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, slowing engine warm-up and degrading cold-start emissions.

causes.text: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P26FD.title: A/C Compressor Internal Control Module Performance
P26FD.summary: The internal control module of an electrically driven A/C compressor (typical on hybrid and BEV vehicles) reports an internal performance fault. Compressor capacity may be reduced or shut down.

causes.text: Internal fault in compressor inverter electronics
Software error in compressor control logic
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P26FE.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Performance
P26FE.summary: The exhaust flow control valve A responds to commands but the resulting flow or back-pressure does not match expectations. Worn flap or carbon coking on the bore.

causes.text: Worn valve flap loses sealing
Carbon coking restricts valve travel

P26FF.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 2
P26FF.summary: During controller auto-configuration the expected throttle input on bank 2 was not detected. Configuration cannot complete and the second throttle path cannot be used.

causes.text: Broken signal wire from throttle B2
Hardware variant mismatch — sensor not installed

P2700.title: Transmission Friction Element A Apply Time Range/Performance
P2700.summary: The transmission control module measured an apply time for friction element A (clutch or band) outside the calibrated window. Indicates worn clutch material, low line pressure, or a degrading shift solenoid.

causes.text: Clutch pack worn
Shift solenoid response degraded
Line pressure too low

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2701.title: Transmission Friction Element B Apply Time Range/Performance
P2701.summary: The time required to apply friction element B (a clutch or band inside the automatic transmission) is outside the expected window. Either too long (worn clutch, low pressure) or too short (sticky valve, mis-calibration).

causes.text: Worn clutch friction plates
Pressure control solenoid drift
Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2702.title: Transmission Friction Element C Apply Time Range/Performance
P2702.summary: The time required to apply friction element C is outside the expected window. Worn clutch, low pressure, or sticky valve.

causes.text: Worn clutch friction plates
Pressure control solenoid drift
Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2703.title: Transmission Friction Element D Apply Time Range/Performance
P2703.summary: The time required to apply friction element D is outside the expected window.

causes.text: Worn clutch friction plates
Pressure control solenoid drift
Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2705.title: Transmission Friction Element F Apply Time Range/Performance
P2705.summary: The time required to apply friction element F is outside the expected window.

causes.text: Worn clutch friction plates
Pressure control solenoid drift
Internal hydraulic leak in apply circuit

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2706.title: Shift Solenoid F
P2706.summary: A general fault in shift solenoid F (the sixth gear-selection solenoid in 6-speed and higher transmissions). Detected through electrical resistance, hydraulic response, or downstream gear engagement check.

causes.text: Aged solenoid coil resistance drift
Worn valve body bore around the solenoid

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2707.title: Shift Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2707.summary: Shift solenoid F is commanded on but does not produce the expected hydraulic response. Spool stuck closed or hydraulic apply circuit blocked.

causes.text: Solenoid spool stuck in closed position
Apply circuit blocked by debris in valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2708.title: Shift Solenoid F Stuck On
P2708.summary: Shift solenoid F stays in the activated state when commanded off. Affected gear stays applied so the transmission cannot shift correctly.

causes.text: Solenoid spool stuck in open position
TCM output driver stuck on
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2709.title: Shift Solenoid F Electrical
P2709.summary: Electrical fault in shift solenoid F — open or shorted coil, or short to ground/battery in the harness.

causes.text: Open solenoid coil
Short to ground or battery in the harness

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P270A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Temperature Too High
P270A.summary: Friction element A inside the automatic transmission has reached over-temperature. Excessive slip during shifts or trailer towing burns the clutch.

causes.text: Excessive slip due to worn clutch or low pressure
Restricted transmission fluid cooler
Sustained heavy load such as trailer towing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2710.title: Shift Solenoid F Intermittent
P2710.summary: Shift solenoid F shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic faults that come and go. Loose connector or marginal coil.

causes.text: Solenoid connector not fully seated
Coil resistance drifts with temperature
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Possible limp mode (locked in one gear)
Slipping or shuddering during gear changes

P2711.title: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P2711.summary: The transmission disengaged mechanically without a corresponding command. The vehicle can free-wheel, which is a safety concern.

causes.text: Clutch piston seal failure releases gear
